nodes.label: Victor Lazzarini
nodes.description: Composer, educator, and leading researcher in sound synthesis and audio programming languages. Professor of Music and Dean of Arts, Celtic Studies and Philosophy at Maynooth University, and core developer of Csound.

nodes.label: Maynooth University
nodes.description: Irish university where Victor Lazzarini is Professor of Music and Dean of Arts, Celtic Studies and Philosophy.

nodes.label: Faust
nodes.description: A functional programming language designed to manipulate audio streams and implement digital signal processing algorithms, with support for compilation to C++ and Csound plugin opcodes.

nodes.label: Yann Orlarey
nodes.description: Creator of the Faust audio programming language. Collaborated with Victor Lazzarini to embed Faust compiler into Csound 6.

nodes.label: Max Mathews
nodes.description: Pioneer of computer music who created MUSIC I in 1957, the first direct digital synthesis program, and developed foundational concepts including unit generators and the compiler for music programs.

nodes.label: MUSIC I
nodes.description: First direct digital synthesis program for the IBM 704 mainframe, created by Max Mathews. Marks the year zero of computer music, with the field approaching its sixtieth anniversary in 2018.

nodes.label: Python
nodes.description: A general-purpose programming language used in the book as a glue and host language for music programming, capable of containing dedicated Csound code or complete signal processing programs.

nodes.label: Granular synthesis
nodes.description: A sound synthesis technique that divides audio into small grains and recombines them. The perceptual result depends on grain rate and duration: low rates with long grains preserve source timbre, high periodic rates create pitch, and irregular rates produce cloud-like textures.

nodes.label: Source-filter model
nodes.description: A signal processing approach that decomposes sound into a source (oscillator) and a modifier (filter), applicable to instrument synthesis and vocal synthesis.

nodes.label: Frequency-domain analysis-synthesis
nodes.description: Technique for sound generation examined in the book through mathematical expressions, graphical plots, and programming examples.

nodes.label: International Linux Audio Conference
nodes.description: Conference where Victor Lazzarini and Yann Orlarey first met in May 2004 in Karlsruhe. Victor was presenting on spectral signal processing applications.

nodes.label: John ffitch
nodes.description: Composer who created Se'nnight using Csound, employing C programs to generate sound sequences with near-chaos components and relying on Csound's backward compatibility.

nodes.label: Steven Yi
nodes.description: Composer and Csound user who developed the piece Transit using Blue and Csound, employing standardized instrument templates and graphical interfaces for composition.

nodes.label: Øyvind Brandtsegg
nodes.description: Composer and live electronics artist who created a feedback piece using audio feedback as the only sound source, with microphone positioning and algorithmic effects processing.

nodes.label: Joachim Heintz
nodes.description: Primary editor and author of the Csound FLOSS Manual, contributing to multiple sections including scanned synthesis, sound modification, samples, MIDI, and digital audio basics across all versions.

nodes.label: Richard Boulanger
nodes.description: Editor of The Csound Book and computer music educator who studied Csound with Barry Vercoe at MIT in 1979 and later worked on DSP-based Csound development and alternate controller research.

nodes.label: Michael Gogins
nodes.description: Developer of an advanced panning method that places maximum power slightly before the panning variable reaches extremity, creating an illusion of movement beyond speaker positions.

nodes.label: François Pinot
nodes.description: Developer who wrote the ctcsound Python API wrapper for Csound in 2015, providing better integration with native Python code and Jupyter Notebooks.

nodes.label: Joe Timoney
nodes.description: Collaborator with Victor Lazzarini on multiple synthesis research papers covering formant analysis, distortion synthesis, and spectral processing.

nodes.label: Rudi Villing
nodes.description: Colleague at Electronic Engineering Department, Maynooth; collaborator with Lazzarini.

nodes.label: Damián Keller
nodes.description: Co-researcher in the Ubiquitous Music (ubimus) group; collaborator with Lazzarini.

nodes.label: Jari Kleimola
nodes.description: Researcher at Aalto University in Finland; collaborator on research contributing to the book.

nodes.label: Vesa Välimäki
nodes.description: Audio researcher who co-authored work on dynamic signal phase distortion using coefficient-modulated allpass filters.

nodes.label: Stéphane Letz
nodes.description: Leader of the Faust development team at GRAME; contributor of foreword to the book.

nodes.label: Maynooth
nodes.description: Location of Maynooth University where Lazzarini works with colleagues in Computer Science and Electronic Engineering.

nodes.label: Aalto University
nodes.description: Finnish university where Lazzarini collaborated on research contributing to the book.

nodes.label: GRAME
nodes.description: An organization that developed INScore, an intelligent display application for OSC-based visualization.

nodes.label: ctcsound
nodes.description: A Python API wrapper for Csound based on Python's ctypes module, written by François Pinot in 2015 as an alternative to the earlier SWIG-generated csnd6.py.

nodes.label: Ubiquitous Music (ubimus) group
nodes.description: Research group with which Lazzarini collaborates; includes Damián Keller and Nuno Otero.

nodes.label: FM Synthesis
nodes.description: A synthesis technique where a modulating oscillator controls the frequency of a carrier oscillator, creating complex timbres through sidebands. The economy of FM lies in its few defining parameters: carrier frequency, modulator frequency, carrier amplitude, and deviation.

nodes.label: Wave-Shaping Synthesis
nodes.description: A synthesis technique using non-linear transfer functions to generate complex waveforms from simple driving signals, producing harmonic content through polynomial or other mathematical functions.

nodes.label: Phase Distortion Synthesis
nodes.description: A synthesis method that applies non-linear transfer functions to the phase increment of a sinusoidal oscillator, formulated as complex modulation PM and capable of generating various waveforms by controlling phase-shaping parameters.

nodes.label: Waveguide Synthesis
nodes.description: A digital synthesis technique that models waves traveling in pipes or on strings using delay lines with feedback to replicate reflections at structural boundaries.

nodes.label: Fourier Transform
nodes.description: A continuous-time, continuous-frequency mathematical method that decomposes a sound waveform into separate sinusoidal functions of different amplitudes, frequencies, and phases.

nodes.label: MIDI Protocol
nodes.description: Musical Instrument Digital Interface protocol for controlling synthesizers and musical devices, with limitations in flexibility and seven-bit precision that OSC was designed to overcome.

nodes.label: OSC Protocol
nodes.description: A modern communication protocol for electronic instruments developed at CNMAT that transmits data over networks (TCP/IP, internet) with higher bandwidth and lower latency than MIDI.

nodes.label: Computer Music Instruments
nodes.description: A book by Victor Lazzarini covering the design, development, and implementation of computer music instruments across various platforms.

nodes.label: Audio Signal
nodes.description: Information-carrying inputs and outputs of processes in a system that can be transduced into mechanical disturbances of a medium such as air, ultimately perceived by the human auditory system.

nodes.label: Digital Signal Processing
nodes.description: The field of manipulating signals represented as discrete samples in computers, converting continuous audio waveforms to discrete digital form.

nodes.label: Signal Representation
nodes.description: Mathematical functions that map one or more parameters to outputs, used to describe and model signals in computer systems.

nodes.label: Waveform
nodes.description: A pattern of pressure variations in air representing sound, which can be represented in time-domain or frequency-domain.

nodes.label: Frequency
nodes.description: The number of wave cycles occurring in a given duration, measured in Hertz (Hz) or cycles per second (cps), ranging from 20 to 20,000 Hz for human hearing.

nodes.label: Amplitude
nodes.description: In digital audio, the sequence of numerical values representing an audio signal, directly related to sound pressure deviations and sound intensity.

nodes.label: Timbre
nodes.description: The quality or color of sound determined by waveform shape, an emergent and multidimensional perceptual quality distinct from pitch and loudness.

nodes.label: Sinusoid
nodes.description: A simple waveform defined by mathematical functions, fundamental to describing physical phenomena and composable to create complex waveforms.

nodes.label: Pitch
nodes.description: The perceptual quality of sound determined by periodicity; humans perceive pitch only when a sound is periodic.

nodes.label: Pressure Wave
nodes.description: A wave that propagates through a medium as compression and rarefaction, one perspective on wave motion.

nodes.label: Velocity Wave
nodes.description: A wave describing particle motion in terms of speed and direction changes, a complementary perspective to pressure waves.

nodes.label: Phase
nodes.description: A parameter of sinusoids that measures the starting point of the waveform cycle, ranging from sine phase (starting at zero) to cosine phase (starting at maximum peak).

nodes.label: Frequency Spectrum
nodes.description: The set of sinusoidal components at different frequencies that compose a complex waveform, each with given amplitude and phase.

nodes.label: Spectrogram
nodes.description: A time-frequency representation created by a sequence of magnitude spectra taken at regular intervals, displayed as a 2D plot showing spectral peaks over time.

nodes.label: Decibel (dB)
nodes.description: A logarithmic unit for measuring amplitude differences, where a 6 dB change represents a doubling or halving of amplitude.

nodes.label: 0dBFS Scale
nodes.description: An amplitude scale based on decibel units with reference to full-scale amplitude, setting 0 dB at maximum value with all other values in the negative range.

nodes.label: 12-Tone Equal-Tempered Scale (12TET)
nodes.description: A pitch scale with twelve pitch classes based on a 12-step logarithmic division of the octave, using letter names A-G with sharps and flats.

nodes.label: Pitch Class
nodes.description: Octave-separated pitches that belong to the same class and share an octave-invariant name in the 12TET system.

nodes.label: Hammond Organ
nodes.description: A classic electronic keyboard instrument featuring tone wheels and a Leslie rotating speaker system, modeled in Csound using waveshaping and Doppler effects.

nodes.label: Musical Signal
nodes.description: A subcategory of audio signals that requires greater precision and quality in transmission, storage, and playback, with a fuller range of frequencies and amplitudes than speech signals.

nodes.label: Cent
nodes.description: A logarithmic unit for measuring pitch intervals, defined as 1/100th of a semitone, calculated as 1200 log₂(p) for an interval ratio p.

nodes.label: Tuning and Temperament
nodes.description: The field of study concerned with constructing frequency scales with different numbers of steps and step sizes.

nodes.label: Pitched Spectrum
nodes.description: A type of musical signal that evokes a clear sense of pitch height, typically composed of frequencies aligned closely with an integral harmonic series.

nodes.label: Fundamental Frequency
nodes.description: The lowest frequency in a harmonic series, serving as the greatest common divisor of the component frequencies and determining the perceived pitch of a signal.

nodes.label: Harmonic Series
nodes.description: A series of frequencies where all components are integer multiples of a fundamental frequency, characteristic of many musical sounds.

nodes.label: Inharmonic Spectrum
nodes.description: Frequency components generated by FM synthesis when the carrier-to-modulator ratio is not a simple integer ratio, producing sidebands at non-integer multiples.

nodes.label: Distributed Spectrum
nodes.description: A complex spectral type featuring a mixture of many closely-spaced components covering a certain frequency range, with no emerging sense of pitch, exemplified by cymbal sounds.

nodes.label: White Noise
nodes.description: An ideal signal containing all frequencies evenly distributed throughout the auditory range, obtained using a generator that produces random numbers every sample.

nodes.label: Transient
nodes.description: Short-lived inharmonic components at the onset of a sound that die away quickly, important in defining the character of instrumental sounds like piano notes.

nodes.label: Vibrato
nodes.description: Periodic modulation of pitch or amplitude in musical performance, characterized by speed (4–8 Hz), depth, timing, and evenness, implemented in Csound through oscillator-based synthesis.

nodes.label: Quasi-Pitched Spectrum
nodes.description: A spectral type with increased ambiguity in pitch assignment, occurring when harmonic and non-harmonic components are mixed or when only a few non-harmonically-related components are present.

nodes.label: Periodic Waveform
nodes.description: A waveform that repeats at a rate determined by the fundamental frequency, capable of evoking a sense of pitch when repeated at a sufficiently fast rate.

nodes.label: Sawtooth Wave
nodes.description: A periodic waveform with a harmonic spectrum containing all integer multiples of the fundamental frequency, used as an example of the relationship between waveform and spectrum.

nodes.label: Sampling Theorem
nodes.description: A fundamental principle stating that to encode a signal with frequency component X, a sampling rate of at least 2X is required, determining the relationship between signal frequency and digital sampling.

nodes.label: Aliasing
nodes.description: A digital audio artifact where frequency components exceeding half the sampling rate fold over into the audible frequency range, appearing as noise or unwanted inharmonic components.

nodes.label: Nyquist Frequency
nodes.description: The maximum frequency that can be represented in a digital signal at a given sample rate, used as the upper limit for component generation in band-limited synthesis.

nodes.label: Quantization
nodes.description: The process of assigning discrete amplitude values to ranges of continuous signal amplitudes, typically using linear quantization to divide the amplitude range into equal-sized regions.

nodes.label: Analog-to-Digital Conversion
nodes.description: The process of converting continuous analog electrical signals into discrete digital sequences by sampling amplitude values at regular time intervals.

nodes.label: Digital-to-Analog Conversion
nodes.description: The process of converting discrete digital signal sequences back into continuous analog signals using D-A converters with anti-aliasing filters.

nodes.label: Band-Limited Synthesis
nodes.description: A signal generation technique that prevents aliasing by limiting the bandwidth of synthesized waveforms according to the fundamental frequency, demonstrated through vco2 and related opcodes.

nodes.label: Dirac Comb
nodes.description: A mathematical function used to formally describe the sampling process, selecting values from a continuous signal at regular intervals.

nodes.label: MUSIC III
nodes.description: An acoustical compiler program created by Max Mathews for the IBM 7904 computer that allowed musicians and composers to create new programs for sound generation using connected building blocks.

nodes.label: MUSIC V
nodes.description: The final iteration of Mathews' MUSIC series, written in FORTRAN in collaboration with Joan Miller, Richard Moore, and Jean-Claude Risset, featuring vector-based processing and widespread adoption.

nodes.label: MUSIC N family
nodes.description: A lineage of computer music programming environments descended from Max Mathews' original MUSIC III design, characterized by modular building-block architecture.

nodes.label: Faust
nodes.description: A functional audio signal processing language used to implement adaptive filtering and synthesis instruments, integrated with Csound for pitch tracking and real-time audio processing.

nodes.label: IBM 7904
nodes.description: A computer used by Max Mathews to run the MUSIC III program in the early 1960s.

nodes.label: Linear Pulse-Code Modulation (Linear PCM)
nodes.description: The most common digital encoding method for handling audio signals in computers, based on quantization and sampling principles.

nodes.label: Dynamic Range
nodes.description: The range of amplitude variation available in a digital audio system, defined as the ratio between maximum and minimum peak amplitudes or maximum signal-to-noise ratio.

nodes.label: Floating-Point Representation
nodes.description: A method of encoding sampled audio values using mantissa and exponent format, offering higher dynamic range than fixed-point integers and maintaining SNR regardless of signal amplitude.

nodes.label: Digital Clipping
nodes.description: An audio distortion artifact that occurs when a signal exceeds the permitted range due to numeric overflow, causing waveform edges to be cut off.

nodes.label: MUSIC N
nodes.description: A paradigm for computer music instrument design based on object-oriented programming principles, using unit generators (opcodes) and DSP programs instantiated as instrument classes.

nodes.label: C++
nodes.description: Programming language used to implement Csound as a class-based object that can be instantiated and embedded in host applications.

nodes.label: C
nodes.description: Universal programming language in which Csound is written, ensuring portability across different computers and long-term technical lifetime of compositions.

nodes.label: Domain-Specific Language (DSL)
nodes.description: Programming languages tailored for specific aspects of instrument development, particularly signal-processing elements, offering built-in components that general-purpose languages lack.

nodes.label: General-Purpose Programming Language (GPPL)
nodes.description: Programming languages like Python, C, and C++ that can be used for computer music instrument development, serving roles in control, user interfaces, and computationally-intensive tasks.

nodes.label: Signal Processing
nodes.description: The mathematical and computational discipline of analyzing, transforming, and generating signals, including continuous-time and discrete-time signals used in audio synthesis.

nodes.label: Just-in-Time Compilation (JIT)
nodes.description: A compilation technique used by Faust to directly compile signal-processing code into loadable objects for efficient execution.

nodes.label: SciPy
nodes.description: Python scientific computing library used for wavfile I/O operations in the pitch shifter and time scaling programs.

nodes.label: NumPy
nodes.description: Python numerical computing library used for implementing wave-shaping synthesis algorithms and Chebyshev polynomial evaluation.

nodes.label: matplotlib
nodes.description: Python plotting library used internally by csoundmagics to display Csound function tables.

nodes.label: pylab
nodes.description: Python plotting and numerical computing library used for FFT, signal processing, and array operations in the audio code examples.

nodes.label: Csound
nodes.description: A free and open-source audio programming language first released in 1986 at MIT by Barry Vercoe. It is a direct descendant of MusicN and has evolved into a modern audio library supporting multiple platforms and APIs.

nodes.label: Csound Application Programming Interface (API)
nodes.description: An application programming interface written in C that allows developers to control Csound instances and harness Csound functionality within host applications. Supports interfaces to Python, C++, and Java.

nodes.label: csnd6
nodes.description: The original Csound Python API wrapper generated by SWIG from Csound's C API, later superseded by ctcsound.

nodes.label: Unit Generator
nodes.description: Modular building blocks in MUSIC III and subsequent programs, each corresponding to an elementary function of sound production or transformation such as oscillator, filter, or adder.

nodes.label: Opcode
nodes.description: The fundamental building block of Csound instruments that implements specific operations for synthesis and audio processing, supporting both traditional and function-like syntax.

nodes.label: oscili
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for interpolating oscillator that reads from a function table, used extensively in additive synthesis instruments for generating individual partials.

nodes.label: linen
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that applies linear fade-in and fade-out envelopes to audio signals, taking parameters for fade-in duration, overall duration, and fade-out duration.

nodes.label: out
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for sending multichannel audio output, replacing outs, outq, outh, and outo for 2, 4, 6, and 8 channels respectively.

nodes.label: Csound Instrument
nodes.description: A class-like structure in Csound that defines synthesis algorithms; instances are created for each note played and reused when available to optimize memory allocation.

nodes.label: Csound Variable Types
nodes.description: Three basic variable types (i, k, a) in Csound that define data content and action time: i-type for initialization scalars, k-type for performance scalars, and a-type for performance vectors.

nodes.label: ksmps
nodes.description: A parameter in Csound that defines the number of audio samples processed per control cycle; can be set locally within UDOs to enable sample-by-sample processing.

nodes.label: sr
nodes.description: The number of samples per second in Csound, with a default value of 44100 Hz and recommended explicit setting.

nodes.label: 0dbfs
nodes.description: A Csound header parameter that sets the maximum amplitude value in the digital domain before clipping, typically set to 1 for normalized amplitude range 0–1.

nodes.label: CsoundPerformanceThread
nodes.description: Helper C++ class that performs a score in a separate thread, allowing the host program to process independently while communicating via message queues.

nodes.label: Software Bus
nodes.description: A communication mechanism in Csound that allows a host application to send and receive data to/from Csound instruments in real time, analogous to hardware mixing console buses.

nodes.label: Faust Stream Operators
nodes.description: Specialized operators in Faust including sequential (:), parallel (,), split (<:), merge (:>), delay (@N), and feedback (˜) for organizing audio stream processing.

nodes.label: faustcompile opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that calls the just-in-time compiler to produce a DSP process from a Faust program at initialization time.

nodes.label: faustaudio opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that creates and runs a compiled Faust program, handling input and output signals.

nodes.label: faustctl opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode used to access and manipulate UI controls in a running Faust DSP instance.

nodes.label: FBAM2 algorithm
nodes.description: A feedback amplitude modulation algorithm implemented as a Faust program in the Shapes application to generate the synthesized tone.

nodes.label: Shapes application
nodes.description: A synthesizer application with two-dimensional control, integrating Python, Csound, and Faust, where users drag a ball to control pitch and volume.

nodes.label: Tkinter
nodes.description: A user interface framework that allows setting callbacks invoked by the event loop at given times, used for updating graphical interfaces and triggering control messages to synthesis engines.

nodes.label: ctcsound package
nodes.description: A Python API package for embedding and controlling Csound instances within Python applications.

nodes.label: reverbsc opcode
nodes.description: A reverb unit implemented in Csound5 based on Sean Costello's work, offering parametric control over feedback level and lowpass filter cutoff.

nodes.label: Subtractive Synthesis
nodes.description: A synthesis method that begins with a complex sound source and refines it by removing partials or frequency spectrum sections using audio filters, conceptually the inverse of additive synthesis.

nodes.label: Additive Synthesis
nodes.description: A synthesis technique that constructs complex spectra by combining multiple sinusoidal components, each with independent amplitude, frequency, and phase control, as demonstrated through multi-oscillator Csound instruments.

nodes.label: Fourier Series
nodes.description: A mathematical representation of any reasonable periodic signal as a weighted sum of integrally-related sines, cosines, or complex exponentials, where the weightings are Fourier coefficients.

nodes.label: GEN 10
nodes.description: A Csound function table generator that creates waveforms from harmonic amplitudes or weights.

nodes.label: ftgen opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode for generating function tables with harmonic content, used to create standard waveform shapes (impulse, sawtooth, square, triangle).

nodes.label: Square Wave
nodes.description: Periodic waveform alternating between +1 and −1, whose Fourier series contains only odd harmonics with amplitude inversely proportional to harmonic number.

nodes.label: Inharmonic Spectra
nodes.description: Sound spectra where frequencies do not align with a harmonic series, found in many non-pitched sounds.

nodes.label: Python
nodes.description: General-purpose scripting language with Csound bindings through the csnd6 module, allowing users to develop music programs that employ Csound as an audio engine.

nodes.label: Oscillator
nodes.description: Unit generators in MUSIC IV used to generate basic waveform signals from pre-defined function tables, including OSCIL, COSCIL, and VOSCIL variants.

nodes.label: Function-table lookup
nodes.description: A technique for generating waveforms by pre-calculating a single cycle in memory and reading from it periodically.

nodes.label: Phase increment
nodes.description: A fundamental operation that advances the phase of an oscillator at a rate determined by frequency, often provided as a separate opcode.

nodes.label: Linear interpolation
nodes.description: A method for improving table-lookup precision by modeling in-between values as straight lines between calculated table positions.

nodes.label: Triangle wave
nodes.description: A periodic waveform with Fourier coefficients of 8(−1)^((n−1)/2)/(π²k²) for odd k, representing a smoother alternative to square and sawtooth waves.

nodes.label: Pulse wave
nodes.description: Periodic waveform whose Fourier series can be derived using definite integral techniques.

nodes.label: vco2 opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates band-limited waveforms by creating multiple function tables organized by octave ranges and switching between them based on frequency.

nodes.label: Cubic interpolation
nodes.description: A higher-order interpolation method (third order) used for improved table-lookup precision in oscillators.

nodes.label: Guard point
nodes.description: A mechanism in Csound function tables that handles interpolation at table boundaries; for power-of-two plus one sizes, it extends the function contour rather than copying the first point.

nodes.label: vco2 opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates band-limited waveforms in multiple modes, including sawtooth, triangle, square, pulse, and user-defined shapes, with automatic table selection based on fundamental frequency.

nodes.label: vco2init opcode
nodes.description: A Csound auxiliary opcode that creates band-limited function tables from arbitrary geometric shapes by analyzing the original shape's Fourier series and constructing tables for different frequency ranges.

nodes.label: flooper2 opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for looping sampled sounds with crossfading, used to transpose pre-recorded audio without aliasing by selecting appropriate band-limited tables.

nodes.label: GEN 1
nodes.description: A Csound function table generator that reads audio from soundfiles and places them in function tables for use as oscillator sources.

nodes.label: GEN 7
nodes.description: A Csound function table generator that draws functions from piecewise linear segments, used to create non-band-limited geometric shapes.

nodes.label: Spectral envelope
nodes.description: A high-level representation of the overall shape of a spectrum showing energy distribution across frequencies, particularly useful for describing noise characteristics rather than discrete partials.

nodes.label: oscili opcode
nodes.description: An interpolating oscillator opcode in Csound that performs linear interpolation when scanning f-tables, requiring 2^n + 1 table sizes to avoid amplitude discontinuities.

nodes.label: vco2ift opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that selects appropriate band-limited function tables based on fundamental frequency for use with ordinary oscillators.

nodes.label: vco2ft opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that works alongside vco2init to expose the mechanism of table selection according to fundamental frequency for use with ordinary opcodes.

nodes.label: rand opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates random sequences for white noise and other noise-based signal sources.

nodes.label: Sampled-sound generators
nodes.description: Signal sources that rely on pre-recorded sounds loaded into function tables, capable of generating any spectral type including noise and non-periodic waveforms.

nodes.label: gauss opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates normally distributed (Gaussian) random values, useful for modeling realistic pitch variations and humanizing synthesis.

nodes.label: cauchy opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates values from a Cauchy distribution, similar in shape to normal distribution but with a flatter curve favoring values away from zero.

nodes.label: randh opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates random values at a specified rate using sample-and-hold interpolation, with configurable seed and noise generator precision.

nodes.label: randi opcode
nodes.description: A Csound random signal generator used to modulate FOF fundamentals and create pitch jitter effects that simulate human singing and acoustic instrument playing.

nodes.label: fractalnoise opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates fractional noise types including pink noise (1/f) and brown noise (1/f²) based on spectral distribution.

nodes.label: rms opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode that computes root mean square amplitude of a signal, used in context-sensitive instruments to broadcast loudness between instruments.

nodes.label: pink noise
nodes.description: Noise where power density decreases 3 dB per octave with increasing frequency (density proportional to 1/f), with each octave containing the same amount of power.

nodes.label: brown noise
nodes.description: Noise with power density proportional to 1/f², derived from Brownian motion and random walk processes, calculable from white noise by summing random values.

nodes.label: band-limited noise
nodes.description: Noise generated by sampling a random generator at a lower rate than the sampling frequency, creating spectral envelopes with peaks and troughs.

nodes.label: envelope follower
nodes.description: A tool that tracks the amplitude of a signal over time using RMS amplitude estimation to shape the envelope of another sound.

nodes.label: fractional noise
nodes.description: A category of noise whose nature is determined by its spectral distribution, characterized by the formula S(f) = 1/f^n.

nodes.label: envelope generator
nodes.description: A signal generator that shapes the amplitude or other parameters of a sound over time, implementable as an oscillator reading a function table.

nodes.label: linseg opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that elaborates on line by allowing an arbitrary number of linear envelope segments, holding the final value when a note continues beyond the envelope duration.

nodes.label: expseg opcode
nodes.description: A Csound envelope opcode that applies exponential curves to envelope segments, addressing dynamic response issues in amplitude control but cannot reach zero or cross polarity.

nodes.label: ADSR envelope
nodes.description: An attack-decay-sustain-release amplitude envelope used to modulate filter cutoff frequency and output amplitude in subtractive synthesis.

nodes.label: Amplitude Modulation (AM)
nodes.description: A synthesis technique where the amplitude of a carrier signal is modulated by a modulator signal, producing sidebands at frequencies equal to the sum and difference of carrier and modulator frequencies.

nodes.label: Frequency Modulation (FM)
nodes.description: A synthesis technique in which modulating frequencies control the pitch of a carrier wave; Csound's GEN12 supports asynchronous FM with synchronized AM and FM modulating frequencies.

nodes.label: Ring Modulation (RM)
nodes.description: A modulation technique equivalent to the multiplication of two signals, where the modulation signal is fed directly to a parameter without adding it to a mean value, producing spectral components at the sums and differences of input frequencies.

nodes.label: Envelope shaping
nodes.description: The application of time-varying envelopes to synthesis parameters including amplitude, pitch, and timbre to model instrumental characteristics.

nodes.label: Heterodyning
nodes.description: A signal processing technique that separates carrier and modulator signals and implements wave shaping through sinusoidal transfer functions.

nodes.label: Pulse Width Modulation
nodes.description: Synthesis technique that gradually transforms a square wave from narrow to wide pulse using modulation, commonly used in analog synthesis to produce varied timbres.

nodes.label: Hard Sync
nodes.description: A synthesis technique mentioned as analogous to the effect of cutting off incomplete waveform cycles in grain generation, creating discontinuities and wide spectra.

nodes.label: Low-Frequency Oscillator
nodes.description: An oscillator operating below 20 Hz used to modulate parameters of sound generators, typically implemented at control rate in Csound.

nodes.label: Digital Filter
nodes.description: A signal processing unit that amplifies or suppresses parts of the spectrum by delaying signals and combining them with different scaling amounts, either with feedback or feedforward paths.

nodes.label: Low Pass Filter
nodes.description: A filter that attenuates high frequencies while allowing low frequencies to pass, characterized by a transfer function with amplitude response decreasing with frequency.

nodes.label: High Pass Filter
nodes.description: A filter that allows frequencies above a cutoff frequency to pass while attenuating lower frequencies, implemented in Csound via atonex and atone opcodes.

nodes.label: Band Pass Filter
nodes.description: A filter that allows a specific range of frequencies to pass while attenuating frequencies outside that range, implemented via butterbp and statevar opcodes in Csound.

nodes.label: Band Reject Filter
nodes.description: A filter that attenuates a specific range of frequencies while allowing frequencies outside that range to pass, available as one of the four outputs of the statevar opcode.

nodes.label: All Pass Filter
nodes.description: A delay line processor combining feedforward and feedback paths with opposite-sign gains of equal magnitude, producing a flat amplitude response across all frequencies while introducing phase shifts.

nodes.label: Resonant Filter
nodes.description: A filter that boosts significantly a small range of frequencies in the spectrum, valued for its unique sound quality in musical applications.

nodes.label: Finite Impulse Response Filter
nodes.description: Finite impulse response filter implemented as a delay line with tapped coefficients, designed via inverse discrete Fourier transform of a desired amplitude response.

nodes.label: Infinite Impulse Response Filter
nodes.description: A filter with feedback streams that has an infinite impulse response, more widely used in source-filter models due to flexibility and ease of application with time-varying parameters.

nodes.label: Tone Filter
nodes.description: A simple first-order IIR filter with 6 dB/octave amplitude response rolloff, useful for gentle removal of high or low frequencies without excessive attenuation.

nodes.label: Butterworth Filter
nodes.description: A digital filter design derived from classic analogue filters, offering maximally flat pass band and good stop band attenuation, available in BP, LP, HP, and BR amplitude responses.

nodes.label: Resonator Filter
nodes.description: A 2nd-order band-pass filter used in various applications, constructed from input signal scaling and one- and two-sample feedback delays with coefficients determined by centre frequency and bandwidth.

nodes.label: tone opcode
nodes.description: A Csound unit generator implementing a lowpass filter that attenuates high frequencies, used in reverberator designs to simulate frequency-dependent energy loss.

nodes.label: atone opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing the high-pass version of the tone filter, implemented slightly differently from the standard high-pass tone filter.

nodes.label: Amplitude Response
nodes.description: The effect of a filter on the amplitude of an input signal, determining the pass and stop bands of the filter.

nodes.label: Phase Response
nodes.description: The action of a filter over the whole phase spectrum, which can be linear or non-linear depending on filter type.

nodes.label: Impulse Response
nodes.description: A sound file or audio signal used in convolution to impart acoustic qualities to another sound, often representing the characteristics of a physical space or system.

nodes.label: Q Factor
nodes.description: A parameter defined as the ratio of frequency to bandwidth (Q = f/B), providing a musically meaningful way to define frequency intervals based on ratios rather than linear differences.

nodes.label: Moog ladder filter
nodes.description: A 4th-order resonant low-pass filter constructed from four 1st-order IIR low-pass sections with a feedback path providing resonance effect, one of the most famous analogue filters for musical applications.

nodes.label: Resonance
nodes.description: An audio effect created by feedback paths in filters that produce a peak at the cutoff frequency, characterized by a parameter typically ranging from 0 to 1.

nodes.label: moogladder filter
nodes.description: A resonant filter implementation in Csound based on the Moog ladder filter design, used for shaping the spectral content of audio signals.

nodes.label: Formant synthesis
nodes.description: A technique using ModFM to emulate a source with band-pass filter characteristics by selecting modulator frequency as resonance centre and calculating modulation index from bandwidth.

nodes.label: User-defined opcode (UDO)
nodes.description: A Csound feature allowing users to define custom opcodes for reusable synthesis and processing functions, such as oscillator banks and vibrato/chorus effects.

nodes.label: Detuned oscillators
nodes.description: Multiple oscillators with slightly different frequencies combined to create a thickened, chorus-like effect in the source signal.

nodes.label: Glottis
nodes.description: The sound-producing element of the vocal mechanism, modeled as a periodic waveform source in vocal synthesis.

nodes.label: reson opcode
nodes.description: A Csound bandpass filter opcode with resonance capability, chosen for its ability to ring and resonate as bandwidth narrows and for CPU efficiency.

nodes.label: Closed-Form Summation Formulae
nodes.description: A mathematical approach demonstrating the relationship between wave-shaping expressions and band-limited spectra through polynomial expansion.

nodes.label: Band-Limited Pulse
nodes.description: A pulse waveform synthesized using closed-form summation of harmonics with equal weight, avoiding aliasing artifacts.

nodes.label: port opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing a tone-like low-pass filter with half-time parameter for smoothing parameter transitions.

nodes.label: Closed-form summation formulae
nodes.description: Mathematical expressions that generate complex spectra by summing sinusoidal components with controlled amplitude decay and frequency ratios, allowing harmonic and inharmonic spectrum generation.

nodes.label: buzz opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that implements band-limited pulse generation, producing normalized output and serving as a better alternative to vco2 pulse waveform mode.

nodes.label: Spectral roll-off
nodes.description: The rate at which harmonic amplitudes decay in a synthesized spectrum, controlled by the parameter 'a' in generalized summation formulae to emulate low-pass filter behavior.

nodes.label: Inharmonic partials
nodes.description: Non-integer frequency ratios used in additive synthesis to create complex timbres, with specific pairing strategies required to avoid discontinuities in Csound function tables.

nodes.label: Sidebands
nodes.description: Series of sum and difference frequencies that appear on either side of the carrier frequency in FM synthesis, calculated as carrier ± integer multiples of the modulator frequency.

nodes.label: John Chowning
nodes.description: Researcher who initially proposed the application of frequency modulation (FM) to musical synthesis in 1973, demonstrating how a modulator can modify a carrier frequency to produce varied dynamic spectra with minimal computational overhead.

nodes.label: Phase Modulation (PM)
nodes.description: A synthesis technique where the instantaneous phase of a carrier oscillator is altered by a modulator, producing virtually identical spectra to FM but without undesirable side-effects. Used in the Yamaha DX7.

nodes.label: Bessel functions of the first kind
nodes.description: Unipolar mathematical functions used in ModFM synthesis that are monotonically decreasing (In(k) > In+1(k)), providing more natural spectral behavior than regular Bessel functions.

nodes.label: Modulation index (I)
nodes.description: A parameter in FM synthesis that controls the degree of distortion applied to the carrier, determining the number of audible sidebands (2I sidebands total, or 2I+1 components including carrier).

nodes.label: Asymmetrical PM synthesis
nodes.description: A variation of PM synthesis where the PM signal is ring-modulated by an exponential function, introducing a symmetry control parameter r that dislocates spectral peaks above or below the carrier frequency.

nodes.label: Asymmetric FM
nodes.description: A phase modulation enhancement that uses a symmetry parameter r to shift spectral peaks above or below the carrier frequency, implemented with Bessel functions and extra multiplies.

nodes.label: Phase-Aligned Formant (PAF) Synthesis
nodes.description: A closed-form summation method that creates formant regions around a centre frequency by ring-modulating a transfer function with a sinusoid, producing a double-sided spectrum.

nodes.label: Split-Sideband Synthesis
nodes.description: A closed-form summation method based on phase modulation that produces four independent outputs containing complex spectra separated into lower-odd, lower-even, upper-odd, and upper-even sideband groups.

nodes.label: Hilbert Transform
nodes.description: An all-pass filter operation that shifts signal phase by π/2 to create quadrature relationships and single-sided spectra for complex-valued signal processing.

nodes.label: Wave-Shaping
nodes.description: A non-linear processing technique inserted into the FBAM feedback path using functions like sine or cosine to modify spectral content.

nodes.label: Single-Sideband Modulation
nodes.description: A modulation technique using analytic signals to produce single-sided spectra, employed in SpSB synthesis to separate upper and lower sidebands.

nodes.label: Analytic Signal
nodes.description: A complex-valued signal representation constructed from a real signal and its Hilbert transform, maintaining 90-degree phase offset between components.

nodes.label: Modified FM Synthesis
nodes.description: A variation on the original phase modulation algorithm referenced as ModFM.

nodes.label: Modified FM Synthesis (ModFM)
nodes.description: A variant of FM synthesis using modified Bessel functions instead of ordinary Bessel functions, producing unipolar spectra without problematic fluctuations and enabling natural dynamic spectrum shaping.

nodes.label: Extended ModFM
nodes.description: An extension of ModFM synthesis that modifies spectral symmetry using additional phase modulation and parameters r and s to control spectrum shape and sidebands.

nodes.label: Phase Aligned Formant (PAF) Synthesis
nodes.description: A distortion synthesis method that creates formant regions by ring modulation of a sinusoid carrier and complex spectrum with low-pass characteristics, using waveshaping with an exponentially shaped transfer function.

nodes.label: FOF Synthesis
nodes.description: Fonction d'Onde Formantique synthesis method that produces a series of partials shaped into formant regions using time-domain grain excitations, originally developed for vocal and instrumental simulation.

nodes.label: Python with PyLab
nodes.description: Programming environment used for implementing ModFM and Extended ModFM synthesis algorithms in the text.

nodes.label: Polynomial Transfer Functions
nodes.description: The most common method for finding transfer functions in wave shaping, based on the principle that polynomial functions produce precisely defined band-limited spectra when driven by sinusoidal signals.

nodes.label: Chebyshev Polynomials
nodes.description: Mathematical polynomials of the first and second kind used to construct wave-shaping transfer functions that produce desired harmonic spectra when driven by cosine or sine waves.
aliases: Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind
Chebyshev polynomial of the second kind
Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind

nodes.label: Band-Limited Spectrum
nodes.description: A spectrum whose highest frequency component never exceeds the order of the polynomial used in wave-shaping synthesis, guaranteeing controlled harmonic content.

nodes.label: Vector Phase-Shaping
nodes.description: An extension of Phase Distortion synthesis that uses a two-dimensional vector (d, v) to control both horizontal and vertical positions of the phase-shaping function's bending point, enabling a wider variety of spectra.

nodes.label: Hyperbolic Tangent Wave Shaping
nodes.description: A wave-shaping technique using the hyperbolic tangent function to generate quasi-band-limited square and sawtooth waves with smoother spectral transitions than polynomial wave shapers.

nodes.label: Band-Limiting
nodes.description: A technique to reduce aliasing artifacts in synthesized waveforms by controlling the bandwidth of generated signals, particularly important in wave-shaping synthesis.

nodes.label: Phase Modulation Synthesis
nodes.description: A synthesis technique where one or more modulator oscillators modulate the phase of carrier oscillators, producing complex spectra determined by Bessel functions and the modulation index.

nodes.label: Carrier-to-Modulator Ratio
nodes.description: A parameter in phase modulation synthesis that controls the frequency relationship between carrier and modulator oscillators.

nodes.label: RMS Analysis
nodes.description: A signal processing technique used in Alma to detect silence by measuring energy levels below a specified dB threshold over a defined time span, enabling segmentation of speech into distinct units.

nodes.label: Phasor Oscillator
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates a ramp signal from 0 to 1 used as the basis for phase-based synthesis.

nodes.label: Table Lookup Synthesis
nodes.description: A synthesis technique where pre-calculated waveform values stored in tables are read by oscillators, with interpolation methods determining output quality.

nodes.label: Modulation Envelope
nodes.description: A time-varying control signal that shapes both amplitude and modulation index to create dynamic spectral changes.

nodes.label: Band-Pass Filter Bank
nodes.description: A parallel arrangement of band-pass filters used to analyze energy distribution across multiple frequency ranges.

nodes.label: Analysis-Synthesis
nodes.description: A technique that extracts features from an input signal and reproduces them using a synthesis model.

nodes.label: ModFM
nodes.description: A summation formula technique for synthesis that produces partials around a centre frequency in a given band, chosen for its ability to derive carrier and modulation frequencies from bandwidth with smooth dynamic spectral changes.

nodes.label: Vocoder
nodes.description: A signal processing technique that analyzes input audio into frequency bands using RMS data to control synthesis energy in each band, implemented here using ModFM synthesis.

nodes.label: Resonant synthesis
nodes.description: A synthesis method that mimics a source-filter combination with resonance control using generalised summation formulae to pack signal generation and spectral modification into a single algorithm.

nodes.label: Generalised formulae
nodes.description: Summation formula techniques for synthesis available in both single-sided and double-sided forms, used for resonant synthesis with control over spectral bandwidth and resonance peaks.

nodes.label: ptrack
nodes.description: A pitch tracker opcode in Csound used to analyze the fundamental frequency of input sound, with results smoothed to remove analysis jitter.

nodes.label: butterbp
nodes.description: A Butterworth bandpass filter opcode in Csound used to filter the input signal in each vocoder band.

nodes.label: phasor
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates a ramp signal from 0 to 1 at a given frequency, used as a phase generator to drive synchronous sinusoid generation in ModFM synthesis.

nodes.label: PAF
nodes.description: A summation formula method capable of producing partials around a centre frequency in a given band, mentioned alongside ModFM and other techniques.

nodes.label: Double-sided generalised formulae
nodes.description: A summation formula variant used to emulate a bandpass source-filter arrangement with resonance control by choosing one frequency as centre of resonance and another as fundamental.

nodes.label: rms
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that computes root-mean-square amplitude of a signal, used to extract energy data from each vocoder band to control synthesis amplitude.

nodes.label: linen
nodes.description: A Csound envelope generator opcode that produces linear attack, sustain, and release segments, used for amplitude shaping in synthesis instruments.

nodes.label: schedule
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that launches instrument instances in parallel, enabling recursive instrument instantiation for generating multiple synthesis bands.

nodes.label: Comb filter
nodes.description: A delay-based filter created by feeding back a delayed signal with controlled gain, producing an amplitude response with regularly spaced peaks. Named for the comb-like shape of its frequency response.

nodes.label: Summation formulae
nodes.description: Mathematical techniques that can replace traditional source-filter combinations in synthesis, allowing complex output spectra to be defined with few parameters.

nodes.label: Delay line
nodes.description: A digital signal processing element that stores and retrieves audio samples with a time delay, used for echo, reverberation, and synthesis applications.

nodes.label: Feedback systems
nodes.description: Audio processing systems where output is fed back into input, used for creating resonance, synthesis, and adaptive signal processing.

nodes.label: Echo effect
nodes.description: A sound processing effect that simulates the reflection of sound against a surface, audible when the reflection is heard at least 1/20th of a second after the direct sound.

nodes.label: Reverberation
nodes.description: The result of sound propagation in an environment with reflective surfaces, characterized by gradual buildup and decay of reflections that convey information about acoustic space and source distance.

nodes.label: Adaptive synthesis
nodes.description: Synthesis techniques where arbitrary input signals can be employed as control and modulation sources, extending traditional synthesis methods.

nodes.label: Variable Delay
nodes.description: A delay line with a movable reading position (tap) that allows dynamic variation of delay time over time, enabling pitch modulation and vibrato effects.

nodes.label: Vibrato
nodes.description: A frequency modulation effect created by varying the delay time of a delay line using a modulating signal such as a sine wave, producing continuous pitch oscillation.

nodes.label: Frequency Modulation via Delay
nodes.description: A technique where pitch variation is achieved by reading and writing to a delay line at different rates, with the frequency deviation dependent on the time derivative of delay modulation.

nodes.label: Physical Modeling
nodes.description: A synthesis technique that simulates mechanical sound-generating systems by mathematically reconstructing the physical properties of modeled systems, differing from other digital synthesis techniques by modeling the instruments themselves rather than their sounds.

nodes.label: Interpolation in DSP
nodes.description: A technique used in variable delay implementations to smooth reading positions in delay line memory, employing linear, cubic, or higher-order methods.

nodes.label: Frequency-Dependent Loss
nodes.description: A characteristic of physical strings where higher frequencies decay faster than lower frequencies, implemented in waveguide models using low-pass filters.

nodes.label: Adaptive FM (AdFM)
nodes.description: A frequency modulation technique that adapts modulation parameters based on input signal characteristics, implemented through resonator structures with pole angle and radius modulation.

nodes.label: Self-modulation
nodes.description: A complex-carrier complex-modulator phase modulation technique where the input signal is used for both carrier and modulator functions.

nodes.label: Pitch tracking
nodes.description: A technique used to estimate the fundamental frequency of a source waveform, enabling synchronization of the grain clock to the source pitch in pitch synchronous granular synthesis.

nodes.label: Single-sideband FM
nodes.description: A variation of FM synthesis that produces only upper or lower sidebands through exponential wave-shaping and ring modulation, allowing asymmetrical spectral control.

nodes.label: Delay-line modulation
nodes.description: A technique that modulates the delay time of a delay line to create frequency modulation effects on input signals.

nodes.label: Asymmetrical FM
nodes.description: Generalization of single-sideband FM that includes a symmetry parameter r to control spectral symmetry of the FM spectrum.

nodes.label: Phase Distortion
nodes.description: A synthesis technique implemented as heterodyned wave shaping using sinusoidal transfer functions, with carrier and modulator signals in quadrature.

nodes.label: GEN 12
nodes.description: Csound function generator that creates tables for modified Bessel function lookup used in asymmetrical FM normalization.

nodes.label: Modified Bessel Function
nodes.description: Mathematical function used to describe the phase and spectral coefficients in feedback FM synthesis, particularly for approximating sawtooth waveforms.

nodes.label: Spectral Symmetry
nodes.description: The property that for real signals, the negative spectrum is the complex conjugate of the positive side, enabling optimization of FFT computation.

nodes.label: Octave Transposition
nodes.description: Effect achieved in adaptive ModFM by setting the carrier-to-modulator ratio c:m to an integer above 1.

nodes.label: Formant
nodes.description: A concentration of acoustic energy around a particular frequency in the speech or instrument spectrum, shaped by spectral envelope in FOF synthesis.

nodes.label: Sideband
nodes.description: Frequency components in FM synthesis that appear at intervals of the modulator frequency above and below the carrier frequency, theoretically infinite in number but limited in audibility by amplitude.

nodes.label: Jean-Claude Risset
nodes.description: A composer and researcher whose historical synthesis instruments, particularly focused on additive synthesis techniques like the famous Risset bell, have been converted into Csound UDO opcodes.

nodes.label: Feedback AM (FBAM)
nodes.description: An amplitude modulation synthesis technique using recursive signal paths where the output is fed back as modulation, creating rich harmonic spectra.

nodes.label: Periodic Linear Time-Varying (PLTV) Filter
nodes.description: A specialist filter component with time-varying coefficients used as the main component for FBAM implementation, characterized by impulse response h(τ,t) and frequency response H(ω,t).

nodes.label: Infinite Impulse Response (IIR) System
nodes.description: A recursive filter architecture used to reinterpret FBAM as a coefficient-modulated one-pole recursive filter.

nodes.label: Feedback Amplitude Modulation (FBAM)
nodes.description: A feedback modulation synthesis technique that uses coefficient-modulated filters and sinusoidal carriers to generate complex spectra with controllable harmonics and formants.

nodes.label: RMS Balance Unit
nodes.description: An adaptive gain control mechanism that measures RMS values of filter input and output to normalize FBAM system gain, which varies significantly with β in a frequency-dependent way.

nodes.label: Non-linear Distortion
nodes.description: A variation technique applied to FBAM to create new algorithms and spectral modifications.

nodes.label: Feedforward Delay Term
nodes.description: An addition to the basic FBAM equation that generates different waveforms through half-sample delay and phase offset modifications without significantly altering the spectrum.

nodes.label: All-pass Topology Filter
nodes.description: A coefficient-modulated filter variant derived from FBAM with feedforward terms, exhibiting similar stability and aliasing behavior to basic FBAM.

nodes.label: Resonator FM
nodes.description: A variant of frequency modulation implemented through second-order resonator filter structures with modulated pole angle and radius, offering more stable behavior than pole-angle modulation alone.

nodes.label: Feedback FM
nodes.description: A frequency modulation technique using delay-line feedback to modify existing sounds and synthesize various types of spectra, allowing arbitrary input signals to be processed.

nodes.label: Delay-line Interpolation
nodes.description: A technique for implementing variable delay in feedback FM using linear or higher-order interpolation methods to handle fractional sample delays.

nodes.label: Grain
nodes.description: A very short sound segment shaped by an envelope function that smoothly fades the grain in and out, typically lasting from a few milliseconds to around half a second.

nodes.label: Von Hann Window
nodes.description: A window function used in spectral analysis with bandwidth Bw = 4fs/Nw, capable of detecting partials in adjacent bins with a minimum frequency deviation range of approximately 172 Hz for Nw=1024 and fs=44100.

nodes.label: Envelope Function
nodes.description: An amplitude-shaping function that smoothly fades grains in and out, with shapes that can be symmetrical or asymmetrical, including exponential, linear-piecewise, triangular, and Gaussian forms.

nodes.label: poscil Opcode
nodes.description: A precise oscillator opcode in Csound that uses interpolation for accurate table reading, recommended as a best practice for audio synthesis.

nodes.label: Synchronous Grain Generation
nodes.description: A type of grain generation technique that produces streams of grains with regular timing patterns.

nodes.label: Asynchronous Grain Generation
nodes.description: A type of grain generation technique that produces clouds of grains with irregular or random timing patterns.

nodes.label: Synchronous Granular Synthesis
nodes.description: A granular synthesis approach where grains are generated at regular intervals controlled by a grain rate parameter, as demonstrated in the partikkel opcode examples.

nodes.label: Asynchronous Granular Synthesis
nodes.description: A granular synthesis approach where grains are statistically distributed in time with a defined grain density rather than at regular intervals, mostly used to create textures with distributed spectra.

nodes.label: Grain Rate
nodes.description: The frequency at which grains are generated. Low rates (< 50 Hz) preserve source timbre; high periodic rates (> 30-50 Hz) create pitch equal to the grain rate; irregular rates produce cloud textures.

nodes.label: Grain Density
nodes.description: The average number of grains generated over a certain period in asynchronous granular synthesis, describing statistical distribution of grains in time.

nodes.label: Gaussian Envelope
nodes.description: A grain envelope shape created using GEN 20 in Csound that produces a narrow envelope, resulting in grains with large bandwidth and pulse-like characteristics.

nodes.label: Von Hann Envelope
nodes.description: An inverted, scaled cosine envelope used in grain generation to create smooth grain boundaries and reduce aliasing artifacts.

nodes.label: GEN 20
nodes.description: A Csound function generator that creates Gaussian-shaped wavetables, suggested as an efficient alternative to direct waveshaping in PAF implementation.

nodes.label: poscil
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for phase-accurate oscillation generation used in grain stream instruments.

nodes.label: phasor
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates a phase ramp from 0 to 1, used as a common phase source for synchronizing grain waveforms and envelopes.

nodes.label: tablei
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for interpolated table reading used to read grain waveforms and envelopes from function tables.

nodes.label: schedule
nodes.description: A Csound opcode used for event scheduling to generate streams of grain events at specified times and rates.

nodes.label: GEN 1 Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound function table generator that reads audio from sound files and fills a table with corresponding samples for use in granular synthesis.

nodes.label: schedule Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that calls an instance of a defined instrument from within the CsInstruments section, taking instrument name/number, start time, and duration as arguments.

nodes.label: Python
nodes.description: A scripting language that can be used to generate grain data and control Csound instruments for granular synthesis applications.

nodes.label: Grain Cloud
nodes.description: A granular synthesis technique where grains are generated as a distributed cloud rather than a sequential stream, creating particle-like textures.

nodes.label: Sampled-Sound Granulation
nodes.description: A granular synthesis technique that uses slices from recorded audio as grain waveforms, enabling granulated resynthesis and time-stretching effects.

nodes.label: Recursive Scheduling
nodes.description: A technique where each grain instrument schedules the next grain, creating an efficient asynchronous granular synthesis design.

nodes.label: syncgrain
nodes.description: A Csound opcode designed to generate streams of grains in a synchronous manner, with parameters controlling amplitude, generation frequency, pitch, grain size, and read position.

nodes.label: fof opcode
nodes.description: A Csound unit-generator that produces spectral output resembling an impulse generator filtered by a bandpass filter, with partials above a fundamental and a spectral peak at the formant frequency.

nodes.label: partikkel
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for granular synthesis that uses multiple source waveforms with separate frequency trajectories and grain shaping to approximate formant synthesis and morph between granular synthesis types.

nodes.label: syncloop
nodes.description: Variant of syncgrain opcode that allows specifying file read start point and looping segments for granular synthesis.

nodes.label: diskgrain
nodes.description: A Csound opcode variant that creates grain streams directly from a sound file rather than a function table.

nodes.label: fof2 opcode
nodes.description: A variation of the FOF opcode in Csound designed to take advantage of synchronous granular synthesis characteristics with dynamic selection of different read positions in source tables.

nodes.label: fog opcode
nodes.description: A variation of the FOF opcode in Csound that provides flexibility in applying the FOF method to sampled-sound material through dynamic read position selection.

nodes.label: partikkel opcode
nodes.description: A unified Csound implementation of all methods of time-domain granular processing (particle synthesis) with up to eight outputs and forty input parameters, supporting multiple grain sources including trainlet synthesis.

nodes.label: trainlet synthesis
nodes.description: A synthesis method within the partikkel opcode that generates an impulse train with control of dynamically-variable harmonics, frequency balance, and fundamental frequency.

nodes.label: syncgrain opcode
nodes.description: A Csound granular synthesis opcode that allows dynamic selection of read positions in source tables for synchronous granular processing.

nodes.label: Discrete Fourier Transform
nodes.description: A mathematical transformation that converts a sequence of samples into frequency-domain representation, fundamental to frequency-domain analysis and synthesis in computer music.

nodes.label: Fast Fourier Transform
nodes.description: A fast algorithm for computing the DFT that exploits mathematical properties to reduce computational complexity, typically working with power-of-two window sizes.

nodes.label: Short-Time Fourier Transform
nodes.description: Variant of Fourier Transform that divides continuous audio into fixed time frames for spectral analysis, enabling sound transformations like time stretching and pitch shifting.

nodes.label: phase vocoder
nodes.description: A spectral analysis and synthesis technique that treats audio as a collection of short time-domain frames in spectral form, enabling flexible time-scale modifications including stretching, compressing, freezing, and jumbling of sounds.

nodes.label: Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT)
nodes.description: A discrete-time, discrete-frequency Fourier transform widely used in spectral processing and the basis for algorithms such as the phase vocoder and sinusoidal modelling.

nodes.label: Gibbs Effect
nodes.description: An overshoot artifact that occurs in band-limited waveforms at discontinuities, caused by truncating an infinite harmonic series to a finite number of terms.

nodes.label: Polar Form Spectrum
nodes.description: A representation of frequency-domain coefficients using magnitude and phase components rather than real and imaginary parts.

nodes.label: Frequency-Domain Analysis
nodes.description: Techniques for analyzing and synthesizing audio signals by transforming between time and frequency domains using FFT/IFFT operations.

nodes.label: Rectangular Window
nodes.description: A window function that applies a rectangular envelope to a signal segment, corresponding to the implicit windowing in direct DFT analysis.

nodes.label: Inverse Discrete Fourier Transform
nodes.description: The inverse operation of the DFT that recovers the original signal from its frequency-domain representation, functioning as an additive synthesis process.

nodes.label: Spectral Smearing
nodes.description: An artifact in DFT analysis where a partial's detection spreads across multiple frequency bins when the input signal does not complete an integer number of cycles over the DFT length.

nodes.label: Windowing
nodes.description: The application of an envelope function to a signal segment to mitigate discontinuities at frame boundaries and reduce spectral artifacts in frequency-domain analysis.

nodes.label: Radix-2 FFT
nodes.description: A Fast Fourier Transform algorithm designed to work with DFT sizes that are exact powers of two, splitting computation into two half-size transforms recursively until reaching size-2 DFTs.

nodes.label: Twiddle Factor
nodes.description: The complex exponential factor e^(-2πjk/N) used in FFT algorithms to combine even and odd frequency components during recursive decomposition.

nodes.label: Bit-Reversal Reordering
nodes.description: A data rearrangement technique used in radix-2 FFT where input indices are reordered by reversing their binary representations, placing odd indices in the second half of the frame.

nodes.label: Fast Fourier Transform (FFT)
nodes.description: A radix-2 FFT algorithm implementation for computing the discrete Fourier transform efficiently, with applications to audio signal analysis and synthesis.

nodes.label: Real FFT (rfft)
nodes.description: An optimized FFT variant for real-valued input signals that exploits DFT symmetry to pack twice the data into a single N/2 complex transform.

nodes.label: Inverse Fast Fourier Transform (IFFT)
nodes.description: The inverse operation of the FFT algorithm that reconstructs time-domain signals from frequency-domain representations.

nodes.label: Convolution Reverb
nodes.description: A frequency-domain technique that imparts the acoustic characteristics of a space onto an input sound by convolving the input with a measured impulse response.

nodes.label: Overlap-Add
nodes.description: A technique for performing fast convolution by slicing input signals and impulse responses, taking DFTs, and reconstructing output through overlapping and addition.

nodes.label: Partitioned Convolution
nodes.description: A frequency-domain convolution method that partitions the impulse response into P segments of power-of-two length, reducing latency compared to single-partition fast convolution while maintaining computational efficiency.

nodes.label: Real FFT
nodes.description: An optimized FFT algorithm variant that exploits the symmetry properties of real-valued signals to reduce computational complexity.

nodes.label: Fast Convolution
nodes.description: An efficient convolution method using DFT and IDFT to perform frequency-domain multiplication instead of time-domain convolution, reducing computational cost for large impulse responses.

nodes.label: FIR Filtering
nodes.description: Finite Impulse Response filtering implemented via convolution, where filter coefficients are derived from the IDFT of a desired frequency response.

nodes.label: Spectral-Domain Delay Line
nodes.description: A delay line operating in the frequency domain where DFT blocks are stored and multiplied by impulse response partitions in partitioned convolution.

nodes.label: Window Function
nodes.description: Amplitude envelope applied to each grain in granular synthesis, defined as a function table that can create soft grains with gradual attacks/decays or percussive/gate-like characteristics.

nodes.label: Short-Time Fourier Transform
nodes.description: An analysis method that divides audio signals into small temporal windows (windowing) of milliseconds duration, each with a standard envelope type (rectangular, triangular, Hanning, Gauss), to capture temporal changes in sound.

nodes.label: Hop Size
nodes.description: A time increment parameter (l) used in STFT analysis that determines the spacing between successive analysis frames; can be much larger than a single sample.

nodes.label: Hamming Window
nodes.description: A raised scaled cosine window defined as w(t) = 0.54 + 0.46 cos(2πt/N), characterized by not having zeros and suitable for spectral analysis.

nodes.label: Spectral Masking
nodes.description: A frequency-domain filtering technique that applies a magnitude mask to suppress or emphasize specific frequency regions in a signal's spectrum.

nodes.label: Cross-Synthesis
nodes.description: A spectral processing technique that multiplies the magnitudes of two input sounds while using the phase of one, emphasizing common spectral components between the sounds.

nodes.label: Cepstrum Transform
nodes.description: A mathematical technique defined as the DFT of the logarithm of the magnitude spectrum, used to extract spectral envelopes by smoothing magnitude spectra through liftering.

nodes.label: Liftering
nodes.description: A process of removing high-order cepstral coefficients to smooth the magnitude spectrum by eliminating high-frequency fluctuations in the cepstral domain.

nodes.label: Spectral Vocoder
nodes.description: A frequency-domain vocoder that extracts the spectral envelope from one sound and applies it to an excitation signal, combining magnitude and phase information for hybrid sound synthesis.

nodes.label: Instantaneous Frequency
nodes.description: The frequency at each sample time, derived from the phase derivative of an oscillator, enabling time-varying frequency analysis in the spectral domain.

nodes.label: Spectral Pitch Shifter
nodes.description: A frequency-domain effect that transposes audio by scaling all frequency components according to a pitch shift factor p, with bin remapping to maintain spectral coherence.

nodes.label: Formant Preservation
nodes.description: A technique for maintaining the original spectral envelope during pitch shifting, particularly important for vocal processing to avoid unnatural Donald Duck effects.

nodes.label: Cepstrum
nodes.description: A signal processing technique used in spectral envelope extraction through iterative application of FFT and liftering to recover log magnitudes.

nodes.label: Inverse Short-Time Fourier Transform
nodes.description: The inverse operation of STFT that reconstructs time-domain audio from spectral frames using overlap-add synthesis.

nodes.label: Time Scaling
nodes.description: A spectral processing technique that stretches or compresses the duration of a sound without affecting its pitch by decoupling analysis and synthesis time positions.

nodes.label: Phase Locking
nodes.description: A technique that locks resynthesis phase to magnitude peak values to reduce phasiness artifacts in time-stretching by preventing phase misalignment between adjacent spectral bins.

nodes.label: Spectral Bin
nodes.description: A frequency component in the FFT output; in phase vocoder processing, partials can span multiple adjacent bins within the window bandwidth.

nodes.label: fsig data type
nodes.description: A specially-designed Csound data type that holds a time-ordered sequence of spectral frames instead of audio samples, enabling seamless mixing with time-domain processing.

nodes.label: pvsanal opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates fsigs from streaming analysis by taking time-domain audio input and producing a sequence of frames at every time point separated by hop size samples.

nodes.label: pvsynth opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that resynthesizes audio from f-signals (frequency-domain signals) produced by phase vocoder analysis.

nodes.label: Spectral processing
nodes.description: Sound transformation techniques operating in the frequency domain, including time stretching, pitch shifting, cross synthesis, and spectral modification.

nodes.label: MIDI
nodes.description: Musical Instrument Digital Interface protocol for transmitting musical control messages as sequences of eight-bit bytes, with seven channel message types including NOTE ON, NOTE OFF, aftertouch, program change, control change, and pitch bend.

nodes.label: Open Sound Control
nodes.description: A network communication protocol for the exchange of control data in electronic music instruments, allowing interaction with a variety of software and hardware controllers both locally and remotely.

nodes.label: mido
nodes.description: A Python MIDI library or module that allows access to physical or virtual MIDI ports for sending and receiving MIDI messages.

nodes.label: pvscale opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that scales the frequency content of a phase vocoder signal by a specified factor, used for pitch shifting and harmonization.

nodes.label: NOTE ON Message
nodes.description: A MIDI message with status byte 144 used to trigger notes, or with zero velocity to represent note-offs.

nodes.label: NOTE OFF Message
nodes.description: A MIDI message with status byte 128 used to stop notes, optionally including note-off velocity data.

nodes.label: Pitch Bend Message
nodes.description: MIDI channel voice message with code 224 carrying two values combined to give a range from −8192 to 8191 for pitch modulation.

nodes.label: Control Change Message
nodes.description: MIDI channel voice message with code 176 containing a control number and value, user-mappable for synthesizer parameter control.

nodes.label: Aftertouch Message
nodes.description: MIDI channel voice message with code 208 generated by applying pressure to a controller keyboard.

nodes.label: Polyphonic Aftertouch Message
nodes.description: MIDI channel voice message with code 166 carrying note-by-note aftertouch control with note number and amount values.

nodes.label: Program Change Message
nodes.description: MIDI channel voice message with code 192 used to change stored parameter programs in synthesizers.

nodes.label: System Exclusive Message
nodes.description: MIDI system message used to send device-specific data such as parameter lists and sample dumps.

nodes.label: FBAM2 Instrument
nodes.description: Faust-based synthesis instrument that can be configured with MIDI UI controls for polyphonic synthesis.

nodes.label: UDP
nodes.description: Network protocol used in Csound for sending and receiving control or modulation data via network opcodes, with packet size limited to MTU of 1,456 bytes.

nodes.label: TCP (Transmission Control Protocol)
nodes.description: A connection-based network transport protocol that guarantees reliable data delivery with congestion control, suitable for stable network audio transmission.

nodes.label: Real-time Transport Protocol (RTP)
nodes.description: A protocol built on top of UDP for audio delivery over IP networks, prioritizing timeliness over reliability with error-correction algorithms.

nodes.label: VCO2 Oscillator
nodes.description: A voltage-controlled oscillator opcode in Csound used for generating waveforms in synthesis instruments.

nodes.label: pythonosc
