nodes.description: A Python module providing OSC server and client functionalities for sending and receiving OSC messages.

nodes.label: WIMP Paradigm
nodes.description: Windows-icons-menus-pointer graphical user interface design paradigm based on graphical containers, icons, menus, and pointer manipulation.

nodes.label: Widget
nodes.description: Basic interface component in GUI design with different graphical representations such as push buttons, tick boxes, sliders, text windows, and pull-down menus.

nodes.label: Qt
nodes.description: Cross-platform graphics library used to build GUI-based applications in Faust stand-alone programs.

nodes.label: GTK
nodes.description: Cross-platform graphics library used to build GUI-based applications in Faust stand-alone programs.

nodes.label: CsoundQT
nodes.description: An integrated development environment for Csound that supports Python scripting through PythonQt, enabling control of the interface, widgets, and the running Csound engine.

nodes.label: Cabbage
nodes.description: A Csound frontend developed since 2007 by Rory Walsh with a main focus on exporting plugins from Csound files to run in a DAW. Currently the most popular way to work with Csound.

nodes.label: Blue
nodes.description: A graphical interface and composition environment for Csound that provides mixer systems, real-time performance tools (BlueLive), score timeline organization, and SoundObject editing capabilities.

nodes.label: Event Loop
nodes.description: Fundamental piece of GUI-based programs that keeps software running while waiting for user input in the form of messages from the operating system.

nodes.label: Canvas Widget
nodes.description: Special Tkinter widget type that implements structured graphics and can be used as a general-purpose widget builder to hold user-drawn elements.

nodes.label: WIMP
nodes.description: A graphical user interface paradigm based on windows, icons, menus, and pointers that has become increasingly seen as limiting for interactive music applications.

nodes.label: Multi-touch screen
nodes.description: An interface technology where position and size of individual touches can be measured, processed and dispatched to applications, expanding beyond the single pointer paradigm.

nodes.label: Arduino
nodes.description: An open-source microcontroller development board based on Atmel AVR processors, widely used for creating custom hardware interfaces for computer music instruments.

nodes.label: Wiring library
nodes.description: A C/C++ library that facilitates programming of Arduino boards, allowing easy input/output operations and hardware integration.

nodes.label: Physical computing
nodes.description: A field of performing technology that emerged from the success of Arduino and similar development boards for creating custom hardware interfaces.

nodes.label: Maker movement
nodes.description: A cultural movement characterized by increased availability of microcontrollers and DIY hardware development that has influenced computer musicians to create custom interfaces.

nodes.label: Atmel
nodes.description: A microcontroller manufacturer whose 8-bit AVR processors are used in Arduino development boards.

nodes.label: BASIC Stamp
nodes.description: A commercial microcontroller board that preceded Arduino as a more expensive alternative for embedded systems development.

nodes.label: ADC
nodes.description: Hardware device that converts continuous analog signals to digital form, typically using low-pass filtering to eliminate high-frequency components above the Nyquist frequency.

nodes.label: PWM
nodes.description: Pulse-Width Modulation, a waveform output method in Arduino boards suitable for driving small electric motors and similar components.

nodes.label: Arduino shield
nodes.description: Pluggable extension boards for Arduino that add functionality such as DAC facilities, MIDI integration, wireless networking, and data card access.

nodes.label: IBM 704
nodes.description: Early mainframe computer used by Max Mathews in New York City in 1957 to synthesize the first computer-generated musical piece.

nodes.label: Cmusic
nodes.description: A music programming system developed in the 1980s using the C language, alongside Csound and other similar systems.

nodes.label: PDP-11
nodes.description: Minicomputer platform that represented an intermediate step in the evolution from mainframes to desktop computers for music computing.

nodes.label: GPU
nodes.description: Graphics processing units repurposed as general-purpose computing platforms (GPGPUs) for music and audio applications.

nodes.label: CARL
nodes.description: Computer music laboratory that developed site-specific software environments portable to similar platforms.

nodes.label: Composer's Desktop Project
nodes.description: Organization that developed interesting audio processing programs for the Atari platform in the early 1990s.

nodes.label: Apple II
nodes.description: Early consumer-oriented microcomputer that gained popularity with hobbyists and early business users.

nodes.label: Macintosh
nodes.description: Apple computer with GUI that spawned considerable interest in computer music software, particularly MIDI-related packages.

nodes.label: Atari
nodes.description: Computer platform that included built-in MIDI interfaces and supported Csound, Cmusic, and CDP software.

nodes.label: UNIX
nodes.description: Operating system that enabled multi-user time-sharing environments and became the basis for scientific computing and music software development.

nodes.label: X Window System
nodes.description: Standard for graphical workstations with WIMP interfaces used in scientific computing and computer music.

nodes.label: MUSIC N paradigm
nodes.description: Emergent set of properties from music programming systems emphasizing programmability and flexible platforms for computer music.

nodes.label: Domain-Specific Language (DSL)
nodes.description: A specialized programming language for music and sound synthesis, used in conjunction with scripting languages and system-implementation languages in the multi-language paradigm.

nodes.label: VST
nodes.description: A plugin system standard for audio and music software that enables complementary software packages to function cooperatively in computer music ecosystems.

nodes.label: LADSPA
nodes.description: A plugin system standard for audio and music software that enables complementary software packages to function cooperatively in computer music ecosystems.

nodes.label: Jack
nodes.description: Audio and MIDI plumbing infrastructure that allows applications to communicate with each other and external devices in computer music ecosystems.

nodes.label: Digital Audio Workstation (DAW)
nodes.description: Software applications that function as central hubs in computer music ecosystems, loading plugins and integrating with other music software for composition and production.

nodes.label: Linux OS
nodes.description: An open-source operating system with a wide range of audio and music software, exemplifying the success of free and open-source software in computer music development.

nodes.label: iOS
nodes.description: A mobile operating system with better support for real-time audio IO and lower latency, enabling music applications through Objective C development.

nodes.label: Android
nodes.description: A mobile operating system that has improved considerably in audio support, enabling music applications through Java and C/C++ development.

nodes.label: HTML 5
nodes.description: The markup language used to create user interfaces for Csound web applications with sliders, buttons, and styled elements.

nodes.label: Javascript
nodes.description: A standardized functional programming language that serves as the engine and major programming language of the World Wide Web and web browsers.

nodes.label: Web Platform
nodes.description: A virtual computing platform delivered through web browsers using HTML 5 and Javascript, extending the computer music ecosystem across different operating systems and hardware.

nodes.label: Digital Music Instrument (DMI)
nodes.description: Self-contained music applications based on audio engines like Csound or Faust, using post-WIMP mobile interfaces for interactive performance control.

nodes.label: Object-Oriented Programming
nodes.description: A programming paradigm used to realize the MUSIC N model through instrument classes and unit generator instances.

nodes.label: Multi-Language Paradigm
nodes.description: A design approach that intermixes domain-specific languages, scripting languages, and system-implementation languages to provide flexible solutions for sound synthesis and music making.

nodes.label: Free and Open-Source Software
nodes.description: A development model that enabled cross-fertilization of ideas in computer music, with seminal software including all MUSIC N systems available as open-source.

nodes.label: Web Audio API
nodes.description: A collection of JavaScript objects supporting audio processing on the web platform, implementing oscillators, envelopes, filters, and providing audio plumbing to the host OS.

nodes.label: Native Client (PNaCl)
nodes.description: A portable browser technology that allows C/C++ code to be compiled and run directly in the browser at near-native speed, used by Csound for efficient web-based audio applications.

nodes.label: Raspberry Pi
nodes.description: Single-board computer platform used in physical computing and music applications.

nodes.label: Beaglebone
nodes.description: An ARM-based low-power CPU board used in DIY computer music platforms.

nodes.label: Music Domain-Specific Language (DSL)
nodes.description: Specialized programming languages designed for audio and music processing, significant across web, desktop, mobile, and DIY platforms.

nodes.label: Internet of Musical Things
nodes.description: An approach to creating small computing devices that can be remotely controlled and connected over a wide area to generate audio and interact with environments.

nodes.label: Desktop computing platform
nodes.description: A mature environment for computer music design and performance with foundations tracing back to the beginnings of computer music.

nodes.label: Mobile devices
nodes.description: Computing platforms not yet fully capable for independent application development in computer music contexts.

nodes.label: Web browsers
nodes.description: Platform requiring underlying general-purpose operating systems for hardware and I/O management in music computing.

nodes.label: Computer music
nodes.description: An established discipline nearly sixty years old, supported by mature platforms and various alternatives for composers, sound designers, researchers, and educators.

nodes.label: Trigonometry
nodes.description: Mathematical foundation for signal processing in computer music, covering angles, trigonometric functions, and their identities used in synthesis formulae.

nodes.label: Complex Numbers
nodes.description: Two-dimensional extension of real numbers used in signal processing, defined as a conjunction of two real numbers with one marked by j.

nodes.label: Unit Circle
nodes.description: Circle of radius 1 used to measure angles linearly on the circumference from 0 to 2π, with angles defined in radians for signal-processing formulae.

nodes.label: Radian
nodes.description: Unit of angle measurement based on the unit circle, where 2π radians equals a full circle and π/2 equals a right angle.

nodes.label: Complex Exponential
nodes.description: The function e^(jx) = cos(x) + j sin(x), fundamental for signal analysis and synthesis, representing a complex sinusoid combining cosine and sine waves.

nodes.label: Z-Transform
nodes.description: A mathematical tool for obtaining the transfer function of a digital filter from its impulse response, using complex polynomial functions with complex variable z.

nodes.label: Transfer Function
nodes.description: In waveshaping synthesis, a function that maps an input signal to a desired output waveform, traditionally found through polynomial spectral matching or other mathematical functions.

nodes.label: Time Shift Operator
nodes.description: The z^(-t) term in z-transform representation, where z^(-1) represents a 1-sample delay and z^(-t) represents a t-sample delay in signal processing.

nodes.label: Differentiation
nodes.description: Mathematical operation that computes the rate of change of a function, used to derive instantaneous frequency from phase and to analyze signal dynamics.

nodes.label: Integration
nodes.description: Mathematical operation that reverses differentiation, used to recover phase from frequency information in oscillators and FM synthesis.

nodes.label: Antiderivative
nodes.description: Inverse operation of differentiation used to evaluate definite integrals and calculate Fourier coefficients.

nodes.label: Vocal Synthesis
nodes.description: Technique for simulating vocal sounds using formant filters and resonance, demonstrated in a vocal quartet simulation instrument.

nodes.label: Formant Filter
nodes.description: A resonant filter used to shape the spectral characteristics of a source signal, with controllable center frequency and bandwidth.

nodes.label: Reverberation
nodes.description: An audio effect simulating natural room reflections and absorption, implemented using combinations of allpass filters, comb filters, and delays to create spacious acoustic environments.

nodes.label: Waveshaping
nodes.description: A non-linear distortion synthesis technique based on mapping an input signal (typically sinusoidal) through a transfer function to produce a desired output waveform, with distortion controlled by a distortion index.

nodes.label: Bandlimited Synthesis
nodes.description: Technique for generating bandlimited waveforms to avoid aliasing, implemented via Blp and Blsum UDOs using closed-form summation formulae.

nodes.label: FFT-based Convolution
nodes.description: A mathematically equivalent but faster convolution method using Fast Fourier Transform, padding signals to power-of-two length, multiplying FFTs, and taking the inverse FFT.

nodes.label: Pitch Shifting
nodes.description: A technique using time-scaling with linear interpolation to transpose grains by factors relative to the original pitch (1.0 = original, 2.0 = one octave up, 0.5 = one octave down).

nodes.label: Python with SciPy
nodes.description: Programming environment used for implementing audio processing algorithms including FFT-based convolution, spectral masking, and cross-synthesis.

nodes.label: Cepstral Analysis
nodes.description: Signal processing technique used in the true_spec_env function to extract spectral envelope by analyzing the log magnitude spectrum.

nodes.label: Mark Dolson
nodes.description: Author of influential tutorial on the phase vocoder in Computer Music Journal.

nodes.label: Flanagan and Golden
nodes.description: Researchers who developed the phase vocoder technique at Bell Labs.

nodes.label: The Audio Programming Book
nodes.description: Comprehensive reference edited by Boulanger and Lazzarini covering digital audio signals, phase vocoder programming, and spectral audio techniques.

nodes.label: Computer Music Journal
nodes.description: Academic journal publishing research on computer music techniques including granular synthesis and signal processing.

nodes.label: Bell Labs
nodes.description: Research facility where Max Mathews and colleagues accomplished the first digital recording and first computer sound synthesis in 1957.

nodes.label: MIT Press
nodes.description: Publisher of foundational computer music texts including Foundations of Computer Music (1985) and The Computer Music Tutorial (1995).

nodes.label: Curtis Roads
nodes.description: Composer and researcher who implemented a simple form of digital granular synthesis in 1975, composed a prototype, and published important articles on granular synthesis in 1978 and 1985.

nodes.label: Miller Puckette
nodes.description: Computer music researcher who published on formant-based audio synthesis using nonlinear distortion and authored The Theory and Technique of Computer Music.

nodes.label: Xavier Rodet
nodes.description: Researcher who developed time-domain formant-wave-function synthesis and the CHANT project for singing voice synthesis.

nodes.label: Xavier Serra
nodes.description: Co-developer of the deterministic plus stochastic decomposition model for sound analysis/synthesis, which formed the basis for ATS refinement.

nodes.label: Julius Smith
nodes.description: CCRMA researcher who developed digital reverberation using closed waveguide networks and published on the history of digital synthesis.

nodes.label: MUSIC IV
nodes.description: A music programming system written for the IBM 7094 computer in collaboration with Joan Miller, introducing the first general model of a music programming system with a three-pass compiler architecture.

nodes.label: Distortion Synthesis
nodes.description: A family of synthesis methods including waveshaping, generalized summation formulae, and frequency/phase modulation that use non-linear processing to generate complex spectra.

nodes.label: PARSHL
nodes.description: Analysis/synthesis program for non-harmonic sounds based on sinusoidal representation, developed by Smith and Serra.

nodes.label: The Audio Programming Book
nodes.description: Comprehensive reference edited by Boulanger and Lazzarini covering STFT, spectral processing, and time-domain audio programming.

nodes.label: Thomas G. Stockham Jr.
nodes.description: Computer scientist who published on high-speed convolution and correlation in 1966, foundational work for digital signal processing in audio.

nodes.label: James Tenney
nodes.description: Composer and theorist who published 'Sound generation by means of a digital computer' in the Journal of Music Theory in 1963.

nodes.label: John Timoney
nodes.description: Researcher who co-authored work on dynamic signal phase distortion using coefficient-modulated allpass filters in 2014.

nodes.label: Noboru Tomisawa
nodes.description: Inventor who patented a tone production method for electronic musical instruments in 1981.

nodes.label: Bernard Widrow
nodes.description: Signal processing researcher who co-authored 'Quantization Noise: Roundoff Error in Digital Computation, Signal Processing, Control, and Communications' in 2008.

nodes.label: Istvan Kollár
nodes.description: Co-author of 'Quantization Noise: Roundoff Error in Digital Computation, Signal Processing, Control, and Communications' published in 2008.

nodes.label: Trevor Wishart
nodes.description: Composer and theorist who authored 'Audible Design' published in 1994, addressing sonic design principles.

nodes.label: Adrian Wood
nodes.description: Author of 'The Physics of Music' published in 1975.

nodes.label: Matthew Wright
nodes.description: Co-developer of Open Sound Control (OSC), a protocol for communicating with sound synthesizers, presented at ICMC 1997.

nodes.label: Adrian Freed
nodes.description: Co-developer of Open Sound Control (OSC), a protocol for communicating with sound synthesizers, presented at ICMC 1997.

nodes.label: Ali Momeni
nodes.description: Co-author of 'Open Sound Control, state of the art 2003' presented at NIME-03 in Montreal.

nodes.label: Open Sound Control
nodes.description: A modern networking protocol developed in the mid-1990s at CNMAT as a flexible alternative to MIDI, using UDP for communication between synthesizers, applications, and remote computers.

nodes.label: Web Audio
nodes.description: A browser-based audio API that Csound can use as an output device when running in a web environment.

nodes.label: Iain McCurdy
nodes.description: Major contributor to the Csound FLOSS Manual, authoring sections on envelopes, panning, filters, delay, reverberation, granular synthesis, convolution, amplitude tracking, and digital audio.

nodes.label: Newman Guttman
nodes.description: Colleague of Max Mathews at Bell Laboratories who realized early computer music pieces including In The Silver Scale and Pitch Study.

nodes.label: Edgard Varèse
nodes.description: Composer intrigued by digital synthesis who presented Pitch Study at the Village Gate in New York City on April 26, 1959, as a manifesto for computer sound synthesis.

nodes.label: MUSIC II
nodes.description: Early computer music program by Max Mathews featuring four-voice polyphony and an ingenious wavetable lookup oscillator design.

nodes.label: Modular Synthesis Approach
nodes.description: Design philosophy introduced by Max Mathews in MUSIC III allowing users to select and connect modules to implement diverse sound synthesis possibilities.

nodes.label: Barry Vercoe
nodes.description: Creator of Csound, a gifted composer who developed the software synthesis language that became a foundational tool for computer music composition and education.

nodes.label: Stanford
nodes.description: University where John Chowning organized one of the first computer music courses in 1969.

nodes.label: IRCAM
nodes.description: Institute for Research and Coordination of Acoustics/Music in Paris, where composer courses were held in the late 1970s and real-time synthesis was explored.
aliases: Institut de Recherche et Coordination Acoustique/Musique

nodes.label: Roger Shepard
nodes.description: Researcher who synthesized twelve tones ascending a chromatic scale that seem to ascend endlessly when repeated, demonstrating auditory illusions.

nodes.label: Stria
nodes.description: A milestone work by John Chowning that was reconstituted from computer score by Kevin Dahan and Olivier Baudouin.

nodes.label: Turenas
nodes.description: A milestone work by John Chowning that was transcribed for four players playing digital percussion live by Laurent Pottier.

nodes.label: Phoné
nodes.description: A work by John Chowning demonstrating synthesis control to make specific sounds emerge from a sonic magma through analysis of ear coherence.

nodes.label: MaxMSP
nodes.description: A real-time flow-based and object-oriented programming environment for music and audio, used for real-time synthesis and processing.

nodes.label: MIT Media Lab
nodes.description: Research institution where work on virtual acoustic rooms and synthetic acoustic spaces was conducted in the 1980s-1990s.

nodes.label: Andrés Cabrera
nodes.description: Contributor to the Csound FLOSS Manual, authoring sections on record and play buffers, CsoundQt frontend, and Python integration.

nodes.label: Csound FLOSS Manual
nodes.description: A comprehensive open-source manual documenting Csound audio programming language, covering synthesis, sound modification, sampling, MIDI, and digital audio fundamentals.

nodes.label: Csound Journal
nodes.description: Publication that featured articles on Csound programming techniques, including Python opcode integration.

nodes.label: Berklee College of Music
nodes.description: Music college where Richard Boulanger conducted research in alternate controllers and sound design, and where students contributed significantly to The Csound Book project.

nodes.label: Spectral Analysis and Synthesis
nodes.description: A frequency-domain technique that automatically detects the frequencies and amplitudes of partials in a target sound for use in additive synthesis and other spectral methods.

nodes.label: Scanned Synthesis
nodes.description: A synthesis technique invented by Max Mathews, Rob Shaw, and Bill Verplank that uses a table-lookup oscillator combined with Newton's mass-spring model to dynamically change f-table values, producing spectrally dynamic sounds.

nodes.label: MUSIC 360
nodes.description: Computer music system written by Barry Vercoe at Princeton University for the IBM 360 computer, derived from MUSIC IVB and MUSIC IVBF, and an ancestor of Csound.

nodes.label: MUSIC 11
nodes.description: A version of MUSIC 360 system for the DEC PDP-11 minicomputer introduced by Barry Vercoe, featuring control (k-) and audio (a-) computation rates for efficient audio synthesis.

nodes.label: Table-lookup Oscillator
nodes.description: A fundamental unit generator in Csound that reads values from function tables via index lookup to generate waveforms.

nodes.label: Joan Miller
nodes.description: Collaborator with Max Mathews on MUSIC IV, written for the IBM 7094 computer.

nodes.label: Acoustic Compiler
nodes.description: A compiler concept introduced by Mathews that converts synthesis programs from instrument definitions and unit generators into efficient binary form, enabling unlimited sound synthesis structures.

nodes.label: Numeric Score
nodes.description: The original means of controlling Csound events, used to specify instrument instances and function table generation with a simple syntax based on statements starting with single-character opcodes.

nodes.label: Function Table
nodes.description: A data structure in Csound that stores numerical values for waveforms, control data, or audio samples. Exists only during a Csound instance and can be saved to or loaded from files.

nodes.label: IBM 7094
nodes.description: Computer for which MUSIC IV was written.

nodes.label: Bandlimited Noise Generator
nodes.description: MUSIC IV unit generators (RANDI and RANDH) providing sample-and-hold and interpolating types for noise generation.

nodes.label: Band-pass Filter
nodes.description: A second-order all-pole band-pass filter unit (FILTER) in MUSIC IV for frequency-selective processing.

nodes.label: Moog
nodes.description: Manufacturer of classic analogue modular synthesizer systems that adopted the unit generator principle from computer music systems.

nodes.label: ARP
nodes.description: Manufacturer of classic analogue modular synthesizer systems that adopted the unit generator principle from computer music systems.

nodes.label: Princeton University
nodes.description: Institution where MUSIC IVB and MUSIC 360 were developed and ported.

nodes.label: Richard Moore
nodes.description: Collaborator with Max Mathews on MUSIC V development.

nodes.label: Catalogue of Computer Synthesized Sounds
nodes.description: Epochal 1969 work by Jean-Claude Risset created with MUSIC V at Bell Telephone Laboratories, demonstrating computer synthesis techniques.

nodes.label: Risset-Shepard tones
nodes.description: An auditory illusion technique demonstrated in Risset's catalogue using interpolating oscillators with phase offsets.

nodes.label: FORTRAN
nodes.description: One of the first scientific high-level programming languages used to write MUSIC IV variants and MUSIC V.

nodes.label: IBM 360
nodes.description: Large computer installation for which MUSIC 360 was written.

nodes.label: Vector-based processing
nodes.description: Audio processing technique in MUSIC V using sample blocks or vectors, which became standard in modern computer music systems.

nodes.label: MIT Experimental Music Studio
nodes.description: The institution where Barry Vercoe introduced MUSIC 11.

nodes.label: DEC PDP-11
nodes.description: A minicomputer platform for which MUSIC 11 was developed, whose popularity grew in the 1970s with the introduction of UNIX.

nodes.label: MIT Electronic Music Studio
nodes.description: The institution where Csound came to light in 1986 as a C-language port of MUSIC 11.

nodes.label: University of Bath
nodes.description: Institution to which the centre of Csound development moved from MIT in the 1990s.

nodes.label: Mills College
nodes.description: Institution where a version of Csound for the Macintosh platform was developed in the 1990s.

nodes.label: Analog Devices Inc.
nodes.description: Commercial company that incorporated extended Csound (a closed-source DSP hardware version) into a project to supply simple synthesizers for embedded applications.

nodes.label: Csound 5
nodes.description: A major re-engineered version of Csound launched in 2006, featuring a plug-in mechanism, programmable GUIs, user-defined unit generators, and an Application Programming Interface (API) for lower-level system control.

nodes.label: Csound 6
nodes.description: Major version of Csound released in 2013 with reorganized code, new language parser, on-the-fly compilation mode, and redesigned API for increased developer flexibility.

nodes.label: Control/Audio Rate Mechanism
nodes.description: A design principle introduced in MUSIC 11 that divides computation into control (k-) and audio (a-) rates, allowing signals that vary slowly (like envelopes) to be computed less frequently than audio signals, improving computational efficiency.

nodes.label: Cmix
nodes.description: A music programming system developed in the 1980s using the C language, alongside Csound and other similar systems.

nodes.label: UNIX Operating System
nodes.description: Operating system whose introduction in the 1970s contributed to the widespread use of MUSIC 11 at various institutions.

nodes.label: MUSIC 4C
nodes.description: Classic music programming system noted in the history of computer music languages.

nodes.label: MIT
nodes.description: Massachusetts Institute of Technology, home to the Studio for Experimental Music where Barry Vercoe developed early computer music languages.

nodes.label: MIT-EMS Csound
nodes.description: Early version of Csound developed at MIT, whose code remains compatible with modern Csound versions.

nodes.label: CSD file format
nodes.description: A unified file format for Csound that combines orchestra and score in a single file, replacing separate .orc and .sco files.

nodes.label: WinXsound
nodes.description: A GUI program with text-editing facilities built on top of the CLI csound frontend.

nodes.label: Pure Data
nodes.description: A visual programming language for audio and multimedia processing, referenced as a source for exporting array data to text files for use in Csound.

nodes.label: Quantisation
nodes.description: The process of representing continuous amplitude values in a finite grid of discrete values, introducing quantisation errors and noise dependent on bit depth precision.

nodes.label: Digital-to-Analogue Converter
nodes.description: Hardware device that converts digital audio signals back to continuous analog form for playback through speakers or audio equipment.

nodes.label: Bit Depth
nodes.description: The number of binary digits used to store amplitude values in digital audio; 16-bit allows 65535 different amplitude values and is standard for high-quality audio.

nodes.label: Floating-point Audio Representation
nodes.description: Internal representation of audio samples using floating-point numbers; Csound typically uses 64-bit double precision internally, though 32-bit single precision is used on some platforms.

nodes.label: Zipper Noise
nodes.description: An audible artefact caused by aliasing in audio signals when control-rate envelopes step at insufficient sampling rates, creating a staircase-like stepping effect.

nodes.label: Control Rate (kr)
nodes.description: The rate at which control variables are recalculated in Csound, determined by the formula kr = sr/ksmps. Historically abbreviated as 'kr' instead of 'cr' because early Csound used 'c' for comments.

nodes.label: Sampling Rate (sr)
nodes.description: The frequency at which samples are taken from an analog signal; must be at least twice the highest frequency component to avoid foldover distortion.

nodes.label: nchnls (Number of Channels)
nodes.description: A Csound system parameter that sets the number of input and output audio channels, with separate nchnls_i for input-only configuration.

nodes.label: Csound Orchestra Code
nodes.description: The instrument definition file in Csound that contains instrument definitions (instr) and function tables (ftable), compiled and loaded before performance.

nodes.label: K-cycle
nodes.description: Control-rate processing cycle in Csound where all active instrument instances perform once, with execution order determined by instrument number and scheduling.

nodes.label: Function Tables
nodes.description: Blocks of computer memory in Csound that store pre-calculated mathematical expression results, used for table-lookup oscillators and other applications since early computer music.

nodes.label: GEN Routines
nodes.description: Csound function table generators for creating waveforms, including sine/cosine generators, line/exponential segment generators, file access, window functions, random functions, and waveshaping routines.

nodes.label: Unit Generators
nodes.description: Csound opcodes that perform audio processing operations, executed in sequence within instrument instances during the performance loop.

nodes.label: Csound Opcodes
nodes.description: Built-in operations and functions in Csound for audio synthesis, processing, and control, including FM synthesis, granular synthesis, filtering, and MIDI operations.

nodes.label: MIDI NOTEON
nodes.description: A MIDI command that can trigger undefined-duration instrument instances in Csound, with corresponding NOTEOFF commands triggering turnoff.

nodes.label: Global Code
nodes.description: Code in Csound that exists outside instruments and executes only once at init-time after compilation, used for one-off computations and event scheduling.

nodes.label: Interpolation
nodes.description: In phase vocoder resynthesis, the pvoc opcode interpolates values between analysis frames when the time-pointer does not align with integer frame numbers.

nodes.label: Wavetables
nodes.description: Function tables in Csound holding one or more cycles of a waveform, typically used as sources for oscillators.

nodes.label: Audio Buffers
nodes.description: Software devices in Csound that store computation results before sending them to their destination, enabling efficient block-based data transfer.

nodes.label: Spin Buffer
nodes.description: The input buffer in Csound's innermost IO layer that holds the most current audio input block and is accessed by input unit generators.

nodes.label: Spout Buffer
nodes.description: The output buffer in Csound's innermost IO layer that accumulates output blocks from all active instruments.

nodes.label: PortAudio
nodes.description: A cross-platform third-party library used by Csound to provide standard real-time audio input/output across major desktop platforms.

nodes.label: Jack IO
nodes.description: A real-time audio input/output kit supported by Csound plug-ins on Linux and OSX platforms.

nodes.label: ADC/DAC
nodes.description: Analog-to-digital and digital-to-analog converters in computers and sound cards that handle signal conversion with built-in anti-aliasing filters.

nodes.label: Jack
nodes.description: The Jack connection kit MIDI implementation that works similarly to its audio counterpart and is particularly useful for inter-application MIDI IO.

nodes.label: ALSA
nodes.description: The low-level audio system on the Linux platform providing good latency performance, used as a Csound backend.

nodes.label: AuHAL
nodes.description: A Csound module providing direct connection to OSX's CoreAudio system with callback-based circular buffering.

nodes.label: libsndfile
nodes.description: A third-party library used by Csound for soundfile I/O, supporting uncompressed and compressed audio formats.

nodes.label: Latency
nodes.description: The time delay from audio input to output or from control input to audio effect, critical for real-time music performance.

nodes.label: Buffer Size
nodes.description: A parameter controlling the number of sample frames processed at once, directly affecting latency and system stability in real-time audio.

nodes.label: Drop-outs
nodes.description: Audio artifacts (clicks) caused when the system cannot produce audio in time to fill the output buffer, resulting from insufficient computing capacity or buffers that are too small.

nodes.label: Offline Audio
nodes.description: Audio computation mode without real-time constraints, used for post-processing and fixed-media composition.

nodes.label: Real-time Audio
nodes.description: Csound's capability to receive score events from external sources in real-time via API, stdin, files, or piped program output.

nodes.label: Pure Data (PD)
nodes.description: A visual programming environment that can load multiple instances of Csound-based plug-ins through the Csound API.

nodes.label: GEN routines
nodes.description: Csound function table generation routines that can be extended via the API.

nodes.label: Csound software bus
nodes.description: A channel-based system in Csound for passing control and audio data between the host application and running instruments, accessed via SetChannel() and GetChannel() methods.

nodes.label: Csound debugger
nodes.description: An experimental debugging mode in the Csound library accessible via the API, supporting breakpoints, stepping, and variable inspection.

nodes.label: CSD file
nodes.description: Csound document format containing instrument definitions in the <CsInstruments> section, numeric scores, and options for system configuration.

nodes.label: GEN routine
nodes.description: Csound subroutines that generate or read data into f-tables, including GEN01 (sound file reading), GEN05, GEN07, and GEN17 with specific parameter constraints.

nodes.label: Csound frontend
nodes.description: User interface applications that host the Csound library, including the basic csound command-line frontend and various IDE implementations.

nodes.label: Audio IO plugin
nodes.description: Backend modules in Csound that handle real-time and offline audio input/output operations and soundfile management.

nodes.label: Instrument instance
nodes.description: A running instantiation of a Csound instrument that progresses through compilation, instantiation, performance, and destruction phases during an event.

nodes.label: print opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode that outputs variable names and their values to the console, used for debugging and displaying computation results.

nodes.label: Csound orchestra preprocessor
nodes.description: A preprocessing system in Csound that allows text modifications before compilation, including include, define, and conditional statements.

nodes.label: Turing-complete language
nodes.description: A property of Csound indicating it has computational capabilities sufficient to solve any computable problem, despite being domain-specific for music.

nodes.label: Audio Rate (sr)
nodes.description: In Csound, the sampling rate at which audio signals are processed, as opposed to control-rate (k-rate) or initialization-rate (i-rate) operations.

nodes.label: Init-pass (Initialization Pass)
nodes.description: The first execution stage in Csound where initialization-time statements and i-time variables are computed before performance begins.

nodes.label: Performance-time
nodes.description: The execution stage in Csound where audio is generated and processed at k-rate or a-rate during the duration of a note event.

nodes.label: Init-time Variable (i-var)
nodes.description: A Csound data type that stores results of init-time computation, identified by variable names starting with lowercase 'i'.

nodes.label: Control-rate Variable (k-var)
nodes.description: A Csound data type updated at every k-cycle during performance time, identified by variable names starting with lowercase 'k'.

nodes.label: Audio-rate Variable (a-var)
nodes.description: A Csound data type that operates at audio sample rate, identified by variable names starting with lowercase 'a'.

nodes.label: Parameter Variable (p-var)
nodes.description: A special i-time variable type in Csound used to access instrument parameter values, where p1 is instrument number, p2 is start time, p3 is duration, and pN accesses additional parameters.

nodes.label: printk opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that runs at performance time, printing a value at regular intervals specified by its first argument (0 prints every k-period).

nodes.label: date opcode
nodes.description: A Csound i-time-only opcode that returns the time in seconds since the Unix Epoch (January 1, 1970).

nodes.label: init operator
nodes.description: A Csound operator that initializes control-rate variables at init-time with a specified value.

nodes.label: Global Space
nodes.description: The area in a Csound orchestra outside any instrument definition where global parameters, functions, tables, and i-rate expressions can be defined.

nodes.label: Initialization Time (i-time)
nodes.description: The execution stage in Csound where variables are initialized and expressions are calculated once at instrument initialization.

nodes.label: Control Rate (k-time)
nodes.description: In Csound, the control cycle executed repeatedly during note performance where k-rate variables and k-time conditionals are evaluated.

nodes.label: Audio Rate (a-time)
nodes.description: The execution stage in Csound where audio-rate variables are updated at sr samples per second, containing vectors of ksmps samples per k-period.

nodes.label: k() Converter
nodes.description: A Csound converter that forces k-time behavior and downsamples signals from sr to kr samples per second.

nodes.label: a() Converter
nodes.description: A Csound converter that interpolates k-rate values to create smooth lines in audio-rate vectors, upsampling from kr to sr samples per second.

nodes.label: rnd() Function
nodes.description: A Csound random number generator function that produces random values, with behavior dependent on execution rate.

nodes.label: interp Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that converts k-rate variables to a-rate and interpolates values between k-cycles for smoother control.

nodes.label: upsamp Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that assigns k-rate values directly to a-rate variables in a more efficient manner than direct assignment.

nodes.label: init Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode used to initialize variables to zero or explicit values at the start of an instrument instance.

nodes.label: Global Variables
nodes.description: Variables in Csound that exist outside instruments and can be accessed by the whole program, prefixed with 'g' and used as patch-cords or busses to connect signals between instruments.

nodes.label: Sine wave synthesis
nodes.description: A fundamental synthesis technique using trigonometric functions like sin() to generate sinusoidal waveforms from ramp inputs scaled to radians.

nodes.label: Polymorphic opcode
nodes.description: An opcode in Csound that can have different implementations depending on its output or input types, such as k-rate or a-rate operations.

nodes.label: Audio I/O subsystem
nodes.description: Csound's system for handling audio input and output across multiple channels using opcodes like in, inch, out, and outch.

nodes.label: oscil opcode
nodes.description: A Csound oscillator opcode used for generating audio signals; has interpolating variant (oscili) and supports different rate variables (a-rate, k-rate) for performance optimization.

nodes.label: oscil3 opcode
nodes.description: A Csound oscillator opcode that performs cubic interpolation using four surrounding table positions for the highest audio quality among basic oscillators.

nodes.label: phasor opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates normalized indices running from 0 to 1 at a specified rate, used to access table values and control waveform frequency by determining the size of jumps in a table.

nodes.label: table opcode
nodes.description: A Csound table reader opcode that produces output given an index and table number, with variants for non-interpolating, linear, and cubic interpolation.

nodes.label: tablew opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcodes for writing values to existing function tables during performance at k-rate or a-rate (tablew) or i-rate (tableiw).

nodes.label: GEN 2
nodes.description: A Csound GEN routine that copies its arguments directly to respective table positions.

nodes.label: GEN 5
nodes.description: A Csound GEN routine that creates exponential curves in function tables.

nodes.label: Table normalization
nodes.description: A Csound feature controlled by the sign of the GEN parameter that rescales created values to 0-1 range for non-negative functions or -1 to 1 for bipolar ones.

nodes.label: diskin opcode
nodes.description: A Csound soundfile reader opcode that can read multi-channel audio files, resample to match Csound's sample rate, and support varispeed playback with pitch control.

nodes.label: soundin opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that plays back sampled sounds from pre-existing sound files without processing possibilities, supporting mono, stereo, and quad output.

nodes.label: line opcode
nodes.description: A Csound unit generator that produces a succession of values over a specified duration, used to create time-pointers for phase vocoder resynthesis.

nodes.label: expon opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that produces envelope segments with concave exponential shapes rather than linear shapes, reflecting the logarithmic nature of amplitude and frequency perception.

nodes.label: transeg opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that allows specification of segment curvature in envelopes, with curvature behavior dependent on whether segments are rising or falling.

nodes.label: cpspch function
nodes.description: A Csound pitch converter function that transforms pch (octave point pitch class) notation to frequency in cycles per second (Hz).

nodes.label: cpsoct function
nodes.description: A Csound pitch converter function that transforms oct (octave point decimal) notation to frequency in cycles per second (Hz).

nodes.label: cpsmidinn function
nodes.description: A Csound pitch converter function that transforms MIDI note numbers to frequency in cycles per second (Hz).

nodes.label: ampdbfs function
nodes.description: A Csound amplitude converter function that transforms decibel (dB) scale values to amplitude, scaled by 0dbfs.

nodes.label: random opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates random values within user-defined minimum and maximum limits at i-time, k-rate, or a-rate according to uniform random distribution.

nodes.label: linrand opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that delivers values from a linear distribution where small values are more likely, useful for adding non-regular durations to notes.

nodes.label: trirand opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that provides triangular distribution centered on zero, with values ranging to ±krange.

nodes.label: exprand opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates values from an exponential distribution, describing time between independently occurring events at a fixed average rate.

nodes.label: bexprand opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode providing a symmetric version of the exponential distribution centered about zero.

nodes.label: poisson opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that returns an integer value representing the number of events occurring within a fixed time-window using Poisson distribution.

nodes.label: weibull opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode providing a variable distribution with two parameters controlling spread and shape of the distribution curve.

nodes.label: betarand opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates values from a beta distribution with two parameters governing behavior at zero and one, producing bell-curve-like shapes.

nodes.label: urandom opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that provides uniformly distributed random values using host computer activity to inject additional randomness beyond pseudo-random generation.

nodes.label: seed opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that sets the starting point for pseudorandom number generation; seed(0) uses system clock, positive integers produce reproducible sequences.

nodes.label: getseed opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that retrieves the current state of the pseudo-random number generator.

nodes.label: Csound Strings
nodes.description: Ordered sets of characters in Csound used for specifying file paths, channel names, and printing messages, stored in S-type variables.

nodes.label: Spectral-Domain Signals
nodes.description: Streaming analysis of audio signals in Csound using f-sig and w-sig variable types for spectral audio manipulation and analysis.

nodes.label: sprintf opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for formatting and conversion of strings using template strings with variable substitution.

nodes.label: prints opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that prints formatted strings to the console, supporting format specifiers like %d, %f, and %s.

nodes.label: f-sig (frequency-domain signal)
nodes.description: A Csound data type that holds time-ordered frames of spectral data generated by spectral analysis opcodes, enabling frequency-domain audio processing and resynthesis.

nodes.label: PVS_AMP_FREQ
nodes.description: A Csound f-sig subtype that carries frames of amplitude and frequency pairs in equally-spaced frequency bins, used for phase vocoder signals and the most commonly used f-sig format.

nodes.label: PVS_AMP_PHASE
nodes.description: A Csound f-sig subtype that carries frames of amplitude and phase pairs, providing polar representation of spectral data.

nodes.label: PVS_COMPLEX
nodes.description: A Csound f-sig subtype that carries frames of real-imaginary (complex) pairs, providing rectangular representation of spectral data.

nodes.label: PVS_TRACKS
nodes.description: A Csound f-sig subtype that carries partial track data with amplitude, frequency, phase information and track IDs, ordered by creation time and frequency.

nodes.label: pvsadsyn opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that resynthesizes audio from amplitude-frequency f-sig data using additive synthesis methods with frequency scaling control.

nodes.label: pvshift opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that processes frequency-domain signals by shifting spectral components, enabling frequency shifting of individual analysis bins.

nodes.label: w-sig (constant-Q signal)
nodes.description: A non-standard Csound frequency-domain data type that carries constant-Q, exponentially-spaced frequency data obtained via the spectrum opcode, used for analysis and visualization.

nodes.label: spectrum opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates w-sig constant-Q frequency-domain data for pitch detection, onset detection, and spectral visualization.

nodes.label: Csound Arrays
nodes.description: Data structures in Csound that can hold collections of values at i-rate, k-rate, or audio-rate, supporting numeric and string types with implicit generation from opcode outputs.

nodes.label: Arrays in Csound
nodes.description: Ordered, homogenous data structures in Csound that support i-time and k-rate indexing, arithmetic expressions, and audio signal handling for multichannel processing.

nodes.label: Audio Arrays
nodes.description: Arrays of audio-rate signals (a-type) used to handle stereo, multichannel signals, and multiple signal sources that can be mixed or further processed.

nodes.label: Spectral-Domain Signals
nodes.description: Frequency-domain representations of audio signals in Csound that provide new kinds of processing methods.

nodes.label: String Arrays
nodes.description: Arrays of strings in Csound that allow indexing at initialization and performance time, enabling dynamic string access.

nodes.label: User-Defined Opcodes
nodes.description: Custom opcodes created by Csound users that encapsulate signal processing logic and follow the same initialization and performance rules as built-in opcodes.

nodes.label: Control Flow Constructs
nodes.description: Language features in Csound including conditional branching, loops, and scheduling that enable high-level programmability.

nodes.label: Vector and Matrix Operations
nodes.description: Operations such as windowing and Fourier transforms that can be performed on arrays in Csound for sound and music computing applications.

nodes.label: Branching
nodes.description: Flow control mechanism in Csound that allows conditional jumps to labeled code sections based on Boolean expressions evaluated at initialization or performance time.

nodes.label: Boolean Expressions
nodes.description: Conditional statements in Csound using comparison operators (==, !=, <, >, <=, >=) and logical operators (&&, ||) that yield true or false results.

nodes.label: Initialization Time (i-time)
nodes.description: The execution stage in Csound where instrument variables are initialized before performance begins, executed once per note event.

nodes.label: igoto
nodes.description: Csound branching statement that performs unconditional or conditional jumps at initialization time only.

nodes.label: goto
nodes.description: Csound branching statement that performs jumps at both initialization and performance time, requiring init-time-only Boolean expressions.

nodes.label: kgoto
nodes.description: Csound branching statement that performs conditional or unconditional jumps at performance time only, allowing k-rate conditions.

nodes.label: timout
nodes.description: Csound opcode that performs time-based branching by jumping to a label when instrument time reaches a specified start time for a specified duration.

nodes.label: timeinsts
nodes.description: Csound opcode that returns the elapsed time of an instrument instance, useful for time-based conditional branching.

nodes.label: Labels
nodes.description: Named markers in Csound code that serve as jump destinations for branching statements, composed of characters and numerals followed by a colon.

nodes.label: pluck
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that implements plucked string synthesis using the Karplus-Strong algorithm.

nodes.label: expseg
nodes.description: A Csound opcode used to control amplitude and frequency arguments in additive synthesis through exponential segment approximation.

nodes.label: linrand
nodes.description: Csound opcode that generates random numbers with linear distribution.

nodes.label: vaset opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that sets individual sample values in an audio-rate vector at a specified index.

nodes.label: event opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcodes that enable triggering of any instrument from a MIDI-triggered instrument, supporting fractional instrument numbers for distinguishing instances.

nodes.label: schedkwhen opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that simplifies triggering subinstruments with parameters for minimum time between calls and maximum simultaneous instances.

nodes.label: expon opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode for generating exponential ramps at k-rate, used for time-varying control with different slope characteristics than linear ramps.

nodes.label: cpspch opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode that converts pitch class notation (octave.pitchclass) to frequency in Hz.

nodes.label: fillarray opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that initializes an array with specified values.

nodes.label: lenarray opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that returns the length (number of elements) of an array.

nodes.label: Recursion in Csound
nodes.description: Programming technique in Csound where instruments call themselves with decremented counters as base cases, used for creating chains of events.

nodes.label: moogladder opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing a Moog-style ladder lowpass filter with resonance control, commonly used in subtractive synthesis.

nodes.label: MIDI NOTE ON/OFF
nodes.description: MIDI channel messages that instantiate instruments with indeterminate duration, controlled by note number and velocity parameters.

nodes.label: Release-time envelope generators
nodes.description: Csound opcodes with release segments (marked with 'r' suffix like expsegr, linsegr) that extend instrument duration and hold values until deactivation.

nodes.label: Tied notes mechanism
nodes.description: A Csound feature allowing one instrument instance to replace an indefinite-duration one while maintaining phase continuity and avoiding abrupt waveform changes.

nodes.label: tival opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode that detects whether the current note is a tied note, enabling conditional behavior for held and tied notes in legato instruments.

nodes.label: tigoto opcode
nodes.description: Csound conditional instruction equivalent to 'on a tied note, igoto', used during initialization to bypass re-initialization of unit generators on tied notes.

nodes.label: Reinitialisation
nodes.description: A Csound mechanism that repeats the initialization pass of an instrument during performance, controlled by the reinit opcode.

nodes.label: reinit opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that triggers reinitialization of a code block from a specified label, enabling dynamic parameter recalculation during performance.

nodes.label: timout opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that forces a branch to a target label for a specified duration, commonly used with reinit to generate periodic retriggering of events.

nodes.label: Fractional instrument numbers
nodes.description: A Csound naming convention using decimal notation (e.g., 1.1, 1.2, 1.3) to assign unique identifiers to multiple instances of the same instrument.

nodes.label: Signal Graph
nodes.description: A representation of a Csound instrument as a directed graph where nodes are unit generators and edges are variables connecting them, conceptually analogous to patch-cords.

nodes.label: Patch-cord
nodes.description: A metaphorical representation of variables in Csound that connect unit generators together in a signal graph, inspired by analog synthesizer design.

nodes.label: compilestr opcode
nodes.description: An init-time Csound opcode that compiles new instrument code provided as a string argument, enabling dynamic instrument addition to a running performance.

nodes.label: compileorc opcode
nodes.description: An init-time Csound opcode that compiles new instrument code from a plain text file, allowing dynamic instrument addition to a running performance.

nodes.label: rigoto opcode
nodes.description: A special goto jump in Csound that is active only at reinit time, allowing conditional branching during reinitialization.

nodes.label: perf-time (performance time)
nodes.description: The performance phase in Csound when unit generators execute their perf-time routines during audio processing.

nodes.label: Feedback Amplitude Modulation (FBAM)
nodes.description: A signal processing technique where an oscillator's output is fed back into its own amplitude input, creating a feedback path with one-ksmps block delay.

nodes.label: modmatrix Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that uses function tables to create complex routings of modulation signals with input parameters, modulation signals, and scaling values.

nodes.label: reverb Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound unit generator that applies reverberation to an audio signal based on a specified reverberation time parameter.

nodes.label: comb Opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode for comb filter echo effect, implemented as a global effect in instr 198.

nodes.label: Patch-cord Metaphor
nodes.description: Conceptual model for signal routing in Csound where busses act as global patch-cords connecting different instrument instances.

nodes.label: chnset opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode that writes values to a software bus channel for communication with the host application.

nodes.label: chnget opcode
nodes.description: A Csound software bus opcode that reads data sent from a host Csound API application on a named channel and assigns it to an output variable.

nodes.label: chnmix opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that sums audio into a named channel rather than overwriting it.

nodes.label: chnclear opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that clears audio data from a named channel after consumption.

nodes.label: chnexport opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that links a software bus channel to a global variable for direct access.

nodes.label: User-Defined Opcode (UDO)
nodes.description: A Csound feature allowing custom opcode creation, including recursive UDOs for elegant implementation of individually controlled partials in additive synthesis.

nodes.label: xin opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode used to access input arguments passed to user-defined opcodes.

nodes.label: xout opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode used to output values from user-defined opcodes.

nodes.label: tablei opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that accesses a stored function table with direct phase control, used for implementing phase modulation by reading a sine wave table.

nodes.label: linsegr opcode
nodes.description: A Csound envelope opcode that senses note release and executes a final envelope segment, used for MIDI-activated notes and score notes with indefinite duration.

nodes.label: Signal Path
nodes.description: The routing of audio signals through unit generators in Csound, which can include feedback links and non-standard connections.

nodes.label: Global Variable
nodes.description: Variables in Csound that can be used as busses to connect instruments, allowing signals to be fed from multiple sources to multiple destinations.

nodes.label: Subinstrument
nodes.description: A Csound mechanism that allows instruments to call other instruments directly as if they were opcodes, with limited i-time argument passing.

nodes.label: User-Defined Opcodes (UDOs)
nodes.description: Custom opcodes in Csound that allow users to define reusable audio processing units with local variables, shared state access, and support for recursion.

nodes.label: setksmps opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that allows setting a local ksmps value within a single instrument, enabling sample-by-sample control rate processing.

nodes.label: Leaky integration
nodes.description: A signal processing technique where the current sample is the sum of the current input and the previous output scaled by a factor close to 1, requiring sample-by-sample processing.

nodes.label: Recursion in Csound
nodes.description: A programming technique in Csound UDOs that allows an opcode to instantiate itself multiple times, enabling dynamic spawning of processes and unit generators.

nodes.label: filelen opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that returns the duration of a soundfile in seconds.

nodes.label: p-variables (parameters)
nodes.description: Csound event parameters (p1, p2, p3, etc.) that are accessible and modifiable by UDOs, including event duration (p3).

nodes.label: Recursive UDO
nodes.description: A UDO that calls itself recursively to implement higher-order filters or parallel filter banks in Csound.

nodes.label: butterbp opcode
nodes.description: A Csound bandpass filter opcode used to separate high, middle, and low frequency components for frequency-dependent stereo imaging in the Leslie speaker simulation.

nodes.label: Csound Score System
nodes.description: A text-based notation system in Csound for defining note events with p-fields (instrument, start time, duration, and parameters), supporting shortcuts and tempo manipulation.

nodes.label: i-statement
nodes.description: Csound score statement that schedules instrument instances with parameters p1 (instrument number/name), p2 (start time), p3 (duration), and p4+ (extra parameters).

nodes.label: f-statement
nodes.description: Csound score statement used to create function tables with GEN routines, specified by table number, creation time, size, GEN code, and parameters.

nodes.label: q-statement
nodes.description: Csound score statement that mutes or unmutes instruments at specified action times before events start.

nodes.label: s-statement
nodes.description: Csound score statement that marks the end of a section and optionally extends it with a pause before the next section.

nodes.label: e-statement
nodes.description: Csound score statement that terminates the final section of a score and causes Csound to exit unless an f 0 statement has been used.

nodes.label: t-statement
nodes.description: Csound score statement that controls tempo processing for a section, allowing fixed tempi, accelerandos, and ritardandos specified in beats per minute.

nodes.label: v-statement
nodes.description: Csound score statement that applies a local time warp factor to subsequent i-statements, multiplying their start times and durations.

nodes.label: x-statement
nodes.description: Csound score statement that skips subsequent statements in a section and moves reading to the next section.

nodes.label: Carry
nodes.description: Csound score preprocessing operation that reduces repetitive typing by carrying values from previous lines in consecutive i-statements, using symbols like dot (.), plus (+), caret operators (^+, ^-), and exclamation (!).

nodes.label: Tempo Processing
nodes.description: Csound score preprocessing feature that allows independent tempo settings per section with time-varying tempi, enabling accelerandos and ritardandos.

nodes.label: Sort
nodes.description: Csound score preprocessing operation that orders i-statements and f-statements by p2 (start time), then p1 (instrument), then p3 (duration), with f-statements taking precedence at equal times.

nodes.label: Next-p and Previous-p
nodes.description: Csound score shorthand symbols (npN and ppN) that copy p-field values from subsequent or previous i-statements, interpreted after carry, tempo, and sort operations.

nodes.label: GEN Routine
nodes.description: Csound function table generation routine specified by code in f-statements, with parameters controlling table content, rescaling, and size.

nodes.label: Beats
nodes.description: Arbitrary time units in Csound scores that are translated to seconds during tempo processing, defaulting to 1 second per beat.

nodes.label: P-field Ramping
nodes.description: A score preprocessing feature that allows parameter values to ramp linearly (using <) or exponentially (using ( or )) between an origin and target value.

nodes.label: P-field Expressions
nodes.description: A preprocessing mode using square brackets that evaluates arithmetic expressions and bitwise logical operators in p-fields, supporting operators like +, -, *, /, ^, %, &, |, and #.

nodes.label: Csound Score Macros
nodes.description: A code reuse mechanism in Csound that allows definition of reusable text blocks in both orchestra and score sections, supporting parameterization and nesting.

nodes.label: Csound Score Loops
nodes.description: A non-sectional loop structure using curly braces that repeats score statements with iteration numbers, supporting nesting up to 39 levels.

nodes.label: Csound Extract Feature
nodes.description: A performance control feature that allows selection of specific instruments and time ranges from a score using an extract file with i, f, and t commands.

nodes.label: scoreline Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound unit generator that accepts strings with i- and f-statements at performance time to issue real-time score events.

nodes.label: scoreline_i Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that allows definition of score fragments for any number of instruments directly in the orchestra, enabling generative event control.

nodes.label: readscore Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound unit generator that works at i-time and allows preprocessing of carry, next-p, previous-p, ramping, expressions and loops in score statements.

nodes.label: rewindscore Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound init-time opcode that rewinds the loaded score to the beginning.

nodes.label: setscorepos Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound init-time opcode that provides general transport control of the score, allowing movement forwards or backwards from the current position in seconds.

nodes.label: Python
nodes.description: A scripting language that can be used as an external score generator in Csound to create numeric scores programmatically.

nodes.label: CSD File Format
nodes.description: Csound's unified file format containing orchestra code, score, and options sections, supporting external score generation via the bin attribute.

nodes.label: cpsmidib Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that translates MIDI note number into Hz while incorporating pitch-bend data.

nodes.label: ampmidi Opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode for receiving and scaling MIDI velocity data, used to map key velocity to number of synthesized partials for brightness control.

nodes.label: midictrl Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that accesses control change data from a specific MIDI channel for parameter modulation.

nodes.label: massign Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that maps MIDI channels to specific instruments, allowing explicit control over default MIDI channel-to-instrument routing.

nodes.label: pgmassign Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that links MIDI program numbers with specific instruments.

nodes.label: midiin Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that reads raw incoming MIDI data including all message types and system exclusive messages.

nodes.label: linenr Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates linear envelopes with attack, sustain, and release times independent of note duration.

nodes.label: maxalloc Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that limits the number of simultaneous instances allocated for a given instrument.

nodes.label: active Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that reports the number of currently active instances of an instrument.

nodes.label: CNMAT
nodes.description: Center for New Music and Audio Technologies where the OSC (Open Sound Control) protocol was developed.
aliases: Center for New Music and Audio Technologies

nodes.label: PortMidi
nodes.description: A cross-platform MIDI library that works with host OS implementations and serves as the default MIDI backend for Csound.

nodes.label: CoreMIDI
nodes.description: Apple's MIDI framework that allows Csound iOS applications to receive MIDI events directly from connected devices.

nodes.label: ALSA raw MIDI
nodes.description: The basic Linux MIDI implementation accessible in Csound using the -+rtmidi=alsa option.

nodes.label: ALSA sequencer
nodes.description: A higher-level MIDI implementation for Linux, accessed using -+rtmidi=alsaseq in Csound.

nodes.label: midion opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that simplifies MIDI note output by automatically handling note-on and note-off messages based on instrument duration.

nodes.label: metro opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates metronome-like triggers at specified frequencies, used to control note density in algorithmic composition.

nodes.label: OSCsend opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that sends Open Sound Control messages to a specified host, port, and address with typed data arguments.

nodes.label: OSClisten opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that receives Open Sound Control messages on a specified port and address, outputting 1 when a new message arrives.

nodes.label: OSCinit opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that initializes OSC communication on a specified port for receiving control data from external devices.

nodes.label: Processing
nodes.description: A Java-based programming language for visual arts with a visual engine that can interact with Csound's audio engine via OSC.

nodes.label: INScore
nodes.description: An application developed at GRAME capable of receiving OSC messages to create, modify, and remove graphical representations in real-time.

nodes.label: SWIG
nodes.description: Simplified Wrapper and Interface Generator tool used to generate the original csnd6.py Python API wrapper from Csound's C API.

nodes.label: netcat (nc)
nodes.description: Command-line utility used to send UDP messages to Csound's UDP server for dynamic code compilation.

nodes.label: Csound UDP Server
nodes.description: Built-in server feature that listens to UDP connections containing Csound code text for dynamic compilation and execution, enabled via --port option.

nodes.label: csnd6 module
nodes.description: Python module consisting of csnd6.py wrapper code and csnd6.so binary library for accessing Csound functionality from Python.

nodes.label: IPython
nodes.description: Specialized Python shell with Notebook interface that can be used to run Csound scripts interactively.

nodes.label: Real-time audio output
nodes.description: Csound performance mode that outputs directly to the digital-to-analogue converter (DAC) using the -odac flag, as opposed to file rendering.

nodes.label: InputMessage()
nodes.description: A Csound API method that dispatches real-time events in standard score format to trigger instruments dynamically during performance.

nodes.label: Csound score format
nodes.description: The standard event notation used by Csound to schedule instrument instances, with parameters like p2 (start time) and p3 (duration).

nodes.label: CsoundMYFLTArray
nodes.description: A utility class in the csnd6 package that handles audio data vectors of ksmps length for channel access and buffer manipulation.

nodes.label: Joseph Fourier
nodes.description: Mathematician who originally explored the idea that complex functions can be decomposed into sinusoidal partials.

nodes.label: Harmonic Spectrum
nodes.description: Frequency components generated by FM synthesis when the carrier-to-modulator ratio is a simple integer ratio, producing sidebands at integer multiples of the carrier and modulator frequencies.

nodes.label: Wavetable Oscillator
nodes.description: Basic sound source in Csound using table-lookup methods with various interpolation techniques.

nodes.label: GEN10
nodes.description: A Csound GEN routine that creates a waveform consisting of harmonically related partials by composing sinusoids and storing the result in a function table.

nodes.label: GEN9
nodes.description: Csound routine for creating tables with generic parameters including phase and relative frequencies.

nodes.label: GEN19
nodes.description: Csound routine for creating tables with generic parameters including phase and relative frequencies.

nodes.label: Spectral Representation
nodes.description: Method of representing sound by showing the components of a signal at a point in time, as opposed to waveform representation over time.

nodes.label: Partial
nodes.description: A simple sine function component in additive synthesis, defined by amplitude envelope and frequency envelope, which can be harmonic or nonharmonic.

nodes.label: GEN10
nodes.description: A GEN Routine in Csound that creates waveforms by adding sine waves with harmonic frequency relationships (1:2:3:4...), enabling synthesis of standard waveforms like sawtooth, square, and triangle.

nodes.label: GEN1
nodes.description: A Csound GEN routine that transfers data from prerecorded soundfiles into function-tables for processing by opcodes like loscil.

nodes.label: gbuzz
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that creates additive tones from harmonically related cosine waves with parameters for number of partials, lowest partial, and amplitude coefficient multiplier.

nodes.label: vco
nodes.description: A Csound voltage-controlled oscillator opcode that can generate sawtooth waves for use as excitation sources in vocoder synthesis.

nodes.label: loscil
nodes.description: An older Csound opcode for playing back audio from function tables with looping and sustain/release capabilities, originally designed as a sampler kernel.

nodes.label: flooper
nodes.description: A Csound opcode family for defining custom looping points with crossfading capabilities.

nodes.label: flooper2
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for playing back sound files loaded into function tables with looping, cross-fade, and pitch modulation capabilities.

nodes.label: rand
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates white noise using a pseudo-random sequence with optional seeding and 16-bit or 31-bit noise generator selection.

nodes.label: Bandlimited Oscillators
nodes.description: Synthesis technique that controls bandwidth to prevent aliasing by limiting harmonic content based on fundamental frequency.

nodes.label: Virtual Analogue Modelling
nodes.description: Synthesis technique that digitally emulates classic analog synthesizer waveforms and their characteristics.

nodes.label: Sampling
nodes.description: Sound synthesis method using recorded audio loaded into function tables for playback and manipulation.

nodes.label: Noise Generation
nodes.description: Synthesis technique for creating non-pitched sounds using pseudo-random number generators.

nodes.label: pinkish opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates approximations to pink noise with a 1/f spectral envelope, using a pseudo-random sequence with seeding options.

nodes.label: pinker opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing Stefan Wenzel's algorithm for pink noise generation with a normalized output and very close 1/f response without periodicity issues.

nodes.label: Stefan Wenzel
nodes.description: Algorithm designer whose pink noise generation method is implemented in the Csound pinker opcode.

nodes.label: Feedforward filter
nodes.description: A type of digital filter with no signal feedback path, typically using longer delays to achieve filtering effects through constructive and destructive interference.

nodes.label: Feedback filter
nodes.description: A type of digital filter that re-injects its output back into its input with a certain delay, typically using one or two sample delays and having non-linear phase response.

nodes.label: resonr opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode variant of the reson resonator filter with centre frequency and bandwidth controls.

nodes.label: resonz opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode variant of the reson resonator filter with centre frequency and bandwidth controls.

nodes.label: Convolution
nodes.description: A signal processing technique that applies the impulse response of a system (such as a room) to an arbitrary sound via an FIR filter, useful for reverberation and time-invariant filtering.

nodes.label: Minimoog Synthesizer
nodes.description: A classic analog electronic musical instrument based on source-modifier design with oscillators, noise generators, and a low-pass resonant filter controlled by envelope generators.

nodes.label: Channel Vocoder
nodes.description: A music instrument design originally developed by the telecommunications industry for speech encoding, which analyzes signal amplitude in separate spectrum bands and resynthesizes using matched synthesis channels.

nodes.label: balance Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that controls the amplitude level of one signal by comparing it to another, functioning as an envelope follower for vocoder band amplitude control.

nodes.label: portk Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound portamento opcode that smoothly transitions from one control signal value to another over a given time, functioning as a first-order low-pass filter on control signals.

nodes.label: xtratim Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that extends the duration of a note to allow the release stage of an envelope to complete on note-off.

nodes.label: lpf18 Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound low-pass filter opcode with resonance and distortion control, used in the TB303 emulation example.

nodes.label: eqfil Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing equalizer filters with band-pass/band-reject designs, featuring gain control in addition to centre frequency and bandwidth.

nodes.label: Bandlimited Pulse
