nodes.description: A distortion synthesis technique that generates a spectrum of harmonic components with equal weight using closed-form summation formulae.

nodes.label: plltrack opcode
nodes.description: A Csound pitch tracker using a phase-locked loop algorithm for real-time pitch detection, with a tendency to gliss at note onsets and offsets.

nodes.label: Hyperbolic Tangent Waveshaping
nodes.description: A waveshaping technique using the hyperbolic tangent function as a transfer function to generate nearly bandlimited square and sawtooth waves with smooth spectral transitions.

nodes.label: Generalized Summation Formulae
nodes.description: A distortion synthesis method using mathematical summation expressions to generate harmonic and inharmonic spectra with controllable spectral roll-off and bandwidth.

nodes.label: Polynomial Spectral Matching
nodes.description: A traditional method for finding transfer functions in waveshaping that uses polynomial functions to precisely produce bandlimited spectra for a given sinusoid.

nodes.label: Yamaha DX Series
nodes.description: A synthesizer series whose operator principle—combining an oscillator with phase modulation capability and ADSR envelope—is modeled in Csound UDOs for flexible PM synthesis.

nodes.label: Operator (FM/PM)
nodes.description: A fundamental building block combining an oscillator whose phase can be modulated with an ADSR envelope, allowing flexible arrangement in complex modulation topologies.

nodes.label: Madsr Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing a multiplying ADSR envelope generator, used in PMOp to control amplitude and timbre evolution.

nodes.label: Feedback Modulation
nodes.description: A complex PM topology where operator outputs feed back into their own phase inputs, requiring ksmps=1 in Csound for proper implementation.

nodes.label: Modified FM Synthesis (ModFM)
nodes.description: A variation of FM/PM synthesis using modified Bessel functions instead of regular Bessel functions, eliminating the characteristic 'wobble' of standard FM and producing more natural spectral evolution.

nodes.label: Csound UDO (User-Defined Opcode)
nodes.description: Csound 7 feature allowing custom opcode definitions with new syntax opcode name(inargs):(outargs) supporting pass-by-reference semantics.

nodes.label: Phase-synchronous synthesis
nodes.description: A technique used in ModFM formant synthesis where carrier and modulation signals share a single phase source for more accurate formant control.

nodes.label: Tonewheel Organ
nodes.description: An electronic organ design that synthesizes sound by summing outputs from rotating wheels that induce currents in pickups, pioneered by the Hammond company.

nodes.label: Hammond Company
nodes.description: The manufacturer that pioneered the tonewheel organ instrument design.

nodes.label: Envelope
nodes.description: Time-varying control signals that shape the amplitude and frequency trajectories of synthesis components.

nodes.label: Vibrato/Chorus Effect
nodes.description: A modulation effect using a short modulated delay line with triangular modulation at a fixed rate, used to enhance organ sounds.

nodes.label: Drawbar
nodes.description: A physical slider control on Hammond organs that adjusts the amplitude level of individual tonewheel components.

nodes.label: Pipe Organ
nodes.description: A traditional acoustic instrument that has used additive synthesis principles for centuries by combining different registrations.

nodes.label: pvsanal opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that performs streaming phase vocoder analysis on an input signal, producing frequency-domain output containing amplitudes and frequencies for each spectral band.

nodes.label: VChorus UDO
nodes.description: A user-defined opcode in Csound that implements delay-line-based vibrato and chorus effects using variable delay and oscillation.

nodes.label: OscBnk UDO
nodes.description: A recursive oscillator bank user-defined opcode in Csound that generates additive synthesis by combining multiple sinusoidal oscillators with pitch transposition control.

nodes.label: f-sig data type
nodes.description: A Csound data type used to represent frequency-domain analysis frames containing amplitude and frequency information for spectral processing.

nodes.label: pvsftw opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that returns a flag indicating whether new analysis data was written to frequency and amplitude tables in phase vocoder analysis.

nodes.label: diskin2 opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for reading audio from a soundfile with pitch transposition capability.

nodes.label: delay opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcodes for creating delay lines: delayr captures sound in a buffer, deltap reads from a specific point, and delayw writes the delayed signal.

nodes.label: delayr opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that reads from a delay buffer, used in conjunction with deltap/deltapi and delayw for multi-tap delay implementations.

nodes.label: delayw opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that writes audio into a delay buffer, used with delayr and deltap/deltapi for delay line implementations.

nodes.label: Time-domain processing
nodes.description: Audio signal processing techniques that act on the samples of a waveform to deliver effects such as echoes, reverberation, pitch shifting, and timbral modification.

nodes.label: Circular buffer
nodes.description: An efficient algorithm for implementing delay lines where samples are kept in place and the read/write position moves circularly through the buffer.

nodes.label: Oscillator bank
nodes.description: A collection of oscillators used in additive synthesis and resynthesis to reconstruct complex timbres from spectral data.

nodes.label: Feedback Delay
nodes.description: A signal processing technique that mixes the output of a delay line back into its input, scaled by a gain factor to prevent instability, creating repeated delays spaced regularly by the delay line length.

nodes.label: Schroeder Reverb
nodes.description: A classic reverb architecture using multiple comb filters in parallel whose outputs feed into a series of all-pass filters to simulate acoustic reflections in a space.

nodes.label: comb opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing the comb filter with parameters for reverberation time and delay, controlling feedback gain indirectly via equation 13.5.

nodes.label: alpass opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing the all-pass filter with the same parameters as the comb filter (reverberation time and delay time).

nodes.label: reverb opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing reverb effects using component reverberators based on comb and all-pass filters.

nodes.label: delayr opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for reading from a delay line, used in conjunction with delayw to implement feedback delay and all-pass filters.

nodes.label: delayw opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for writing to a delay line, used with delayr to create feedback delay and all-pass filter implementations.

nodes.label: Feedback Delay Network (FDN)
nodes.description: A reverb architecture using multiple delay lines cross-fed according to a feedback matrix to create complex reflections.

nodes.label: Reverb Effect
nodes.description: An audio effect that simulates acoustic reflections and reverberation using delay lines and filters.

nodes.label: hrtfreverb Opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode implementing binaural diffuse-field reverb based on FDN design for spatial audio effects.

nodes.label: deltap opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for reading taps from a delay line at fixed positions.

nodes.label: deltapi opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for reading delay line taps with linear interpolation.

nodes.label: deltap3 opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for cubic-interpolated variable delay tap reading used in time-domain effects.

nodes.label: deltapn opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for reading delay line taps with delay time specified in samples.

nodes.label: deltapx opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for reading delay line taps with user-defined higher-order interpolation up to 1,024 points.

nodes.label: dconv opcode
nodes.description: A fast internal Csound opcode for convolution-based reverb using spectral processing.

nodes.label: nreverb opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that implements reverberation with configurable reverb time and frequency.

nodes.label: Multitap Delay
nodes.description: A delay line with multiple taps or outputs at different positions along its length, providing smaller delay times to simulate reflections in a space.

nodes.label: Flanger
nodes.description: An audio effect originally produced by playing two tape copies at slightly different speeds, creating notches in the audio spectrum that sweep back and forth to produce a characteristic 'jet airplane' effect.

nodes.label: Hybrid Reverb
nodes.description: A reverb design combining convolution for early reflections with a standard algorithm or FDN for the diffuse tail.

nodes.label: Low-Frequency Oscillator (LFO)
nodes.description: A modulation source used to vary delay time in effects like flanger and vibrato, producing periodic waveforms such as sine, triangle, or sawtooth.

nodes.label: Chorus
nodes.description: An audio effect that creates asynchrony between an original signal and a delayed copy by modulating delay time with a noise generator or LFO, typically using delay times over 10 ms without feedback.

nodes.label: Frequency Modulation (FM)
nodes.description: A side-effect of varying delay time where pitch changes occur due to reading from delay memory at a different pace than writing, dependent on the derivative of delay modulation.

nodes.label: delayr
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for reading from a delay buffer, used to define buffer length and retrieve delayed audio.

nodes.label: delayw
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that writes audio samples to a delay line buffer.

nodes.label: randi
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for bandlimited noise generation used as a modulation source in chorus effects.

nodes.label: Triangle Waveform
nodes.description: A modulation waveform whose derivative is a square wave, causing pitch to jump between two fixed values when used for delay modulation.

nodes.label: Cosine Waveform
nodes.description: A modulation waveform whose derivative is a sine wave, causing pitch to glide continuously between maximum and minimum values in vibrato effects.

nodes.label: Pitch Modulation
nodes.description: A secondary effect in chorus where delay time variation causes slight period changes in pitch, dependent on both modulation amount and rate.

nodes.label: Chorus
nodes.description: Effect that makes one instrument sound like multiple instruments by adding the original signal to a frequency-modulated delayed signal, typically delayed 20-30 msec.

nodes.label: Doppler Shift
nodes.description: The perceived change in frequency of a waveform due to a moving sound source, modeled digitally using variable delay lines to simulate source movement toward or away from a listener.

nodes.label: Pitch Shifter
nodes.description: An audio effect that creates continuous pitch changes using two phase-offset sawtooth wave modulators controlling two taps of a delay line, with envelope windowing to hide discontinuities.

nodes.label: deltap3 opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for tapping a delay buffer with cubic interpolation, providing higher quality than deltapi.

nodes.label: GEN 20
nodes.description: A Csound function table generator that creates a triangle window, used for envelope windowing in pitch shifter effects.

nodes.label: LFO Modulation
nodes.description: A modulation source that oscillates at sub-audio rates, typically used to control parameters like delay time or amplitude to create time-varying effects.

nodes.label: Phase Shifter
nodes.description: An audio effect that combines a signal with a phase-modified version to create cancellation of certain frequencies, implemented using cascaded all-pass filters.

nodes.label: Harmoniser
nodes.description: A vocal/instrument effect that tracks fundamentals and creates pitch-shifted versions to generate harmonic content.

nodes.label: Filter Coefficient
nodes.description: Gain values (a1, a2, b1, b2) that determine the behavior of a digital filter in feedback and feedforward paths.

nodes.label: Regalia and Mitra
nodes.description: Designers of a well-known equaliser filter design used in Csound's eqfil opcode.

nodes.label: eqfil opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for equaliser filtering based on the Regalia and Mitra design, capable of boosting or cutting frequency bands.

nodes.label: rifft opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode for inverse fast Fourier transform, used to convert frequency domain specifications into impulse responses.

nodes.label: GEN7
nodes.description: A Csound GEN routine that draws line segments between specified points to create waveforms such as sawtooth and square waves.

nodes.label: Head-Related Transfer Functions
nodes.description: Filter frequency responses that model how the head and outer ears modify sounds, enabling precise spatial placement of audio via headphones through binaural processing.

nodes.label: Binaural Audio
nodes.description: Audio delivery directly to two ears using HRTFs and inter-aural time delays to create spatial localization cues for the listener.

nodes.label: hrtfmove / hrtfmove2
nodes.description: Csound unit generators designed to move sound sources smoothly in 3D binaural space using two different algorithms.

nodes.label: hrtfstat
nodes.description: Csound opcode for static 3D binaural source placement.

nodes.label: hrtfearly
nodes.description: Csound opcode providing high-fidelity early reflections for binaural reverb processing.

nodes.label: Ambisonics
nodes.description: A technique of three-dimensional sound projection that encodes spatial information of recorded or synthesized sound fields in multiple channels independent of loudspeaker arrangement.

nodes.label: Michael Gerzon
nodes.description: Developer of ambisonics for periphony (full-sphere 3D reproduction).

nodes.label: B-format
nodes.description: Standard ambisonics channel format consisting of omnidirectional (W) and directional (X, Y, Z) components that can be weighted and decoded for speaker arrays.

nodes.label: bformenc1
nodes.description: Csound opcode for encoding mono signals into first-, second-, and third-order ambisonics b-format.

nodes.label: bformdec1
nodes.description: Csound opcode for decoding ambisonics b-format signals for various loudspeaker configurations, including dual-band decoding and near-field compensation.

nodes.label: Brian Carty
nodes.description: Author of an example combining ambisonic to binaural decoding in Csound.

nodes.label: Multichannel Spatial Audio
nodes.description: Methods for encoding and decoding sound field information for multichannel audio composition and reproduction across multiple loudspeakers.

nodes.label: Inter-aural Time Delay
nodes.description: Time difference between sound arrival at each ear, used as a localization cue in binaural and ambisonic audio.

nodes.label: Inter-aural Intensity Difference
nodes.description: Amplitude difference between sounds at each ear, encoded in HRTFs to provide spatial localization cues.

nodes.label: Vector Base Amplitude Panning
nodes.description: A method for spatial audio panning that uses vector formulation to determine channel gains based on speaker directions and source position, extending simple stereo panning to multiple channel setups.

nodes.label: pan2 opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for managing stereo channels with optional mode parameter, providing practical stereo panning control.

nodes.label: vbap opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that distributes a monophonic sound source among speakers according to azimuth position, producing an audio array with signals for each speaker.

nodes.label: vbaplsinit opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that defines a loudspeaker layout for VBAP, specifying dimensions, number of speakers, and their directional locations in angles.

nodes.label: Sinusoidal Modelling
nodes.description: A spectral processing approach that models sound as a sum of time-varying sinusoidal tracks with variable amplitude, frequency, and phase, preserving phase information during resynthesis.

nodes.label: ATS
nodes.description: A spectral processing method for sinusoidal modelling implemented in Csound.

nodes.label: Magnitude Spectrum
nodes.description: The collection of all detected sinusoid amplitudes derived from spectral analysis, symmetric at zero frequency.

nodes.label: Phase Spectrum
nodes.description: The collection of phase values for detected sinusoids in spectral analysis, anti-symmetric at zero frequency.

nodes.label: Hanning Window
nodes.description: A window function created by an inverted cosine wave, offset and scaled to range between 0 and 1, used in DFT analysis to minimize spectral smearing by smoothing segment edges.

nodes.label: Inverse Discrete Fourier Transform (IDFT)
nodes.description: The inverse operation of the DFT that reconstructs a time-domain signal from its frequency-domain spectral representation.

nodes.label: GEN 10
nodes.description: A Csound GEN routine that uses a simplified version of the Fourier transform to generate waveforms from harmonic amplitudes.

nodes.label: GEN 9
nodes.description: A Csound GEN routine that implements a more complete version of the Fourier transform for waveform generation.

nodes.label: GEN 19
nodes.description: A Csound GEN routine that implements a more complete version of the Fourier transform for waveform generation.

nodes.label: rfft opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that performs forward real-signal discrete Fourier transform, converting waveform arrays to spectrum arrays.

nodes.label: rifft opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that performs inverse real-signal discrete Fourier transform, converting spectrum arrays back to waveform arrays.

nodes.label: Waterfall plot
nodes.description: A 3D visualization of a spectrogram showing frequency, time, and amplitude on separate axes to represent time-varying spectral content.

nodes.label: ftconv opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing fast partitioned convolution that reads impulse responses from function tables and allows real-time processing of large IRs with adjustable partition size.

nodes.label: dconv opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing direct convolution that reads impulse responses from function tables, suitable for smaller IRs with minimal latency.

nodes.label: pconvolve opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for fast partitioned convolution that reads impulse responses directly from soundfiles.

nodes.label: window opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that applies a window function to an input signal for spectral analysis.

nodes.label: shiftin opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that copies input samples into an array for spectral processing operations.

nodes.label: pvsynth opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode that performs inverse Fourier transformation (IFFT), converting frequency domain signals back to time domain audio.

nodes.label: Sliding Phase Vocoder
nodes.description: A variant of the phase vocoder algorithm using an iterative DFT that operates sample-by-sample, enabling audio-rate modulation of spectral data at the cost of higher computational expense.

nodes.label: pvscale opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that performs pitch shifting by scaling all frequencies in a phase vocoder frame by a scalar multiplier, with alias-free upward transposition.

nodes.label: pvshift opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that performs frequency shifting by offsetting spectral data by a fixed amount, creating inharmonic spectra from harmonic inputs.

nodes.label: mincer opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that reads audio from a function table and applies phase vocoder-based pitch scaling with phase locking to reduce artifacts.

nodes.label: temposcal opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode using streaming vocoder techniques for independent pitch and time-stretch control during playback.

nodes.label: pvanal utility
nodes.description: A Csound utility that performs phase vocoder analysis and produces PVOCEX-format spectral files for use with streaming opcodes.

nodes.label: f-sig spectral type
nodes.description: A Csound data type that wraps spectral data, its description (DFT size, hop size), and frame count for phase vocoder operations.

nodes.label: Formant Extraction
nodes.description: A technique for correcting spectral distortion in pitch-shifted vocal sounds by extracting and preserving formant regions (resonance peaks) that characterize vowel sounds.

nodes.label: J. A. Moorer
nodes.description: Researcher who originally proposed the iterative DFT algorithm used in the sliding phase vocoder.

nodes.label: Cepstrum Processing
nodes.description: A frequency-domain technique defined as the DFT of the log magnitude spectrum, used to detect and extract formants by identifying amplitude undulations in spectral frames.

nodes.label: Formant Correction
nodes.description: A technique that extracts and reapplies formants to transposed sounds to correct distortion caused by frequency changes, enabling realistic harmonization and pitch correction.

nodes.label: pvswarp opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that manipulates the spectral envelope independently of frequencies, allowing stretching, compression, or shifting of the envelope.

nodes.label: pvsbandp opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing a band-pass filter for phase vocoder signals with trapezoid-shaped frequency response defined by transition parameters.

nodes.label: pvsbandr opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing a band-reject filter for phase vocoder signals with trapezoid-shaped frequency response.

nodes.label: pvsmaska opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that applies an arbitrary amplitude curve from a function table to filter a phase vocoder signal.

nodes.label: pvsfilter opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode that applies spectral filtering where one sound's spectrum filters another, with intensity dependent on the filter sound's amplitudes.

nodes.label: pvstencil opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that performs stencilling by comparing a signal to a mask bin-per-bin and scaling amplitudes below the mask threshold, useful for noise reduction.

nodes.label: GEN43
nodes.description: A Csound function table generator that reads phase vocoder data from a file and creates a single frame of average amplitudes for use as a noise print mask.

nodes.label: pvscross opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that performs cross-synthesis by combining the frequencies of one phase vocoder stream with a mix of amplitudes from two streams.

nodes.label: pvsvoc opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that applies the spectral envelope of one phase vocoder stream to the frequencies of another, producing results similar to channel vocoding.

nodes.label: pvsmorph opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that implements spectral interpolation, morphing between two signals by independently interpolating their amplitudes and frequencies.

nodes.label: Timescaling
nodes.description: A technique for changing the duration of audio signals without altering their frequencies by reading through sequences of audio frames at different rates.

nodes.label: mincer opcode
nodes.description: A Csound function-table-reading opcode that implements timescaling and independent pitch transposition using phase locking to reduce artifacts in extreme time stretching.

nodes.label: temposcal opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that performs timescaling with automatic detection of attack transients to preserve note onsets and prevent smearing during tempo scaling.

nodes.label: pvstanal opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode variant of temposcal that produces phase vocoder streams (fsigs) as output for timescaling streaming PV signals without phase locking.

nodes.label: pvsfread opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that loads entire phase vocoder analysis files into memory and reads from them using a time position parameter.

nodes.label: pvsdiskin opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that reads phase vocoder analysis files directly from disk using a timescaling factor parameter.

nodes.label: pvsbuffer opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that sets up a circular memory buffer for writing and reading phase vocoder streams, enabling real-time PV stream time manipulations.

nodes.label: pvsbufread opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that reads from a phase vocoder circular buffer at specified time positions, with optional frequency band selection via ilo and ihi parameters.

nodes.label: pvsbufread2 opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that allows per-bin delay times for amplitudes and frequencies independently, enabling multiple delay times for different spectral bands.

nodes.label: Spectral Delay
nodes.description: A time-domain effect applied in the spectral domain using phase vocoder buffers, allowing frequency-dependent delay and manipulation as shown in the pvsdelay instrument.

nodes.label: PVOCEX format
nodes.description: The phase vocoder file format used throughout Csound for storing phase vocoder analysis data.

nodes.label: Partial Tracking
nodes.description: The central component of sinusoidal modelling that searches for spectral peaks, determines their position, and matches them across successive time points to create continuous frequency tracks.

nodes.label: Instantaneous Frequency Distribution
nodes.description: A DFT-based analysis method used in Csound to produce frames of amplitudes, frequencies, and phases from an input signal for sinusoidal modelling.

nodes.label: pvsarp opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that transforms PV stream amplitudes by boosting one bin and attenuating others, usable with an LFO for partial arpeggiation effects.

nodes.label: pvsblur opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode that reduces FFT artifacts by averaging FFT windows over a specified time duration to smooth spectral data.

nodes.label: pvsmix opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that performs ultra-seamless mixing by combining the loudest bins from two different PV inputs.

nodes.label: pvsosc opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that produces a variety of audio waveforms directly in the spectral domain.

nodes.label: pvsifd opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that applies Instantaneous Frequency Distribution to an audio input signal, producing frames of amplitudes, frequencies, and phases.

nodes.label: partials opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that performs sinusoidal partial tracking, taking amplitude and frequency data and outputting sinusoidal track data in PVS_TRACKS format.

nodes.label: sinsyn opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for faithful additive resynthesis of sinusoidal tracks using cubic interpolation and phase information, slower but more accurate than alternatives.

nodes.label: resyn opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for additive resynthesis that uses phases from track starting points and cubic interpolation, allowing frequency scaling.

nodes.label: tradsyn opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for amplitude-frequency-only additive synthesis using linear interpolation, more efficient than sinsyn and resyn but less accurate.

nodes.label: binit opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that converts partial track streams into equal-bandwidth bin-frame PV signals for further processing or overlap-add synthesis.

nodes.label: Residual Extraction
nodes.description: A spectral processing technique that separates sinusoidal tracks from transient and noisy components by subtracting accurate sinusoidal resynthesis from the original signal.

nodes.label: GEN 9
nodes.description: A Csound function table generator that creates complex waveforms from harmonically related sinusoids with specified partial numbers and amplitudes.

nodes.label: Analysis Transformation and Synthesis (ATS)
nodes.description: A specialized type of spectral modelling using sinusoidal tracking with opcodes like ATSread, ATSreadnz, ATSaddnz, ATSsinnoi, ATSbufread, and ATScross for analysis and resynthesis.

nodes.label: Bark scale
nodes.description: A psychoacoustic frequency scale that divides human hearing into 25 critical bands, used in ATS analysis for noise component representation.

nodes.label: Signal-to-Mask Ratio (SMR)
nodes.description: A psychoacoustic measure used in ATS analysis to determine whether spectral peaks are perceptually masked and should be included in sinusoidal tracks.

nodes.label: trcross opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that performs cross-synthesis of two sinusoidal track signals by matching and blending their amplitudes and frequencies.

nodes.label: trfilter opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that filters sinusoidal tracks using an amplitude response function table.

nodes.label: trscale opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that performs frequency scaling (transposition) of sinusoidal partial tracks.

nodes.label: trshift opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that performs frequency shifting (offsetting) of sinusoidal partials.

nodes.label: ATSA
nodes.description: A Csound utility program that performs ATS (Analysis Transformation and Synthesis) analysis on audio signals, producing analysis files with sinusoidal tracks and residual noise data.

nodes.label: ATSread opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that returns the amplitude and frequency of a single partial from an ATS analysis file.

nodes.label: ATSadd opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that synthesizes deterministic data from ATS files using table lookup oscillators with linear interpolation of amplitude and frequency values.

nodes.label: ATSreadnz opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that returns the energy of a Bark band at a specified time from ATS analysis.

nodes.label: ATSaddnz opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that resynthesizes the residual noise part of an ATS analysis, either the whole noisy part or a selection of noise bands.

nodes.label: ATSinfo opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that queries and returns metadata about an ATS analysis file, including sample rate, frame size, number of partials, and duration.

nodes.label: Mode filter
nodes.description: A Csound filter that simulates a mass-spring-damper system, used in the examples for resonant filtering of noise and impulse signals.

nodes.label: pvread opcode
nodes.description: A Csound unit generator that reads frequency and amplitude values from individual analysis bins of a phase vocoder data file for custom additive synthesis.

nodes.label: pvsbin opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode that extracts single amplitude-frequency pairs from f-signals for specialized resynthesis or analysis data manipulation.

nodes.label: Microsound
nodes.description: Book by Curtis Roads describing granular synthesis techniques including Glisson, Pulsar, Grainlet, and Trainlet synthesis.

nodes.label: Fourier Analysis
nodes.description: Mathematical principle stating that periodic signals can be represented as sums of sinusoidal waves (harmonics), each with frequency, amplitude, and phase.

nodes.label: tablewa opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that records live audio into a table for use as a source waveform in granular effects processing, implemented as a circular buffer.

nodes.label: Granular Effects Processing
nodes.description: Application of granular techniques to a live audio stream as source material, allowing transformational potential while retaining immediacy and interactivity of live audio effects.

nodes.label: Grain Duration
nodes.description: The length of individual grains in milliseconds. Long grains (> 50 ms) preserve timbre and pitch; short grains affect harmonic structure but not perceived pitch when grain rate is high.

nodes.label: Grain Delay
nodes.description: A granular processing effect that records live audio into a circular buffer and reads it back as grains, with delay time controlled by the difference between record and playback positions.

nodes.label: samplepos Parameter
nodes.description: A normalized parameter (0.0 to 1.0) in partikkel that sets the relative read position within a source audio waveform for grain playback.

nodes.label: Granular Reverb
nodes.description: An artificial reverberant effect created using granular techniques and overlapping time-stretch processes to simulate reverberant environments without modeling real acoustic spaces.

nodes.label: Time Stretching
nodes.description: A granular synthesis application that extends or stretches a sound in the time domain by reading source samples at a reduced rate, revealing inner details by slowing tempo.

nodes.label: linseg
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that creates linear segments for time-varying control signals, used to generate frequency glissandos and other parameter movements.

nodes.label: Grain Masking
nodes.description: A technique for selective muting and control of individual grains, including amplitude control, pitch trajectories, frequency modulation, output channel mixing, and source waveform selection.

nodes.label: FDN Reverb
nodes.description: Feedback Delay Network reverb, referenced as a comparison for intuitive feedback level control in granular reverb design.

nodes.label: Microsound
nodes.description: A reference work by Curtis Roads that defines grain masking as selective muting of individual grains with amplitude control.

nodes.label: octaviation effect
nodes.description: A perceptual pitch effect created in granular synthesis by modulating the amplitude or pitch of alternating grains, causing the perceived pitch to drop by one octave despite pitch changes.

nodes.label: channel masking
nodes.description: A granular synthesis technique that routes individual grains to different output channels, enabling spatial distribution, selective processing, and multi-speaker configurations.

nodes.label: freeverb opcode
nodes.description: A high-quality stereo reverb unit in Csound based on public-domain C++ source code, using eight parallel comb filters per channel followed by four parallel allpass filter units.

nodes.label: butterlp opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing a Butterworth low-pass filter, used in the channel masking example to selectively filter grains.

nodes.label: butterhp opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing a Butterworth high-pass filter, used in the channel masking example to selectively filter grains.

nodes.label: Trainlet
nodes.description: A synthesized waveform source used in partikkel alongside sampled waveforms for grain generation.

nodes.label: Clock Synchronisation
nodes.description: A technique for synchronizing the grain rates of multiple granular synthesis instances through soft synchronization, where sync pulses from a master clock nudge the phase of slave clocks.

nodes.label: partikkelsync opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that provides synchronization pulses and phase information for partikkel instances, enabling clock synchronization between multiple granular synthesis processes.

nodes.label: Grain Distribution
nodes.description: A parameter controlling the temporal displacement of individual grains within a period of 1/grainrate using stochastic distribution.

nodes.label: Pitch Synchronous Granular Synthesis (PSGS)
nodes.description: A granular synthesis technique that links the grain clock to the fundamental frequency of a source sound, enabling formant shifting while preserving the original pitch.

nodes.label: Formant Shifting
nodes.description: A technique that manipulates the formants of a sampled sound to create the perceptual illusion of changing the size or gender characteristics of the sound source.

nodes.label: Glisson Synthesis
nodes.description: A granular synthesis variant where each grain has an independent frequency trajectory, creating a short glissando within the grain duration.

nodes.label: Grainlet Synthesis
nodes.description: A granular synthesis technique inspired by wavelet synthesis where grain duration and frequency are linked through an inverse relationship, allowing parametric linkage between synthesis parameters.

nodes.label: Pulsar Synthesis
nodes.description: A granular synthesis technique where sound particles (pulsarets) are followed by silent intervals, with the total duration forming a pulsar period and duty cycle controlling the spectral characteristics.

nodes.label: Wavelet Synthesis
nodes.description: A synthesis technique based on wavelets, short signal segments encapsulating a constant number of cycles, which inspired grainlet synthesis.

nodes.label: fof2 opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for formant synthesis that demonstrates particle-based formant synthesis techniques.

nodes.label: Trainlets
nodes.description: A granular synthesis variant that creates periodic trains of grains with controllable parameters including grain duration and train frequency.

nodes.label: Pulsars
nodes.description: A granular synthesis type that uses pulse-like grain structures with controllable parameters.

nodes.label: Glissons
nodes.description: A granular synthesis variant that creates glissando-like effects through pitch sweep parameters applied to individual grains.

nodes.label: Asynchronous Granular Synthesis
nodes.description: A granular synthesis type where grain timing is not synchronized to a regular clock, allowing for more random or probabilistic grain generation.

nodes.label: Waveform Mixing
nodes.description: A technique in granular synthesis that blends multiple source waveforms with controllable relative amplitudes through masking tables.

nodes.label: ftmorf opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that morphs between different function tables, used to gradually transition between masking tables in granular synthesis.

nodes.label: Grain Envelope
nodes.description: The amplitude shape applied to individual grains in granular synthesis, controlling attack, sustain, and decay characteristics.

nodes.label: Modal Synthesis
nodes.description: A physical modeling approach developed by Calvet, Laurens and Adrien in 1990 that represents vibrating objects as collections of simpler substructures, each characterized by modes of vibration captured as modal data including frequencies and damping coefficients.

nodes.label: Finite Difference Methods
nodes.description: A physical modeling approach that can produce very realistic results but with considerable computational costs.

nodes.label: Karplus-Strong Algorithm
nodes.description: A physical modelling technique for synthesizing plucked string sounds by filling a buffer with random values and iteratively calculating the mean of adjacent values, creating a smoothing effect that produces periodic behavior with rich overtone structure.

nodes.label: pluck opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing physical modeling of plucked string instruments with various pluck methods and initialization options.

nodes.label: wgpluck opcode
nodes.description: Fuller waveguide plucked string implementation in Csound using different filters and tuning schemes than the basic pluck opcode.

nodes.label: wgbow opcode
nodes.description: A Csound waveguide physical modeling opcode that simulates bowed string instruments with pressure and vibrato control.

nodes.label: mandol opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode extending the waveguide model to mandolin pairs of strings at slightly different pitches.

nodes.label: repluck opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode providing limited sympathetic string sound by including an audio excitement signal in the plucked string model.

nodes.label: streson opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode modeling a string as a resonator with no initial pluck, providing sympathetic vibration effects.

nodes.label: wgclar opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode for clarinet waveguide synthesis using Perry Cook's reed model with table lookup for non-linear reed behavior.

nodes.label: Perry Cook
nodes.description: Researcher whose work on physically inspired stochastic event modeling (PhISEM) forms the basis for Csound's physical modeling opcodes for percussion instruments.

nodes.label: dcblock2 filter
nodes.description: Csound filter used to remove DC offset from waveguide wind instrument output.

nodes.label: mode opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that implements modal resonator synthesis, used to simulate vibrating modes of physical objects like wood plates and membranes.

nodes.label: marimba opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that implements a marimba physical model using four modal resonances with controls for decay, amplitude, and frequency.

nodes.label: vibes opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing a vibraphone physical model based on four modal resonances.

nodes.label: gogobel opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing a gogo bell physical model using four modal resonances.

nodes.label: wgflute opcode
nodes.description: A Csound waveguide flute opcode that models flute excitation based on a nonlinear jet fluctuating over the lip hole with an open pipe at both ends.

nodes.label: wgbrass opcode
nodes.description: A Csound waveguide brass opcode that models brass instrument excitation controlled by the mass, spring constant, and damping of the lip.

nodes.label: Finite Difference Method
nodes.description: A numerical technique for solving differential equations by discretizing time and space into grids and approximating derivatives with difference equations.

nodes.label: Finite Difference Scheme
nodes.description: A numerical method for solving differential equations by discretizing space and time, used in physical modeling of stiff strings and other resonant systems.

nodes.label: Waveguide Model
nodes.description: A physical modeling approach developed by Smith, Cook, et al. between 1982-1993 that is the only physical modeling technique used in commercial applications and forms the basis of synthesizers manufactured by Yamaha, Korg, and Roland.

nodes.label: barmodel opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that models a thin metal bar using finite difference schemes, with parameters for clamping, stiffness, and strike quality.

nodes.label: prepiano opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that models a prepared piano using three interacting stiff strings with optional preparations like rattles and rubbers.

nodes.label: platerev opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for modeling a two-dimensional stiff rectangular plate excited by audio signals, allowing defined stiffness, aspect ratio, and multiple excitation points.

nodes.label: Physically Inspired Models
nodes.description: A class of instrument models introduced by Cook that use stochastic methods to approximate physical behavior without solving differential equations.

nodes.label: Spring-Mass System
nodes.description: A physical modeling approach where all interactions are modeled as combinations of springs, masses, and dampers, discretized using methods like Euler's method.

nodes.label: Euler's Method
nodes.description: A numerical integration technique for solving differential equations by calculating acceleration, velocity, and position at each time step, used in discrete physical modeling.

nodes.label: CORDIS-ANIMA
nodes.description: A project demonstrating spring-mass and damper abstractions for physical modeling, referenced as an alternative approach to finite difference methods.

nodes.label: Masspring UDO
nodes.description: A user-defined operator in Csound that models a spring-mass system with external displacement, spring constant, dampening, and mass parameters.

nodes.label: GPU Parallelism
nodes.description: A computational approach being used to alleviate performance issues in finite difference physical modeling schemes.

nodes.label: Spring-mass network
nodes.description: A physical system composed of interconnected masses linked by springs with characteristics of mass, stiffness, dampening, and initial velocity.

nodes.label: scanu opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that implements a mass-spring physical model with parameters for mass, stiffness, damping, and centering, capable of audio injection for motion control.

nodes.label: scans opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that reads scanu output using scan trajectories defined by f-tables, allowing non-consecutive table index reading for sound generation.

nodes.label: Wave terrain synthesis
nodes.description: A synthesis technique that scans 3D function tables using two independent oscillators to modulate x and y axes, producing sonic results similar to amplitude modulation but with greater dynamism through moving elliptical indexes.

nodes.label: Modal modelling
nodes.description: A physical modelling approach that can produce realistic sounds for struck objects.

nodes.label: Finite difference schemes
nodes.description: Computational methods used in physical modelling to simulate complex instrument components such as stiffness and non-simple interactions.

nodes.label: Csound Haiku
nodes.description: A set of nine real-time generative pieces composed in 2011, exhibited as a sound installation in book form with Csound code typed on semi-transparent paper using a mechanical typewriter.

nodes.label: SuperCollider
nodes.description: Software for real-time audio synthesis and algorithmic composition, mentioned as a competitor to Csound in event generation and pattern-based working.

nodes.label: rspline opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates a smooth spline between minimum and maximum values with user-specified minimum and maximum frequencies.

nodes.label: jspline opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates random spline curves, used for high-frequency pitch modulation to add airiness to sounds.

nodes.label: FLTK opcodes
nodes.description: Csound opcodes for creating graphical user interfaces, used to build workbenches for exploring synthesizer cell timbres despite threading issues in real-time use.

nodes.label: alwayson opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode used to trigger instruments to remain permanently active, employed in Haiku I for the reverb instrument.

nodes.label: Generative music
nodes.description: Compositional approach where pieces generate note events algorithmically rather than from a traditional score, allowing variation on each performance.

nodes.label: Haiku I
nodes.description: First piece in the Csound Haiku set, featuring six voices using the gbuzz opcode to create brass-like tones with slowly evolving glissandi.

nodes.label: rspline opcode
nodes.description: A Csound random spline generator that produces smooth random modulation between specified amplitude and rate limits.

nodes.label: jspline opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates random pitch variation using spline interpolation, used in the scanned synthesizer example for dynamic pitch modulation.

nodes.label: gbuzz opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates a buzz tone with modulation of the lowest partial number and amplitude coefficient multiplier, used for additive synthesis.

nodes.label: screverb opcode
nodes.description: A Csound reverb opcode used to add spatial depth and timbral interest to synthesized sounds.

nodes.label: reverbsc opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing stereo reverb using Schroeder reverberator architecture, used to enhance physical modeling examples.

nodes.label: GEN 17 function table
nodes.description: A Csound function generator that creates step functions defining probability distributions, used in Haiku VIII for time gaps and note durations.

nodes.label: poscil opcode
nodes.description: A Csound interpolating oscillator opcode that reduces quantization artifacts when playing wavetables at low frequencies.

nodes.label: poscil3 opcode
nodes.description: A Csound cubic-interpolating oscillator opcode that provides higher-quality wavetable playback with reduced artifacts.

nodes.label: Timbre modulation
nodes.description: The technique of varying the spectral content of a sound over time using random or controlled modulation.

nodes.label: Polyrhythm
nodes.description: The simultaneous use of contrasting rhythmic patterns at different speeds, explored in Csound Haiku II.

nodes.label: wguide2 opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing a double waveguide algorithm with first-order low-pass filters on each delay line, producing plucked or struck string-like sounds.

nodes.label: wguide1 opcode
nodes.description: A Csound waveguide opcode providing a simple waveguide model consisting of a delay line fed into a first-order low-pass filter with feedback loop.

nodes.label: hsboscil opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates a tone comprising a stack of partials spaced an octave apart, shaped by a spectral window function.

nodes.label: Csound Haiku III
nodes.description: A composition by Iain McCurdy using the wguide2 opcode as its synthesis cell, employing waveguide physical modeling with inharmonic spectra.

nodes.label: Csound Haiku IV
nodes.description: A composition by Iain McCurdy using the hsboscil opcode to create periodic gestural clusters with morphing sound spectra, enhanced by ring modulation.

nodes.label: Spectral window
nodes.description: A function in hsboscil that shapes the emphasis of partials in a harmonic stack, can be shifted to introduce higher or lower partials.

nodes.label: vdelay opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that implements a variable delay line with audio-rate delay time control, ranging from 1 sample period to a maximum delay time.

nodes.label: Csound Haiku V
nodes.description: A generative composition using phaser2 opcode to create struck wooden bars and sustained metallic sounds, with a continuous motor rhythm and periodic punctuating gestures.

nodes.label: Csound Haiku VI
nodes.description: A generative piece modeling six resonating strings using the wguide1 waveguide opcode, excited by pink noise impulses with strumming effects and continuous detuning.

nodes.label: phaser2 opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing a series of second-order all-pass filters useful for creating inharmonically positioned resonances that imitate struck resonating objects.

nodes.label: strumming effect
nodes.description: A synthesis technique in Haiku VI where multiple waveguides are excited with randomly delayed impulses to simulate guitar string strumming.

nodes.label: Csound Haiku VII
nodes.description: A Csound composition using GEN 2 function tables for rhythmic sequences, GEN 9 tables for inharmonic spectra, and gbuzz synthesis with descending chromatic pitch modulation.

nodes.label: Csound Haiku VIII
nodes.description: A generative composition using layered note streams with random pitch, duration, and effects including pitch bends and frequency shifting via Hilbert transformation.

nodes.label: Csound Haiku II
nodes.description: An earlier Csound Haiku piece that uses GEN 2 function tables for rhythmic sequences, referenced as a methodological precedent.

nodes.label: GEN 2 function table
nodes.description: A Csound function table generator used to store sequences of duration values for rhythmic material.

nodes.label: GEN 9 function table
nodes.description: A Csound function table generator used to create inharmonic spectra for bell-like and resonating sounds.

nodes.label: seqtime opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that converts a sequence of duration values into a series of triggers for note events.

nodes.label: vdelay3 opcode
nodes.description: A variable delay opcode in Csound that uses milliseconds as the time unit, similar to vdelay.

nodes.label: schedkwhennamed opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode variant that schedules instrument instances by name rather than number, allowing dynamic event generation.

nodes.label: Pointillism
nodes.description: A compositional technique using discrete, isolated note events to create waves of gestures where individual voices remain distinguishable.

nodes.label: Aleatoric music
nodes.description: Music incorporating chance or random elements, used in Haiku VIII with discrete duration values for note events.

nodes.label: Csound Haiku IX
nodes.description: A generative piece based on sweeping arpeggios following harmonic series intervals with overlapping notes and spectral texture effects.

nodes.label: hilbert opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing Hilbert transformation, used to apply frequency-shifting effects to notes in Haiku VIII.

nodes.label: schedkwhen opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for conditional event scheduling based on trigger signals, used to trigger note generation in Haiku VIII.

nodes.label: randomh opcode
nodes.description: A Csound random function generator that produces new random numbers at a user-defined rate, holding the previous value until a new value is generated.

nodes.label: frequency shifting
nodes.description: Audio effect applied conditionally to longer notes in Haiku VIII using Hilbert transformation to create spectral modulation.

nodes.label: Alvin Lucier
nodes.description: Composer known for the piece 'I Am Sitting in a Room', which demonstrates room filtering effects through repeated tape recording and playback.

nodes.label: Agostino Di Scipio
nodes.description: Author of a reading on sound synthesis by iterated nonlinear functions, investigating chaos theory applications in digital sound synthesis since 1991.

nodes.label: Audio Feedback
nodes.description: Technique where audio from speakers is captured by microphones and processed to create sound, used as the sole sound source in Brandtsegg's piece.

nodes.label: Spectral Panning
nodes.description: Technique used to spread timbral components to different locations in the performance space, applied in Brandtsegg's feedback piece.

nodes.label: Adaptive Filtering
nodes.description: Digital signal processing technique using filters that selectively reduce or maintain feedback at specific frequencies in real time.

nodes.label: ftmorf opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode for morphing between function tables, used to gradually transition spectral profiles in the adaptive equalizer.

nodes.label: Algorithmic Composition
nodes.description: A compositional approach using generative processes and control structures to create musical sequences, demonstrated through multiple Csound examples.

nodes.label: Feedback Piece
nodes.description: A live electronic composition by Øyvind Brandtsegg using microphone feedback, adaptive parametric equalization, granular processing, and spectral panning, performed with two directional microphones and EMG muscle sensors.

nodes.label: Reaper
nodes.description: Digital audio workstation used as the main VST host for the Feedback Piece, providing signal I/O, metering, routing, and mixing.

nodes.label: AudioMulch
nodes.description: Audio host software used for effects automation and parameter control in the Feedback Piece.

nodes.label: Hadron Particle Synthesizer
nodes.description: Granular synthesis plugin used to extend the sonic palette of the Feedback Piece with noisy, intermittent, and pitch-shifted textures.

nodes.label: Peiman Koshravi
nodes.description: Audio researcher who developed circumspectral panning techniques, which inspired the spectral panning approach used in the Feedback Piece.

nodes.label: Denis Smalley
nodes.description: Composer and theorist whose work on spatial audio techniques influenced the spectral panning methods used in the Feedback Piece.

nodes.label: Adaptive Parametric Equalizer
nodes.description: Feedback reduction technique using a pitch tracker to control a band-stop filter that dynamically targets feedback frequencies.

nodes.label: EMG Sensors
nodes.description: Electromyography muscle activity sensors used to control microphone gain in the Feedback Piece performance, enabling expressive control and feedback safety.

nodes.label: Ed Severinghaus
nodes.description: Designer and builder of the BodySynth EMG system used for live performance control.

nodes.label: Vinko Globokar
nodes.description: Composer who created the piece Toucher as a modification of syllable-based rhythmic practice applied to Bertolt Brecht's Galileo.

nodes.label: Bertolt Brecht
nodes.description: Playwright whose work Galileo was referenced in Vinko Globokar's compositional practice.

nodes.label: Knuth
nodes.description: A live electronics instrument implemented in CsoundQt that analyzes rhythm and vowel frequencies in speech to trigger sounds in real time via MIDI, with parameters for threshold, frequency range, and delay.

nodes.label: Alma
nodes.description: A live electronics instrument that analyzes spoken word into sounding units of varying sizes (phonemes, syllables, words) and plays back the recorded past in four distinct modes: scratching particles, syllable reordering, metric rhythm control, and FFT-based bell-like transformations.

nodes.label: BodySynth
nodes.description: EMG (electromyography) system built by Ed Severinghaus in the 1990s for controlling sound through muscle signals.

nodes.label: pvspitch
nodes.description: Csound opcode that analyzes the fundamental frequency of a signal in the frequency domain, used for vowel detection in speech analysis.

nodes.label: FFT Analysis
nodes.description: Fourier Transform analysis technique used to convert audio signals from time domain to frequency domain, with configurable window sizes and overlap parameters.

nodes.label: Rhythm Analysis
nodes.description: Technique for detecting and analyzing rhythmic patterns in speech, particularly syllable-based rhythm used in Knuth.

nodes.label: Live Electronics
nodes.description: Real-time audio processing and synthesis techniques applied to incoming audio signals using effects chains and spectral manipulation.

nodes.label: Ich geh mit meiner Laterne
nodes.description: German children's song that inspired Joachim Heintz's conceptual approach to live electronics with spoken word.

nodes.label: Toucher
nodes.description: Composition by Vinko Globokar that modifies traditional syllable-based rhythmic practice applied to Bertolt Brecht's Galileo.

nodes.label: FFT-based Sound Transformation
nodes.description: A spectral processing technique used in Alma's fourth mode to extract prominent partials from speech snippets and transform them into bell-like, pitched, slowly-decaying sounds.

nodes.label: Live Electronics with Spoken Word
nodes.description: A compositional and improvisational approach that processes real-time or recorded speech through digital signal processing to create new musical and sonic textures.

nodes.label: Toucher
nodes.description: A composition by Vinko Globokar referenced as a conceptual precedent for compositional approaches using speech analysis and transformation.

nodes.label: IsSilence Opcode
nodes.description: A custom Csound opcode that detects silence in audio by comparing RMS values against a dB threshold, used in Alma for segmenting speech into sounding units.

nodes.label: Ludwig Wittgenstein
nodes.description: Philosopher whose texts were used by Joachim Heintz as source material for compositional studies in the Alma project.

nodes.label: Se'nnight
nodes.description: Composition by John ffitch featuring seven loose sections, using Csound with C programs for sound generation, Henon functions, and ambisonic spatial rendering.

nodes.label: Drums and Different Canons
nodes.description: A series of seven compositions by John ffitch exploring the onset of chaos using recurrence relations and chaotic maps.

nodes.label: Hénon Map
nodes.description: A pair of recurrence equations (xn+1 = 1 − axn² + yn, yn+1 = bxn) used to generate chaotic sequences mapped to musical parameters like frequency and duration.

nodes.label: Torus Map
nodes.description: A mathematical map used alongside the Hénon map in the first Drums and Different Canons composition to govern synthetic marimba and bell sounds.

nodes.label: Lorenz Map
nodes.description: A chaotic dynamical system used in compositions Stalactite and For Connie from the Drums and Different Canons series.

nodes.label: 3rd International Csound Conference
nodes.description: Conference held in St. Petersburg in 2015 where Joachim Heintz presented a study on Alma reading text.

nodes.label: St. Petersburg
nodes.description: City where the 3rd International Csound Conference was held in 2015.

nodes.label: Chirikov standard map
nodes.description: A torus-based chaotic map used in the development of Se'nnight to generate gesture sequences for drums and canons.

nodes.label: Jon Nelson
nodes.description: Csound instrument designer who created the original synthetic marimba and drum instruments used in Se'nnight.

nodes.label: Synthetic marimba
nodes.description: A modal-modelling Csound instrument originally designed by Jon Nelson and updated by ffitch for spatial positioning in Se'nnight.

nodes.label: fmbell
nodes.description: A Csound FM synthesis instrument used in Se'nnight with the attack removed to create a third synthetic instrument.

nodes.label: Mark Applebaum
nodes.description: Composer whose piece Pre-Composition influenced ffitch's approach to multi-channel composition.

nodes.label: Pre-Composition
nodes.description: A piece by Mark Applebaum that addresses challenges of performing eight-channel works.

nodes.label: Jhaptaal
nodes.description: A Hindustani rhythm pattern (dhin na | dhin dhin na | tin na | din din na) used as the basis for 5/4 time in Se'nnight.

nodes.label: Terry Riley
nodes.description: Composer whose music inspired Steven Yi to create Transit, a work involving long feedback delay lines.

nodes.label: Henon function
nodes.description: Mathematical function used in Se'nnight to generate sound sequences and control parameters in compositional structures.

nodes.label: HRTF opcodes
nodes.description: Csound opcodes used in Se'nnight for spatial audio processing in small studio environments before ambisonic rendering.

nodes.label: bformenc1
nodes.description: Csound opcode for encoding a monophonic sound source and its localization into B-format spatial information (w, x, y, z components).

nodes.label: bformdec1
nodes.description: Csound opcode for ambisonic B-format decoding used to render high-order audio to stereo, quad, or octal formats.

nodes.label: Transit
nodes.description: A composition by Steven Yi created using Csound and Blue, featuring reused instruments, customized sounds, and temporal layering with different BPM settings for score and delay processing.

nodes.label: diskin2
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that reads audio files directly from hard disk, supporting large file sizes and various playback operations including pitch control and looping.

nodes.label: transeg
nodes.description: Csound opcode for generating transient envelopes, used in Se'nnight to create amplitude envelopes for the entire work.

nodes.label: hrtfstat
nodes.description: Csound HRTF opcode used in Se'nnight for spatial audio processing of the marimba sound.

nodes.label: William Light
nodes.description: Developer of the 'Tempo-Sync Stereo Delay' effect contributed to BlueShare, a built-in online instrument and effects exchange platform within Blue.

nodes.label: In Transit
nodes.description: A composition by Steven Yi created using Blue's mixer and effects system, featuring four instruments routed through feedback delay and reverb processing.

nodes.label: SID Synthesis
nodes.description: Synthesis technique based on the SID chip found in Commodore 64 computers, implemented in the b64 instrument used in In Transit.

nodes.label: BlueShare
nodes.description: A built-in online instrument and effects exchange platform available within Blue for sharing user-developed instruments and effects.

nodes.label: blueMixerOut
nodes.description: A pseudo-opcode in Blue that outputs instrument signals to the mixer, auto-generating global audio-rate variables for signal bussing.

nodes.label: BlueLive
nodes.description: A real-time performance feature within Blue that supports MIDI keyboard input, hardware MIDI systems, and score generation through SoundObjects for live instrument performance and sketching.

nodes.label: SoundObjects
nodes.description: Items in Blue that generate Csound code, typically score, with various editor interfaces including GenericScore, Clojure, and PianoRoll types for different compositional approaches.

nodes.label: pcount opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode used to determine the number of p-fields given for an event, enabling flexible instrument design that processes different note formats.

nodes.label: Noctilucent Clouds
nodes.description: A composition by Victor Lazzarini that uses spectral delay processing to transform recordings of Time-Lines IV for piano, structured in two 241-second sections with an inverted arch dynamic form.

nodes.label: Spectral Delays
nodes.description: Delay lines created in the frequency domain that act on specific sub-bands of the spectrum, applying different delay times to each frequency band independently.

nodes.label: pvsmix
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that mixes phase vocoder signals in the frequency domain, accounting for masking effects.

nodes.label: GEN5
nodes.description: A Csound function table generator that creates exponential curve segments, used to define delay time curves across frequency bands.

nodes.label: Variable delay processor
nodes.description: A processor with time-varying delay parameters that can transition between resonant filtering and echo effects.

nodes.label: Inverse comb filter
nodes.description: A filter placed in the feedback path with varying delay time to alter high-frequency comb filter peaks.

nodes.label: Time-Lines IV
nodes.description: A piano composition by Victor Lazzarini used as source material for Noctilucent Clouds, featuring repeated-note rhythmic figures and an ABA structural form.

nodes.label: Spectral delay processing
nodes.description: A signal processing technique used in Noctilucent Clouds that scrambles and obscures the original piano texture through variable delays and feedback.

nodes.label: Flanging
nodes.description: A classic audio processing technique used in Noctilucent Clouds to transform source material.

nodes.label: Graphic equaliser
nodes.description: An audio processing tool implemented in Csound to adjust the overall spectral envelope during post-production mastering of Noctilucent Clouds.

nodes.label: makecsd utility
nodes.description: A command-line tool for packaging Csound source code and audio files into a single CSD file for distribution and performance.

nodes.label: Edinburgh
nodes.description: City where Noctilucent Clouds was premiered in October 2012.

nodes.label: Timelines + Clouds
nodes.description: A sister piece to Noctilucent Clouds for piano and live electronics, designed to be performed with Csound, sharing some instruments and processing ideas.

nodes.label: Kevin Karplus and Alex Strong
nodes.description: Physical modeling synthesis algorithm used in the pluck opcode to generate plucked string sounds with dynamic filtering.

nodes.label: Ørjan Brandtsegg
nodes.description: Composer and researcher who created feedback pieces and contributed to particle synthesis and granular synthesis research.

nodes.label: James Timoney
nodes.description: Researcher who contributed to feedback amplitude modulation synthesis and spectral processing with GPUs.

nodes.label: Synthesis Toolkit (STK)
nodes.description: C++ toolkit of audio synthesis classes and instruments developed by Perry Cook at CCRMA.

nodes.label: The Csound Book
nodes.description: A comprehensive educational book by Richard Boulanger covering Csound language structure, synthesis algorithms, signal processing, and sound design techniques with accompanying CD-ROM containing example orchestras and scores.

nodes.label: CCRMA
nodes.description: Center for Computer Research in Music and Acoustics at Stanford University; research center for digital audio and synthesis.
aliases: Center for Computer Research in Music and Acoustics
Centre for Computer Research in Music and Acoustics

nodes.label: Linux Audio Conference
nodes.description: Annual conference series featuring papers on audio synthesis, Csound, and open-source audio software.

nodes.label: International Computer Music Conference
nodes.description: Major annual conference for computer music research and composition.

nodes.label: James A. Moorer
nodes.description: Computer music researcher who published on discrete summation formulas for complex audio spectra synthesis, phase vocoder applications, and reverberation.

nodes.label: Studio for Experimental Music
nodes.description: MIT laboratory where MUSIC 360 and MUSIC 11 were developed.

nodes.label: DX7
nodes.description: A digital FM synthesis keyboard synthesizer whose algorithms and envelope parameters are being emulated in this Csound implementation.

nodes.label: Michael Wright
nodes.description: Developer of Open Sound Control protocol with Adrian Freed.

nodes.label: Edgar Varèse
nodes.description: Pioneering electronic music composer whose works are included in recommended listening.

nodes.label: Hlöðver Sigurðsson
nodes.description: Core developer of Csound who has worked on modernization and the Csound-WASM version.

nodes.label: Rory Walsh
nodes.description: Contributor to the Csound FLOSS Manual, authoring sections on Csound in Ableton Live, VST plugins, Cabbage frontend, and digital audio basics.

nodes.label: Csound 7
nodes.description: A major version of Csound featuring full flexibility of variable naming, extended array features, for-loops, and explicit type declarations.

nodes.label: Csound-WASM
nodes.description: A Web Assembly module version of Csound that allows it to be used inside any browser as a JavaScript library.

nodes.label: outall opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that sends an audio signal to all available output channels.

nodes.label: Xavier Dole
nodes.description: Translator who translated the Csound FLOSS Manual Getting Started section to French.

nodes.label: Unity game engine
nodes.description: A game development platform that Csound can be integrated into via its API.

nodes.label: Bela Board
nodes.description: A microcomputer platform on which Csound can be used for audio applications.

nodes.label: outall opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that outputs an audio signal to all configured output channels.

nodes.label: Hanover University of Music
nodes.description: An institution where Joachim Heintz taught Csound to young composers, contributing feedback for the tutorial development.

nodes.label: Spectral Resynthesis
nodes.description: A technique discussed in the Csound FLOSS Manual related to understanding sounds through their spectral components.

nodes.label: Simple Harmonic Motion
nodes.description: A mathematical concept describing constant movement of a point on a circle, fundamental to understanding sine waves and sound phenomena.

nodes.label: line opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode similar to linseg that generates a line but continues moving beyond the target value rather than stopping.

nodes.label: k-rate (control rate)
nodes.description: Variables in Csound that are recomputed at the control-rate (typically 4410 times per second), primarily used for storing and updating envelopes and sub-audio control signals.

nodes.label: a-rate (audio rate)
nodes.description: Variables in Csound that are arrays or vectors updated at the audio sampling-rate (typically 44100 times per second), used for storing output signals of oscillators and filters.

nodes.label: Sample rate
nodes.description: The number of audio samples per second, with common values including 44100 Hz (CD standard), 48000 Hz (video standard), and higher rates like 96000 or 192000 Hz.

nodes.label: Guido van Rossum
nodes.description: Creator of the Python programming language, referenced in the manual for coding style conventions.

nodes.label: Pure Data
nodes.description: A visual audio programming language that uses object boxes and symbolic cables to represent signal flow, with equivalent concepts to Csound's sr, ksmps, and nchnls.

nodes.label: ksmps (Control Block Size)
nodes.description: The number of audio samples collected in one control-rate package or block in Csound, defining the time resolution of control signals. Recommended values are powers of two such as 32 or 64.

nodes.label: nchnls (Number of Channels)
nodes.description: The number of output channels in Csound, with nchnls_i optionally specifying input channels separately.

nodes.label: 0dbfs (Zero dB Full Scale)
nodes.description: The amplitude value representing maximum level in Csound, recommended to be set to 1 rather than the default 32767.

nodes.label: Github
nodes.description: The hosting platform where Cabbage source code and pre-compiled binaries are distributed.

nodes.label: p-fields (parameter fields)
nodes.description: Parameters in Csound scores that control instrument events: p1 (instrument number), p2 (start time), p3 (duration), and p4+ (instrument-specific parameters like amplitude and frequency).

nodes.label: mtof opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that converts MIDI note numbers to their corresponding frequency values.

nodes.label: i-rate
nodes.description: Variables in Csound that are changed and updated at the note-rate, evaluated at initialization-time and remain constant throughout the duration of a note-event.

nodes.label: MIDI note numbers
nodes.description: A standardized system for specifying musical pitches where C4 is note 60, with each semitone represented by an increment or decrement of one.

nodes.label: glissando
nodes.description: A musical technique of sliding smoothly from one pitch to another, implemented in Csound using linear segment opcodes.

nodes.label: string
nodes.description: A data type in Csound consisting of a sequence of characters enclosed in double quotes, used for text values such as file names.

nodes.label: chromatic scale
nodes.description: A musical scale consisting of consecutive semitones, each represented by adjacent MIDI note numbers.

nodes.label: ftom opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that converts frequency values to MIDI note numbers, functioning as the reverse of mtof.

nodes.label: Equal temperament
nodes.description: The current preferred tuning method for western instruments, dividing each octave into 12 equal semitones with a ratio of 2^(1/12) ≈ 1.059463.

nodes.label: A4 standard pitch
nodes.description: The reference pitch for keyboard instruments, standardized to 440 Hz since 1939, though historically variable and often performed higher at 443 Hz.

nodes.label: Vienna conference 1885
nodes.description: The first international conference to fix a standard pitch, which was set to 435 Hz.

nodes.label: ISA London conference 1939
nodes.description: International Federation of the National Standardizing Association conference in London where 440 Hz was fixed as the standard pitch for A4.

nodes.label: Decibel (dB) scale
nodes.description: A logarithmic relative scale for measuring amplitude in audio, where 0 dB represents the maximum possible amplitude in digital audio and negative values represent proportional reductions.

nodes.label: MIDI note number
nodes.description: A numerical representation of pitch in MIDI where A4 is note 69 and each semitone increment represents a frequency ratio of 2^(1/12).

nodes.label: Frequency to MIDI conversion
nodes.description: The process of converting between raw frequency values in Hz and MIDI note numbers, essential for pitch perception in music synthesis.

nodes.label: Proportional vs. linear frequency transitions
nodes.description: A comparison of two pitch glissando methods: proportional (constant ratio, perceived as constant pitch decay) versus linear (constant frequency subtraction, perceived as uneven pitch movement).

nodes.label: ampdb opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that converts decibel values to amplitude values, available at i-rate (ampdb:i) and k-rate (ampdb:k) for static and time-varying conversions.

nodes.label: Digital audio amplitude
nodes.description: The representation of sound intensity in digital systems using bit depth (16-bit, 24-bit, 32-bit), where the maximum possible value is set as 0 dB.

nodes.label: Archytas of Tarentum
nodes.description: An ancient Greek mathematician from the early 4th century B.C. who formulated the concept of arithmetic mean as a mathematical proportion.

nodes.label: Arithmetic series
nodes.description: A mathematical sequence where successive terms have equal differences, contrasting with geometric series in the context of frequency and amplitude transitions.

nodes.label: Geometric series
nodes.description: A mathematical sequence where successive terms have equal ratios, used to describe proportional transitions in frequency and amplitude perception.

nodes.label: Weber-Fechner law
nodes.description: A principle describing how human sensory perception responds proportionally to stimulus intensity, relevant to understanding decibel and MIDI scales.

nodes.label: Archytas
nodes.description: Ancient Greek mathematician who described the geometric mean in mathematical terms.

nodes.label: Euclid
nodes.description: Ancient Greek mathematician who described geometric construction of the geometric mean in Elements (VI.8).

nodes.label: Geometric Mean
nodes.description: Mathematical concept where the ratio of larger to mean equals the ratio of mean to smaller; used in proportional relationships.

nodes.label: Golden Ratio
nodes.description: Irrational number famous for usage in art and nature, related to geometric mean and approximated by Fibonacci numbers.

nodes.label: Fibonacci Numbers
nodes.description: Sequence of numbers that approximate the golden ratio when used as ratios.

nodes.label: C Programming Language
nodes.description: Programming language first released in 1972 that enabled Csound to separate human-readable source code from machine-specific implementations.

nodes.label: Musical Sounds from Digital Computers
nodes.description: 1962 article by Mathews, Pierce and Guttman introducing p-fields on computer cards for music synthesis parameter specification.

nodes.label: Pierce
nodes.description: Co-author of the 1962 article 'Musical Sounds from Digital Computers' with Mathews and Guttman.

nodes.label: Guttman
nodes.description: Co-author of the 1962 article 'Musical Sounds from Digital Computers' with Mathews and Pierce.

nodes.label: schedulek opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode similar to schedule but operating at k-rate for dynamic instrument scheduling during performance.

nodes.label: nstrnum opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that retrieves the positive integer number internally assigned to a named instrument.

nodes.label: CsInstruments section
nodes.description: The section of a Csound .csd file containing the orchestra code that defines instruments and their behavior.

nodes.label: CsScore section
