nodes.description: The section of a Csound .csd file containing score lines that trigger instrument instances at specified times with durations and parameters.

nodes.label: CsOptions section
nodes.description: The section of a Csound .csd file that sets general performance options such as real-time output, file rendering, MIDI device selection, and console message levels.

nodes.label: .orc file format
nodes.description: Legacy Csound file format containing instrument definitions and orchestra code, used separately from .sco score files.

nodes.label: .sco file format
nodes.description: Legacy Csound file format containing score lines and event data, used separately from .orc orchestra files.

nodes.label: Csound command-line execution
nodes.description: Method of running Csound from a terminal or command line with syntax like 'csound -o dac -m 128 my_instruments.orc my_score_lines.sco' using flags for options.

nodes.label: Csound Reference Manual
nodes.description: The official documentation for Csound opcodes and language features, available online and for download.

nodes.label: turnoff2 opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode for stopping running instrument instances, though ineffective for stopping self-triggering instruments.

nodes.label: puts opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that prints a string on a new line when a trigger input changes value.

nodes.label: Blue
nodes.description: A frontend for Csound developed by Steven Yi that provides sophisticated possibilities for working with score events as objects.

nodes.label: if opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for conditional branching that allows program flow to depend on specified conditions using if, elseif, else, and endif keywords.

nodes.label: goto opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that implements jump-to-label mechanism for creating loops and non-linear program flow.

nodes.label: Pseudorandom number generator
nodes.description: A computational algorithm that generates sequences of numbers that appear random but are deterministic based on an initial seed value.

nodes.label: Format string
nodes.description: A string containing placeholders (like %d, %f, %s) that are filled with variable values during output, similar to C programming language conventions.

nodes.label: randomi opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates interpolated random values, drawing lines between randomly generated points at a specified density per second.

nodes.label: Random Walk
nodes.description: A stochastic process where each step applies a deviation to the previous state, limiting movement to certain ranges rather than allowing jumps anywhere within boundaries.

nodes.label: Markov Chain
nodes.description: A probabilistic model based on a number of possible states with defined probabilities for transitions between states, used in music for sequences of pitches or notes.

nodes.label: Gaussian Distribution
nodes.description: A bell-curve probability distribution described mathematically as exp(−x²)/sqrt(2π), characterized by symmetric spread around a mean value and commonly used in random number generation for audio effects.

nodes.label: seed function
nodes.description: A Csound function that initializes the random number generator with a specific value to control reproducibility of random sequences.

nodes.label: Web IDE
nodes.description: An online IDE for Csound started in 2018 that allows users to create an account and use Csound in their browser without installation.

nodes.label: Tarmo Johannes
nodes.description: Csound developer who authored the Minimal HTML example demonstrating control of Csound using HTML sliders.

nodes.label: Eduado Moguillansky
nodes.description: Maintainer of CsoundQt frontend alongside Tarmo Johannes.

nodes.label: CoreAudio
nodes.description: Apple's native audio framework for iOS that handles audio input/output and integration with Csound applications.

nodes.label: ctrl7 opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for receiving MIDI controller data (CC messages) from external controllers or virtual sliders, with configurable channel, controller number, and value range.

nodes.label: MIDI synthesis
nodes.description: Integration of MIDI keyboard input with additive synthesis, allowing real-time control of timbre through key velocity mapping to partial count.

nodes.label: Table interpolation
nodes.description: A technique in oscillators to estimate values between table points, essential for avoiding artifacts when reading wavetables at various frequencies.

nodes.label: printarray opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that prints i-rate or k-rate arrays, triggering output when the trigger input changes from 0 to 1.

nodes.label: printf_i opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for formatted i-rate printing with a trigger input that prints only when the trigger is larger than zero.

nodes.label: printk2 opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that prints k-rate variable values only when they change, reducing output verbosity.

nodes.label: printks opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for formatted k-rate printing with a fixed time interval between print outputs.

nodes.label: printf opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for formatted k-rate printing that uses a trigger input rather than a fixed time interval.

nodes.label: genarray opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates arrays with values in a specified range.

nodes.label: sprintfk opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that formats strings at control-rate, updating at each k-cycle.

nodes.label: strchar opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that retrieves the ASCII code number of a character at a specified position in a string.

nodes.label: Audio Vector
nodes.description: A block of ksmps audio samples processed together in a single k-cycle, allowing efficient batch calculation rather than sample-by-sample processing.

nodes.label: Performance Pass
nodes.description: The main execution phase in Csound where instruments generate audio signals through repeated control and audio cycles.

nodes.label: vaget opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode used to extract and examine individual audio samples from within an audio vector during a k-cycle.

nodes.label: k-rate variables
nodes.description: Control-rate variables in Csound that are updated once per control cycle (k-cycle), slower than audio-rate but faster than initialization-rate.

nodes.label: i-rate variables
nodes.description: Initialization-rate variables in Csound that are set once during the initialization pass and remain constant during performance.

nodes.label: a-rate variables
nodes.description: Audio-rate variables in Csound that process samples at the audio sampling rate; optimization involves reusing variables to reduce memory allocation.

nodes.label: Initialization pass
nodes.description: The phase in Csound execution that occurs at the beginning of each note or score event, where i-rate variables are updated.

nodes.label: ksmps parameter
nodes.description: A Csound parameter that specifies the number of audio samples processed in each control cycle.

nodes.label: Øyvind Brandtsegg
nodes.description: Co-author of Csound examples demonstrating initialization and performance pass concepts.

nodes.label: rireturn opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that marks the end of a reinitialization pass, allowing control flow to return to k-rate processing.

nodes.label: Initialization and Performance Pass
nodes.description: Csound execution model distinguishing between initialization pass (i-pass) and performance pass (k-pass and a-pass) for variable handling.

nodes.label: Audio Variables (a-variables)
nodes.description: Csound audio-rate variables that persist across instrument instances unless explicitly reinitialized, potentially causing undesired artifacts.

nodes.label: Control Variables (k-variables)
nodes.description: Csound control-rate variables that can retain values from previous instances if not explicitly initialized.

nodes.label: Fractional Instrument Numbers
nodes.description: Csound feature allowing multiple instances of an instrument to be called with fractional note numbers for individual control.

nodes.label: --sample-accurate option
nodes.description: A Csound 6 command-line option that enables sample-accurate event timing and envelope generation between control cycles.

nodes.label: Sample-accurate processing
nodes.description: A Csound option that enables precise sample-level accuracy in envelope and control rate operations, preventing clicks and timing artifacts.

nodes.label: Sample-by-sample processing
nodes.description: A Csound technique for implementing digital filters and real-time audio processing by iterating through individual audio samples within a control block.

nodes.label: strcpyk opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that performs string assignment at both initialization and performance time.

nodes.label: rnd31 opcode
nodes.description: A Csound bipolar random number generator opcode used to create frequency and amplitude deviations in additive synthesis partials.

nodes.label: Envelope click artifact
nodes.description: An audible click that can occur at the end of short envelopes when ksmps block size causes the envelope to terminate prematurely.

nodes.label: igoto statement
nodes.description: A Csound control flow statement for jumping to a label at initialization time, used to skip initialization code.

nodes.label: Control Cycle
nodes.description: A pass during instrument performance in which all k-rate and a-rate variables are renewed, with duration determined by ksmps.

nodes.label: Fast Fourier Transform (FFT)
nodes.description: Mathematical algorithm used in Csound for real-time spectral processing via phase vocoder opcodes (pvs).

nodes.label: Local Scope
nodes.description: Variable scope in Csound where variables are defined and recognized only within a specific instrument.

nodes.label: Global Scope
nodes.description: Variable scope in Csound where variables are recognized across multiple instruments, defined by prefixing 'g' before the type character.

nodes.label: User-Defined Opcode (UDO)
nodes.description: Custom operations in Csound allowing programmers to define reusable functions like linrnd_low, linrnd_high, and trirnd for probability distributions.

nodes.label: Canonical Csound Manual
nodes.description: Official reference documentation for Csound covering types, constants, variables, and all language features.

nodes.label: Local Variables
nodes.description: Variables in Csound that are scoped to individual instrument instances and do not persist across instruments.

nodes.label: oscils opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates a sine wave oscillator at audio rate with specified amplitude, frequency, and phase.

nodes.label: outs opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode for writing audio signals to the output device, supporting stereo and multi-channel output.

nodes.label: max_k opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that calculates the maximum value of an audio signal over a specified number of control cycles.

nodes.label: Audio Bussing
nodes.description: A technique in Csound where multiple instruments add their audio signals to a global audio variable, similar to a mixing bus.

nodes.label: Global Audio Variables
nodes.description: In Csound, global audio variables (prefixed with 'ga') that function like buses to transfer audio signals between multiple instruments.

nodes.label: chn Opcodes
nodes.description: Csound opcodes (chnset, chnget, chnmix, chnclear) that provide an alternative to traditional g-variables for inter-instrument communication using string-based channel names.

nodes.label: Control Structures
nodes.description: Programming constructs in Csound including if-then-else statements, loops (while, until, loop), and conditional branching at i-time and k-time.

nodes.label: oscil3
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for cubic-interpolated oscillator synthesis.

nodes.label: reson
nodes.description: A bandpass filter opcode in Csound that can produce dramatic variations in amplitude depending on bandwidth value and includes two modes of amplitude balancing.

nodes.label: freeverb
nodes.description: A Csound reverb opcode that processes audio signals with configurable parameters.

nodes.label: pan2
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for stereo panning that distributes audio between left and right channels.

nodes.label: diskin
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that reads sound files and creates audio arrays, with individual channels accessible as array elements.

nodes.label: filenchnls opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode that returns the number of channels in an audio file, used to determine if a file is mono or stereo.

nodes.label: loop opcodes
nodes.description: Family of Csound opcodes (loop_lt, loop_le, loop_gt, loop_ge) for creating counted loops at i-time or k-time with comparison conditions.

nodes.label: if-then-else control structure
nodes.description: Csound conditional branching mechanism that evaluates conditions and executes different code blocks based on the result.

nodes.label: if-goto control structure
nodes.description: Older Csound conditional branching method using labels and goto statements (igoto/kgoto) for both i-time and k-time control flow.

nodes.label: Csound parser
nodes.description: Csound 5.14 introduced a new parser that allows conditional expressions to be written without parentheses.

nodes.label: timeinstk opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode that returns the current k-cycle number from the start of an instrument instance.

nodes.label: loop_lt opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that creates loops by incrementing an index and testing against a maximum value, enabling iterative sequence generation.

nodes.label: loop_le opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode that counts upwards and checks if a value is less than or equal to a threshold.

nodes.label: loop_gt opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode that counts downwards and checks if a value is greater than a threshold.

nodes.label: loop_ge opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode that counts downwards and checks if a value is greater than or equal to a threshold.

nodes.label: while/until loops
nodes.description: Loop control structures introduced in Csound 6 that allow conditional iteration similar to other programming languages.

nodes.label: tableiw opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that writes i-rate values to a function table at a specified index.

nodes.label: Time Loops
nodes.description: Control structures in Csound for triggering events at regular intervals, implemented via metro opcode, timout, internal clock, or self-triggering.

nodes.label: Glissando Effect
nodes.description: A musical effect where pitch slides smoothly from one frequency to another, created using exponential frequency envelopes.

nodes.label: exitnow opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode for exiting the Csound performance, used as a termination method in recursive instrument examples.

nodes.label: GEN01
nodes.description: A Csound function table generator for reading sound files into function tables, suitable for storing impulse responses up to stereo.

nodes.label: GEN02
nodes.description: A GEN Routine in Csound that stores explicitly defined values one by one into a function table.

nodes.label: GEN20
nodes.description: A Csound GEN routine for generating standard window functions including Hamming, Hanning, Bartlett, Blackman, Blackman-Harris, Gaussian, Kaiser, Rectangle, and Sinc windows.

nodes.label: Wavetable Synthesis
nodes.description: A synthesis technique in Csound that periodically cycles through f-tables containing composite waveforms to generate periodic signals.

nodes.label: Sample Playback
nodes.description: Technique of loading audio samples into Csound function tables and playing them back using opcodes like poscil3.

nodes.label: table3 opcode
nodes.description: An interpolating variation of the table opcode in Csound for cubic interpolation table reading.

nodes.label: tablexkt opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode offering ultimate interpolation quality when reading from function tables.

nodes.label: poscil3 opcode
nodes.description: A Csound oscillator with cubic interpolation that reads tables at k-rate or a-rate with high precision and no power-of-two restriction.

nodes.label: ftsave opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that saves function table data to disk, capable of storing multiple tables in a single file.

nodes.label: ftsavek opcode
nodes.description: A k-time opcode in Csound that writes function table contents to a file during performance in text or binary format.

nodes.label: ftload opcode
nodes.description: An i-time opcode in Csound that loads previously saved function table files back into memory.

nodes.label: ftloadk opcode
nodes.description: A k-time opcode in Csound that loads previously saved function table files during performance.

nodes.label: ftaudio opcode
nodes.description: An opcode introduced in Csound 6.12 that writes recorded audio from a function table to a soundfile on disk.

nodes.label: GEN23 routine
nodes.description: A Csound GEN routine that reads numerical data from a text file and populates a function table. Supports various separators including newlines, spaces, tabs, and commas.

nodes.label: GEN05
nodes.description: A GEN routine that creates exponential envelope segments, operating similarly to GEN07 but with exponential rather than linear shapes.

nodes.label: GEN07
nodes.description: A GEN routine that creates function tables in the manner of the linseg opcode, where the user defines segment duration for envelope creation.

nodes.label: GEN08
nodes.description: A GEN routine that creates curved functions forming the smoothest possible line between user-defined breakpoints, useful for window functions and envelope shapes in granular synthesis.

nodes.label: GEN09
nodes.description: A GEN routine for additive synthesis that allows control over partial number and phase in harmonic waveform generation.

nodes.label: GEN11
nodes.description: A Csound function table generator that creates waveforms using the same parameters as gbuzz, offering a more efficient option when performance-time modulation is not needed.

nodes.label: GEN16
nodes.description: A GEN routine for creating envelope functions with user-defined breakpoints and individual segment curvature control (concave, straight, or convex).

nodes.label: GEN17
nodes.description: A GEN routine used to generate histogram-type functions useful in algorithmic composition and work with probabilities.

nodes.label: GEN19
nodes.description: An advanced GEN routine for additive synthesis that extends GEN10 and GEN09 with control over partial strength, number, phase, and DC offset of each partial.

nodes.label: GEN25
nodes.description: A GEN routine for creating exponential envelope segments, operating similarly to GEN05.

nodes.label: GEN27
nodes.description: A GEN routine that creates exponential envelope functions where the user defines absolute time for each breakpoint from the beginning of the envelope.

nodes.label: GEN30
nodes.description: A GEN routine that uses FFT to create band-limited versions of source waveforms, preventing aliasing by limiting partials to those below the Nyquist frequency.

nodes.label: GEN41
nodes.description: A GEN routine used to generate histogram-type functions useful in algorithmic composition and work with probabilities.

nodes.label: GEN42
nodes.description: A GEN routine used to generate histogram-type functions useful in algorithmic composition and work with probabilities.

nodes.label: directory opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that scans a directory and returns an array of file names as strings.

nodes.label: loscilx opcode
nodes.description: A recent Csound opcode for reading multichannel audio files with more than two channels from function tables.

nodes.label: lenarray opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that reports the length of arrays, with support for multidimensional arrays and both init-time and performance-time variants.

nodes.label: fillarray opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that initializes and fills arrays with specified values.

nodes.label: strtod opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that converts strings to numeric values.

nodes.label: minarray opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that returns the smallest element of a numerical array.

nodes.label: maxarray opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that returns the largest element of a numerical array.

nodes.label: sumarray opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that calculates the sum of all elements in an array.

nodes.label: cmp opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that compares array elements to scalars or other arrays using relational operators.

nodes.label: scalearray opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that destructively rescales array values to a new minimum and maximum range.

nodes.label: sorta opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that returns an array with elements sorted in ascending order.

nodes.label: sortd opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that returns an array with elements sorted in descending order.

nodes.label: limit opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that constrains audio or control signals within specified upper and lower limits.

nodes.label: interleave opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that creates a new array by alternating values from two input arrays.

nodes.label: deinterleave opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that splits an array into two arrays by separating alternating values.

nodes.label: slicearray opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that creates a new array from a contiguous or strided slice of an existing array.

nodes.label: trim opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that shortens or lengthens arrays at performance time by reducing size on trigger signals.

nodes.label: copyf2array opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that copies data from a function table to an array.

nodes.label: copya2ftab opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that copies array content to a function table.

nodes.label: tab2array opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that copies a slice of a function table into an array with optional stride support.

nodes.label: pvs2array opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that copies Fast Fourier Transform data from an f-signal into an array.

nodes.label: pvsfromarray opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that copies array content to an f-signal containing FFT data.

nodes.label: pvs2array opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that exports f-signal (frequency-domain signal) data to a k-rate array, storing amplitude-frequency pairs for spectral processing.

nodes.label: pvsfromarray opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that reads modified spectral data from an array back into an f-signal for resynthesis.

nodes.label: reshapearray opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that transforms one-dimensional arrays into two-dimensional arrays and vice versa.

nodes.label: getrow/getcol opcodes
nodes.description: Csound opcodes that extract rows or columns from 2D arrays as 1D arrays.

nodes.label: setrow/setcol opcodes
nodes.description: Csound opcodes that assign 1D arrays as rows or columns of 2D arrays.

nodes.label: getrowlin opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that retrieves rows from 2D arrays with interpolation between adjacent rows for non-integer indices.

nodes.label: printarray opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for printing array contents with customizable formatting.

nodes.label: Spectral High-Pass Filter
nodes.description: A filtering technique implemented in Csound by zeroing the amplitudes of low-frequency FFT bins to remove frequencies below a threshold.

nodes.label: FFT Size
nodes.description: The number of samples used in Fast Fourier Transform analysis; determines frequency resolution and the number of spectral bins (N/2+1 pairs for size N).

nodes.label: Live Events in Csound
nodes.description: The mechanism for triggering instrument instances at various times through score calls, MIDI, OSC, GUI widgets, or from within other instruments using event opcodes.

nodes.label: FLTK widgets
nodes.description: A library of graphical user interface controls integrated into Csound for real-time interactive parameter control.

nodes.label: Initialization Pass
nodes.description: The first phase of Csound execution where i-rate variables are initialized and instruments are set up before the performance cycle begins.

nodes.label: Performance Pass
nodes.description: The phase of Csound execution where control cycles execute instruments repeatedly at k-rate, processing audio in real-time.

nodes.label: timek opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that returns the current control cycle number during the performance pass.

nodes.label: FLTK
nodes.description: A fast, performant, cross-platform graphical user interface library integrated into Csound for building interactive control instruments with panels, sliders, knobs, and other widgets.

nodes.label: foscili opcode
nodes.description: A built-in Csound opcode that implements FM synthesis in a single line of code, taking arguments for amplitude, frequency, carrier/modulator ratio, index, and waveshape.

nodes.label: release opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode that detects the last k-cycle of an instrument instance, useful for implementing fade-out segments.

nodes.label: cpsmidi opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode for receiving MIDI note frequency information, used to set base frequency in MIDI-controlled additive synthesis.

nodes.label: follow opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that outputs a-rate amplitude tracking using a sample-and-hold method with a user-definable period parameter.

nodes.label: Threshold crossing detection
nodes.description: A technique for triggering events based on whether an input signal crosses a defined amplitude threshold from below to above or vice versa.

nodes.label: Event pool
nodes.description: A collection of instrument events generated at init-time within an instrument and executed later according to their timing parameters.

nodes.label: i-time loop
nodes.description: A control structure in Csound that executes calculations at initialization time to generate multiple instrument events.

nodes.label: Real-time event triggering
nodes.description: Methods for triggering instrument events dynamically during performance using MIDI, widgets, or live score input.

nodes.label: event_i opcode
nodes.description: An i-rate Csound opcode that triggers instrument events once at initialization, used for calling other instruments or building function tables.

nodes.label: schedulek
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that schedules instrument events and allows passing strings as p-fields.

nodes.label: metro
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates trigger pulses at a specified frequency (Hz) to control grain density in granular synthesis.

nodes.label: scoreline
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that allows passing strings as p-fields in score events.

nodes.label: compileorc
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that compiles instrument definitions from a saved .orc orchestra file.

nodes.label: compilestr
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that compiles instrument definitions contained in a string at runtime.

nodes.label: oscils
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for oscillator synthesis.

nodes.label: oscilb
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for oscillator synthesis (used in example code).

nodes.label: FiltFb
nodes.description: A user-defined opcode that combines filtering and feedback delay, demonstrated in the Csound manual with resonant filtering and variable delay time.

nodes.label: vdelayx
nodes.description: A variable delay opcode in Csound that uses seconds as the time unit and allows interpolation sample count configuration between 4 and 1024.

nodes.label: xin
nodes.description: A Csound statement used within UDO definitions to receive input arguments from the calling instrument.

nodes.label: xout
nodes.description: A Csound statement used within UDO definitions to return output values to the calling instrument, analogous to outlets in Max/MSP or Pure Data.

nodes.label: Filtered Delay with Feedback
nodes.description: A signal processing technique combining resonant filtering, variable delay, and feedback to create complex time-varying timbral effects.

nodes.label: Opus123_FiltFb
nodes.description: A user-defined opcode that embeds the FiltFb UDO, demonstrating nested UDO composition with randomized filter frequency and delay time.

nodes.label: setksmps Feature
nodes.description: A Csound feature allowing local modification of the ksmps (samples per control cycle) value within a user-defined opcode, enabling finer control resolution.

nodes.label: #include Statement
nodes.description: A Csound preprocessor directive that allows loading user-defined opcode definitions from external text files into a .csd file.

nodes.label: UDO Overloading
nodes.description: A Csound feature allowing multiple user-defined opcodes to share the same name with different input/output types, with Csound selecting the appropriate version based on context.

nodes.label: Default Arguments in UDOs
nodes.description: A Csound feature providing shorthand notation for default parameter values in user-defined opcodes, such as 'o' for i-rate 0, 'p' for i-rate 1, and 'O', 'P', 'V', 'J' for k-rate defaults.

nodes.label: reson Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound built-in opcode implementing a resonant filter with center frequency and Q factor control.

nodes.label: vdelayx Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound built-in opcode implementing variable delay with interpolation, used in the FiltFb example for time-varying delay effects.

nodes.label: buzz Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound built-in opcode generating a band-limited buzz waveform, used as a sound source in the third instrument example.

nodes.label: Array Operations
nodes.description: Csound features for manipulating arrays of values, including permutation and random shuffling operations.

nodes.label: Recursive Synthesis
nodes.description: A synthesis approach where a UDO calls itself iteratively to generate multiple partials until a termination condition is met.

nodes.label: State Variable Filter
nodes.description: A digital filter design that produces lowpass, bandpass, and highpass outputs simultaneously using bilinear transform and sample-by-sample processing.

nodes.label: Csound Macro System
nodes.description: A preprocessor feature in Csound that allows code blocks to be defined once and referenced multiple times using macro names, with support for parameterized macros with arguments.

nodes.label: Bilinear Transform
nodes.description: A digital filter design technique used to pre-warp cutoff frequencies in state variable filters for accurate frequency response.

nodes.label: wgpluck2 opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing waveguide plucked string synthesis, used to simulate bass guitar and similar plucked instruments.

nodes.label: Functional Syntax
nodes.description: A programming style in Csound6.1 that allows opcodes to be nested directly as function arguments rather than storing intermediate results in variables.

nodes.label: FLTK GUI
nodes.description: A graphical user interface toolkit integrated with Csound for creating complex control panels with repeated sections.

nodes.label: Functional Syntax
nodes.description: A programming style in Csound that uses function notation with explicit rate declarations (:a, :k, :i) to specify at which rate opcodes perform.

nodes.label: Jean Baptiste Joseph Fourier
nodes.description: Mathematician (1768–1830) who theorized that any function can be decomposed into a sum of simple harmonic motion, foundational to Fourier analysis and the phase vocoder.

nodes.label: mpulse
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates a train of impulses, used as an alternative sound source in subtractive synthesis.

nodes.label: Fourier's Theorem
nodes.description: Mathematical principle stating that any periodic function can be described as a sum of weighted sine waves with frequencies that are integer multiples of a fundamental.

nodes.label: GEN09 routine
nodes.description: A Csound GEN routine that allows control of frequency multiplier and phase (0-360°) of each partial in addition to amplitude, enabling inharmonic waveform creation.

nodes.label: cpspch opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode that converts pitch notation (note and octave divided into 12 parts) into frequency in hertz.

nodes.label: ampdbfs opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that converts decibel values relative to full scale (dBFS) to linear amplitude.

nodes.label: Introductory Catalogue of Computer Synthesized Sounds
nodes.description: 1969 work by Jean-Claude Risset documenting computer-synthesized sounds, including bell-like timbres used as reference material for additive synthesis examples.

nodes.label: Impulse Wave
nodes.description: Waveform created by adding harmonics of equal strength, demonstrating basic additive synthesis principles.

nodes.label: Spectral Dynamics
nodes.description: Technique of creating time-varying spectral content by triggering individual partial sub-instruments, enabling dynamic control of harmonic evolution.

nodes.label: Random Variations in Synthesis
nodes.description: Method of introducing natural-sounding deviations in frequency, amplitude, and duration of partials to simulate characteristics of acoustic instruments.

nodes.label: Risset Bell
nodes.description: A classic additive synthesis instrument created by Jean Claude Risset that models the complex harmonic evolution of a bell sound, implemented as a Csound UDO opcode.

nodes.label: buzz opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates a signal with equal-strength harmonics for any desired frequency, providing a workaround for pulse-train limitations in sampled systems.

nodes.label: hsboscil opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for additive synthesis where all partials are spaced an octave apart, with a masking window that can be shifted to enable spectral morphing.

nodes.label: moogladder opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing a 4-pole/24dB per octave resonant lowpass filter with authentic vintage character, inspired by Minimoog synthesizer design.

nodes.label: Minimoog synthesizer
nodes.description: A classic analog synthesizer from 1970 that inspired the design of subtractive synthesis examples in Csound, featuring two oscillators and a resonant lowpass filter.

nodes.label: hilbert opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that performs Hilbert filtering, used for frequency shifting in the hsboscil example to warp intervals between partials.

nodes.label: Spectral morphing
nodes.description: Technique of evolving from one instrumental timbre to another through parametric interpolation. Chowning used this technique in FM synthesis to create smooth transitions between different instrument timbres.

nodes.label: Risset glissando
nodes.description: A pitch-shifting effect created by shifting the entire spectrum up or down independent of the masking window location, as implemented in hsboscil.

nodes.label: mididefault opcode
nodes.description: A Csound MIDI interoperability opcode that allows instruments to be controlled from either the score or a MIDI keyboard with default p-field substitution.

nodes.label: butlp opcode
nodes.description: A Csound lowpass filter based on Butterworth filter design that produces a sharp cutoff slope with slightly greater CPU overhead.

nodes.label: buthp opcode
nodes.description: A Csound Butterworth highpass filter opcode with steep cutoff slopes and minimal ripple at the cutoff frequency.

nodes.label: ntrpol opcode
nodes.description: Csound interpolation opcode used to morph between two audio sources (pulse and pink noise) in real-time during vowel synthesis.

nodes.label: Bandpass Filter
nodes.description: A filter that allows frequencies within a specific band to pass while attenuating frequencies outside that band, used in parallel arrangements for timbral synthesis.

nodes.label: Hand Bell Analysis
nodes.description: Spectral analysis data of hand bell timbres used to derive frequency ratios for parallel filter banks in subtractive synthesis.

nodes.label: Formant Filtering
nodes.description: Technique using bandpass filters tuned to spectral resonances (formants) to simulate vowel sounds and the resonating properties of the human vocal tract.

nodes.label: Pulse Waveform
nodes.description: Periodic waveform source used to approximate human vocal cord buzzing in vowel synthesis, generated via vco2 opcode.

nodes.label: GEN07 Function Table
nodes.description: Csound linear break-point function table used to store formant data (frequency, bandwidth, intensity) for different vowels and voice types.

nodes.label: Csound Manual
nodes.description: Official Csound documentation containing formant data for simulating vowel sounds across different voice types (bass, tenor, alto, soprano, counter-tenor).

nodes.label: butbp opcode
nodes.description: Csound Butterworth bandpass filter opcode mentioned as an alternative to reson for vowel synthesis.

nodes.label: Vowel Synthesis
nodes.description: Technique for synthesizing human vowel sounds using formant filtering with five resonant peaks to simulate mouth and head resonance.

nodes.label: Alex Hofmann
nodes.description: Author of multiple Csound FM synthesis examples in the FLOSS Manual, including trumpet, bell, and feedback modulation implementations.

nodes.label: foscil opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that implements FM synthesis by automatically computing carrier and modulator frequencies from a fundamental frequency and ratio factors.

nodes.label: Index of Modulation
nodes.description: A parameter defined as the ratio of frequency deviation amplitude to modulating frequency (I = AM : FM), controlling the bandwidth and number of significant sidebands in FM synthesis.

nodes.label: Carrier Frequency
nodes.description: The primary oscillator frequency in FM synthesis that is modulated by the output of a modulator oscillator to produce complex timbres.

nodes.label: Modulator Frequency
nodes.description: The frequency (FM) of the oscillator that modulates the carrier frequency in FM synthesis, determining how frequently the deviation occurs.

nodes.label: Frequency Deviation
nodes.description: The amount by which the modulator alters the carrier frequency, measured in Hz and determined by the modulator amplitude.

nodes.label: oscil opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode for generating audio-rate oscillations from a function table. Used to generate individual harmonics in tone-wheel organ and FM synthesis instruments.

nodes.label: Marijana Janevska
nodes.description: Co-author of Csound FM synthesis examples in the FLOSS Manual, including parallel and multiple carrier FM implementations.

nodes.label: Yamaha DX7
nodes.description: A commercial FM synthesizer that implements phase modulation rather than classic frequency modulation, allowing feedback algorithms and featuring over 200 performance parameters.

nodes.label: Multiple Modulator FM
nodes.description: An FM configuration where more than one oscillator modulates a single carrier oscillator, with parallel and serial configurations possible.

nodes.label: Multiple Carrier FM
nodes.description: An FM configuration where one modulator simultaneously modulates two or more carrier oscillators.

nodes.label: Sabelithe
nodes.description: John Chowning's first FM composition dating from 1966 to 1971, featuring a dramatic moment around 4 minutes 50 seconds where a drum morphs into a trumpet using spectral morphing.

nodes.label: powershape opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that performs waveshaping by raising samples to a user-defined power exponent while retaining polarity in the negative domain.

nodes.label: distort opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode authored by Barry Vercoe that waveshapes signals using a transfer function with soft-knee compression and dynamic input gain control.

nodes.label: GENtanh
nodes.description: A Csound GEN routine that creates hyperbolic tangent (tanh) transfer functions for use in waveshaping operations.

nodes.label: Soft-knee Compression
nodes.description: A compression technique applied before waveshaping in the distort opcode to improve spectral behavior and control dynamic range.

nodes.label: Hyperbolic Tangent Function
nodes.description: A common transfer function used in waveshaping that produces an S-curve; adjustable start and end values control the aggressiveness of distortion.

nodes.label: Extended Csound
nodes.description: A real-time version of Csound developed by Barry Vercoe using Analog Devices 21060 floating-point DSP accelerators.

nodes.label: CHANT
nodes.description: An original program that implemented FOF synthesis with formant motion controlled by ifmode parameter, serving as the model for Csound's fof opcode.

nodes.label: Sawtooth Waveform
nodes.description: A waveform used in the pulse oscillator implementation, generated using the oscili opcode at the same frequency as the desired pulse wave.

nodes.label: grain3 opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for granular synthesis that supports randomization of phase and pitch within grains, with parameters for formant frequency, grain duration, and density.

nodes.label: Physical Modelling
nodes.description: A synthesis approach that models physical processes and time-varying systems to produce sound, focusing on mathematical descriptions rather than wave tables and oscillators.

nodes.label: Mass-Spring Model
nodes.description: A classical physical modelling technique that represents oscillating processes in nature as connections of masses and springs, producing sine-wave-like outputs through iterative state calculations.

nodes.label: Martin Neukom
nodes.description: Author of the ambisonics UDO examples in the Csound FLOSS Manual demonstrating encoding, decoding, and distance-based spatial audio techniques.

nodes.label: Signale Systeme Klangsynthese
nodes.description: A 2003 book by Martin Neukom covering signal systems and sound synthesis, including the mass-spring model explanation used in the Csound manual.

nodes.label: Bartlett Window
nodes.description: A window function used as an amplitude envelope for grains in granular synthesis, employed in grain3 randomization examples.

nodes.label: Balthasar van der Pol
nodes.description: Dutch electrical engineer who derived the Van der Pol differential equation describing nonlinear dynamics of vacuum tube circuits.

nodes.label: Van der Pol Oscillator
nodes.description: A nonlinear self-sustained oscillator that can be synchronized by an external force, characterized by a natural frequency and nonlinearity factor. The synchronization range increases with the nonlinearity factor and excitation amplitude.

nodes.label: Mass-Spring System
nodes.description: A simple physical model where acceleration is proportional to deflection, used as a basic example of physical modeling synthesis in Csound.

nodes.label: Damping
nodes.description: A parameter in physical models proportional to velocity that reduces oscillation amplitude over time, implemented by multiplying velocity by (1 - d) at each time step.

nodes.label: Nonlinear Resonator
nodes.description: A resonant system where acceleration is an arbitrary nonlinear function of position, allowing for frequency-dependent behavior and complex spectral content.

nodes.label: Self-Sustained Oscillator
nodes.description: An oscillator that compensates for energy loss through an internal energy source, such as the Van der Pol oscillator with negative damping when |x| < 1.

nodes.label: setksmps
nodes.description: A Csound statement that sets the control rate sample period within an instrument, necessary for sample-by-sample physical modeling calculations.

nodes.label: Waveguide
nodes.description: A mechanism that limits the extent of oscillations, such as a vibrating string fixed at both ends or a pipe, used in physical modeling to emulate these physical constraints through delay.

nodes.label: wgbow opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that implements an emulation of a bowed string using waveguide physical modeling, with parameters for bow pressure and bowing position modulation at k-rate.

nodes.label: wgbrass opcode
nodes.description: A Csound waveguide opcode for modeling brass instruments, where tone production depends on the relationship between intended pitch and lip tension.

nodes.label: wgbowedbar opcode
nodes.description: A Csound waveguide opcode for modeling bowed bars, noted for being unstable and requiring caution during real-time experimentation to protect ears and loudspeakers.

nodes.label: barmodel opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode by Stefan Bilbao that models struck metal bars, wooden bars, tubular bells, and other resonant inharmonic objects with parameters for stiffness, strike position, and strike velocity.

nodes.label: Stefan Bilbao
nodes.description: Designer of the barmodel opcode for physical modeling of struck metal bars and resonant objects in Csound.

nodes.label: clip opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode used for amplitude limiting and protection against loud signals during real-time physical modeling experimentation.

nodes.label: butlp opcode
nodes.description: A Butterworth low-pass filter opcode in Csound used for filtering physical modeling synthesis output.

nodes.label: pareq opcode
nodes.description: A parametric equalizer opcode in Csound that adds the capability of creating low and high shelving filtering.

nodes.label: Rob Shaw
nodes.description: Co-developer of scanned synthesis, working at Interval Research between 1998 and 1999.

nodes.label: Bill Verplank
nodes.description: Co-developer of scanned synthesis, working at Interval Research between 1998 and 1999.

nodes.label: Interval Research
nodes.description: Research organization where scanned synthesis was developed by Verplank, Shaw, and Mathews.

nodes.label: PhISEM
nodes.description: Physically Inspired Stochastic Event Modeling; a set of algorithms in Csound that mimic percussion instruments relying on collisions between sound-producing objects.

nodes.label: Matt Gilliard
nodes.description: Developer of the scantable opcode for quick scanned synthesis implementation in Csound.

nodes.label: Christopher Saunders
nodes.description: Author of multiple Csound examples demonstrating scanned synthesis, scan trajectories, and amplitude control techniques.

nodes.label: scantable opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for scanned synthesis that uses amplitude, frequency, and profile f-tables to generate dynamically evolving timbral spectra.

nodes.label: tambourine opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing PhISEM physical modeling of a tambourine with parameters for amplitude, decay, number of timbrels, damping, and resonant frequencies.

nodes.label: bamboo opcode
nodes.description: A Csound physical modeling opcode that simulates the sound of a bamboo instrument.

nodes.label: sleighbells opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing PhISEM physical modeling of sleighbells.

nodes.label: scantable opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that synthesizes time-varying timbre using a table lookup oscillator or animates an f-table for use in other Csound opcodes.

nodes.label: scanu opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that sets a dynamic wavetable into motion, taking 18 arguments to configure mass-spring models with flexible scanned synthesis capabilities.

nodes.label: scans opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that works in tandem with scanu to scan dynamic tables in ways a table-lookup oscillator cannot.

nodes.label: Paris Smaragdis
nodes.description: Developer who wrote multiple random number generator opcodes for Csound in 1995, including betarnd, bexprnd, cauchy, exprnd, gauss, linrand, pcauchy, poisson, trirand, unirand, and weibull.

nodes.label: Stephen Yi
nodes.description: Creator of the Scanned Matrix editor included in the Blue frontend for Csound.

nodes.label: Scanned Matrix
nodes.description: A convention describing the shape of connections of masses in a mass-spring model, allowing non-linear connections between masses to create multi-dimensional string behaviors.

nodes.label: GEN23
nodes.description: A Csound function generator that reads ASCII files to populate f-tables, used for loading scan trajectory data like spiral patterns.

nodes.label: GEN21
nodes.description: A Csound GEN routine for creating f-tables with various random distributions including Uniform, Linear, Triangular, Exponential, Gaussian, Cauchy, Beta, Weibull, and Poisson distributions.

nodes.label: dcblock2 opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that removes DC offset from audio signals.

nodes.label: adsr opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode implementing the classic ADSR (Attack, Decay, Sustain, Release) envelope, producing control values between 0 and 1.

nodes.label: f-table
nodes.description: An array of floating-point values in Csound stored in RAM for sound generation, created by GEN routines and typically sized as powers of two (2^n or 2^n+1).

nodes.label: Scan Trajectory
nodes.description: A table-based specification of the order in which indices of a scanned synthesis matrix are read, enabling non-sequential access patterns like spiral or reverse reading.

nodes.label: Audio Injection
nodes.description: A technique in scanned synthesis where audio-rate signals are used to add motion to the mass-spring model instead of using hammer-based excitation.

nodes.label: cosseg opcode
nodes.description: A recently introduced Csound envelope opcode that applies cosine transfer functions to envelope segments, providing smooth gradual building and arrival without polarity restrictions.

nodes.label: Envelope design
nodes.description: The process of shaping amplitude, pitch, or other parameters in sound synthesis using attack, sustain, and release segments.

nodes.label: Function table envelope
nodes.description: Envelope shapes stored in Csound function tables and read by oscillators, allowing custom envelope shapes not possible with standard opcodes.

nodes.label: Exponential curve
nodes.description: A non-linear envelope curve that provides more natural dynamic response than linear segments when applied to amplitude control.

nodes.label: Cosine transfer function
nodes.description: A mathematical function applied to envelope segments in cosseg to create smooth gradual transitions without polarity restrictions.

nodes.label: lpshold opcode
nodes.description: A Csound looping opcode that generates envelopes with held constant break points, used to create looping basslines in the style of a Roland TB303.

nodes.label: loopseg opcode
nodes.description: A Csound looping opcode that defines looping envelopes with linear segments, allowing modulation at k-rate.

nodes.label: looptseg opcode
nodes.description: An elaboration of loopseg that allows definition of individual segment shape (convex, linear, or concave) using type parameters, crucial for TB303-style filter envelopes.

nodes.label: Roland TB303
nodes.description: A synthesizer whose design characteristics, including note on/off, hold, and filter envelope decay shaping, are emulated using Csound looping opcodes.

nodes.label: Envelope generation
nodes.description: The technique of shaping amplitude and filter characteristics over time to emulate acoustic instrument behavior and create musical gesture.

nodes.label: Panning and spatialization
nodes.description: The spatial positioning of sounds in stereo or multichannel space to guide hearing and create musical meaning through location.

nodes.label: Panning
nodes.description: A spatialization technique that locates sounds between left and right speakers using amplitude modulation, with various methods including equal power, square root, and sine-based approaches.

nodes.label: Routing
nodes.description: A spatialization technique that connects an audio signal directly to one speaker, offering binary left-or-right positioning.

nodes.label: 3D Binaural Encoding
nodes.description: A spatialization technique using spectral data files (HRTF) to simulate head-related filtering and inter-aural delay effects for 3D spatial audio.

nodes.label: hrtfmove2 opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for 3D binaural audio reproduction that positions a sound source in three-dimensional space around the listener using HRTF transfer functions.

nodes.label: Philipp Henkel
nodes.description: Co-author of Csound examples demonstrating routing and spatialization techniques.

nodes.label: Equal Power Panning
nodes.description: A panning method using square root functions or sine/cosine curves to maintain constant perceived loudness as sound moves between speakers.

nodes.label: Azimuth
nodes.description: The horizontal direction of a sound source expressed as an angle in binaural encoding, used in HRTF-based spatialization.

nodes.label: Elevation
nodes.description: The vertical angle by which a sound deviates from the horizontal plane in binaural encoding, used in HRTF-based spatialization.

nodes.label: hrtfmove2 opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that applies binaural 3D processing using head-related transfer functions to create stereo output with spatial positioning via azimuth and elevation parameters.

nodes.label: vbaplsinit opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode placed in the orchestra header that defines loudspeaker positions in degrees for VBAP spatialization.

nodes.label: outch opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that directs audio to specific output channels, allowing dynamic speaker configuration changes at k-rate and non-sequential channel assignment.

nodes.label: Ville Pulkki
nodes.description: Researcher who introduced the spread parameter for VBAP (Vector Base Amplitude Panning) to control the distribution of sound across speakers.

nodes.label: vbapg
nodes.description: Csound opcode variant of VBAP that returns the gains (amplitudes) of speakers instead of the audio signal itself.

nodes.label: First-order Ambisonics
nodes.description: Ambisonics encoding using four basic dimensions (w, x, y, z) requiring at least 4 speakers for correct projection.

nodes.label: Second-order Ambisonics
nodes.description: Ambisonics encoding with additional directional components (r, s, t, u, v) requiring at least 6 speakers (9 for 3D) for correct projection.

nodes.label: Third-order Ambisonics
nodes.description: Ambisonics encoding with additional directional components (k, l, m, n, o, p, q) requiring at least 8 speakers (16 for 3D) for correct projection.

nodes.label: Ambisonics2D
nodes.description: A two-dimensional analogy to Ambisonics that encodes only sound waves in the horizontal plane, requiring fewer channels than full three-dimensional Ambisonics.

nodes.label: Zak space
nodes.description: A Csound memory buffer used to store and accumulate B-format channels across multiple instruments before decoding.

nodes.label: Amplitude panning
nodes.description: A panning technique used in Ambisonics decoding that positions sound sources by considering only the direction to the source.

nodes.label: Ambisonics Equivalent Panning (AEP)
nodes.description: A low-cost method to calculate loudspeaker signals directly from spatial coordinates at arbitrary order without requiring B-format encoding.

nodes.label: ambi2D_encode_n
nodes.description: Csound UDO that encodes a monophonic sound source into 2D ambisonics B-format channels at any order with azimuth control.

nodes.label: ambi2D_decode_basic
nodes.description: Csound UDO that decodes 2D ambisonics B-format to multiple speaker outputs using basic decoding without phase correction.

nodes.label: ambi2D_dec_inph
nodes.description: Csound UDO implementing in-phase decoding for 2D ambisonics, using weighted factors and normalization to avoid negative amplitudes and phase inversion.

nodes.label: ambi2D_enc_dist_n
nodes.description: Csound UDO encoding ambisonics with distance correction, simulating sound source proximity through amplitude reduction and filtering.

nodes.label: In-phase Decoding
nodes.description: Ambisonics decoding technique using weighting factors dependent on order to prevent negative amplitudes and phase inversion in loudspeaker signals.

nodes.label: za variables
nodes.description: Csound global audio variables used for inter-instrument communication, employed in ambisonics examples to pass B-format channels between encoding and decoding instruments.

nodes.label: Distance Simulation in Ambisonics
nodes.description: Technique for encoding spatial cues of sound source distance through amplitude reduction, air absorption filtering, and direct/indirect sound ratio manipulation.

nodes.label: Ambisonics UDOs
nodes.description: User-defined opcodes in Csound for encoding and decoding Ambisonics B-format channels up to 8th order.

nodes.label: Spherical Harmonics
nodes.description: Mathematical functions representing direction to virtual sound sources, used to compute Ambisonics B-format channels in semi-normalised form.

nodes.label: Lowpass Filter
nodes.description: A filter that attenuates high frequencies while passing low frequencies, demonstrated in Csound using convolution with impulse response files at various cutoff frequencies (3 kHz, 1 kHz, 300 Hz).

nodes.label: Cartesian Coordinates
nodes.description: X, Y, Z coordinate system used to define sound source positions before transformation to polar/spherical coordinates.

nodes.label: Polar Coordinates
nodes.description: Azimuth and distance representation used in 2D Ambisonics encoding, derived from Cartesian coordinates via xy_to_ad UDO.

nodes.label: Spherical Coordinates
nodes.description: 3D coordinate system using radial distance r, elevation δ, and azimuth angle θ for positioning virtual sound sources.

nodes.label: fout opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode for writing B-format channels to sound files.

nodes.label: zawm opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode for writing audio to zak space variables used in Ambisonics encoding.

nodes.label: zar opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode for reading audio from zak space variables in Ambisonics decoding.

nodes.label: Ambisonics Equivalent Panning (AEP)
nodes.description: Panning function combining Ambisonics encoding and in-phase decoding to calculate gain for speakers based on distance to virtual sound source, with formula P(γ,m) = (1/2 + 1/2 cos γ)^m.

nodes.label: Distance Encoding
nodes.description: Ambisonics technique encoding virtual sound source distance using gain functions and Doppler effects for realistic spatial simulation.

nodes.label: Doppler Effect
nodes.description: The frequency shift caused by the rotation of the Leslie speaker horn and scoop, simulated in Csound using delay lines with variable time-delay taps.

nodes.label: Highpass Filter
nodes.description: A filter that attenuates low frequencies while passing high frequencies, demonstrated in Csound using convolution with impulse response files at various cutoff frequencies.

nodes.label: bqrez opcode
nodes.description: A Csound multi-mode filter that can function as a resonant highpass filter (mode 1) or resonant lowpass filter among other configurations.

nodes.label: Moog synthesizer
nodes.description: An analog synthesizer that was among the most advanced sound facilities at well-equipped electronic music centers in the late 1970s.

nodes.label: Resonance / Q
nodes.description: An exaggerated ripple at the cutoff frequency of a filter, controlled by the Q factor to emphasize frequencies near the cutoff point.

nodes.label: AEP UDO
nodes.description: A Csound User-Defined Opcode for ambisonics encoding and panning that supports any order integer or fractional values.

nodes.label: bqrez opcode
nodes.description: A multimode filter opcode in Csound that provides several different filter types within a single opcode, selectable via an i-rate input argument.

nodes.label: butbp opcode
nodes.description: A Butterworth-based bandpass filter opcode in Csound that allows control over cutoff frequency and bandwidth.

nodes.label: vcomb opcode
nodes.description: A comb filter opcode in Csound that allows for performance time modulation of the loop time parameter.

nodes.label: clfilt opcode
nodes.description: A multimode filter opcode in Csound offering additional filter controls such as filter design and number of poles to create unusual sound filters.

nodes.label: rbjeq opcode
nodes.description: A comprehensive multimode filter opcode in Csound including highpass, lowpass, bandpass, bandreject, peaking, low-shelving and high-shelving filter types.

nodes.label: statevar opcode
nodes.description: A filter opcode in Csound that outputs from four filter types simultaneously—highpass, lowpass, bandpass and bandreject—allowing smooth morphing between them.

nodes.label: svfilter opcode
nodes.description: A filter opcode in Csound similar to statevar but with just highpass, lowpass and bandpass filter types.

nodes.label: moogladder
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing the Moog ladder filter, a classic analog filter design.

nodes.label: moogvcf
nodes.description: Csound opcode implementing a Moog-style voltage-controlled filter with cutoff frequency and resonance control.

nodes.label: lpf18
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing an 18dB low-pass filter.

nodes.label: Delay Effect
nodes.description: A DSP technique using buffers to create echo, chorus, flanging, pitch shifting, and filtering effects.

nodes.label: Anton Kholomiov
nodes.description: Author of Csound filter comparison example based on wobble bass sound design.

nodes.label: Jacob Joaquin
nodes.description: Author of 'Exploring Analog Synth Techniques in Csound' tutorial and The Csound FAQ; co-author of The Csound FrontPage.

nodes.label: butterlp
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing a Butterworth low-pass filter.

nodes.label: mvclpf1
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing a Moog VCF ladder filter variant (mvclpf1).

nodes.label: Delay with Feedback
nodes.description: A digital audio effect where delayed signal is mixed back into the input to create multiple echoes that gradually attenuate based on a feedback ratio.

nodes.label: Tap Delay Line
nodes.description: A delay effect technique that reads audio from within a delay buffer at variable positions using opcodes like deltap, deltapi, deltap3, or deltapx.

nodes.label: Multi-tap Delay
nodes.description: A delay effect using multiple taps within a single delay buffer to create multiple delayed copies of the input signal at different delay times.

nodes.label: deltap opcode
nodes.description: A Csound unit generator that reads from a delay line at a fixed tap point, used to extract multiple delayed signals from a single delay buffer.

nodes.label: deltapi opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that reads from a variable delay line at a time specified by a control or audio-rate variable, enabling pitch shifting and time-stretching effects.

nodes.label: deltapx opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for tapping a delay buffer with the highest quality interpolation, highest computational expense.

nodes.label: vdel opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode group for variable delay lines that establishes one delay line per opcode, useful for one or few taps.

nodes.label: nreverb opcode
nodes.description: A Csound reverb opcode based on the Schroeder reverb design with parameters for reverb time and high frequency diffusion.

nodes.label: Zak patching system
nodes.description: A Csound patching system similar to a recording studio patch bay that allows audio routing between instruments using numbered channels at a, k, or i-rate.

nodes.label: zakinit opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that initializes zak storage space for both audio and control rate channels.

nodes.label: zawm opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that writes and mixes audio into a zak channel.

nodes.label: zdf_ladder opcode
nodes.description: A Csound filter opcode implementing a zero-delay feedback ladder filter.

nodes.label: Flanger effect
nodes.description: A modulation effect historically created by playing two tape recordings of the same material with one tape speed-varied, creating comb-filter-like sweeping effects.

nodes.label: Reverberation
nodes.description: An audio effect applied after the frequency modulation instrument in the signal flow, with user-controllable delay parameter.

nodes.label: zar opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode for reading from an audio channel, used to input signals into effect instruments.

nodes.label: zacl opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that clears zak audio channels after use.

nodes.label: Schroeder reverb design
nodes.description: A reverb algorithm design proposed in the early 1960s by physicist Manfred Schroeder using parallel comb filters followed by allpass filters.

nodes.label: Manfred Schroeder
nodes.description: A physicist who proposed the Schroeder reverb design in the early 1960s, a foundational algorithm for digital reverberation.

nodes.label: Allpass filter
nodes.description: A modified comb filter with uniform frequency response and frequency-specific phase response, often deployed in series to accumulate reflections from one filter into the next.

nodes.label: Chebyshev Polynomial
nodes.description: Mathematical functions used in waveshaping synthesis to create harmonic distortion and spectral transformation.

nodes.label: Bit Depth Reduction
nodes.description: A waveshaping technique where a small function table without interpolation reduces the effective bit depth of a signal, creating a staircase quantization effect.

nodes.label: cent
nodes.description: Csound function returning the frequency multiplier for a given number of cents, enabling microtonal pitch calculations.

nodes.label: ftlen
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that returns the length of a function table.

nodes.label: Csound 6.14 Release
nodes.description: Version of Csound used as the basis for the opcode overview in the FLOSS Manual, released in May 2020.

nodes.label: Time Compression
nodes.description: A granular synthesis technique that decreases the duration over which a pointer moves through a sound file.

nodes.label: rnd31 opcode
nodes.description: A bipolar random generator opcode in Csound that outputs values within a specified range for creating random deviations in granular synthesis parameters.

nodes.label: fox.wav
nodes.description: A test sound file included in the Csound HTML Manual containing the phrase 'the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog'.

nodes.label: sndwarp
nodes.description: Csound opcode for time stretching and pitch shifting that operates in two modes: stretch factor mode and pointer control mode, with configurable grain size and density parameters.

nodes.label: Software Channels
nodes.description: Csound mechanism for inter-instrument communication using named channels with chnset, chnmix, and chnclear opcodes to route audio and control signals between instruments.

nodes.label: granule
nodes.description: High-level Csound unit generator for granular synthesis developed by Allan S. C. Lee with 22 parameters for controlling grain characteristics, supporting multiple voices and random offset.

nodes.label: Live Granular Synthesis
nodes.description: Application of granular synthesis to real-time audio input by continuously writing live input to a circular buffer table and reading from it with variable delay and transposition.

nodes.label: sndwarp opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for time-stretching and pitch-shifting audio using granular synthesis with pointer position control.

nodes.label: moogvcf2 opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing a resonant lowpass filter for audio processing.

nodes.label: grain opcode
nodes.description: Csound unit generator for granular synthesis written by Paris Smaragdis that uses a function table as source with grain density controlled by xdens parameter.

nodes.label: grain2 opcode
nodes.description: A relatively simple Csound opcode for granular synthesis that requires grain frequency, grain size, waveform table, envelope waveform, random frequency variation, and grain overlap parameters.

nodes.label: Bjørn Houdorf
nodes.description: Author of a granular synthesis example using the grain opcode in Csound.

nodes.label: pconvolve
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for real-time convolution using the uniformly partitioned overlap-save algorithm with minimal latency, accepting impulse response files directly without pre-loading into function tables.

nodes.label: ftconv
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for function table convolution that requires impulse responses to be stored in function tables first, allowing transformations before convolution and supporting multichannel files.

nodes.label: GEN52
nodes.description: A Csound function table generator designed for working with multichannel files in convolution operations.

nodes.label: Overlap-Save Algorithm
nodes.description: A partitioned convolution algorithm used by pconvolve that minimizes latency in real-time convolution processing.

nodes.label: convolve
nodes.description: Csound opcode that uses FFT-based convolution, more efficient than direct convolution when the impulse response is long or comparable in length to the input signal.

nodes.label: cross2
nodes.description: A Csound opcode related to FFT-based cross synthesis rather than traditional convolution reverb.

nodes.label: liveconv opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode that extends ftconv to allow dynamic reloading of impulse response tables partition by partition without artifacts.

nodes.label: Fast Fourier Transform
nodes.description: Computationally efficient version of the Digital Fourier Transform using power-of-two window sizes, implemented in all audio programming languages.

nodes.label: Oeyving Brandtsegg
nodes.description: Co-author of Csound liveconv example demonstrating dynamic impulse response reloading.

nodes.label: Sigurd Saue
nodes.description: Author of Arduino sketch example demonstrating serial transmission of multiple analog and digital inputs with variable-length integer handling.

nodes.label: J.B. Fourier
nodes.description: Mathematician (1768-1830) who developed the Fourier Transform method for approximating periodic functions using trigonometric functions.

nodes.label: Digital Fourier Transform
nodes.description: Fourier Transform adapted for digital audio with finite amplitude values per frame, offering computational simplifications over analog FT.

nodes.label: Time-Frequency Tradeoff
nodes.description: The fundamental tradeoff in FFT analysis where larger window sizes provide better frequency resolution but worse time resolution, and vice versa.

nodes.label: pvstanal
nodes.description: Csound opcode that performs phase vocoder analysis on audio signals, extracting spectral data with parameters for amplitude scaling, pitch scaling, FFT size, and overlap.

nodes.label: von Hann Window
nodes.description: A window function used in FFT analysis, selectable in Csound pvsanal with iwintype parameter value 1, also known as Hanning window.

nodes.label: Frequency Resolution
nodes.description: The precision with which FFT analysis can distinguish between different frequencies, directly related to window size and fundamental frequency of the analysis window.

nodes.label: F-signal
nodes.description: Frequency-domain signal type in Csound phase vocoder opcodes, resulting from Fourier Transform of time-domain audio signals.

nodes.label: pvsvoc opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that performs phase vocoder cross-synthesis by combining amplitudes of one sound with frequencies of another, with interpolation flexibility.

nodes.label: pvscross opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that performs cross-synthesis by combining frequencies of one sound with amplitudes of another, with user-controlled scaling.

nodes.label: pvsfilter opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that performs spectral filtering by taking frequencies from one sound and multiplying by amplitudes of another.

nodes.label: Spectral Shifting
nodes.description: A frequency-domain effect that adds or subtracts a fixed amount to bin frequencies, resembling ring modulation but with formant preservation options.

nodes.label: pvsmooth opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode that reduces FFT artifacts by applying low-pass filtering to amplitudes and frequencies of f-signals with adjustable cutoff parameters.

nodes.label: pvstrace opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode that selects and outputs only the N loudest bins from an f-signal, optionally returning bin numbers as an array.

nodes.label: Farhad Ilaghi Hosseini
nodes.description: Co-author of Csound example demonstrating pvsmooth and pvsblur artifact reduction techniques.

nodes.label: Phase Vocoding
nodes.description: Spectral analysis and resynthesis technique enabling time-stretching and pitch-shifting while preserving spectral characteristics.

nodes.label: Spectral Crossing
nodes.description: Technique of blending or morphing between two audio sources by combining their spectral data.

nodes.label: Spectral Filtering
nodes.description: The process of filtering FFT analysis components using band-pass and notch filters defined by trapezoidal spectral envelopes.

nodes.label: FFT Artifacts
nodes.description: Unwanted side effects occurring in FFT processing such as during extreme time-stretching, reducible through smoothing and blurring techniques.

nodes.label: Juan Pampin
nodes.description: Developer of the ATS (Analysis-Transformation-Synthesis) technique, which represents analyzed signals as deterministic and stochastic components.

nodes.label: Julius Orion Smith
nodes.description: Co-developer of the deterministic plus stochastic decomposition model for sound analysis/synthesis, which formed the basis for ATS refinement.

nodes.label: Oscar Pablo Di Liscia
nodes.description: Author of examples demonstrating ATS resynthesis in Csound and creator of a Pure Data toolkit for real-time synthesis of ATS spectral data.

nodes.label: Istvan Varga
nodes.description: Ported the ATSA program to Csound as a command-line utility.

nodes.label: ATS (Analysis-Transformation-Synthesis)
nodes.description: A sound analysis and resynthesis technique that decomposes signals into deterministic (sinusoidal trajectories) and stochastic (residual noise) components, with spectral weighting based on Signal-to-Mask-Ratio.

nodes.label: ATS File Format
nodes.description: A binary file format storing sound analysis as sinusoidal trajectories with instantaneous frequency, amplitude, and phase, plus residual noise energy in 25 critical bands.

nodes.label: ATSH
nodes.description: A C program using GTK graphics for visualizing and plotting ATS analysis files.

nodes.label: Qatsh
nodes.description: A Qt 4 port GUI program for displaying and analyzing ATS analysis files.

nodes.label: Common Lisp Music (CLM)
nodes.description: Environment in which ATS was initially developed before being ported to Csound.

nodes.label: Critical Bands
nodes.description: Frequency bands based on human auditory perception, used in ATS analysis with 25 standard bands for noise representation.

nodes.label: Jean-Philippe Meuret
nodes.description: Developer of a sound editor tool for Speed Dreams project, available on SourceForge.

nodes.label: ATSread
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that reads deterministic ATS data from analysis files, outputting frequency/amplitude pairs of sinusoidal trajectories for specific partials.

nodes.label: ATSreadnz
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that reads noise data from ATS files, delivering k-rate energy values for requested critical bands (1-25).

nodes.label: ATSbufread
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that reads an ATS file and stores frequency and amplitude data into an internal table for use by other opcodes.

nodes.label: ATSinterpread
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that reads an ATS table and outputs amplitude values by interpolating between two frequency trajectories closest to a given frequency.

nodes.label: ATSpartialtap
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that reads an ATS table and outputs frequency and amplitude k-rate values of a specific partial number.

nodes.label: ATSinfo
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that retrieves metadata from ATS analysis files, such as duration.

nodes.label: FFT-based Spectral Analysis
nodes.description: Analysis technique involving tradeoff between temporal and frequency resolution, used as basis for ATS analysis methods.

nodes.label: ATS Synthesis
nodes.description: A method of sound analysis and resynthesis using deterministic (sinusoidal) and stochastic (noise) components, allowing independent manipulation of analyzed data.

nodes.label: Reson filter
nodes.description: A band-pass resonator filter used in Csound for filtering noise into specific frequency bands.

nodes.label: Gaussian noise
nodes.description: A type of noise generated using the gauss opcode in Csound for stochastic sound synthesis.

nodes.label: Deterministic plus Stochastic representation
nodes.description: A sound analysis model that separates signals into deterministic (sinusoidal) and stochastic (noisy) components, allowing independent time-stretching without FFT artifacts.

nodes.label: ATS Resynthesis
nodes.description: A technique for analyzing and resynthesizing audio using ATS (Analysis-Transformation-Synthesis) files with deterministic and residual components.

nodes.label: ATSsinnoi opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that resynthesizes ATS analysis files using sinusoidal and noise components with control over partials, offset, and increment.

nodes.label: ATSbufread opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that reads ATS analysis data into a buffer for use with other ATS opcodes.

nodes.label: ATSpartialtap opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that extracts amplitude and frequency values for individual partials from ATS data.

nodes.label: Zwicker/Fastl
nodes.description: Researchers cited for work on critical bands used in ATSaddnz noise band synthesis (25 critical bands).

nodes.label: ATScross opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that performs interpolation and cross-synthesis between two ATS analyses, allowing amplitude and frequency morphing between different sound sources.

nodes.label: fout opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that writes audio signals to disk in various formats including PCM, floating-point, and integer representations.

nodes.label: monitor opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that creates an audio signal from a mix of all audio output from all instruments for recording or monitoring.

nodes.label: sndloop opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that records audio into a buffer and immediately plays it back in a loop with modifiable speed and crossfade.

nodes.label: GEN01 function table
nodes.description: A Csound function table generator that loads audio files into RAM for playback, supporting mono or stereo files.

nodes.label: sensekey opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that senses activity on the computer keyboard for real-time control.

nodes.label: ftgen GEN routine
