nodes.description: A Csound function table generation routine used to create and initialize function tables for audio data storage.

nodes.label: Modulo operation
nodes.description: A mathematical operation (%) used in Csound to wrap buffer indices around the end of a function table for circular playback.

nodes.label: loscil3 opcode
nodes.description: An enhanced version of loscil offering cubic interpolation for smoother playback from function tables.

nodes.label: lposcil opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode allowing looping points to be changed at k-rate during note playback.

nodes.label: midichn opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode that returns the MIDI channel number of the currently triggered instrument.

nodes.label: notnum opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode that returns the MIDI note number of the currently triggered instrument.

nodes.label: ctrl14 opcode
nodes.description: A 14-bit version of the ctrl7 opcode that provides improved resolution for MIDI controller data.

nodes.label: ctrl21 opcode
nodes.description: A 21-bit version of the ctrl7 opcode offering even higher resolution for MIDI controller data.

nodes.label: pchbend opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that reads MIDI pitch bend wheel data and allows specification of minimum and maximum output values.

nodes.label: aftouch opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that reads MIDI aftertouch data for modifying note parameters during playback.

nodes.label: initc7 opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that initializes MIDI controller values to a specified starting value rather than defaulting to minimum.

nodes.label: changed opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates a trigger whenever its input value changes, used to optimize MIDI controller message output.

nodes.label: 7-bit quantisation
nodes.description: MIDI controller resolution limitation providing only 128 possible values, causing stepping artifacts and poor parameter control.

nodes.label: GEN tables
nodes.description: Function tables in Csound used to store controller data, waveforms, and other numerical sequences for synthesis and processing.

nodes.label: Controller data recording
nodes.description: Technique in Csound for capturing real-time controller movements with timestamps, allowing playback and modification of recorded gestures.

nodes.label: FLpanel opcode
nodes.description: A Csound Fltk opcode that creates a graphical window container with customizable dimensions, position, border style, and color properties.

nodes.label: FluidSynth
nodes.description: Audio engine integrated with Csound for reading and playing SoundFont files in real-time via MIDI control.

nodes.label: Soundfont
nodes.description: Sample libraries used for MIDI playback, typically in .sf2 format, that can be loaded and controlled through Csound's fluidsynth opcodes.

nodes.label: MIDI File Playback
nodes.description: The process of reading and playing back MIDI files in Csound, with support for parsing MIDI channels to different instruments and soundfonts.

nodes.label: MIDI Output
nodes.description: Csound's ability to output MIDI data in real-time to hardware synthesizers, external devices, or other software using the -Q flag and midiout opcode.

nodes.label: midiout Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for sending raw MIDI data including note-on/off, continuous controller, pitch bend, and system exclusive messages.

nodes.label: midion2 opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that extends midion functionality by allowing explicit control of note generation through a trigger input.

nodes.label: moscil opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for generating monophonic MIDI melodic lines with explicit control over note durations and pauses between notes.

nodes.label: line function
nodes.description: A Csound function that generates a linear ramp of values over time, used for continuous controller data generation.

nodes.label: Processing
nodes.description: Programming language for image processing, video recording and playback, with OSC communication capabilities via the oscP5 library.

nodes.label: oscP5
nodes.description: OSC library for Processing that enables sending and receiving Open Sound Control messages.

nodes.label: liblo
nodes.description: Library used by the OSCsend_lo variant in Csound for OSC message transmission.

nodes.label: netP5
nodes.description: Processing library that provides NetAddress functionality for creating remote locations for OSC message sending.

nodes.label: Csound OSC opcodes
nodes.description: Csound opcodes including OSCsend, OSCinit, OSClisten, OSCcount, OSCraw, and OSCbundle for Open Sound Control communication.

nodes.label: Firmata

nodes.label: Csound Data Types
nodes.description: Four basic data types in Csound: i-type (initialization), k-type (scalar), a-type (audio vector), and f-type (spectral frame), used to pass data between opcodes.

nodes.label: Max for Live
nodes.description: A music production tool that can be programmed in JavaScript for algorithmic control and integration.

nodes.label: MuseScore
nodes.description: An open source score editor that supports JavaScript for algorithmic generation of notated scores.

nodes.label: csdl.h
nodes.description: The header file that defines the Csound opcode API for developing plugin opcodes.

nodes.label: Sample-accurate mode
nodes.description: A Csound 6 feature that allows opcodes to process audio with sample-level precision by handling offset and early parameters.

nodes.label: OENTRY structure
nodes.description: A registration structure in Csound that defines opcode metadata including name, dataspace size, timing flags, and function pointers.

nodes.label: Oscillator opcodes
nodes.description: Csound opcodes that can generate control or audio rate signals with different outputs for each signal type.

nodes.label: Dynamic library
nodes.description: A compiled module format for Csound plugin opcodes that can be loaded at runtime.

nodes.label: vco opcode
nodes.description: An oscillator whose frequency can be modulated by a control voltage, foundational to analog synthesizer design and the conceptual basis for FM synthesis.

nodes.label: Sean Costello
nodes.description: Audio engineer whose stereo reverb algorithm is implemented as the reverbsc opcode in Csound.

nodes.label: Jezar
nodes.description: Audio engineer whose stereo reverb algorithm is implemented as the freeverb opcode in Csound.

nodes.label: Iannis Xenakis
nodes.description: Composer who developed stochastic processes for music generation, using random distributions to control pitch, timbre, speed, amplitude, and note density; referenced for his crowd behavior metaphor in musical composition.

nodes.label: Stefan Stenzel
nodes.description: Audio engineer credited with the pinker pink noise algorithm implemented in Csound.

nodes.label: MIDI Opcodes
nodes.description: Csound opcodes for MIDI input/output including note number conversion, velocity, controller data, and pitch bend handling.

nodes.label: Faust Integration
nodes.description: Csound opcodes for instantiating and running Faust programs, including compilation and control adjustment.

nodes.label: CsBeats
nodes.description: A domain-specific language included with Csound tailored to concepts of beats, rhythm, and standard western notation for score composition.

nodes.label: Pysco
nodes.description: A Python-based tool for generating Csound score events with functions like score(), event_i(), p_callback(), and pmap() for preprocessing and postprocessing score data.

nodes.label: Perl
nodes.description: A scripting language that can be used to preprocess Csound scores, as demonstrated in score generation examples.

nodes.label: Csound Score Language
nodes.description: The classical text-based score notation system for Csound that uses i statements for note events, m/n statements for section repetition, and s statements for section markers.

nodes.label: Score Preprocessing
nodes.description: A technique in Csound that allows scores to be passed through external binaries or scripts before synthesis, enabling dynamic score generation and manipulation.

nodes.label: cue() Context Manager
nodes.description: A Pysco feature that manages time in scores by allowing local time normalization within measures, eliminating manual recalculation of global start times.

nodes.label: Tito Latini
nodes.description: Author of a Csound score example demonstrating Perl script preprocessing for random seed control in score generation.

nodes.label: CMask
nodes.description: An application that produces Csound score files using tendency masks—time-variant boundaries that define ranges for score parameters like amplitude, pitch, and duration.

nodes.label: nGen
nodes.description: A free multi-platform command-line tool for generating Csound event-lists and standard MIDI files, written in C and designed by composer Mikel Kuehn.

nodes.label: Mikel Kuehn
nodes.description: Composer who designed and wrote nGen, a tool for creating Csound score files and MIDI files.

nodes.label: Aleck Brinkman
nodes.description: Creator of Score11, a note list preprocessor that inspired nGen's syntax.

nodes.label: Leland Smith
nodes.description: Creator of the Score program, which influenced the design of nGen.

nodes.label: André Bartetzki
nodes.description: Developer who created CMask for MacOS9, Windows, and Linux platforms.

nodes.label: Anthony Kozar
nodes.description: Developer who ported CMask to OSX.

nodes.label: Score11
nodes.description: A note list preprocessor available for Linux Intel from the Eastman Computer Music Center that influenced nGen's design.

nodes.label: Score
nodes.description: A program created by Leland Smith for music notation and score generation that influenced nGen.

nodes.label: Tendency Mask
nodes.description: A core concept in CMask: an area limited by two time-variant boundaries that defines a space of possible values for score parameters.

nodes.label: Eastman Computer Music Center
nodes.description: Institution that distributes Score11 for Linux Intel platforms.

nodes.label: athenaCL
nodes.description: A software tool for creating musical structures that renders music as polyphonic event lists and can convert to diverse output formats including Csound scores, MIDI files, and specialized formats.

nodes.label: Common Music
nodes.description: A music composition system that transforms high-level algorithmic representations into control protocols for sound synthesis, generating output via MIDI, OSC, CLM, FOMUS, and Csound.

nodes.label: Grace
nodes.description: A graphical realtime algorithmic composition environment implemented in JUCE (C++) and S7 Scheme, providing drag-and-drop cross-platform composition with support for S7 Scheme and SAL languages.

nodes.label: S7 Scheme
nodes.description: A coding language used in Grace for designing musical algorithms.

nodes.label: SAL
nodes.description: An easy-to-learn but expressive algol-like language for designing musical algorithms in Grace.

nodes.label: Amplitude Tracking
nodes.description: A signal processing technique that extracts and follows the changing amplitude envelope of an audio signal using mathematical averaging or filtering methods.

nodes.label: downsamp opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that converts audio-rate signals to control-rate signals.

nodes.label: JUCE
nodes.description: A C++ framework used for implementing cross-platform graphical applications like Grace.

nodes.label: follow2 opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that performs a-rate amplitude tracking with separate attack and decay time smoothing on upward and downward amplitude slopes.

nodes.label: Dynamic Gating
nodes.description: A technique that uses threshold-based or amplitude-change-based mechanisms to mute or unmute audio signals in response to their dynamic characteristics.

nodes.label: Amplitude Triggering
nodes.description: A method of generating event triggers based on detected changes in audio signal amplitude, used to initiate synthesis or processing events.

nodes.label: Csound HTML Manual
nodes.description: Official documentation for Csound that includes reference materials and example sound files.

nodes.label: pitch opcode
nodes.description: The oldest pitch tracking opcode in Csound, offering the widest range of input parameters and capable of outputting tracking signals in octave format with optional quantization.

nodes.label: pitchamdf opcode
nodes.description: A Csound pitch tracking opcode using the Average Magnitude Difference Function method, slightly more accurate than pitch but with higher CPU demand.

nodes.label: pvspitch opcode
nodes.description: A Csound pitch tracker using streaming FFT technology that takes an f-signal input and attempts to mimic human ear pitch perception, though it may jump to wrong octaves with vibrato.

nodes.label: ptrack opcode
nodes.description: A Csound pitch tracker based on an algorithm by Miller Puckette that uses streaming FFT analysis internally on normal audio signals.

nodes.label: centroid opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that tracks the spectral centroid of a signal rather than the harmonic fundamental, useful for identifying different instruments playing the same note.

nodes.label: pvscent opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that tracks spectral centroid using FFT, requiring an f-sig input, related to centroid but with different input requirements.

nodes.label: Spectral Centroid
nodes.description: The center of gravity of a spectrum, used to characterize and distinguish different instruments playing the same note based on their timbral characteristics.

nodes.label: PyQcsObject
nodes.description: The interface object for scripting CsoundQt from Python, providing methods to control CsoundQt's interface, edit files, manage widgets, and interface with the running Csound engine.

nodes.label: PythonQt
nodes.description: A library that enables Python scripting support in CsoundQt, allowing interaction with the interface, widgets, and Qt libraries.

nodes.label: Qt Libraries
nodes.description: Cross-platform application framework whose classes can be used from Python in CsoundQt to build custom interfaces.

nodes.label: Amplitude and Pitch Tracking
nodes.description: Techniques in Csound for analyzing audio signals to detect changes in amplitude and spectral content for real-time control.

nodes.label: Universally Unique Identifier
nodes.description: A unique identifier string used in CsoundQt to reference widgets and other objects.

nodes.label: Score Generation
nodes.description: The algorithmic creation of musical scores through computational methods, often used to generate Csound score files.

nodes.label: Qt toolkit
nodes.description: Cross-platform GUI framework accessed via PythonQt for building custom interfaces in CsoundQt.

nodes.label: QInputDialog
nodes.description: Qt class used to create dialog boxes for user input in CsoundQt Python scripts, supporting getInt, getDouble, getItem, and getText methods.

nodes.label: Qt
nodes.description: A cross-platform application framework used for creating graphical user interfaces in CsoundQt.

nodes.label: Digital Signal Processing
nodes.description: The general term for any modification applied to sounds in the digital domain.

nodes.label: Frequency Domain
nodes.description: A representation of a signal considering its frequency components, obtained through Fourier Transform from time-domain signals.

nodes.label: p-field
nodes.description: Parameter fields in Csound score statements that carry values for instrument parameters, with substitution operators for interpolation and macro expansion.

nodes.label: The Csound Book
nodes.description: Comprehensive reference edited by Richard Boulanger containing chapters on FM synthesis and synthesizer emulation in Csound.

nodes.label: Introductory Catalogue of Computer Synthesized Sounds
nodes.description: A seminal work by Jean-Claude Risset (1969) documenting computer-synthesized sounds, adapted in the Amsterdam Catalog for Csound.

nodes.label: Amsterdam Catalog
nodes.description: A collection by John-Philipp Gather adapting Jean-Claude Risset's famous sound catalogue for use with Csound.

nodes.label: Digital Audio
nodes.description: Fundamental topic covering sound waves, transduction, sampling, and the sampling theorem as explained in the manual's final section.

nodes.label: Sine Wave
nodes.description: The simplest type of waveform describing simple harmonic motion, used as a fundamental example in digital audio basics.

nodes.label: Transducer
nodes.description: Device found in microphones that converts acoustical energy in the form of pressure waves into electrical signals for recording.

nodes.label: Harry Nyquist
nodes.description: Swedish physicist who formalized the sampling theorem in the 1920s, establishing the principle that a digital recording device cannot represent frequencies above half the sampling rate.

nodes.label: Quantization noise
nodes.description: Noise resulting from amplitude values being rounded up or down during digitization when bit depth is insufficient, most apparent in low-amplitude signals.

nodes.label: Bit-crunching
nodes.description: A deliberate use of low bit depth quantization to add noise to a signal, commonly employed by electronic musicians and implementable in Csound.

nodes.label: Dither
nodes.description: A small noise signal added to digital audio before conversion to analogue to reduce the more noticeable noise created by quantization.

nodes.label: ftgen
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for generating function tables, used to create waveforms with specific harmonic content.

nodes.label: CD Audio
nodes.description: Audio standard using a sample rate of 44100 Hz (44.1 kHz) and 16-bit resolution, allowing representation of frequencies up to 22050 Hz.

nodes.label: Glitch music
nodes.description: A modern musical genre that intentionally makes a feature of the spectral distortion that aliasing induces in digital audio.

nodes.label: Wavelength
nodes.description: The spatial extension of one cycle of a periodic sound, calculated as the ratio of sound velocity to frequency, abbreviated as λ (lambda).

nodes.label: Period
nodes.description: The time duration of one complete cycle of a periodic sound, calculated as the reciprocal of frequency.

nodes.label: Octave
nodes.description: A musical interval defined by a frequency ratio of 2:1, where doubling a frequency value produces a note one octave higher.

nodes.label: Semitone
nodes.description: One of twelve equal intervals in an octave under equal temperament tuning, with a frequency ratio of 2^(1/12).

nodes.label: Perfect Fifth
nodes.description: A musical interval represented by a frequency ratio of 3/2, spanning seven semitones.

nodes.label: Logarithmic Scale
nodes.description: A mathematical representation used in music and science where quantities vary over a large range; musical intervals are represented as frequency ratios on a logarithmic scale.

nodes.label: Human Hearing Range
nodes.description: The frequency range audible to human ears, generally stated as 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz (20 kHz), with upper limits decreasing with age due to presbyacusis.

nodes.label: Fletcher-Munson Curves
nodes.description: A psychoacoustic concept describing how human hearing sensitivity varies across frequencies, explaining why very low frequencies require more power to be heard.

nodes.label: Equal-tempered scale
nodes.description: Tuning system dividing the octave into 12 equal semitones, present on each MIDI keyboard, with A4 standardized at 440 Hz (or 457 Hz in the example).

nodes.label: Pythagorean tuning
nodes.description: Historical tuning system using frequency ratios based on perfect fifths (3:2), demonstrated in Csound with scale ratios 1, 9/8, 81/64, 4/3, 3/2.

nodes.label: Meantone tuning
nodes.description: Historical European tuning system using ratios 1, 10/9, 5/4, 4/3, 3/2, suitable for certain musical contexts.

nodes.label: Pch notation
nodes.description: Csound pitch representation using floating-point numbers where the integer part denotes octave (middle C = 8.00) and fractional part denotes semitones.

nodes.label: Oct notation
nodes.description: Csound pitch representation dividing octaves into acoustically equal steps, enabling microtonal divisions like 10 equal steps per octave.

nodes.label: Cent
nodes.description: Unit dividing one semitone into 100 equal parts, used to denote microtonal deviations; one cent equals a multiplier of 2^(1/1200).

nodes.label: mton opcode
nodes.description: Csound function returning note names from MIDI note numbers.

nodes.label: cpsoct opcode
nodes.description: Csound function converting oct notation values to frequency in cycles per second.

nodes.label: Quarter tone
nodes.description: Microtonal interval equal to 50 cents or half a semitone, representable in MIDI as fractional note numbers (e.g., 69.5 for A4 + 50 cents).

nodes.label: Csound FLOSS Manual
nodes.description: Educational documentation for Csound covering pitch, frequency, and tuning systems.

nodes.label: Sound Intensity Level (SIL)
nodes.description: A measurement of the amount of power on a certain surface, expressed in Watts per square meter (W/m²), with a reference value of 10⁻¹² W/m² at the threshold of hearing.

nodes.label: Sound Pressure Level (SPL)
nodes.description: A measurement based on sound pressure deviations, with a reference value of 2·10⁻⁵ Pa, where sound intensity is proportional to the square of sound pressure (I ∝ P²).

nodes.label: Root Mean Square (RMS)
nodes.description: A measurement of the effective mean of amplitudes over a time span, calculated by squaring N samples, dividing by N, and taking the square root.

nodes.label: 0dbfs Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that sets the reference level for zero dB as full scale, typically set to 1 in modern audio programming to prevent clipping above that value.

nodes.label: Fletcher-Munson Curves
nodes.description: Equal loudness curves describing how human hearing sensitivity varies across frequencies, with peak sensitivity around 3000 Hz.

nodes.label: Frequency Ratio
nodes.description: A proportional relationship between frequencies, such as 5/4 proportion, used to calculate new frequencies from a reference frequency.

nodes.label: Cent Difference
nodes.description: A logarithmic measure of pitch difference where 1200 cents equals one octave, calculated as c = log₂(f₁/f₂)·1200.

nodes.label: H. Fletcher
nodes.description: Co-author of the foundational 1933 paper on equal loudness curves in human hearing.

nodes.label: W. A. Munson
nodes.description: Co-author of the foundational 1933 paper on equal loudness curves in human hearing.

nodes.label: Pseudo-random generator
nodes.description: A deterministic algorithm that generates sequences of numbers with statistical properties of randomness, repeating after a cycle determined by bit size (e.g., 65536 steps for 16-bit).

nodes.label: Uniform distribution
nodes.description: A probability distribution where all values in a given range are equally likely, the default output of computer pseudo-random generators.

nodes.label: Seed (random number generation)
nodes.description: The initial input value to a pseudo-random generator that determines the entire sequence of generated numbers.

nodes.label: Random walks
nodes.description: A type of random process where successive values depend on previous values, used in algorithmic composition.

nodes.label: Delay line opcodes (delayr, deltapi, delayw)
nodes.description: Csound opcodes for creating delay buffers and reading/writing delayed signals, used extensively in this patch for feedback delay effects.

nodes.label: Charles Dodge
nodes.description: Composer and audio engineer who suggested an effective method for stereo panning using square root gain factors to maintain consistent perceived sound level.

nodes.label: Thomas A. Jerse
nodes.description: Co-author of 'Computer Music' (1985), which served as a model for many random number generator opcodes in Csound.

nodes.label: Computer Music
nodes.description: A 1985 book by Charles Dodge and Thomas A. Jerse that provided foundational material on random distributions and number generation techniques used in Csound opcode design.

nodes.label: Linear distribution
nodes.description: A probability distribution where either lower or higher values in a range are more likely, implemented by comparing two uniform random numbers and selecting the minimum or maximum.

nodes.label: Triangular distribution
nodes.description: A probability distribution where values in the middle of a range are more likely than those at the borders, with linear probability transitions, implemented by averaging two uniform random numbers.

nodes.label: Random Distribution
nodes.description: Compositional technique controlling probability distributions (uniform, linear, triangular, exponential, gaussian) to shape musical parameters like pitch and duration.

nodes.label: Overtone Scale
nodes.description: A pitch scale based on harmonic partials, starting from the second partial and extending upward, used as an alternative to equal temperament.

nodes.label: Csound Opcode
nodes.description: A unit operation in Csound that performs audio processing or control tasks, with initialization and performance-rate execution, subject to parameter validation.

nodes.label: Rejection Sampling
nodes.description: A method for generating random numbers with a given probability or density function by first generating uniformly distributed random numbers and accepting or rejecting them based on a density function.

nodes.label: Probability Function
nodes.description: A mathematical function describing the relative frequency of occurrence of discrete random variables, where all probabilities sum to 1.

nodes.label: Density Function
nodes.description: A mathematical function describing the probability distribution of continuous random variables, where the area under the function equals 1.

nodes.label: rand_density opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates random numbers with a user-defined density function using rejection sampling.

nodes.label: rand_probability opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates random numbers with a user-defined probability function using rejection sampling.

nodes.label: Signals, Systems and Sound Synthesis
nodes.description: A book by Martin Neukom covering mathematical foundations of sound synthesis including random processes and rejection sampling.

nodes.label: GEN17 routine
nodes.description: A Csound GEN routine used to generate histograms that define probabilities of certain notes and rhythmic gaps occurring.

nodes.label: uniform random distribution
nodes.description: A probability distribution in which any value within defined limits has equal chance of occurrence.

nodes.label: non-uniform distributions
nodes.description: Random distributions in which certain values have greater chance of occurrence over others, often more useful and musical than uniform distributions.

nodes.label: For-Loops in Csound
nodes.description: Control flow structures in Csound 7 supporting iteration over arrays with syntax 'for var in [array] do' and optional counter variable.

nodes.label: diskin opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode for reading audio files with optional playback rate control and looping parameters.

nodes.label: reverb2 opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode implementing a reverb effect with configurable parameters for room size and decay.

nodes.label: transeg opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode for generating transient envelope segments with specified duration, shape, and target values.

nodes.label: Giorgio Zucco
nodes.description: Author of 'Sound Synthesis with Csound', a comprehensive guide to Csound 5 programming covering real-time synthesis, MIDI, and graphical interfaces.

nodes.label: Gabriel Maldonado
nodes.description: Musician and researcher who introduced GUI opcodes to Csound through CsoundAV, integrating FLTK (Fast Light Toolkit) and OpenGL for 3D graphics capabilities.

nodes.label: CsoundAV
nodes.description: An enhanced version of Csound (January 2002, last release 2005) with support for graphical interfaces, OpenGL graphics, and direct audio interface integration.

nodes.label: OpenMusic
nodes.description: A graphical environment that can use Csound as a synthesis engine for controlling sound generation through MIDI and algorithmic composition.

nodes.label: Trapped
nodes.description: A historical Csound composition by Richard Boulanger included in the standard Csound installation as a didactic example.

nodes.label: qutecsound
nodes.description: An excellent integrated editor included in Csound5 with syntax highlighting, analysis/resynthesis tools, widget creation, and opcode documentation.

nodes.label: MIDI Control
nodes.description: Musical Instrument Digital Interface operations in Csound for receiving and sending MIDI data, including note on/off, control change, and pitch bend.

nodes.label: Filter Design
nodes.description: Audio filtering techniques in Csound including lowpass, highpass, and resonant filters such as moogladder, moogvcf, and lpf18.

nodes.label: Oscillator Opcodes
nodes.description: Csound opcodes for waveform generation including oscil, oscili, oscil3, poscil, and loscil variants.

nodes.label: Linear Algebra Opcodes
nodes.description: Csound opcodes for matrix and vector operations, including la_i and la_k families for mathematical computations on audio data.

nodes.label: Envelope Generation
nodes.description: The process of shaping the amplitude contour of a sound over time using attack, sustain, and release segments.

nodes.label: STK opcodes
nodes.description: Perry Cook's Synthesis Toolkit in C++, an open-source library of synthesis opcodes for physical modeling.

nodes.label: Blue
nodes.description: A Csound editor by Steven Yi that resembles a multitrack sequencer interface, offering tools for composition and score control.

nodes.label: Cabel
nodes.description: An experimental graphical Csound editor similar to Max, Open Music, and Pure Data, with last release in 2006.

nodes.label: ATS
nodes.description: A next-generation opcode for analysis and resynthesis, including real-time capabilities.

nodes.label: Loris
nodes.description: A next-generation opcode for analysis and resynthesis, including real-time capabilities.

nodes.label: PVS
nodes.description: A next-generation opcode for analysis and resynthesis, including real-time capabilities.

nodes.label: CSoundAV
nodes.description: A version of Csound by G. Maldonado with extended capabilities.

nodes.label: G. Maldonado
nodes.description: Developer who implemented the fof3 opcode variant in CsoundAV.

nodes.label: CSoundAC
nodes.description: An experimental version of Csound for algorithmic composition developed by Michael Gogins.

nodes.label: Audacity
nodes.description: Open-source audio editing software that can be integrated with WinXound for external audio editing.

nodes.label: FLTK
nodes.description: A graphical user interface library used in Csound that may require compatibility flags in versions after 5.14.

nodes.label: White noise synthesis
nodes.description: A sound synthesis technique using random signal generation with complex spectral density, commonly employed in subtractive synthesis.

nodes.label: p-fields
nodes.description: Parameters in Csound score that define instrument behavior, including instrument number (p1), attack time (p2), and duration (p3).

nodes.label: Csound variable types
nodes.description: Different variable types in Csound including audio variables (a-rate), initialization variables (i-rate), control variables (k-rate), and global variables (g-rate).

nodes.label: Initialization-rate variables
nodes.description: Variables in Csound prefixed with 'i' that are set once at instrument initialization.

nodes.label: Csound header
nodes.description: The section of a Csound program that defines system parameters such as sample rate, control rate, and number of channels.

nodes.label: Conditional logic (if-then)
nodes.description: Programming construct in Csound that executes code blocks based on whether specified conditions are true or false.

nodes.label: sum opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that adds multiple audio signals together, equivalent to direct addition of variables.

nodes.label: physical modeling synthesis
nodes.description: A synthesis technique that models the physical behavior of acoustic instruments, exemplified in Csound by the pluck opcode for simulating plucked strings.

nodes.label: WAV audio format
nodes.description: An uncompressed audio file format supported by Csound with configurable bit depths (8, 16, 24, or 32-bit floating point).

nodes.label: AIFF audio format
nodes.description: Big-endian audio file format recommended for UNIX and Macintosh computers in Csound soundfile operations.

nodes.label: Zucco
nodes.description: Author of Sound Synthesis with Csound, providing practical examples of granular synthesis and partikkel opcode usage.

nodes.label: Sound Synthesis with Csound
nodes.description: A book by Zucco covering signal synthesis techniques and audio processing in Csound, including chapters on synthesis methods, envelopes, and glissandi.

nodes.label: jitter opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode that adds random frequency variation to create natural-sounding modulation effects.

nodes.label: jitter2 opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode similar to jitter but allowing definition of parameters for three separate points with different amplitude and frequency.

nodes.label: Vibrato
nodes.description: A modulation technique in which frequency is varied periodically, controlled in real-time via MIDI sliders in the examples.

nodes.label: Tremolo
nodes.description: A periodic variation in amplitude created by modulating the amplitude of an oscillator with a low-frequency signal.

nodes.label: Step sequencer
nodes.description: A sequencing technique found in analog synthesizers and modern instruments that controls melodic structures through discrete pitch values.

nodes.label: ARP synthesizer
nodes.description: Historic analog synthesizer from the 1970s featuring voltage-controlled oscillators and modulation capabilities.

nodes.label: Tremolo
nodes.description: A modulation technique where an oscillator modulates the amplitude of an audio signal, creating periodic volume variation.

nodes.label: Stereo Panning
nodes.description: A technique for positioning audio signals in the stereo field by varying amplitude distribution between left and right channels using control variables.

nodes.label: Autopan
nodes.description: A dynamic panning effect that continuously moves sound across the stereo field at a controllable speed using oscillation.

nodes.label: Head Related Transfer Function (HRTF)
nodes.description: A 3D audio spatialization technique using an artificial head model to simulate how sound affects human hearing perception in three dimensions.

nodes.label: rnd opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates random numbers within a given range, useful for creating random frequency variations in granular synthesis.

nodes.label: schedwhen opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for scheduling instrument events with specified instrument number, start time, and duration.

nodes.label: birnd Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates random values in a bipolar range (e.g., -1 to 1), used for random panning.

nodes.label: Generative Music Technique
nodes.description: A compositional method using algorithmic processes to create evolving musical sequences with controlled randomness and timing variation.

nodes.label: Sound Synthesis with Csound
nodes.description: A book by Zucco demonstrating practical Csound synthesis techniques including algorithmic composition and generative music.

nodes.label: Direct Csound
nodes.description: A live-performance-optimized version of Csound released by Gabriel Maldonado in June 1998, synchronized to Csound 3.494.

nodes.label: Gen 09
nodes.description: An enhanced variant of Gen10 in Csound allowing definition of harmonics in any order with independent amplitude and phase (in degrees).

nodes.label: Gen 07
nodes.description: A Csound function generation routine for defining complex amplitude envelopes and waveforms using linear segments.

nodes.label: Gen 08
nodes.description: A Csound function generation routine for defining spline curves with harmonious and smooth characteristics.

nodes.label: Gen 11
nodes.description: A Csound function generation routine for additive synthesis using cosine partials, similar to buzz and gbuzz opcodes but more limited.

nodes.label: Virtual MIDI Keyboard
nodes.description: A Csound controller tool introduced in version 5.07 providing a virtual keyboard with configurable MIDI channels, program changes, and sliders.

nodes.label: Csound 5.13
nodes.description: A standard version of Csound integrating nearly all opcodes from CsoundAV (except OpenGL) with improved portability and future feature support.

nodes.label: ASIO Driver
nodes.description: Audio driver technology used in Windows-based Csound implementations to reduce latency during live performance.

nodes.label: -+rtmidi=virtual flag
nodes.description: A Csound command-line flag that activates virtual MIDI keyboard input for real-time performance control.

nodes.label: External MIDI Controllers
nodes.description: Hardware or software MIDI devices (keyboards, sliders, faders) that send control data to Csound via MIDI ports for real-time parameter modulation.

nodes.label: Autopan
nodes.description: A stereo panning effect that automatically moves the audio signal between left and right channels at a controllable rate.

nodes.label: Declick Envelope
nodes.description: An amplitude envelope applied to audio output to prevent clicks and pops at note onset and release.

nodes.label: MIDI File Import
nodes.description: The ability to read and process MIDI files in Csound using the -F flag to load external MIDI sequences.

nodes.label: Zucco
nodes.description: Author of Sound Synthesis with Csound, providing practical examples of phase modulation, waveshaping, and distortion synthesis techniques.

nodes.label: cpstmid opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that converts MIDI note numbers to frequency using alternative tuning systems and microtonal scales defined in a function table.

nodes.label: vincr opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that accumulates audio signals by adding values to a variable, used for mixing signals from multiple instruments.

nodes.label: clear opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that resets global variables to zero to prevent signal accumulation artifacts.

nodes.label: Touch OSC
nodes.description: A software tool for creating custom OSC control interfaces on mobile devices (iPhone, iPad, Android) with widgets like sliders, buttons, and joysticks.

nodes.label: Matt Wright
nodes.description: Researcher at CNMAT who co-developed the OSC (Open Sound Control) protocol.

nodes.label: Microtonal scales
nodes.description: Alternative tuning systems that divide the octave into intervals smaller than traditional semitones and tones, such as quarter tones.

nodes.label: OSClisten opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that receives OSC messages from external controllers like Touch OSC, enabling real-time parameter control from mobile devices.

nodes.label: FLknob opcode
nodes.description: A Csound FLTK widget opcode that creates rotary knob controls with multiple visual types (3-D, pie, clock, flat) for parameter control.

nodes.label: FLvalue opcode
nodes.description: A Csound Fltk opcode that displays the numeric output value from control widgets like knobs and sliders.

nodes.label: FLcolor opcode
nodes.description: A Csound Fltk opcode that sets RGB color values for graphical interface elements like panels and containers.

nodes.label: FLtabs opcode
nodes.description: A Csound Fltk opcode that organizes multiple overlapping windows within a single panel container, accessible via tab buttons.

nodes.label: FLgroup opcode
nodes.description: A Csound Fltk opcode that defines a grouped area within a tabbed interface for organizing related controls.

nodes.label: FLrun opcode
nodes.description: A Csound Fltk opcode that initializes the graphical thread and activates the user interface rendering engine.

nodes.label: GUI (Graphical User Interface)
nodes.description: Interactive visual control interfaces built with Fltk in Csound for managing virtual synthesizers, samplers, and signal processors.

nodes.label: FLslider opcode
nodes.description: A Csound FLTK widget opcode that creates horizontal and vertical slider controls for real-time parameter manipulation.

nodes.label: FLbutton opcode
nodes.description: A Csound FLTK widget opcode that creates button controls with customizable graphical symbols and states.

nodes.label: FLjoy opcode
nodes.description: A Csound FLTK widget opcode that creates a joystick control with two-axis (x-y) output, suitable for vector synthesis and spatial control.

nodes.label: FLsetColor opcode
nodes.description: A Csound FLTK opcode that sets the RGB color properties of graphical control objects.

nodes.label: FLsetTextSize opcode
nodes.description: A Csound FLTK opcode that controls the font size of labels on graphical control objects.

nodes.label: Vector synthesis
nodes.description: A synthesis technique that uses joystick-like controls to interpolate between multiple sound sources or synthesis parameters.

nodes.label: Exponential scaling
nodes.description: A parameter scaling method in Csound controls where iexp = -1 produces exponential output values, useful for frequency and filter controls.

nodes.label: Linear scaling
nodes.description: A parameter scaling method in Csound controls where iexp = 0 produces linear output values.

nodes.label: FLbutBank opcode
nodes.description: A Csound FLTK opcode that creates a grid of button controls organized in rows and columns.

nodes.label: FLsetVal opcode
nodes.description: A Csound FLTK opcode that programmatically sets the value of a graphical control object at k-rate or i-rate.

nodes.label: QuteCsound
nodes.description: An integrated development environment for Csound featuring syntax highlighting, code completion, and widget-based GUI construction without writing code in the .csd file.

nodes.label: csound~
nodes.description: A Max/MSP external object that enables communication and integration between Csound and Max/MSP for GUI construction.

nodes.label: csoundapi~
nodes.description: A Pure Data external for integrating Csound with Pure Data, developed by Victor Lazzarini.

nodes.label: Ableton Live
nodes.description: A music sequencer and production environment that can integrate with Csound through Max for Live.

nodes.label: CsoundforLive
nodes.description: A package of 120 plugins directed by Richard Boulanger that integrates Csound's synthesis power into Ableton Live, including granular synthesis, spectral processing, samplers, and effects.

nodes.label: Karlheinz Stockhausen
nodes.description: A composer who created Mantra (1969-70) for two pianos and ring modulators, demonstrating the artistic application of ring modulation techniques.

nodes.label: Bruno Maderna
nodes.description: Composer whose work 'Notturno' is a historical example of subtractive synthesis.

nodes.label: mxadsr opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates an ADSR envelope with maximum value control, used for operator envelope shaping in phase modulation.

nodes.label: Modal Frequency Ratios
nodes.description: Frequency relationships derived from the vibrational modes of physical materials, used as partial tables in additive synthesis to create realistic instrument timbres.

nodes.label: Small Handbell
nodes.description: A modal frequency model consisting of 22 sinusoids with harmonic ratios based on the vibrational characteristics of a small handbell, used as an example in additive synthesis.

nodes.label: Additive Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates multiple partial sinusoids with specified harmonic ratios, enabling flexible reuse of code for different spectral models.

nodes.label: Notch Filter
nodes.description: A filter used to eliminate the passage of frequencies within a defined bandwidth, creating a narrow rejection band.

nodes.label: White Noise Filtering
nodes.description: A historical example of subtractive synthesis where filters are applied to white noise to create complex timbres.

nodes.label: Tonex Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that implements a bank of low-pass filters connected in series, with parameters for cutoff frequency and number of filter layers.

nodes.label: FLcount Widget
nodes.description: A graphical object in Csound's FLTK interface for selecting from a database of partial tables in real-time MIDI control applications.

nodes.label: Partials Database
nodes.description: A collection of 12 partial tables stored in a file (partials.h) containing different harmonic ratio sets for use in additive synthesis.

nodes.label: atonex opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode variant of tonex that implements a bank of high-pass filters connected in series.

nodes.label: statevar opcode
nodes.description: A Csound state-variable filter opcode with four independent outputs (high-pass, low-pass, band-pass, band-reject) in a single filter, using cutoff frequency and Q factor parameters.

nodes.label: FLTK GUI
nodes.description: A graphical user interface toolkit integrated with Csound for real-time parameter control, used here to create sliders and buttons for live electronics processing.

nodes.label: buzz oscillator
nodes.description: A Csound oscillator that generates a buzz waveform with harmonic content, used in the bandpass filter examples.

nodes.label: Moog lowpass filter
nodes.description: A voltage-controlled filter implementation in Csound used for filtering scanned synthesis output with frequency and resonance control.

nodes.label: fofilter opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing FOF (formant generator) synthesis, a type of granular synthesis used for vocal tract simulation.

nodes.label: mxadsr opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing ADSR envelope generation with attack, decay, sustain, and release parameters.

nodes.label: pareq opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for parametric equalization, used to construct parametric equalizers with defined cutoff frequency and bandwidth with gain.

nodes.label: rbjeq opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for parametric equalization suitable for building parametric equalizers.

nodes.label: clfilt opcode
nodes.description: A multi-pole low-pass and high-pass filter opcode in Csound supporting Butterworth, Chebyshev Type I, and Chebyshev Type II filter types with configurable pole count.

nodes.label: Mantra
nodes.description: A composition by Karlheinz Stockhausen (1969-70) for two pianos and ring modulators, exemplifying the use of ring modulation in contemporary music.

nodes.label: Yamaha
nodes.description: Manufacturer that implemented FM synthesis in their popular DX7 synthesizers following Chowning's publication.

nodes.label: DX7
nodes.description: A historic FM synthesis synthesizer introduced by Yamaha in 1983, the first commercial implementation of Chowning's FM synthesis technique.

nodes.label: DC offset
nodes.description: A positive constant value added to a modulating signal to convert it from bipolar to unipolar form, used in amplitude modulation synthesis.

nodes.label: Chebyshev filter
nodes.description: A filter type available in Csound with two variants (Type I and Type II), offering steeper roll-off than Butterworth filters.

nodes.label: Yamaha TX81Z
nodes.description: A synthesizer in the DX series that, unlike other models, featured operators with waveform types beyond sinusoids.

nodes.label: Portamento
nodes.description: Pitch glide technique between notes, implemented in Csound legato instruments through pitch ramps or as a substitute using crescendo shapes on tied notes.

nodes.label: MIDI Keyboard
nodes.description: A keyboard controller that sends MIDI data to control synthesizer parameters such as pitch and amplitude.

nodes.label: Feedback Synthesis
nodes.description: A synthesis technique where the output of an oscillator is fed back into its own input, creating complex timbral variations.

nodes.label: Operator Routing
nodes.description: A method of connecting multiple synthesis operators (carriers and modulators) in different configurations to control signal flow and create complex timbres.

nodes.label: Waveshape Synthesis
nodes.description: A non-linear distortion technique that alters the harmonic content of a signal by changing its waveform shape, implemented via table lookup in Csound.

nodes.label: Non-linear Distortion
nodes.description: Audio processing technique that alters signal harmonics through non-linear transformation, including clipping and waveshaping methods.

nodes.label: loscil opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that reads audio samples from a table (Gen01), limited to files under one minute duration, storing samples in RAM.

nodes.label: soundin opcode
nodes.description: A simple Csound opcode for reading audio files with minimal editing capabilities.

nodes.label: Gen49
nodes.description: A Csound function generator that imports MP3 audio files (mono or stereo) into a table.

nodes.label: vibr opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that produces continuous micro-variations similar to a low-frequency oscillator, used to naturalize electronic sounds.

nodes.label: linsegr opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates linear envelope segments with release time.

nodes.label: notnum opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that returns the MIDI note number (0-127) of a pressed key.

nodes.label: balance opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode for amplitude normalization used in FM synthesis instruments.

nodes.label: randomi opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates random values within a specified range at control rate.

nodes.label: BBcutm opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode for creating complex rhythmic loops similar to electronic styles like drum and bass, with parameters for tempo, subdivisions, and phrase repetition.

nodes.label: SoundFont
nodes.description: Proprietary audio format by E-mu Systems for sample-based synthesis, containing sampled instruments and synthesizer structures.

nodes.label: sndloop opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode for recording and sample playback of audio buffers in memory with pitch control and crossfade.

nodes.label: E-mu Systems
nodes.description: Company that created the proprietary SoundFont audio format.

nodes.label: Sample-based synthesis
nodes.description: Synthesis technique using sampled structures such as additive and subtractive synthesis or acoustic instruments.

nodes.label: Drum and bass
nodes.description: Electronic music style that can be created using the BBcutm opcode for complex rhythmic loops.

nodes.label: Dennis Gabor
nodes.description: Physicist who first developed granular synthesis theory in 1947, proposing that signals can be conceived as combinations of short sonic grains.

nodes.label: Barry Truax
nodes.description: Composer and researcher who first proposed a real-time granular synthesis implementation using the DMX-1000 digital signal processor in 1986 and composed Riverrun (1988).

nodes.label: Malström (Reason)
nodes.description: A commercial granular synthesis module in the Reason DAW.

nodes.label: Reaktor (Native Instruments)
nodes.description: A commercial granular synthesis tool by Native Instruments.

nodes.label: Thom Johansen
nodes.description: Co-developer of the Partikkel opcode, introduced in Csound 5.07 in 2007.

nodes.label: Torgeir Strand Henriksen
nodes.description: Co-developer of the Partikkel opcode in Csound.

nodes.label: Grain Size
nodes.description: Parameter controlling the duration of individual grains in granular synthesis.

nodes.label: Transposition Control
nodes.description: Parameter allowing pitch shifting of grain sources via joystick or MIDI control.

nodes.label: Waveform Selection
nodes.description: Choice between multiple waveform shapes (square, sawtooth, sine, triangle) for grain generation.

nodes.label: Random Grain Rate Variation
nodes.description: Stochastic component applied to grain rate to create variation and avoid periodic artifacts.

nodes.label: Soft Synchronization
nodes.description: Technique for synchronizing multiple partikkel instances with controllable phase offset between stereo channels.

nodes.label: Audio File Granulation
nodes.description: Granular synthesis applied to pre-recorded audio samples stored in function tables.

nodes.label: Chant
nodes.description: Research project by Xavier Rodet and colleagues on formant synthesis extending from voice synthesis to general synthesis applications.

nodes.label: STK library
nodes.description: A library of physical modeling instruments integrated into the Windows version of Csound, containing numerous acoustic instrument models.

nodes.label: Korg M1
nodes.description: A famous workstation synthesizer using PCM (pulse code modulation) synthesis with sampled instrument timbres stored in ROM.

nodes.label: PCM synthesis
nodes.description: A synthesis technique based on digital sampling of acoustic instruments to build a timbre database, often combined with subtractive synthesis.

nodes.label: wguide1
nodes.description: A Csound opcode modeling a plucked string using a delay line and first-order lowpass filter.

nodes.label: wguide2
nodes.description: A Csound opcode modeling a struck plate with two parallel delay lines and two lowpass filters.

nodes.label: streson
nodes.description: A Csound opcode modeling a plucked string resonator.

nodes.label: mpulse
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates impulses at specified time intervals to excite resonators.

nodes.label: STK (Synthesis ToolKit in C++)
nodes.description: A comprehensive physical modeling library offering emulations of acoustic instruments, integrated into Csound for Windows.

nodes.label: Gary P. Scavone
nodes.description: Co-creator of the STK (Synthesis ToolKit in C++), a physical modeling library for acoustic instrument emulation.

nodes.label: Scott Lindroth
nodes.description: Contributor of modal frequency ratio tables for objects and instruments in the Csound manual.

nodes.label: Dahina tabla
nodes.description: A percussion instrument with documented modal frequency ratios [1, 2.89, 4.95, 6.99, 8.01, 9.02] used as an example for physical modeling in Csound.

nodes.label: STKClarinet
nodes.description: A Csound opcode from the STK library that emulates a clarinet instrument with frequency and amplitude parameters.

nodes.label: Mass-Spring-Damper Model
nodes.description: A physical modeling approach used by the mode opcode to simulate resonator behavior with resonance frequency and damping.

nodes.label: Modalsynth UDO
nodes.description: A user-defined opcode in Csound that generates modal resonators from a table of modal ratios, implementing a generative process for resonator construction.

nodes.label: Spectrum
nodes.description: A signal represented as a series of harmonics obtained from Fourier decomposition, where each harmonic has its own frequency, amplitude, and phase.

nodes.label: Richard Dobson
nodes.description: Author of the legato instrument design section in The Csound Book, demonstrating practical implementation of tied notes and expressive performance techniques in Csound.

nodes.label: PVS Opcodes
nodes.description: Modern real-time phase vocoder opcodes introduced in Csound5 by Victor Lazzarini, overcoming limitations of earlier time-deferred analysis methods.

nodes.label: Harmonizer
nodes.description: A signal processing technique that pitch-shifts audio while preserving vocal formants and vowel quality, capable of generating multiple transpositions simultaneously.

nodes.label: pvsblur opcode
nodes.description: A Csound spectral processing opcode that applies frequency and amplitude averaging to create a low-pass filter-like effect on spectral data.

nodes.label: pvsbandp opcode
nodes.description: A Csound spectral band-pass filter opcode that filters FFT analysis components within a trapezoidal spectral envelope.

nodes.label: pvsbandr opcode
nodes.description: A Csound spectral notch (band-reject) filter opcode that removes frequencies within a specified range from FFT analysis data.

nodes.label: Spectral Blur
nodes.description: A spectral processing technique that averages frequency and amplitude values across time windows, creating a low-pass filtering effect on spectral data.

nodes.label: Real-time Audio Processing
nodes.description: Csound's orientation toward continuous audio output to a DAC or file, requiring chunk-by-chunk processing rather than batch computation.

nodes.label: multitap opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that creates multiple delay instances with individual gain values for each delay line in a simplified manner.

nodes.label: pvsbufread opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that reads from a phase vocoder buffer at specified time and frequency range parameters for spectral delay effects.

nodes.label: Digital Signal Processing (DSP)
nodes.description: Algorithmic processes that transform input sound through stages of analog-to-digital conversion, processing, and digital-to-analog conversion.

nodes.label: Feedback delay technique
nodes.description: A signal processing method that multiplies a delayed signal by a numerical factor and sums it with itself repeatedly, with feedback values typically between 0 and 1 to avoid signal explosion.

nodes.label: Spectral delay
nodes.description: A delay effect applied in the spectral domain using phase vocoder techniques with multiple reading points at different frequency ranges.

nodes.label: flanger opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing the flanger effect with delay and feedback parameters.

nodes.label: Phaser effect
nodes.description: A signal processing technique using allpass filters arranged in series, modulated by one or more LFOs, and summed with the original signal to create the phaser effect.

nodes.label: phaser2 opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode dedicated to phaser effect processing, with a simplified version called phaser1.

nodes.label: vincr opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for accumulating audio signals into global variables, used in signal routing and mixing.

nodes.label: clear opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for clearing global audio variables after processing, used in signal routing workflows.

nodes.label: chnset opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for setting named audio channels using text strings, enabling more readable signal routing.

nodes.label: chnget opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for retrieving audio signals from named channels using text strings.

nodes.label: connect opcode
nodes.description: A modern Csound opcode for connecting signals between instruments using named channels and string-based routing.

nodes.label: alwayson opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that activates a specified instrument for the entire duration defined in the score.

nodes.label: outleta opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for sending audio signals to named bus channels for inter-instrument communication.

nodes.label: inleta opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for receiving audio signals from named bus channels in inter-instrument routing.

nodes.label: ins opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for reading external audio input from a microphone or audio interface.

nodes.label: reverbsc opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing stereo reverb using Schroeder reverberator architecture.

nodes.label: wguide1 opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing a waveguide resonator for physical modeling synthesis.

nodes.label: PVS opcodes
nodes.description: Csound opcodes for phase vocoder spectral processing, including spectral delay, blur, and notch filtering.

nodes.label: Signal routing
nodes.description: Techniques for connecting and directing audio signals through multiple processing stages in Csound compositions and performances.

nodes.label: pvsbuffer opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that creates a buffer for storing phase vocoder data, enabling time-based spectral delay and manipulation.

nodes.label: Small_Handbell opcode
nodes.description: A custom Csound opcode (included from Small_Handbell.h) that models resonant filtering with frequency and Q parameters, used in the resonator instrument.

nodes.label: Live Electronics GUI Patch
nodes.description: A Csound real-time audio processing system featuring multiple spectral and time-domain effects (pitch shifting, spectral delay, resonance, blur, notch filtering) controlled via FLTK interface.

nodes.label: Phase Vocoder Synthesis
nodes.description: A spectral audio processing technique using FFT analysis, manipulation in the frequency domain, and resynthesis, extensively demonstrated in this patch for pitch shifting and spectral effects.

nodes.label: Harmonizer Effect
nodes.description: A digital audio effect that shifts pitch using variable delay lines with feedback, capable of producing interval cycling or flanger effects depending on delay time and LFO settings.

nodes.label: pan opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for spatial audio panning that supports quadraphonic (4-channel) output with x,y coordinate control for sound positioning in space.

nodes.label: Quadraphonic Spatialization
nodes.description: A real-time spatial audio technique using four output channels with front-left, front-right, rear-left, and rear-right speaker positions for immersive sound field control.

nodes.label: Phase Vocoder Processing
nodes.description: A spectral audio processing technique using FFT analysis and resynthesis to enable pitch shifting, time-stretching, and spectral manipulation without changing duration or pitch independently.

nodes.label: PWGL
nodes.description: A visual programming language for music composition and algorithmic score generation, based on Lisp concepts and featuring OpenGL graphics.

nodes.label: Patchwork
nodes.description: An early computer-assisted composition environment developed at IRCAM in the early 1990s.

nodes.label: Carlos Agon
nodes.description: Developer of the omChroma library for OpenMusic, which interfaces with Csound and Diphone synthesis engines.

nodes.label: Marco Stroppa
nodes.description: Co-developer of the omChroma library for OpenMusic.

nodes.label: Karim Haddad
nodes.description: Developer of the Om2Csound library, which enables creation of Csound scores within OpenMusic.

nodes.label: Matti Laurson
nodes.description: Co-developer of Patchwork, an early computer-assisted composition environment.

nodes.label: omChroma
nodes.description: A library for OpenMusic based on modular synthesizer concepts, enabling interface with Csound and Diphone synthesis engines.

nodes.label: Om2Csound
nodes.description: A library developed by Karim Haddad that enables creation of Csound scores within OpenMusic.

nodes.label: Diphone
nodes.description: A synthesis engine developed at IRCAM for speech and sound synthesis, no longer actively maintained.

nodes.label: OpenGL
nodes.description: A graphics API providing multi-platform support, hardware acceleration, and 2D/3D graphics capabilities used in PWGL.

nodes.label: Common Lisp
nodes.description: A programming language used as the basis for OpenMusic and PWGL visual programming environments.

nodes.label: Computer-Assisted Composition
nodes.description: An area of electroacoustic music involving algorithmic composition environments where composers formalize and process musical material.

nodes.label: User-Defined Opcode (UDO)
nodes.description: A technique in Csound that allows programmers to write custom modules and encapsulate code fragments for reuse, written directly in the Csound language rather than C.

nodes.label: Hipersaw
nodes.description: A Csound UDO opcode that implements a supersaw-inspired waveform using seven detuned sawtooth oscillators with independent pitch modulation, similar to Roland synthesizer designs.

nodes.label: Vectrosynth
nodes.description: A vector synthesis instrument created by the author that uses converted Risset and Chowning UDO libraries, available on csound.com.

nodes.label: Csound.com
nodes.description: A web resource where Csound instruments and libraries, including Vectrosynth, are hosted and shared.

nodes.label: Dr. Robert Cooper
nodes.description: Csound evangelist to whom The Csound Book is dedicated in memory.

nodes.label: Jon Christopher Nelson
nodes.description: Author of the chapter on Csound's GEN routines in The Csound Book, explaining waveshaping, normalization, and frequency modulation techniques.

nodes.label: Hans Mikelson
nodes.description: Author of the dynamical systems synthesis section in The Csound Book, demonstrating implementation of chaotic attractors and orbital mechanics as tone generators.

nodes.label: Dave Phillips
nodes.description: Author of 'A Csound Introductory Tutorial' and Linux/Csound FAQ; developer of Csound for LINUX.

nodes.label: Eric Lyon
nodes.description: Author of the reverberation design chapter in The Csound Book, demonstrating advanced reverberator techniques using Csound unit generators and allpass/comb filter networks.

nodes.label: Roger King
nodes.description: Author of 'Csound for Artists: Building Unique Virtual Instruments for Your Compositions' tutorial.

nodes.label: Keith Hamel
nodes.description: Author of '12-Week Csound Course' tutorial.

nodes.label: Arthur B. Hunkins
nodes.description: Composer of 'Via Creativa/Via Transformativa', 'Gifts', 'Lux Hominum', and 'Et Vitam Venturi III' featured in The Csound Book.

nodes.label: Burton Beerman
nodes.description: Instructor at Bowling Green State University whose students contributed selected compositions to the CD-ROM.

nodes.label: Richard Karpen
nodes.description: Csound composer and educator who created a composition analyzing Pibroch (Scottish bagpipe music) using pvread opcode for spectral manipulation.

nodes.label: Hubert Howe
nodes.description: Composer at Princeton who worked with Music 4, adding controllable envelope onsets (envlp) and optimizing code for IBM 7094.

nodes.label: Godfrey Winham
nodes.description: Composer at Princeton who contributed to Music 4 development, adding envelope controls and later writing a Fortran version (Music4BF).

nodes.label: Ken Steiglitz
nodes.description: Engineer at Princeton who discovered that analog feedback filters could be represented with digital samples, contributing to early digital sound design.

nodes.label: Stephen Haflich
nodes.description: MIT researcher who connected an organ keyboard for real-time Music 11 performance and developed a two-dimensional conducting sensor using Polaroid sonar cells.

nodes.label: Larry Beauregard
nodes.description: Flutist who collaborated with Barry Vercoe at IRCAM on real-time pitch-following and score-following technology for live instrument accompaniment.

nodes.label: Kevin Peterson
nodes.description: MIT student who assisted in the development of Csound in 1985.

nodes.label: Alan Delespinase
nodes.description: MIT student who assisted in the development of Csound in 1985.

nodes.label: Bill Gardner
nodes.description: Researcher who produced the MIT HRTFs dataset used in the hrtfer implementation, recorded using the KEMAR mannequin.

nodes.label: Dan Ellis
nodes.description: MIT student who assisted in Csound development and demonstrated real-time Csound control through drum pattern sensing at ICMC 1990.

nodes.label: Rich Steiger
nodes.description: Developer of OEDIT, a graphical orchestra editor for Music 11.

nodes.label: Music 4
nodes.description: Early computer music language created by Max Mathews and distributed to Princeton and Stanford in the early 1960s.

nodes.label: Music 5
nodes.description: A successor program to Music 1, completed in the 1960s, that overcame many limitations of early computer music synthesis and influenced later software like Csound.

nodes.label: Music 1
nodes.description: The first computer music synthesis program, created by Max Mathews in 1957 on an IBM 704, which produced a 17-second piece using a new musical scale.

nodes.label: The Technology of Computer Music
nodes.description: A 137-page book by Max Mathews that described the Music 5 program in detail as both tutorial and reference, contributing to its widespread adoption.

nodes.label: SHARC 21060
nodes.description: A floating-point digital signal processor from Analog Devices used in Extended Csound for real-time audio processing and synthesis.

nodes.label: Real-time synthesis
nodes.description: The capability to synthesize music in real-time on general-purpose computers, made possible by advances in processor speed and software like Extended Csound.

nodes.label: Interval Research Corporation
nodes.description: Research organization that supported Richard Boulanger's work on alternate controllers and sound design at Berklee College of Music.

nodes.label: Analog Devices
nodes.description: Company that initiated the Extended Csound Project, resulting in DSP-based Csound development from 1995–1997.

nodes.label: Scotty Vercoe
nodes.description: Collaborator with Richard Boulanger on the Extended Csound Project at Analog Devices from 1995–1997.

nodes.label: Jean Piché
nodes.description: Initial lead of the Csound documentation team and developer of Cecilia, a Csound front-end.

nodes.label: David Boothe
nodes.description: Csound documentation team member who produced and maintained the Canonical Public Csound Reference Manual in PDF and HTML formats.

nodes.label: The Csound CD-ROM
nodes.description: Interactive multimedia extension of The Csound Book featuring hundreds of orchestras, instrument anthologies, and front-end tools.

nodes.label: Kim Cascone
nodes.description: Composer and contributor to The Csound Book with a chapter on Recontextualizing Ambient Music.

nodes.label: LPC (Linear Predictive Coding)
nodes.description: An analysis technique for modeling the vocal tract by analyzing and resynthesizing speech and vocal sounds.

nodes.label: Orchestra File
nodes.description: A text-based Csound file (typically with .orc extension) that defines instruments by interconnecting opcodes that generate or modify audio signals.

nodes.label: Score File
nodes.description: A text-based Csound file (typically with .sco extension) that contains note events and parameter data used to perform user-defined instruments.

nodes.label: Sound Rendering
nodes.description: The process in Csound of translating text-based instruments and score data into audio output, analogous to image rendering in computer graphics.

nodes.label: Csound orchestra file
nodes.description: A Csound file that defines instruments (instr) using opcodes and signal routing, rendered line-by-line from top to bottom.

nodes.label: Csound score file
nodes.description: A text file defining musical events with p-fields (parameters) that Csound sorts, normalizes, and translates into a score.srt file for performance.

nodes.label: etude1.sco
nodes.description: A Csound score file demonstrating function table definitions and note-statements for sound design exercises.

nodes.label: etude1.orc
nodes.description: A Csound orchestra file containing instrument definitions used in conjunction with etude1.sco.

nodes.label: Frequency Modulation Synthesis
nodes.description: Synthesis technique using modulation index to control sidebands, integrated with pvread for dynamic timbral control in Csound.

nodes.label: Analog-to-Digital Converter (ADC)
nodes.description: A device that converts continuous analog signals into discrete digital samples with specified bit precision, such as 16-bit linear quantization.

nodes.label: Digital-to-Analog Converter (DAC)
nodes.description: A device that converts a sequence of digital samples back into a continuously varying analog voltage for audio playback.

nodes.label: Anti-aliasing lowpass filter
nodes.description: A low-pass filter used in D-A converters with cutoff frequency set to half the sampling rate to remove alias spectra and prevent audible artifacts.

nodes.label: Sampling
nodes.description: The process of converting acoustic waveforms into digital signals by measuring amplitude at regular intervals using an ADC.

nodes.label: Digital audio clipping
nodes.description: Distortion that occurs when the sum of multiple note amplitudes exceeds the maximum representable value of a digital converter (e.g., 32767 for 16-bit audio).

nodes.label: 16-bit digital converter
nodes.description: A digital-to-analog converter capable of representing 65536 possible amplitude values in the range –32768 to +32767, providing approximately 90 dB of dynamic range.

nodes.label: GEN5
nodes.description: A Csound GEN routine for computing exponential function tables, used for creating exponential envelope contours.

nodes.label: GEN7
nodes.description: A Csound GEN routine for computing linear function tables, used for creating linear envelope contours.

nodes.label: Bipolar Function
nodes.description: A function with symmetrical excursion above and below zero, typically normalized in Csound to the range -1 to +1.

nodes.label: Unipolar Function
nodes.description: A function with excursion in one direction only, typically positive, normalized in Csound to the range 0 to +1.

nodes.label: LFO-based Amplitude Gating
nodes.description: A technique using a low-frequency oscillator to modulate amplitude by retriggering an envelope multiple times during a note event.

nodes.label: envlpx opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for envelope generation used in complex modulation algorithms to control amplitude and index parameters of operators.

nodes.label: dispfft opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that plots signals in the frequency domain using the Fast Fourier Transform method.

nodes.label: display opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for visualizing control-rate or audio-rate signals on screen during performance.

nodes.label: GEN5
nodes.description: A Csound function generator that creates exponential curves for envelope design.

nodes.label: GEN7
nodes.description: A Csound function table generator for creating piecewise linear tables, used to set up pulse waveforms for frequency-dependent modulation.

nodes.label: Chorusing
nodes.description: An audio effect that thickens a sound by adding slightly detuned copies, simulating multiple voices attempting to sing the same pitch with slight variations.

nodes.label: Spectral Fusion
nodes.description: A technique that uses simultaneous modulation of two spectra to create the auditory illusion that they belong to the same sound source.

nodes.label: cpspch value converter
nodes.description: Csound value converter that translates octave-point-pitch-class notation to Hz frequency values, supporting microtonal specification.

nodes.label: ampdb value converter
nodes.description: Csound value converter that converts decibel values to raw linear amplitude values.

nodes.label: Octave-point-pitch-class notation
nodes.description: Notation system where octaves are whole numbers and pitch classes are two decimal digits, enabling intuitive pitch specification in Csound.

nodes.label: Microtonal music
nodes.description: Music using pitch divisions smaller than the standard semitone, specifiable in Csound using extended decimal places in cpspch notation.

nodes.label: areson opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode for resonant filtering in signal processing.

nodes.label: Butterworth filters
nodes.description: A family of filters in Csound (butterlp, butterhp, butterbp, butterbr) known for steeper slopes, flatter frequency response in the pass-band, and greater stability than earlier filter designs.

nodes.label: Cascade filter design
nodes.description: A higher-order filter implementation that avoids coefficient sensitivity issues by cascading multiple lower-order filter stages.

nodes.label: Analog synthesis
nodes.description: Early synthesis approach where filters defined the sound of classic instruments.

nodes.label: Csound Score Statements
nodes.description: Text-based commands in Csound scores that begin with specific letters (a, s, f, t) to control note-lists, timing, and tempo.

nodes.label: Advance Statement
nodes.description: A Csound score command (a) that advances the beat-count without generating sound, allowing rendering to skip to a specific point in a composition.

nodes.label: Section Statement
nodes.description: A Csound score command (s) that divides a score into sections and resets start-time counting to 0.

nodes.label: Dummy f-statement
nodes.description: A Csound score command (f 0) used to insert silence or extend score sections without loading a function table.

nodes.label: Carry Symbol
nodes.description: A Csound score shortcut (.) that copies a p-field value from one note-statement to the next.

nodes.label: Ramp Symbol
nodes.description: A Csound score shortcut (<) that linearly interpolates between two p-field values over multiple notes.

nodes.label: p2 Increment Symbol
nodes.description: A Csound score shortcut (+) that automatically calculates note start-time by adding the previous note's start-time and duration.

nodes.label: Tempo Statement
nodes.description: A Csound score command (t) that sets the tempo in beats per minute; default is 60 BPM (1 beat per second).

nodes.label: etude5.sco
nodes.description: A Csound score file by Richard Boulanger demonstrating score statements and symbols for sound design.

nodes.label: Etude 5
nodes.description: A Csound sound design exercise demonstrating filter design, tempo control, and score shortcuts.

nodes.label: Etude 6
nodes.description: A Csound sound design exercise demonstrating global variables, reverb, and panning using external effects processing.

nodes.label: Discrete Panning
nodes.description: Stereo panning technique using scalar multiplication (ipan and 1-ipan) to control left/right signal amplitude distribution.

nodes.label: etude6.orc
nodes.description: Csound orchestra file containing four globo-spatial instruments with panning and global reverb enhancements.

nodes.label: ENVLPX opcode
nodes.description: An interpolating single scan opcode in Csound that scans f-tables to determine envelope shapes, particularly for attack portions.

nodes.label: TABLEI opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that performs table lookup with interpolation, used for reading soundfile data from f-tables.

nodes.label: GEN9 routine
nodes.description: A Csound function table generator that creates composite waveforms by adding partials with specified relative strengths, capable of generating inharmonic partials with unique phase dispositions.

nodes.label: GEN8
nodes.description: A Csound GEN routine that creates smooth cubic spline curves for function tables.

nodes.label: GEN6
nodes.description: A Csound GEN routine that creates cubic polynomial function segments using groupings of three ordinate values.

nodes.label: GEN3
nodes.description: A flexible Csound GEN routine that creates polynomial functions over specified ordinate values with any number of coefficients for waveshaping.

nodes.label: GEN13
