nodes.description: A Csound GEN routine that uses Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind to create waveshaping functions with specified harmonic partials and relative strengths.

nodes.label: GEN14
nodes.description: A Csound GEN routine that uses Chebyshev polynomials of the second kind to create waveshaping functions, producing slightly gentler curves than GEN13.

nodes.label: GEN15
nodes.description: A Csound GEN subroutine that creates two f-tables for phase-quadrature waveshaping, separating harmonic partials with phases 0-179 and 180-359 into distinct tables.

nodes.label: GEN4
nodes.description: A Csound GEN subroutine that analyzes a waveshaping function and creates a complementary amplitude normalization f-table to maintain consistent peak amplitude.

nodes.label: Signification
nodes.description: A waveshaping amplitude normalization procedure that inverts the phase of consecutive pairs of harmonics by 180 degrees to minimize unpredictable amplitude fluctuations.

nodes.label: Phase-Quadrature
nodes.description: A waveshaping technique that generates sounds containing individual harmonics with arbitrarily specified phases using two complementary f-tables.

nodes.label: GEN12
nodes.description: A Csound GEN subroutine that generates the logarithm of a modified Bessel function, providing amplitude scaling factors for asynchronous FM instruments.

nodes.label: Marc Le Brun
nodes.description: Researcher (Le Brun 1979) who developed the phase-quadrature waveshaping instrument and documented waveshaping amplitude normalization techniques.

nodes.label: Palamin and Palamin
nodes.description: Researchers (Palamin and Palamin 1988) who described the asynchronous FM instrument using the formula I(r−1/r) for amplitude-modulated frequency modulation.

nodes.label: GEN2
nodes.description: Csound GEN routine that transfers parameter values directly into a table, useful for algorithmic applications including melody generation and twelve-tone rows.

nodes.label: randh
nodes.description: Csound opcode for generating random values at k-rate, used for algorithmic melody generation.

nodes.label: Twelve-Tone Row
nodes.description: A serial composition technique where all twelve chromatic pitches are arranged in a specific order, implemented in Csound using GEN2 function tables.

nodes.label: Computer Music Tutorial
nodes.description: A comprehensive reference work by Curtis Roads covering synthesis techniques including wave terrain synthesis.

nodes.label: Computer Music
nodes.description: A reference work by Dodge and Jerse providing explanations of random distributions and their applications to composition.

nodes.label: Computer Music
nodes.description: A 1985 book by C. Dodge and T. Jerse published by Schirmer Books, referenced as foundational computer music literature.

nodes.label: Csound Command-Line Flags
nodes.description: Command-line options prefixed with '-' that control Csound output format, sample size, header format, MIDI input, and other system behaviors.

nodes.label: Csound Compilation Process
nodes.description: The translation of orchestra and score files into an internal form usable by Csound's control components, involving error checking and opcode initialization.

nodes.label: K-rate (control-rate)
nodes.description: The control-rate sampling in Csound that acts as the master clock, processing audio in blocks of ksmps samples to optimize performance.

nodes.label: Csound Performance System
nodes.description: The runtime scheduler in Csound that manages note initialization, deactivation, and k-rate function calls in time order across active instruments.

nodes.label: Samples Out of Range
nodes.description: A warning condition in Csound when computed audio amplitudes exceed the resolution of the digital-to-analog converter, such as exceeding 32,768 for 16-bit samples.

nodes.label: Real-time Performance
nodes.description: The ability of a Csound orchestra and score to render audio faster than or equal to the duration of the piece, determined by comparing rendering time to total score duration.

nodes.label: MIT Csound 3.483
nodes.description: A specific version of Csound released July 6, 1998, documented in the examples.

nodes.label: Function Table (ftable)
nodes.description: A data structure in Csound that stores waveforms or analysis data, generated by GEN routines and referenced by instruments during synthesis.

nodes.label: P-field (Parameter Field)
nodes.description: A numbered parameter passed from the score to a Csound instrument, with p1 reserved for instrument number and p2 for start time; maximum 800 p-fields permitted.

nodes.label: Csound Error Handling
nodes.description: A classification system for Csound messages including fatal errors (irrecoverable), errors (user mistakes in opcodes), warnings (potential issues), and information messages.

nodes.label: GEN1 (Deferred Table Allocation)
nodes.description: A Csound function table generation method that defers space allocation until data are ready, requiring determinable input file size.

nodes.label: MIDI Channel
nodes.description: A communication pathway in Csound for assigning MIDI input to specific instruments, requiring proper channel assignment and configuration.

nodes.label: Sampling rate optimization
nodes.description: A Csound performance tuning technique balancing audio quality and computation speed; standard rates include 8000, 11025, 22050, 32000, and 44100 Hz.

nodes.label: Control rate optimization
nodes.description: A Csound performance technique where setting control rate to one-tenth to one-hundredth of sampling rate can speed up instruments by over 400%.

nodes.label: Vibrato synthesis
nodes.description: A modulation technique in Csound where using k-rate variables instead of a-rate variables for the modulation signal improves oscillator efficiency.

nodes.label: Table Lookup
nodes.description: A technique for retrieving precomputed values from a table, which in Csound is slower than direct function computation.

nodes.label: Envelope Scaling
nodes.description: A technique for applying amplitude envelopes to oscillators, which can be optimized by scaling at the opcode argument level.

nodes.label: delay1 opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode used to implement the convolution sum for direct convolution when the impulse response signal is short.

nodes.label: cpspch notation
nodes.description: Csound pitch notation system using octave.pitch-class format (e.g., 8.00 for C, 8.01 for C#) that can be abstracted with macros.

nodes.label: WAVE format
nodes.description: Little-endian audio file format recommended for x86 and DEC Alpha computers in Csound soundfile operations.

nodes.label: Expression Evaluation in Csound Scores
nodes.description: Feature allowing arithmetic expressions within square brackets in Csound scores, supporting operations +, -, *, / with floating-point calculation.

nodes.label: Csound Version 3.48
nodes.description: Version of Csound that introduced the r directive for repeated sections in the score language.

nodes.label: m statement (mark)
nodes.description: A Csound score statement that marks a source position and file, associating it with a given name for later reference in n statements.

nodes.label: n statement (name/recall)
nodes.description: A Csound score statement that includes score from a previously marked location, referred to by name, until the end of the section.

nodes.label: b statement (base-clock)
nodes.description: A Csound score statement that sets the internal base-clock, adding a new base-time to all subsequent note-on events until the next b directive or section end.

nodes.label: v statement (tempo control)
nodes.description: A Csound score statement that modifies the speed at which time passes for a portion of the score, allowing independent simultaneous tempo control.

nodes.label: t statement (time-warping)
nodes.description: A Csound score statement that varies the rate at which time passes globally in the score.

nodes.label: + shorthand (time continuation)
nodes.description: A Csound score shorthand where + in the p2 field sets a note's start-time to immediately follow the previous event's end, calculated as previous p2+p3.

nodes.label: ^+ shorthand (relative time)
nodes.description: An extended Csound score shorthand that sets a note-event's start-time relative to the previous note-event's p2+p3, with optional offset (e.g., ^+.25, ^+-1).

nodes.label: Verse and chorus structure
nodes.description: A musical form where verses alternate with repeated chorus sections, which can be efficiently implemented in Csound using m and n statements.

nodes.label: Rondo form
nodes.description: A musical structure with repeated sections, implementable in Csound using mark and name statements for efficient score organization.

nodes.label: Canon (musical form)
nodes.description: A compositional technique where multiple voices play the same melody at different times, which can be created in Csound using the b statement to overlap motifs.

nodes.label: Minimal music
nodes.description: A musical style that can employ phase-shifting of themes, implementable in Csound using the v directive for independent tempo control.

nodes.label: Charles Ives
nodes.description: Composer known for works employing independent time scales for simultaneous melodic ideas, a technique that can be emulated in Csound using the v directive.

nodes.label: Csound Macro Language
nodes.description: Extensions to Csound that provide shortcuts and organizational tools for score writing, including macro expansion and various score statements.

nodes.label: Stephen David Beck
nodes.description: Author of the chapter on designing acoustically viable instruments in Csound, discussing synthesis design principles and acoustic instrument modeling.

nodes.label: Heinrich Helmholtz
nodes.description: Late 19th-century physicist who developed classical acoustic theory describing the physics of musical and instrumental sound.

nodes.label: Acoustic Viability
nodes.description: A design aesthetic providing composers with principles to create powerful, expressive and evocative sounds by recognizing the importance of instrument acoustics and its relationship to expression.

nodes.label: Classical Acoustic Theory
nodes.description: Theories developed by Helmholtz describing instrument sounds as periodic vibrations with harmonic content and amplitude envelopes.

nodes.label: Modern Acoustic Theory
nodes.description: Contemporary understanding of acoustics recognizing that harmonic content and timbre change dynamically over time and with performance intensity.

nodes.label: Amplitude Envelope
nodes.description: The change of overall amplitude over time, consisting of attack, steady state, and decay sections.

nodes.label: Initial Transient
nodes.description: Rapid and unpredictable changes in harmonic content during the attack portion of a sound.

nodes.label: Linear-Predictive-Coding
nodes.description: A sophisticated mechanism developed from additive and subtractive synthesis principles using computer systems with fast processing speeds.

nodes.label: Clarinet
nodes.description: An acoustic instrument with three distinct registers (Chalumeau, throat, and clarion) demonstrating the relationship between frequency and timbre through resonant zones or formants.

nodes.label: Formants
nodes.description: Resonant zones in acoustic instruments that are uniquely related to the size and shape of the instrument and its resonator, giving instruments their timbral characteristics.

nodes.label: AM Synthesis
nodes.description: Amplitude modulation synthesis that, like FM, provides tools to dynamically alter timbre and connect amplitude with spectral content.

nodes.label: Richard W. Dobson
nodes.description: Author of the chapter on designing legato instruments in Csound, discussing expressive synthesis techniques including vibrato and swell envelopes.

nodes.label: F-tables (Function Tables)
nodes.description: Csound's lookup tables used as transfer-functions to translate and sculpt relationships between synthesis parameters in non-linear ways.

nodes.label: Legato
nodes.description: A performance technique in which pitch changes during the sustain stage of an extended note without breaks, requiring a single mechanism for pitch and volume variation.

nodes.label: Legato Instrument Design
nodes.description: Technique for creating expressive musical instruments in Csound that achieve continuity of loudness and pitch from note to note, supporting slurred and tied notes with dynamic shaping.

nodes.label: Messa di voce
nodes.description: Classical vocal and instrumental technique of swelling and relaxing amplitude on a single note, implemented in legato instruments through dynamic shaping.

nodes.label: Hold Feature (Negative p3)
nodes.description: Csound score mechanism using negative duration values to indicate held or tied notes, allowing the second note to take over the data space of the first.

nodes.label: Legato Synthesis
nodes.description: A technique for synthesizing smooth, connected notes with pitch ramps, amplitude envelopes, and portamento to simulate natural instrument performance.

nodes.label: Dynamic Inflection
nodes.description: Variation of amplitude from note to note or within a note, a primary component of expression on melody instruments.

nodes.label: Modern French School (Flute)
nodes.description: A flute performance tradition characterized by the combination of vibrato and inflection within notes.

nodes.label: Swell Envelope
nodes.description: Dynamic amplitude envelope that creates crescendo and decrescendo effects in synthesized notes, implemented additively in Csound instruments.

nodes.label: Flute Modeling
nodes.description: Synthesis approach modeling flute performance characteristics including vibrato as volume variation, independent vibrato and fingering mechanisms, and dynamic range limitations.

nodes.label: Violin Modeling
nodes.description: Synthesis approach modeling violin performance where vibrato is pitch variation and fingering/vibrato mechanisms are coupled, affecting applicability to fast passage-work.

nodes.label: Attack Tone
nodes.description: The initial transient character of a musical note, analogous to vocal consonants, subject to individual refinement and variation by advanced players.

nodes.label: Flute synthesis
nodes.description: Electroacoustic modeling of flute timbre including attack characteristics, chiff noise, and register-dependent filtering.

nodes.label: Chiff attack
nodes.description: Complex semichaotic noise burst component that characterizes the tongued attack of flute notes, approximated by mixing shaped noise with the main tone.

nodes.label: Syrinx
nodes.description: Solo flute composition by Debussy originally written as incidental music for a play without bar-lines or expression marks.

nodes.label: instr 705
nodes.description: Csound orchestra instrument implementing a full legato flute with chiff attack noise, featuring conditional logic for tied notes and register-dependent filtering.

nodes.label: Defensive programming
nodes.description: Programming practice in Csound that handles edge cases and invalid parameter values gracefully, allowing composers to use convenient score values without strict validation.

nodes.label: Andrew Horner
nodes.description: Co-author of a chapter on contiguous-group wavetable synthesis of the French horn in Csound, developing expressive synthesis models for wind instruments.

nodes.label: Lydia Ayers
nodes.description: Co-author with Andrew Horner on contiguous-group wavetable synthesis techniques for French horn modeling in Csound.

nodes.label: Marcel Moyse
nodes.description: French flute pedagogue whose teaching style emphasizes a particular interpretive approach to classical flute repertoire.

nodes.label: Til Eulenspiegel's Merry Pranks
nodes.description: Orchestral work by Strauss featuring a prominent opening horn solo used as a test case for the contiguous-group wavetable synthesis model.

nodes.label: Contiguous-Group Wavetable Synthesis
nodes.description: A wavetable synthesis technique that allocates harmonics into disjoint groups (fundamental, harmonics 2-3, 4-7, 8+) with separate amplitude envelopes, inspired by group synthesis methods.

nodes.label: French Horn
nodes.description: A brass instrument with conical bore and wide range (F2 to F5 on MIDI scale) characterized by a mellow, ethereal sound due to its bell orientation.

nodes.label: Kleczkowski
nodes.description: Researcher who introduced the concept of group synthesis using disjoint sets of harmonics in wavetables in 1989.

nodes.label: Zwicker and Terhardt
nodes.description: Researchers who studied critical bands in frequency perception, providing perceptual motivation for the harmonic grouping strategy in 1980.

nodes.label: Richard Strauss
nodes.description: Composer of Til Eulenspiegels' Merry Pranks, whose horn solo was used to verify the wavetable synthesis model.

nodes.label: Til Eulenspiegels' Merry Pranks
nodes.description: Orchestral work by Richard Strauss featuring a well-known horn solo that covers the full range of the instrument.

nodes.label: French Horn Synthesis
nodes.description: Wavetable synthesis model designed to emulate the spectral and dynamic characteristics of the French horn using grouped harmonic envelopes.

nodes.label: Group Synthesis Model
nodes.description: Synthesis approach that uses multiple harmonic groups with different amplitude envelopes (linear, squared, cubed, fourth power) to approximate spectral evolution.

nodes.label: Pseudo-Random Number Generator
nodes.description: Deterministic algorithm that produces sequences appearing random without inspection of the algorithm; Csound uses a 16-bit generator with formula Xn = 15625 Xn-1 + 1 mod 2^16 for reproducible compositions.

nodes.label: Brian Evans
nodes.description: Author of the FM synthesis chapter in The Csound Book, demonstrating implementation of Chowning's FM instruments and morphing techniques.

nodes.label: Carrier and Modulator Oscillators
nodes.description: In FM synthesis, the carrier is the oscillator being modulated, while the modulator defines the vibrato or frequency modulation applied to the carrier.

nodes.label: c/m Ratio
nodes.description: The ratio of carrier frequency to modulator frequency. Simple rational ratios produce harmonic spectra, while irrational ratios produce inharmonic spectra.

nodes.label: foscili opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode for frequency modulation oscillation with dynamic index control, used in instrument 1115 for FM synthesis with amplitude and spectral envelopes.

nodes.label: Hammond B3 organ
nodes.description: Tone-wheel organ with 91 tone wheels and drawbars for controlling harmonic content. Features rotating speaker effects and is modeled in Csound using oscil opcodes.

nodes.label: Leslie speaker
nodes.description: A rotating speaker system powered by a tube amplifier, consisting of a stationary high-frequency driver with rotating horn and a low-frequency driver with rotating scoop, creating Doppler and directional effects.

nodes.label: Tone wheel
nodes.description: A rotating disk in the Hammond organ that generates periodic waveforms at different frequencies, with phase variation based on wheel number and time.

nodes.label: Resonant lowpass filter
nodes.description: Key component in analog synthesizer design that attenuates high frequencies while introducing a peak at the cutoff frequency through careful coefficient adjustment.

nodes.label: GEN8
nodes.description: A Csound function table generator for creating piecewise linear waveshaping tables used to simulate distortion.

nodes.label: Analog synthesizer
nodes.description: Electronic instrument that generates sound using oscillators, filters, and envelope generators; the classic design is modeled digitally in Csound.

nodes.label: Tone-wheel organ
nodes.description: Classic electronic keyboard instrument modeled in Csound using multiple oscillators with harmonic drawbars to simulate the sound of electromechanical organs.

nodes.label: Rotating speaker
nodes.description: Audio effect that simulates the Doppler effect using oscillating delay taps with phase separation to create spatial modulation, implemented as instrument 1004 in the Csound example.

nodes.label: Oppenheim, Willsky, and Young 1983
nodes.description: Reference work on filter theory cited for understanding differential equations and frequency response analysis in filter design.

nodes.label: Roland TB-303
nodes.description: A sought-after analog synthesizer known for its unique filter character and distinctive sound, which prevents self-oscillation by introducing distortion at high resonance.

nodes.label: Difference Equation
nodes.description: A discrete-time approximation of differential equations used to implement analog filter behavior in digital systems, relating output samples to input and previous output samples.

nodes.label: Distortion Filter
nodes.description: A filter technique that simulates the TB-303's behavior by isolating the resonating portion of a signal, passing it through a distortion table, and adding it to a lowpass-filtered signal.

nodes.label: Fourier
nodes.description: Mathematician (1768–1830) who developed theoretical principles stating that any signal can be expressed as a sum of sines or cosines with different amplitudes, frequencies, and phases.

nodes.label: Frequency-Domain Synthesis
nodes.description: A synthesis approach based on Fourier's principle that any signal can be decomposed into and reconstructed from sinusoidal components with specific amplitude, frequency, and phase parameters.

nodes.label: Rajmil Fischman
nodes.description: Author of the chapter on classic synthesis techniques in Csound, providing detailed explanations and examples of additive, subtractive, and other synthesis methods.

nodes.label: The Sorcerer's Apprentice
nodes.description: A musical work by Dukas used in the additive synthesis example to demonstrate synthetic bassoon timbre.

nodes.label: Paul Dukas
nodes.description: Composer of The Sorcerer's Apprentice, whose work is referenced in the additive synthesis examples.

nodes.label: Backus
nodes.description: Author cited for providing data on the frequency and amplitude components of a bassoon-like sound used in additive synthesis examples.

nodes.label: Dynamic Spectrum Synthesis
nodes.description: A synthesis approach where amplitude and frequency of each spectral component change throughout the duration of a sound, requiring time-dependent control of multiple oscillators.

nodes.label: oscil1 opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for generating control-rate oscillations, used in the chapter for time-varying amplitude and frequency fluctuation control in dynamic spectrum synthesis.

nodes.label: Panning Algorithm
nodes.description: A spatial audio technique implemented in Csound using equal-power pan and wide-stereo effects to position sound sources between or beyond stereo speakers.

nodes.label: Pulse Train
nodes.description: A signal containing an infinite number of harmonics with the same relative amplitude, approximated in practice by combining as many harmonics as possible up to the auditory range threshold.

nodes.label: Bandreject Filter
nodes.description: One of four classic filter types that rejects frequencies within a specified band while passing others, also called a notch filter.

nodes.label: Filter Cascade
nodes.description: A filter connection method where the output of one filter is used as the input of another to achieve sharper frequency responses.

nodes.label: Parallel Filter Connection
nodes.description: A filter connection method where two or more filters share the same input and have their outputs mixed into one signal to achieve complex response curves.

nodes.label: Csound rand opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates white noise by producing random numbers at each sample.

nodes.label: Csound buzz opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that produces a pulse train with as many harmonics as possible given the sampling rate.

nodes.label: Csound reson opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing a bandpass resonant filter used in subtractive synthesis.

nodes.label: Csound randi opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates random control-rate values, used for dynamic filter modulation.

nodes.label: Csound linen opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates a linear envelope with attack, sustain, and release segments.

nodes.label: Filter Roll-off
nodes.description: The slope of transition between pass and stop regions in a filter, measured in decibels per octave, representing the change in attenuation when frequency is doubled.

nodes.label: Cutoff Frequency
nodes.description: In filter design, the frequency value at which attenuation is –3 dB, equivalent to a drop in amplitude by a factor of about 0.71.

nodes.label: Vowel Articulation Synthesis
nodes.description: A synthesis technique that models vocal chord mechanisms by passing a rich pulse through parallel bandpass filters with center frequencies and bandwidths corresponding to human speech formants.

nodes.label: Carrier-to-Modulator Ratio
nodes.description: The ratio between carrier and modulator frequencies (c/m ratio) that determines whether the output spectrum is harmonic or inharmonic; integer ratios produce harmonic results.

nodes.label: instr 1110
nodes.description: A Csound instrument implementing ring modulation with separate function tables for carrier and modulator signals.

nodes.label: instr 1111
nodes.description: A dynamic ring modulation instrument in Csound with time-varying amplitude, carrier frequency, carrier-to-modulator ratio, and modulation fraction.

nodes.label: Distortion Index
nodes.description: A parameter (K) representing the amplitude of the input signal to a waveshaper that controls the prominence of higher harmonics and the amount of distortion applied.

nodes.label: Csound table opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that implements transfer functions for waveshaping by using sample values as indices into a function table.

nodes.label: Csound oscil opcode
nodes.description: A Csound oscillator opcode used to generate sinusoidal input signals for waveshaping processing.

nodes.label: instr 1113
nodes.description: A dual waveshaping Csound instrument that produces brass-like fanfare by mixing two waveshapers with different frequency characteristics in a 0.8:0.2 proportion.

nodes.label: instr 1114
nodes.description: A simple static FM Csound instrument demonstrating frequency modulation synthesis with variable modulation index values.

nodes.label: Chebyshev Functions
nodes.description: Mathematical functions used as waveshaping functions to produce various combinations of harmonics when applied to sinewaves.

nodes.label: Instrument 1115
nodes.description: Csound FM instrument demonstrating dynamic FM synthesis with time-varying amplitude and spectral envelopes for modeling bell, woodwind, brass, and membranophone sounds.

nodes.label: Whitfield
nodes.description: Researcher cited for psychoacoustic findings on the threshold of human pitch and amplitude recognition at approximately 50 milliseconds.

nodes.label: Russell Pinkston
nodes.description: Author of the chapter on constrained random event generation and retriggering in Csound, demonstrating advanced instrument design techniques.

nodes.label: Formant-Wave-Function Synthesis
nodes.description: A synthesis technique developed from the combination of subtractive and granular synthesis.

nodes.label: Wavelet Analysis and Synthesis
nodes.description: A signal analysis technique mentioned alongside granular synthesis for experimentation with short cyclic waveforms.

nodes.label: instr 1201
nodes.description: A simple Csound FM instrument implementing Chowning's FM synthesis with shared envelope for modulator and carrier, capable of imitating brass, woodwind, bassoon, clarinet, and bell timbres.

nodes.label: instr 1202
nodes.description: An improved Csound FM instrument using the foscili opcode with independent envelopes for modulation index and carrier amplitude, providing greater parametric control.

nodes.label: Operator
nodes.description: In DX7-style synthesis, an operator is a pair consisting of an oscillator and an envelope generator, used to build complex modulation algorithms.

nodes.label: Stacked Modulators
nodes.description: A complex modulation algorithm where a single carrier is modulated by a modulator that is itself modulated by a second modulator, producing distinctly different results in PM versus FM.

nodes.label: David Bristow
nodes.description: Co-author with John Chowning of FM Theory and Applications, referenced for DX7 parameter mapping.

nodes.label: GEN2
nodes.description: Csound GEN routine for direct data entry into function tables, used to store parameter data without automatic rescaling when the GEN number is negative.

nodes.label: FM Theory and Applications
nodes.description: Book by John Chowning and David Bristow providing documentation on FM synthesis and DX7 parameter mapping for synthesizer emulation.

nodes.label: Opcode DX/TX Editor
nodes.description: Software editor for Yamaha DX7/TX synthesizers; its manual appendix provided accurate information on envelope generator rates, levels, and frequency tables.

nodes.label: Operator Algorithm
nodes.description: A configuration of 6 operators in FM synthesis where algorithm 16 features a loop topology with carrier and modulator relationships.

nodes.label: Velocity Sensitivity
nodes.description: A parameter controlling how MIDI note velocity affects operator envelope levels and amplitude modulation in FM synthesis.

nodes.label: Rate Scaling
nodes.description: A parameter that adjusts envelope rates based on pitch to maintain consistent envelope behavior across the keyboard.

nodes.label: Csound table opcode
nodes.description: An opcode for reading values from function tables, used extensively to retrieve operator parameters and envelope data.

nodes.label: Csound phasor opcode
nodes.description: An opcode generating a ramp signal from 0 to 1 at audio rate, used to drive oscillator phase in FM synthesis.

nodes.label: Csound linseg opcode
nodes.description: An opcode generating piecewise linear envelopes at control rate, used to implement multi-segment envelope generators.

nodes.label: Csound oscili opcode
nodes.description: An opcode for interpolated table-lookup oscillation at audio rate, used for carrier and modulator signal generation.

nodes.label: Csound expseg opcode
nodes.description: An opcode generating exponential segment envelopes, used to implement the LFO amplitude envelope in this code.

nodes.label: Chowning/Bristow Book
nodes.description: A reference work providing amplitude scaling data for FM synthesis operator output levels used in this Csound DX7 emulation.

nodes.label: DX7 Algorithm 16
nodes.description: A specific operator routing algorithm from the Yamaha DX7 synthesizer being emulated in this Csound instrument.

nodes.label: Operator Modulation
nodes.description: In FM synthesis, operators can serve as carriers or modulators; this implementation requires different amplitude scaling tables for each role.

nodes.label: D. Bristow
nodes.description: Co-author with John Chowning of FM Theory and Applications—By Musicians for Musicians (1985).

nodes.label: Allan S. C. Lee
nodes.description: Author of the granular synthesis chapter in The Csound Book, demonstrating practical applications of granular synthesis techniques.

nodes.label: Bastiaans
nodes.description: Mathematician who mathematically verified Gabor's theory of granular synthesis in 1985.

nodes.label: Lippe
nodes.description: Composer who has used granular synthesis techniques since 1993.

nodes.label: Yamaha Music Foundation
nodes.description: Publisher of FM Theory and Applications—By Musicians for Musicians by Chowning and Bristow in 1985.

nodes.label: Opcode Systems
nodes.description: Software company based in Palo Alto, California that published the DX/TX Editor/Librarian Manual in 1986.

nodes.label: William Schottstaedt
nodes.description: Researcher who published on the simulation of natural instrument tones using frequency modulation with complex modulating waves in 1977.

nodes.label: GEN1 subroutine
nodes.description: A Csound subroutine that creates function tables in sizes of powers of two for storing waveform data.

nodes.label: random number generator
nodes.description: A Csound feature seeded by the iseed parameter to produce random offsets and variations in grain parameters across multiple voices or channels.

nodes.label: Martin Bastiaans
nodes.description: Author of 1985 work on sliding-window representation of signals, relevant to granular synthesis theory.

nodes.label: Michael Clarke
nodes.description: Author of the preceding section on granular use of FOG synthesis in Csound, exploring the intersection of time and frequency in composition.

nodes.label: FOG Synthesis
nodes.description: A granular synthesis technique adapted from FOF synthesis for granulating soundfiles, enabling time-stretching, pitch-shifting, and texture creation through controlled grain parameters.

nodes.label: Formant frequency
nodes.description: A parameter in FOF processing that controls the pitch and resonant qualities of processed samples, allowing frequency domain effects like FM, chorusing, delay, and flanging.

nodes.label: Vocal imitation
nodes.description: A synthesis application using multiple fof opcodes with a common fundamental frequency and complex vibrato modeled on the CHANT program, with formant data for different vowels.

nodes.label: Formant bandwidth
nodes.description: A parameter (kband) that determines the bandwidth of the formant region at -6dB and controls the exponential decay rate of the local envelope.

nodes.label: Envelope attack time
nodes.description: A parameter (kris) that controls the rise time of the excitation envelope and determines the skirtwidth at -40dB in the spectral domain.

nodes.label: Uncertainty principle
nodes.description: A principle from modern physics with a parallel in the inverse relationship between time and frequency in FOF synthesis, where longer local envelope segments produce narrower bands of partials.

nodes.label: FOG unit-generator
nodes.description: A Csound opcode implementing FOG synthesis with parameters for amplitude, density, pitch, speed, and grain envelope control.

nodes.label: basmrmba.aif
nodes.description: A bass marimba phrase soundfile used as example material for FOG synthesis demonstrations in The Csound Book.

nodes.label: Per Byrne Villez
nodes.description: Author of the FOF processing chapter in The Csound Book, demonstrating advanced techniques including octaviation and khoomei vocal synthesis.

nodes.label: Tambura
nodes.description: A 4-stringed drone instrument in the bass register used in Indian classical music, used as an example sample for FOF processing in Csound.

nodes.label: Jitter
nodes.description: A technique using random modulation of pitch to recreate the natural fluctuations found in human singing and acoustic instrument performance.

nodes.label: Phase difference
nodes.description: A technique where the same sample is offset in time (skiptime) between channels to create subtle timbral changes and equalization effects.

nodes.label: Octaviation
nodes.description: A FOF technique that gradually removes or introduces every other granule in the FOF pulse-train by deviating the fundamental in octave steps, creating effects like sound disintegration or multiple voices.

nodes.label: Khoomei (Sygyt)
nodes.description: A Mongolian and Tuvan singing style that produces a mid-range vocal drone with a piercing melody by reinforcing resonances within the singer's nasal cavities, originating from shepherds imitating wind sounds.

nodes.label: Tuva, Siberia
nodes.description: A region where khoomei throat singing originated, along with Mongolia, as a vocal technique inspired by natural wind sounds.

nodes.label: Mongolia
nodes.description: A region where khoomei throat singing technique originated and is practiced.

nodes.label: Stochastic processes
nodes.description: Compositional approach where all musical transitions are governed by random values drawn from suitable probability distributions, pioneered by Xenakis for generating pitch, timbre, speed, amplitude, and note density.

nodes.label: Pseudo-random numbers
nodes.description: Approximation of true randomness used in deterministic computers, necessary because true randomness is impossible within computational systems.

nodes.label: Declicking envelope
nodes.description: Amplitude envelope technique that removes sudden amplitude jumps when starting and stopping random sequences to prevent audible clicks.

nodes.label: David A. Jaffe
nodes.description: Researcher who published criteria for evaluating synthesis techniques in the Computer Music Journal.

nodes.label: Standard deviation
nodes.description: The square root of variance, used as a dimensionless measure of spread in a probability distribution, typically represented by σ.

nodes.label: instr 1602
nodes.description: A Csound instrument demonstrating a chorusing effect using Gaussian frequency deviation around a 333 Hz center frequency, with random pitch variations on multiple oscillators.

nodes.label: Poisson distribution
nodes.description: Discrete probability distribution describing the number of independent events occurring at a random rate, available in Csound via the poisson opcode with parameter lambda.

nodes.label: Exponential distribution
nodes.description: A probability distribution with mathematical form a*exp(−ax), describing asymmetric decay from an initial peak, used to model waiting times in continuous processes.

nodes.label: Binomial distribution
nodes.description: A discrete probability distribution arising from repeated independent trials (such as coin tosses), which converges to the normal distribution as the number of trials approaches infinity.

nodes.label: Law of Large Numbers
nodes.description: A statistical principle stating that as the number of tests increases, the observed distribution better approximates the underlying theoretical distribution.

nodes.label: Weibull distribution
nodes.description: Flexible probability distribution available in Csound that can transition between exponential and Gaussian shapes depending on parameter t, useful for smooth transitions between distribution types.

nodes.label: Beta distribution
nodes.description: Probability distribution in Csound with parameters a and b; when both are less than 1, it concentrates probability at the ends of the range, useful for bimodal musical control.

nodes.label: Cauchy distribution
nodes.description: Probability distribution in Csound with more values away from the peak than Gaussian distribution, usable as an alternative for certain musical control scenarios.

nodes.label: Blue Noise
nodes.description: Noise where power density increases with frequency (density proportional to f), said to be good for dithering applications.

nodes.label: Moore
nodes.description: Developer of an algorithm for generating pink noise with approximately pink frequency distribution, cited in the context of Csound synthesis techniques.

nodes.label: Gardner 1978
nodes.description: A reference work on pink noise generation algorithms, cited as foundational for Moore's pink noise algorithm.

nodes.label: Synthetic Instruments
nodes.description: Digitally created instruments that can sound too clean and sterile without the addition of noise and randomness to simulate physical instrument characteristics.

nodes.label: Duffing's equation
nodes.description: A nonlinear differential equation (x'' + x = e*x³) used to generate periodic and chaotic oscillations for sound synthesis, expressible as an overtone series via additive synthesis.

nodes.label: van der Pol's equation
nodes.description: A nonlinear differential equation (y'' + ey'(1-y) + y = 0) that exhibits cyclical behavior and can be used to generate repetitive musical structures.

nodes.label: Popcorn Simulator (instr 1704)
nodes.description: A Csound instrument that generates percussive popcorn-like sounds using white noise, bandpass filtering, and random event retriggering with variable gap durations.

nodes.label: Three-Part Gesture Instrument (instr 1705)
nodes.description: A complex Csound instrument combining randomly gated oscillators, amplitude modulation, percussive sequences, and panning effects to create a complete musical phrase or gesture.

nodes.label: oscil1i opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for interpolated oscillation with linear interpolation, used to apply overall panning curves stored in function tables.

nodes.label: Constrained Random Event Generation
nodes.description: A technique in Csound for generating random musical events within specified boundaries and timing constraints, demonstrated through the popcorn and gesture instruments.

nodes.label: Reinit Block
nodes.description: A Csound programming structure that allows selective reinitialization of code sections during performance, enabling dynamic parameter updates.

nodes.label: reinit statement
nodes.description: Csound control structure that reinitializes code blocks during note execution, enabling dynamic parameter changes and algorithmic event generation.

nodes.label: Constrained Random Event Generation
nodes.description: Technique for generating random musical parameters (pitch, duration, panning) within carefully defined constraints using lookup tables and seed values.

nodes.label: Gesture Instrument
nodes.description: Multi-part Csound instrument design that sequences three distinct musical gestures using timout and branching control structures.

nodes.label: C Minor 7 Chord
nodes.description: Pitch class set (C, Eb, G, Bb) used as constraint for melodic choices in the algorithmic music generator example.

nodes.label: instr 1705
nodes.description: Three-part gesture Csound instrument demonstrating constrained random event generation with timout-based sequencing.

nodes.label: instr 1706
nodes.description: Algorithmic music generator Csound instrument that produces short compositions with constrained random pitch, duration, and panning selections.

nodes.label: Martin Dupras
nodes.description: Author of the chapter on global Csound instruments for meta-parameter control in The Csound Book.

nodes.label: Cscore
nodes.description: A Csound utility that makes working with score data relatively straightforward.

nodes.label: Constrained Random Music Instrument (instr 1706)
nodes.description: A Csound instrument that uses tables to constrain random pitch, duration, and amplitude values for algorithmic music generation.

nodes.label: timout/reinit
nodes.description: A Csound retriggering mechanism that allows multiple notes to be generated within an instrument, though notes cannot overlap.

nodes.label: ADSR Generator
nodes.description: An envelope generator implementing attack, decay, sustain, and release stages for amplitude control in synthesizers.

nodes.label: Time-Varying Stochastic Generator
nodes.description: A meta-control instrument that generates complex random values with specific distributions (such as Gaussian) for use in sound-producing instruments.

nodes.label: Probability Mask
nodes.description: A stochastic generator that picks random numbers uniformly between two instantaneous time-varying values, achieved by rescaling random number generator output.

nodes.label: samphold opcode
nodes.description: A Csound unit generator that stores and outputs signal values, used to maintain the state of the Schmitt trigger output.

nodes.label: Feedback Instruments
nodes.description: Csound technique for creating feedback loops by sending an instrument's output back to itself, with applications in physical modeling and nonlinear systems.

nodes.label: Context-Sensitive Instruments
nodes.description: Csound technique allowing instruments to listen to and respond to each other's output through global variables, enabling inverse amplitude relationships.

nodes.label: Digital Waveguide Modeling
nodes.description: A computationally efficient method of expressing the wave equation for sound synthesis, based on bi-directional delay lines to simulate traveling waves and reflections.

nodes.label: Kevin Karplus
nodes.description: Co-developer of the Karplus-Strong algorithm for plucked string synthesis.

nodes.label: Alex Strong
nodes.description: Co-developer of the Karplus-Strong algorithm for plucked string synthesis.

nodes.label: Wave Equation
nodes.description: A differential equation that describes the behavior of waves in a medium, fundamental to physical modeling of acoustic instruments.

nodes.label: DC Blocker
nodes.description: A special type of filter used in waveguide instruments to prevent offset from zero that can produce off-scale values when fed back into the system.

nodes.label: Global Feedback Instrument
nodes.description: A Csound instrument technique using global variables to pass data between instruments for meta-parameter control and feedback synthesis.

nodes.label: Waveguide Slide-Flute (instr 1902)
nodes.description: Csound instrument implementing Perry Cook's slide-flute model using embouchure and bore delay lines with cubic nonlinearity.

nodes.label: Waveguide Clarinet (instr 1903)
nodes.description: Csound instrument derived from Perry Cook's clarinet model using bi-directional delay lines and feedback tables.

nodes.label: Waveguide Drum
nodes.description: Two-dimensional waveguide model extending the technique to membrane simulation with delay lines representing wave propagation between four corners.

nodes.label: Bi-directional Delay Line
nodes.description: Two coupled delay lines whose outputs feed each other's inputs, used in clarinet and drum models.

nodes.label: Feedback Table
nodes.description: Lookup table in the clarinet model that varies feedback based on pressure difference, accounting for reed stiffness variations.

nodes.label: Edward Lorenz
nodes.description: Discoverer of the Lorenz Attractor, one of the first chaotic systems discovered, which describes convection currents in gases or liquids.

nodes.label: Lorenz Attractor
nodes.description: A chaotic system defined by differential equations that exhibits strange attractor behavior with repetitive yet nonrepeating paths, used to generate unusual timbres.

nodes.label: Strange Attractor
nodes.description: A type of chaotic system that exhibits complex, nonrepeating yet bounded behavior, used in Csound to generate unusual and bizarre timbres.

nodes.label: Waveguide Square Drum (instr 1904-1905)
nodes.description: A Csound instrument implementing a physical model of a square drum using bidirectional delay lines and feedback, capable of producing bongo, conga, and marimba-like sounds.

nodes.label: Lorenz Attractor Instrument (instr 1908)
nodes.description: A Csound instrument that sonifies the Lorenz Attractor equations, using differential equation approximation to generate chaotic audio output.

nodes.label: R. Erik Spjut
nodes.description: Author of the signal processing chapter in The Csound Book, providing examples and explanations of filter design, modulation techniques, and DSP applications in Csound.

nodes.label: Rössler Attractor
nodes.description: A chaotic dynamical system defined by three coupled differential equations, implemented in Csound as a tone generator using numerical integration methods.

nodes.label: Planet Orbiting in Binary Star System
nodes.description: A physical simulation instrument in Csound that models gravitational dynamics of a planet orbiting two stars, using Newton's laws of gravity and momentum.

nodes.label: James Gleick
nodes.description: Author of Chaos (1987), referenced for the mathematical definition of the Rössler Attractor.

nodes.label: A. K. Dewdney
nodes.description: Author of The Armchair Universe (1988), referenced for the binary star system orbital mechanics concept.

nodes.label: Dynamical Systems
nodes.description: Mathematical systems that evolve over time according to differential equations, used in Csound as tone generators and modulation sources.

nodes.label: Polar Form
nodes.description: Representation of complex numbers using magnitude and phase angle, commonly used in signal processing.

nodes.label: Mathematica
nodes.description: A computational software tool that can calculate Fourier series and Fourier coefficients for periodic functions, useful for generating function tables in Csound.

nodes.label: Continuous-time signals
nodes.description: Signals that have a value at any instant of time, such as sin(2πf₀t) and cos(2πf₀t), representing physical phenomena like sound and temperature.

nodes.label: Discrete-time signals
nodes.description: Signals that only have values at fixed instants of time, naturally represented in computers as values stored in successive memory locations.

nodes.label: Periodic signals
nodes.description: Signals where x(t) = x(t + T) for some period T, with fundamental frequency f₀ and fundamental period T₀ = 1/|f₀|.

nodes.label: Euler formula
nodes.description: Mathematical notation e^(j2πf₀t) = cos(2πf₀t) + j·sin(2πf₀t) used as shorthand for representing sinusoidal signals in signal processing.

nodes.label: GEN9
nodes.description: A Csound function generator designed to create a table with one period of a periodic function from Fourier coefficients.

nodes.label: GEN10
nodes.description: A Csound function generator designed to create a table with one period of a periodic function from Fourier coefficients.

nodes.label: GEN19
nodes.description: A Csound function generator designed to create a table with one period of a periodic function from Fourier coefficients.

nodes.label: Discrete-Time Fourier Transform
nodes.description: The sampled-signal version of the Fourier transform, calculating frequency content from discrete samples where frequency is expressed as a fraction of the sampling frequency.

nodes.label: Impulse
nodes.description: A special aperiodic signal: in continuous time, infinitely tall and thin with area 1; in discrete time, a single sample of value 1 surrounded by zeros. Contains all frequencies in equal strength.

nodes.label: Band-Limited Signal
nodes.description: A signal whose frequency content is limited to certain frequency ranges or bands, with zero energy outside those ranges.

nodes.label: dispfft
nodes.description: A Csound built-in function for plotting the magnitude of a Fourier transform.

nodes.label: Band-Limited Signal
nodes.description: A signal whose frequency content is restricted to frequencies below one-half the sample rate to prevent aliasing.

nodes.label: Linear Time-Invariant Systems
nodes.description: Systems where output is directly proportional to input and behavior is independent of when the input occurs, useful for predictable signal processing.

nodes.label: Linear Time-Invariant (LTI) System
nodes.description: A system whose impulse response can be used to determine the response to any input signal through convolution.

nodes.label: Frequency Response
nodes.description: The transfer function H(f) that describes how an LTI system responds to different frequencies; the Fourier transform of the impulse response.

nodes.label: pvoc opcode
nodes.description: The basic Csound unit generator for phase vocoder resynthesis that uses a time-pointer index to access analysis frames and perform interpolation between frames.

nodes.label: Parametric Equalization
nodes.description: A filter type used for musical purposes that allows adjustment of frequency, gain, and bandwidth parameters.

nodes.label: Shelving Filter
nodes.description: A filter type used for musical purposes that boosts or cuts frequencies above or below a specified frequency.

nodes.label: Block Diagram
nodes.description: A graphical representation of difference equations using summation operators, delay operators, and coefficient multipliers.

nodes.label: Inverse Fourier Transform
nodes.description: Mathematical technique used to calculate raw filter coefficients from a desired frequency response in FIR filter design.

nodes.label: cvanal
nodes.description: Csound utility that converts filter coefficient soundfiles to frequency response data for use with the convolve opcode.

nodes.label: Voice Scrambler
nodes.description: A DSP application that reverses the frequency spectrum of a band-limited voice signal using amplitude modulation and filtering, making speech unintelligible.

nodes.label: Spectral data types
nodes.description: Csound feature based on perceptual methods for gathering and storing auditory-relevant data to enable computer instruments to extract musically important information from audio signals.

nodes.label: wsig
nodes.description: A connecting data object in Csound spectral processing that contains spectral magnitudes and self-defining metadata about spectrum analysis parameters.

nodes.label: Pitch detection
nodes.description: A perceptually-based feature detection method in Csound spectral opcodes that gradually mounts evidence favoring a certain pitch.

nodes.label: Computational auditory pathways
nodes.description: A framework for music understanding developed by Barry Vercoe that models human auditory perception within Csound instruments.

nodes.label: specptrk opcode
nodes.description: Csound pitch tracking opcode that detects pitch by matching spectral data against a harmonic partial template using cross-correlation.

nodes.label: specdiff opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode that calculates positive differences between consecutive spectral frames, functioning as a delta analyzer and energy onset detector.

nodes.label: specfilt opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode that injects spectral values into first-order lowpass filters attached to each frequency channel.

nodes.label: specsum opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode that sums energy sensation across all frequency bins to produce a composite control signal.

nodes.label: Beat Tracking and Tempo Following
nodes.description: Application of Csound spectral processing to detect audible beats and follow changing tempo in human-like fashion by modeling energy integration.

nodes.label: Fletcher-Munson Scaling
nodes.description: Psychoacoustic scaling applied in spectral processing to simulate the frequency-favoring effect of the auditory canal.

nodes.label: Povel and Okkerman 1981
nodes.description: Psychoacoustic research on human energy integration and rhythmic perception cited for understanding auditory system behavior.

nodes.label: Cross-Correlation
nodes.description: Signal processing technique used in specptrk to match spectral data against harmonic partial templates for pitch detection.

nodes.label: Parabolic Interpolation
nodes.description: Technique employed in specptrk to achieve pitch resolution higher than the frequency bins-per-octave of the originating spectrum.

nodes.label: harmon4 opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that generates up to four vocal transpositions while preserving formants, requiring an Extended Csound accelerator card for optimal performance.

nodes.label: tempest opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode for beat and tempo estimation using short-term echoic memory modeling and rhythmic expectation.

nodes.label: ICMC 1990
nodes.description: International Computer Music Conference where Barry Vercoe and Dan Ellis demonstrated live beat-tracking control of musical performance.

nodes.label: Analog Devices 21060
nodes.description: Floating-point DSP accelerator used in Extended Csound for real-time audio processing.

nodes.label: Digital Delay Line
nodes.description: A fundamental audio signal processing mechanism that records an input signal, stores it in a circular buffer, and plays it back with a variable delay time.

nodes.label: Tape Echo
nodes.description: An analog studio effect created by simultaneously monitoring record and playback heads of a tape recorder, serving as the conceptual model for digital delay lines.

nodes.label: International Computer Music Conference 1996
nodes.description: Professional conference where Alessandro Cipriani's works have been selected for performance and included on official CDs (ICMC95, ICMC99).

nodes.label: FIR filters
nodes.description: Finite Impulse Response filters that can be constructed using delay opcodes in Csound.

nodes.label: Slapback echo
nodes.description: A stereo echo effect created by delaying a plucked string sound at different delay times to produce multiple echoes.

nodes.label: Variable Delay Line
nodes.description: A digital delay technique where the playback point speed varies relative to the record point, producing changes in both delay time and perceived pitch.

nodes.label: Delay-Line Vibrato
nodes.description: A vibrato effect created by applying a low-frequency oscillator to the delay time parameter of a variable delay line, causing periodic pitch fluctuation.

nodes.label: Flanging
nodes.description: An audio effect created by combining an original signal with a delayed copy whose delay time varies slowly, producing a distinctive sweeping 'wooshing' sound.

nodes.label: Global Variables in Csound
nodes.description: Variables prefixed with 'g' in Csound that persist across instrument instances and can be used for inter-instrument communication and effects sends.

nodes.label: Crossfading
nodes.description: A technique of smoothly transitioning between two audio signals by modulating their gains, used in pitch shifters to avoid clicks at delay buffer wraparound points.

nodes.label: Delay buffer wraparound
nodes.description: The point where a delay line's read pointer reaches the end of the buffer and wraps back to the beginning, which can produce audible clicks if not gated properly.

nodes.label: Digital Delay Lines
nodes.description: Flexible audio processing functions capable of creating effects such as harmonization, flanging, and reverberation through variable delay times and feedback.

nodes.label: Moorer (1979)
nodes.description: A reference text providing in-depth technical and mathematical information on reverberation design.

nodes.label: Begault (1994)
nodes.description: Referenced study on auditory localization, ITD envelope onset times, pan pots, precedence effect, and head movements.

nodes.label: Standing Waves
nodes.description: Acoustic phenomenon where waveforms that fit the distance between opposing walls are reinforced, resulting in frequency-dependent room coloration.

nodes.label: Interaural Time Delay
nodes.description: The time interval between sound entering one ear and entering the other, used by the auditory system for sound localization.

nodes.label: I Am Sitting in a Room
nodes.description: Composition by Alvin Lucier that demonstrates room resonance and filtering effects by repeatedly recording and playing back spoken voice in a room.

nodes.label: tone opcode
nodes.description: Csound lowpass filter opcode with gradual rolloff characteristics, useful for simulating natural high-frequency attenuation in sound propagation.

nodes.label: butterlp opcode
nodes.description: Csound Butterworth lowpass filter opcode with sharp cutoff, useful for isolating spectral bands.

nodes.label: deltap opcode
nodes.description: Csound delay tap opcode used to extract signals from delay lines at specific time points.

nodes.label: randi opcode
nodes.description: Csound random impulse generator opcode used to create band-limited white noise.

nodes.label: linseg opcode
nodes.description: Csound linear segment envelope generator opcode used to create time-varying control signals.

nodes.label: Room acoustics and filtering
nodes.description: The acoustic phenomenon where room resonances and reflections filter and color sound, creating spatial and tonal effects.

nodes.label: Stereo diffusion of reflections
nodes.description: Technique for simulating spatial distribution of acoustic reflections across a stereo field using multiple delay taps and reverb channels.

nodes.label: White noise for reverberator testing
nodes.description: Method of testing reverberators using band-limited white noise with sharp attack to reveal transient response characteristics.

nodes.label: Feedback Loop
nodes.description: A recirculating delay line where output is fed back into input, fundamental to reverberator design for simulating the buildup of acoustic reflections.

nodes.label: Stereo Reverberator
nodes.description: A reverberator design that processes audio on two channels independently, using decorrelated delay and filter networks to create realistic spatial reverberation.

nodes.label: Reson bandpass filter
nodes.description: Csound opcode (reson) used to break input signals into frequency bands for creative multiband reverberation design.

nodes.label: Stereo reverb design
nodes.description: Reverberation architecture using parallel allpass and comb filters with decorrelated delay times to create spatial effects.

nodes.label: Metallic reverb
nodes.description: Creative reverb effect achieved by passing signals through series of comb filters with strong resonances at specific frequencies.

nodes.label: Multiband reverb
nodes.description: Reverberation design that breaks input into frequency bands using reson filters, each modulated by slowly changing envelopes for phase movement.

nodes.label: Nested Allpass Filter
nodes.description: Multiple allpass filters arranged in series and surrounded by additional allpass filters to simulate dense reflections in room reverberation.

nodes.label: Digital Reverberation
nodes.description: Computer-based simulation of acoustic reverberation using delay lines and filters to create a sense of space and presence.

nodes.label: Small Room Reverberator
nodes.description: A reverb processor combining double and single nested allpass filters with prefiltering and feedback paths to simulate small room acoustics.

nodes.label: Gardner reverberator
nodes.description: A reverb algorithm architecture using cascaded allpass filters and delays, implemented in multiple room-size variants.

nodes.label: Small room reverb (instr 2402)
nodes.description: Csound instrument implementing a small room reverberator using double nested allpass and single nested allpass filters.

nodes.label: Medium room reverb (instr 2403)
nodes.description: Csound instrument implementing a medium room reverberator with double nested allpass followed by single nested allpass.

nodes.label: Large room reverb (instr 2404)
nodes.description: Csound instrument implementing a large room reverberator using two allpass filters in series followed by nested allpass stages.

nodes.label: Elijah Breder
nodes.description: Co-author of the chapter on Csound-based auditory localization, focusing on spatial audio and 3D sound perception.

nodes.label: David McIntyre
nodes.description: Co-author of the chapter on Csound-based auditory localization and 3D audio systems.

nodes.label: Lord Rayleigh
nodes.description: Pioneer in binaural sound localization research who performed experiments in 1876 and 1907 on interaural time and intensity differences.

nodes.label: William G. Gardner
nodes.description: Author of 'The Virtual Acoustic Room' thesis from MIT Media Lab (1992), relevant to spatial audio design.

nodes.label: hrtfer opcode
nodes.description: Csound unit generator that performs spectral modifications using Head Related Transfer Functions (HRTFs) to create three-dimensional auditory space illusions.

nodes.label: Head Related Transfer Functions (HRTFs)
nodes.description: Spectral modifications that process mono signals to create left/right audio pairs simulating 3D spatial audio perception.

nodes.label: Binaural localization
nodes.description: The ability to localize sound sources in three-dimensional space using interaural time differences (ITDs) and interaural intensity differences (IIDs).

nodes.label: Interaural time differences (ITDs)
nodes.description: Temporal differences in sound arrival between the two ears, used for localizing sound sources particularly at lower frequencies.

nodes.label: Interaural intensity differences (IIDs)
nodes.description: Amplitude differences between the two ears caused by head shadowing effects, particularly important for higher frequency localization.

nodes.label: 3D audio
nodes.description: Spatial audio techniques that create the illusion of sound sources positioned in three-dimensional space using spectral modifications and binaural processing.

nodes.label: Eli Breder
nodes.description: Author of the hrtfer unit generator chapter in The Csound Book, implementing HRTF-based 3D audio spatialization.

nodes.label: Duplex Theory of Localization
nodes.description: Theory suggesting that interaural intensity differences (IIDs) and interaural time differences (ITDs) operate over exclusive frequency regions, with a boundary around 1.5 kHz.

nodes.label: Interaural Time Difference (ITD)
nodes.description: Temporal difference in sound arrival between the two ears, used by the auditory system for localization below approximately 1.5 kHz.

nodes.label: Interaural Intensity Difference (IID)
nodes.description: Amplitude difference between the two ears caused by head shadow effect, used for localization above approximately 1.5 kHz.

nodes.label: Precedence Effect
nodes.description: Auditory system's ability to localize a sound source within a reverberant environment, also known as the Haas effect or Blauert's law of the first wavefront.

nodes.label: Head-Related Transfer Function (HRTF)
nodes.description: The filtering process of the outer ears that imposes amplitude and phase changes as a function of sound source location, used to simulate spectral cues for localization.

nodes.label: Cone of Confusion
nodes.description: Concept describing how points on a conical surface extending from a listener's ear can have identical IID and ITD values, creating ambiguity in localization.

nodes.label: Pinnae
nodes.description: Outer ear structures responsible for spectral alterations of incoming soundwaves through directional filtering.

nodes.label: Middlebrooks and Green 1991
nodes.description: Study on head shadow effect and interaural intensity differences at frequencies above 1.5 kHz.

nodes.label: Hiranaka and Yamasaki 1982
nodes.description: Study showing that different people exhibit different HRTFs but share similar spectral patterns.

nodes.label: Asano, Suzuki, and Sone 1990
nodes.description: Study on HRTF measurements and spectral patterns in auditory localization.

nodes.label: Genuit 1984
nodes.description: Study on directionally dependent spectral alterations caused by the upper body in the 100 Hz–2 kHz range.

nodes.label: hrtfer unit generator
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that implements HRTF-based filtering for 3D audio spatialization, taking a mono audio signal and azimuth/elevation parameters to produce stereo left-right output.

nodes.label: KEMAR mannequin
nodes.description: A dummy head and torso from MIT that approximates human ear features and is used to produce generalized HRTFs for 3D audio systems.

nodes.label: Keith Martin
nodes.description: Co-creator with Bill Gardner of the MIT HRTFs dataset, a comprehensive set of head-related transfer functions for 3D audio.

nodes.label: Transaural audio
nodes.description: Loudspeaker-based 3D audio playback technique that loses spatial detail due to unknown nonlinear transformations imposed by the listening environment.

nodes.label: Dolby Surround
nodes.description: Multispeaker surround sound system that manipulates volume levels in an array of speakers to create virtual sound source placement.

nodes.label: Cross-talk cancellation
nodes.description: Technique used to improve transaural loudspeaker playback by approximating binaural listening conditions.

nodes.label: R. Erik Spjut
nodes.description: Author of the chapter on convolution in Csound, discussing mathematical and practical applications of convolution in computer music.

nodes.label: strset opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that stores filenames in the orchestra and passes them as p-field values from the score for use in instruments.

nodes.label: Convolution
nodes.description: A signal processing technique that combines two signals (an audio signal and an impulse response) to create effects such as echoes and reverberation.

nodes.label: Direct Convolution
nodes.description: A convolution method using equation 26.1 that does not introduce delay, unlike the method used in the convolve opcode.

nodes.label: Gaussian Reverb
nodes.description: A reverberation technique using a decaying exponential envelope applied to a random signal generated by the gauss opcode, considered more realistic than uniform reverb.

nodes.label: diff opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that emphasizes high frequencies and de-emphasizes low ones by taking the difference between neighboring sound samples, with a 6 dB per octave slope.

nodes.label: lpread opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for LPC resynthesis that reads analysis data and tracks fundamental frequency and residual amplitude.

nodes.label: lpreson opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for linear-predictive-coding resynthesis used in sound transformation and morphing applications.

nodes.label: Magdalena Klapper
nodes.description: Author of the chapter on Csound's ADSYN, LPREAD, and LPRESON opcodes, focusing on additive synthesis and linear-predictive-coding techniques.

nodes.label: Morphing
nodes.description: A sound transformation technique using analysis/resynthesis to create smooth transitions between different sound sources or timbres.

nodes.label: Heterodyne Filter Analysis
nodes.description: An analysis technique that decomposes harmonic or quasi-harmonic sounds by multiplying the signal with sine and cosine waveforms at fundamental and harmonic frequencies, using orthogonality properties to extract amplitude and frequency pairs.

nodes.label: ADSYN
nodes.description: A Csound opcode for additive resynthesis that takes amplitude, frequency, and speed control signals plus a harmonic analysis file to resynthesize sounds with independent transposition and time-scaling.

nodes.label: Fourier Theory
nodes.description: Mathematical theory stating that any function can be decomposed into a sum of simple harmonic motion, applied to sound analysis and synthesis.

nodes.label: Orthogonality
nodes.description: A mathematical property of sine and cosine functions that is essential to heterodyne filter analysis, allowing extraction of individual frequency components from complex signals.

nodes.label: allpole filter
nodes.description: A type of filter with several smooth peaks used in LPC to model the vocal tract characteristics, where filter poles represent points of resonance or formant regions.

nodes.label: LPC Synthesis
nodes.description: Linear Predictive Coding synthesis technique for resynthesizing natural sounds through analysis and reconstruction using filter coefficients and pitch information.

nodes.label: lpread opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode that reads LPC analysis files and creates four control signals: root-mean-square of residual and original signals, normalized error signal, and pitch.

nodes.label: lpreson opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode that performs LPC resynthesis using control signals from lpread and an input audio signal (excitation source such as noise, pulse-train, or original sound).

nodes.label: lpfreson opcode
nodes.description: Formant-shifted version of the lpreson opcode in Csound for modified LPC resynthesis.

nodes.label: vpvoc opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode extending phase vocoder processing and synthesis capabilities.

nodes.label: pvinterp opcode
nodes.description: A Csound unit generator that performs cross-synthesis with interpolation between both frequency and amplitude data from multiple analysis files.

nodes.label: pvcross opcode
nodes.description: A Csound unit generator that performs cross-synthesis by combining amplitude data from different phase vocoder analysis files.

nodes.label: Analysis-based-synthesis
nodes.description: Techniques that derive spectral data from audio signals and use this data to produce synthetic versions or new sounds.

nodes.label: Csound Phase Vocoder
nodes.description: A Csound unit generator system for analyzing and resynthesizing sound using phase vocoder techniques, including the pvanal analysis program and pvoc resynthesis opcode.

nodes.label: Window Size
nodes.description: In phase vocoder analysis, the number of samples included in each FFT analysis window, affecting frequency resolution.

nodes.label: Overlap
nodes.description: In phase vocoder analysis, the number of overlapping analysis windows, related to window-size and hop-size by the formula: overlap = window-size/hop-size.

nodes.label: Frame Rate
nodes.description: The number of analysis frames per second in phase vocoder data, calculated from hop-size and sampling rate.

nodes.label: Time Pointer
nodes.description: A Csound control mechanism using line segments or curves to selectively preserve or stretch different temporal portions of a sound during phase vocoder processing.

nodes.label: Breakpoint Function
nodes.description: A representation of phase vocoder analysis data where each frequency bin contains time-indexed frequency and amplitude envelopes.

nodes.label: pvanal program
nodes.description: A Csound analysis program that produces phase vocoder data files containing frequency and amplitude information for resynthesis.

nodes.label: Spectral Envelope Preservation
nodes.description: A phase vocoder technique (ispecwp argument) that maintains formant characteristics when transposing pitch by rescaling amplitudes across the frequency range.

nodes.label: Pibroch
nodes.description: A centuries-old Scottish classical bagpipe form characterized by slow movement and sudden pitch leaps, used as source material for spectral analysis.

nodes.label: pvread opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that reads analysis data from phase vocoder files to generate control functions for frequency and amplitude arguments of oscillators.

nodes.label: vpvoc opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode identical to pvoc that takes the result of tableseg or tablexseg and uses the resulting function table to apply spectral enveloping to phase vocoder analysis data.

nodes.label: tableseg opcode
nodes.description: A Csound unit generator that interpolates linearly between values stored in f-tables to produce time-varying functions, used for dynamic spectral envelope control.

nodes.label: tablexseg opcode
nodes.description: A Csound unit generator similar to tableseg that performs exponential interpolation between f-table values to create time-varying functions.

nodes.label: Spectral Enveloping
nodes.description: A technique using vpvoc with tableseg or tablexseg to dynamically scale the amplitudes of analysis bins, creating effects like lowpass, highpass, bandpass, and bandreject filtering.

nodes.label: pvbufread opcode
nodes.description: A Csound unit generator that accesses data from phase vocoder analysis files for use in cross-synthesis operations.

nodes.label: Michael A. Pocino
nodes.description: Author of the analog waveshaping chapter in The Csound Book, focusing on efficient implementation of analog signal processing techniques in Csound.

nodes.label: pvinterp
nodes.description: Csound opcode for phase vocoder interpolation that enables cross-synthesis and morphing between two analyzed sound files with dynamic control over time, amplitude, and pitch.

nodes.label: pvbufread
nodes.description: Csound opcode for reading phase vocoder analysis files into a buffer for use with pvinterp and other phase vocoder operations.

nodes.label: Linear Predictive Coding (LPC) Analysis
nodes.description: Speech analysis technique that extracts pitch, spectral envelope, and other parameters for resynthesis and cross-synthesis applications.

nodes.label: Comparator
nodes.description: Analog waveshaping circuit that compares an input signal to a reference voltage and produces high or low output, creating pulse-like waveforms from audio signals.

nodes.label: table
nodes.description: Csound opcode for table lookup operations, enabling waveshaping and other signal transformations using function tables.

nodes.label: Pulse Wave Oscillator
nodes.description: An oscillator with variable pulse width, implemented in Csound using a sawtooth oscillator and a comparator to produce pulses of varying widths.

nodes.label: Comparator Waveshaping
nodes.description: A technique using table-lookup comparators to implement audio-rate relational and logical operations without setting control rate equal to sampling rate.

nodes.label: Schmitt Trigger
nodes.description: A circuit component that detects zero-crossings of a signal by ignoring values between two thresholds, used to generate clean pulse waves from noisy guitar signals.

nodes.label: Guitar Sub-Octave Generator
nodes.description: A technique that inverts the signal during every other cycle to make a guitar sound one octave lower when mixed with the original signal.

nodes.label: Michael Pochino
nodes.description: Author of the chapter on efficient implementation of analog waveshaping in Csound, demonstrating audio-rate comparator techniques for guitar signal processing.

nodes.label: Audio-Rate Operations
nodes.description: Signal processing operations performed at the audio sampling rate in Csound, enabling high-fidelity waveshaping and comparisons.

nodes.label: Sub-octave Generator
nodes.description: A signal processing technique that inverts every other cycle of an input waveform to produce an output one octave lower, implemented using divide-by-two counters and phasors.

nodes.label: Divide-by-Two Counter
nodes.description: A circuit that generates a square wave at half the frequency of an input pulse wave by detecting sign changes at pulse edges.

nodes.label: Guitar Signal Processing
nodes.description: Application of digital signal processing techniques to guitar audio, including sub-octave generation and harmonic synthesis.

nodes.label: Robin Whittle
nodes.description: Developer of the zak opcodes, which provide flexible routing methods between effects routines in Csound.

nodes.label: ZAK opcodes
nodes.description: Csound opcodes for inter-instrument communication and audio signal routing, including zaw, zar, zawm, and zacl for writing, reading, mixing, and clearing audio channels.

nodes.label: Compressor
nodes.description: Dynamics processing effect that reduces dynamic range by monitoring input signal level and varying gain applied to output, with common compression levels of 2:1 and 4:1.

nodes.label: Limiter
nodes.description: A compressor variant with severe compression curves (10:1 or 100:1) that prevents signal levels from exceeding a specified limit.

nodes.label: Noise Gate
nodes.description: Dynamics processing effect that removes unwanted background noise and hiss by silencing signals below a specified threshold while allowing higher-level signals to pass.

nodes.label: De-Esser
nodes.description: Dynamics effect that reduces artifacts from consonant sounds such as 's' and 'p' by monitoring high-frequency components and applying compression based on filtered signal level.

nodes.label: Distortion
nodes.description: Audio effect that operates in the nonlinear range of an amplifier, producing a distorted version of the input signal.

nodes.label: Multieffects Processor
