nodes.description: Audio processing system combining multiple effect categories including dynamics processing, filtering, and pitch effects with flexible routing capabilities.

nodes.label: Noise Gate
nodes.description: An audio processor that removes static or system noise by setting output gain to zero when sound is below a threshold level.

nodes.label: De-esser
nodes.description: Audio processor that attenuates sibilant frequencies using a highpass filter and RMS-based gain control, implemented as instr 3012.

nodes.label: Tube Amplifier Distortion
nodes.description: Nonlinear distortion characteristic of vacuum tube amplifiers, described as warmer and more musical than other distortion types, modeled through waveshaping.

nodes.label: Three-band Equalizer
nodes.description: Audio processor that independently controls gain of low, mid, and high frequency bands using Butterworth filters, implemented as instr 3018.

nodes.label: Wah-wah Pedal
nodes.description: Lowpass filter effect incorporating vowel-derived resonances that sweep between 'ahh' and 'ooh' sounds to create characteristic wah-wah character.

nodes.label: zaw opcode
nodes.description: Csound opcode for writing to an audio channel, used to output processed signals from effect instruments.

nodes.label: nlfilt opcode
nodes.description: Non-linear filter opcode in Csound that avoids the need to set kr = sr and provides simpler code for resonant filter design.

nodes.label: Wah-wah
nodes.description: Guitar effect implemented using lowpass and resonant filters with formant modeling, controlled by an oscillator.

nodes.label: Delay-based pitch shifter
nodes.description: An audio effect that modulates pitch by varying the delay time of a signal using an oscillator, implemented in Csound using delayr and deltapi opcodes.

nodes.label: Tremolo
nodes.description: A periodic variation in the volume of a sound, implemented by multiplying the input signal by a low-frequency oscillating sine wave between 0 and 1 in amplitude.

nodes.label: Panner
nodes.description: An audio effect that sweeps a signal from one stereo channel to another by multiplying channels with complementary low-frequency sine waves 180 degrees out of phase.

nodes.label: Stereo delay with cross feedback
nodes.description: A delay effect that independently delays left and right channels with cross-channel feedback, allowing delayed signals from each channel to mix with the original in either channel.

nodes.label: Csound archives
nodes.description: A repository of Csound examples and implementations, including many reverb designs that can be modified for custom multieffects systems.

nodes.label: cpsxpch
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that converts values to generate non-12-note equal-tempered scales.

nodes.label: Auto-panner
nodes.description: An LFO-based audio effect that oscillates a signal between left and right channels using modulation.

nodes.label: entry.c
nodes.description: A Csound source file that defines opcode syntax, argument types, and performance-time requirements.

nodes.label: AUXCH structure
nodes.description: Csound memory management structure designed for allocating buffers used in delay-lines and similar algorithms.

nodes.label: auxalloc function
nodes.description: Csound function for allocating space via the AUXCH structure with automatic housekeeping and space recovery.

nodes.label: gensub function
nodes.description: Csound function in fgens.c that manages table initialization routines and can be extended with new GEN types.

nodes.label: fgens.c
nodes.description: Csound source file containing GEN routine implementations and the gensub function.

nodes.label: OPDS field
nodes.description: Header field in opcode data structures for organizing opcode chaining and managing initialization and performance steps.

nodes.label: Cscore
nodes.description: A Csound utility for score manipulation and processing, implemented in cscore.c and supporting functions.

nodes.label: Marc Resibois
nodes.description: Author of the opcode implementation chapter in The Csound Book, demonstrating practical techniques for adding custom unit generators to Csound.

nodes.label: The C Programming Language (2nd ed.)
nodes.description: Reference text by Kernighan and Ritchie published in 1988 by Prentice Hall, cited for C programming knowledge.

nodes.label: Phil Winsor
nodes.description: Author of 'Computer Music in C' (1991), a reference for computer music programming.

nodes.label: Computer Music in C
nodes.description: Book by Phil Winsor published in 1991 by Tab Books, covering computer music programming techniques.

nodes.label: IMPULSE opcode
nodes.description: A simple example opcode designed to generate a single pulse of given amplitude, used to demonstrate basic opcode design principles in Csound.

nodes.label: Mini Moog emulation
nodes.description: A physical modeling opcode in Csound (moog1.c) that emulates the classic Moog synthesizer.

nodes.label: Plucked string emulation
nodes.description: A Csound opcode (pluck.c) that emulates the sound of plucked string instruments using physical modeling techniques.

nodes.label: Block Processing
nodes.description: Csound's processing model where opcodes compute small blocks of samples sequentially and send them to output, rather than computing entire instrument buffers at once.

nodes.label: OPDS Structure
nodes.description: A required component at the beginning of every Csound opcode data structure that allows the Csound kernel to handle invocation and registration of instruments uniformly.

nodes.label: cs.h Header File
nodes.description: A Csound header file that contains definitions for OPDS and global variables like ksmps, required for opcode development.

nodes.label: entry.c
nodes.description: A Csound file that maintains the opcodlst array, defining all available opcodes and their syntax for the Csound language.

nodes.label: Impulse Opcode Example
nodes.description: A sample opcode implementation used throughout the chapter to demonstrate Csound opcode development, generating an impulse at the start of a note.

nodes.label: Dynamic Amplitude Modifier
nodes.description: A compressor/expander-type unit opcode that modifies signal amplitude as a function of its power content, implementing compression, expansion, limiting, and noise gating effects.

nodes.label: Compression Ratio
nodes.description: A parameter controlling the strength of amplitude modification in compression/expansion algorithms, where a ratio of one leaves sound unchanged, greater than one expands, and less than one compresses.

nodes.label: Compressor
nodes.description: An audio processor that reduces the amplitude of signal peaks to make sound more uniform, commonly used to smooth transient attacks.

nodes.label: Expander
nodes.description: An audio processor that increases the dynamics of a signal's tail by amplifying quiet portions while leaving loud portions unchanged.

nodes.label: Limiter
nodes.description: An audio processor that ensures output signal level does not exceed a given threshold value, preventing hard clipping in digital recording systems.

nodes.label: DAM opcode
nodes.description: A custom Csound unit generator implementing dynamic audio processing with modes for compression, expansion, limiting, and noise gating.

nodes.label: Compressor/Limiter
nodes.description: Dynamic range processing algorithm that reduces gain above a threshold using compression ratios and adjustable attack/release times.

nodes.label: Opcode Data Structure
nodes.description: C struct containing OPDS header, input/output signal pointers, parameters, and state variables needed to maintain opcode instance state across processing calls.

nodes.label: Delay Line Effects
nodes.description: Time-domain audio processing in Csound including flanging, chorus, pitch shifting, and harmonization using delay lines.

nodes.label: TB-303
nodes.description: Classic analog synthesizer emulated in Csound as a tone wheel organ with rotating speaker effects.

nodes.label: Paul Lansky
nodes.description: Electroacoustic composer with works including notjustmoreidlechatter, Fantasies and Tableaux, and Things She Carried.

nodes.label: John R. Pierce
nodes.description: Computer music researcher; co-author of Current Directions in Computer Music Research (1989) and composer of early digital synthesis works.

nodes.label: The Computer Music Tutorial
nodes.description: Foundational textbook by Curtis Roads published in 1996 by MIT Press.

nodes.label: Electroacoustic Music
nodes.description: Musical discipline combining electronic and acoustic elements, taught and researched by Riccardo Bianchini.

nodes.label: Digital Sound Synthesis
nodes.description: Technique of generating sound using digital computation and algorithms.

nodes.label: Morton Subotnick
nodes.description: Composer of electronic music, creator of Silver Apples of the Moon.

nodes.label: Silver Apples of the Moon
nodes.description: Electronic music composition by Morton Subotnick, released on Wergo label.

nodes.label: Isao Tomita
nodes.description: Electronic music composer, creator of Tomita's Greatest Hits.

nodes.label: Alejandro Vinao
nodes.description: Composer of Son Entero and Triple Concerto, featured in recommended listening.

nodes.label: Formant Analysis
nodes.description: Acoustic analysis of vowel sounds across different vocal ranges (soprano, alto, tenor, bass, countertenor) with frequency, amplitude, and bandwidth values.

nodes.label: Sound Intensity
nodes.description: Measurement of acoustic power in watts per square meter and decibels, ranging from threshold (0 dB) to pain threshold (120 dB).

nodes.label: Pitch Conversion
nodes.description: Csound opcodes and functions for converting between different pitch representations including octave-point-class, cycles-per-second, and MIDI note numbers.

nodes.label: CPS (cycles per second)
nodes.description: Frequency measurement in Hertz used in Csound for specifying pitch values.

nodes.label: Csound Error Messages
nodes.description: Diagnostic output system in Csound that reports fatal errors, warnings, and informational messages during compilation and performance of audio synthesis.

nodes.label: MIDI in Csound
nodes.description: Real-time MIDI event handling in Csound, allowing instruments to receive and respond to MIDI channel data and note events.

nodes.label: Function Table (ftable)
nodes.description: A data structure in Csound that stores waveforms, lookup tables, and other audio data for use by synthesis and processing opcodes.

nodes.label: PVOC Format
nodes.description: A phase vocoder file format used in Csound for time-stretching and pitch-shifting analysis data.

nodes.label: PVOC
nodes.description: Phase vocoder analysis/synthesis tool referenced in Csound error messages.

nodes.label: MIDI Support in Csound
nodes.description: Csound opcodes for MIDI input/output, note control, and real-time message handling including midiin, midiout, noteon, and noteoff.

nodes.label: Instrument Control
nodes.description: Csound features for managing instrument invocation, duration, real-time performance, and scheduling including schedule, turnon, and turnoff opcodes.

nodes.label: Signal Generators
nodes.description: Csound opcodes for generating audio signals including oscillators, phasors, envelope generators, and table access functions.

nodes.label: fmvoice opcode
nodes.description: Csound FM synthesis opcode designed to simulate vocal timbres with vowel, tilt, and vibrato parameters.

nodes.label: fmbell opcode
nodes.description: Csound FM synthesis opcode for generating bell-like timbres with frequency modulation and vibrato control.

nodes.label: fmrhode opcode
nodes.description: Csound FM synthesis opcode for emulating Rhodes electric piano sounds.

nodes.label: fmmetal opcode
nodes.description: Csound FM synthesis opcode for generating metallic timbres through frequency modulation.

nodes.label: STFT Resynthesis (Vocoding)
nodes.description: A signal processing technique in Csound using phase vocoder opcodes (pvoc, pvadd, pvinterp, pvcross) for time-stretching and spectral manipulation.

nodes.label: LPC Resynthesis
nodes.description: Linear Predictive Coding resynthesis technique in Csound using opcodes like lpread, lpreson, and lpfreson for voice and speech synthesis.

nodes.label: moog Opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that emulates the Moog synthesizer ladder filter with amplitude, frequency, and filter control parameters.

nodes.label: Signal Modifiers
nodes.description: A category of Csound opcodes that process and transform audio signals through filtering, envelope shaping, delay, and effects.

nodes.label: Filter Opcodes
nodes.description: Csound opcodes for frequency-selective filtering including tone, reson, moogvcf, butterworth, and biquad filters.

nodes.label: Envelope Modifiers
nodes.description: Csound opcodes for shaping amplitude envelopes including linen, linenr, envlpx, and envlpxr.

nodes.label: Delay Opcodes
nodes.description: Csound opcodes for time-domain signal delay including delayr, delayw, vdelay, and multitap.

nodes.label: Reverberation Opcodes
nodes.description: Csound opcodes for spatial reverberation effects including reverb, comb, alpass, and waveguide implementations.

nodes.label: Convolution Opcodes
nodes.description: Csound opcodes for convolution-based processing and morphing including convolve and cross2.

nodes.label: Spatialization Opcodes
nodes.description: Csound opcodes for panning and spatial audio processing including pan, locsig, space, and hrtfer.

nodes.label: Zak Patch System
nodes.description: A Csound subsystem for inter-opcode communication using global memory arrays for audio and control signals.

nodes.label: Signal Input and Output
nodes.description: Csound operations for reading and writing audio signals, including in, ins, out, outs, soundin, diskin, and file I/O operations.

nodes.label: Csound Score Syntax
nodes.description: Csound score language features including macro definitions, conditional compilation, and file inclusion for organizing musical parameters.

nodes.label: MIDI Real-Time Events
nodes.description: Csound capability to read MIDI real-time events from devices and MIDI file event streams for live performance and file-based control.

nodes.label: Csound Utility Programs
nodes.description: Analysis and processing utilities including sndinfo, hetro, lpanal, pvanal, cvanal, and pvlook for sound file analysis and spectral processing.

nodes.label: STFT analysis
nodes.description: Short-Time Fourier Transform analysis for time-frequency decomposition of audio signals.

nodes.label: Hetrodyne analysis
nodes.description: Analysis technique for tracking frequency components and partials in audio signals using heterodyning.

nodes.label: Chaos Systems
nodes.description: Mathematical models including Duffing's equation, Lorenz attractor, and Rössler attractor used for generating complex, non-periodic sound synthesis.

nodes.label: Auditory Localization
nodes.description: The perception of sound source direction using spectral cues, head movement, cone of confusion, and Doppler effects.

nodes.label: J. ffitch
nodes.description: Csound developer and contributor referenced in the index of The Csound Book.

nodes.label: W. G. Gardner
nodes.description: Researcher who developed the Gardner reverb algorithm using allpass filters.

nodes.label: D. Gabor
nodes.description: Theoretical contributor referenced in relation to granular synthesis concepts.

nodes.label: A. Horner
nodes.description: Researcher who developed the Horner-Ayers algorithm for contiguous-group synthesis.

nodes.label: H. Helmholtz
nodes.description: Acoustic theorist referenced in relation to initial transient and acoustic theory.

nodes.label: Henning Mikelson
nodes.description: Csound composer and developer credited with work on FM synthesis, waveguide instruments, and reverberation design.

nodes.label: Carla Lippe
nodes.description: Contributor to granular synthesis techniques in Csound.

nodes.label: Waveguide Instruments
nodes.description: Physical modeling synthesis using Karplus-Strong algorithm and mathematical models for plucked-string and percussion instruments.

nodes.label: Riccardo Bianchini
nodes.description: Italian composer, electroacoustic music professor, and software developer born in Milan in 1946. Professor of Electroacoustic Music at conservatories in Pescara, Milan, and Rome since 1974.

nodes.label: Alessandro Cipriani
nodes.description: Italian composer and electroacoustic music specialist who studied at Conservatorio S.Cecilia in Rome and with Barry Truax. He has taught electroacoustic music at Ist. Mus. V. Bellini in Catania since 1995 and is a co-founder of Edison Studio in Rome.

nodes.label: James Dashow
nodes.description: Author of a reading on dyad controlled additive synthesis in the Virtual Sound book.

nodes.label: Virtual Sound
nodes.description: A comprehensive textbook on sound synthesis and signal processing theory and practice with Csound, published by ConTempo in 2000 as an English translation of the 1998 Italian edition Il Suono Virtuale.

nodes.label: ConTempo
nodes.description: Italian publisher based in Rome that published Virtual Sound and related computer music materials.

nodes.label: MUSIC360
nodes.description: A predecessor to Csound, authored by Barry Vercoe.

nodes.label: MUSIC11
nodes.description: A predecessor to Csound, authored by Barry Vercoe.

nodes.label: Waveshaping Synthesis
nodes.description: A synthesis technique that uses function tables of various shapes to generate signals, employing the table opcode and GEN routines.

nodes.label: Nicola Bernardini
nodes.description: Author of a reading on Csound and Linux in the Virtual Sound book.

nodes.label: Eugenio Giordani
nodes.description: Lecturer who discusses the implementation of Barry Truax's granular synthesis method in Virtual Sound.

nodes.label: DirectCsound
nodes.description: Real-time Csound implementation with interactive control features including MIDI activation and virtual control interfaces.

nodes.label: VMCI
nodes.description: Virtual Midi Control Interface, a tool for interactive control in Csound with slider panels, virtual joystick panels, and virtual keyboard panels.

nodes.label: WCShell
nodes.description: A Windows graphical shell application for Csound, written in Microsoft Visual Basic 5.00, providing a command console, text editor, and utility programs for orchestra and score file management.

nodes.label: Modulation Synthesis
nodes.description: A basic sound synthesis technique covered in Virtual Sound, including amplitude and frequency modulation methods.

nodes.label: Filters and Delay Line Effects
nodes.description: Sound processing techniques including reverberation, echo, and chorus effects explained in Virtual Sound using Csound.

nodes.label: Virtual Sound
nodes.description: A comprehensive manual on Csound by Riccardo Bianchini and Alessandro Cipriani, designed for musicians learning digital sound synthesis from beginner to advanced levels.

nodes.label: Deferred-time Synthesis
nodes.description: Sound synthesis where the process takes longer than the duration of the generated sound, requiring the output to be stored to disk and played back later.

nodes.label: Conservatory of Pescara
nodes.description: An Italian conservatory where electronic music classes were taught in 1977, which formed the basis for this book.

nodes.label: EMS synthesizer
nodes.description: An analog synthesizer that was among the most advanced sound facilities at well-equipped electronic music centers in the late 1970s.

nodes.label: Sound synthesis
nodes.description: The theory and practice of generating sound using computers and electronic devices, a primary focus of this book.

nodes.label: Sound processing
nodes.description: The modification and transformation of sampled or synthesized sound through computer algorithms.

nodes.label: audio variable (a-rate)
nodes.description: In Csound, a variable whose name begins with 'a' that is updated at the sampling rate and stores audio-rate signal values.

nodes.label: Virtual Sound
nodes.description: A book by Bianchini and Cipriani that teaches Csound sound synthesis and audio processing techniques.

nodes.label: Filter
nodes.description: A device that allows some frequencies to be emphasized over others, essential for subtractive synthesis.

nodes.label: Flow-charts
nodes.description: A graphical representation method for visualizing procedures and linked events, using rectangular boxes for actions and diamond boxes for conditional tests.

nodes.label: MAX
nodes.description: A graphical computer music software with a user interface for representing musical procedures visually.

nodes.label: KYMA
nodes.description: A graphical computer music software with a user interface for representing musical procedures visually.

nodes.label: Patchwork
nodes.description: A graphical computer music software with a user interface for representing musical procedures visually.

nodes.label: Foldover
nodes.description: An aliasing phenomenon where frequency components higher than half the sampling rate are folded back into the audible range, causing distortion.

nodes.label: Oversampling
nodes.description: A technique where D-A converters work at sampling rates at least 4 times higher than the nominal value to shift aliased components above the anti-aliasing filter passband.

nodes.label: ilimit opcode
nodes.description: A Csound opcode that constrains initialization variables within specified upper and lower limits.

nodes.label: Standard MIDI File (SMF)
nodes.description: A standard file format established in 1993 for storing MIDI data in a format common to commercial software products like sequencers and notation programs.

nodes.label: Tremolo
nodes.description: A sound effect created through slight amplitude modulation using a control-rate modulating signal at sub-audio (infrasonic) frequencies.

nodes.label: Carrier Oscillator
nodes.description: In FM synthesis, the primary oscillator whose frequency is modulated by a modulator oscillator to produce the output signal.

nodes.label: Modulator Oscillator
nodes.description: In FM synthesis, the oscillator whose waveform controls the frequency deviation of the carrier oscillator.

nodes.label: Peak Frequency Deviation
nodes.description: The maximum amount by which the carrier frequency deviates from its base frequency in FM synthesis, calculated as the modulation index multiplied by the modulator frequency.

nodes.label: Critical Band
nodes.description: The smallest frequency difference between two components that allows the human ear to perceive them as separate and distinct sounds rather than a single sound.

nodes.label: Foldover Phenomenon
nodes.description: An aliasing effect that occurs when FM synthesis generates frequencies higher than the Nyquist frequency, causing them to fold back into the audible frequency range with phase shifts.

nodes.label: Reverberation Time
nodes.description: The time it takes for echoes to decrease in amplitude by 60 dB, a main acoustical characteristic of a room or hall.

nodes.label: GEN02 Routine
nodes.description: A Csound GEN routine that transfers parameter values into a memory table for use with function tables, with optional normalization.

nodes.label: Norbert Wiener
nodes.description: Mathematician and theorist who wrote on spatio-temporal continuity, quantum theory, and music (1964).

nodes.label: Abraham Moles
nodes.description: Researcher who contributed to granular synthesis approach in 1969.

nodes.label: Riverrun
nodes.description: A 1988 tape piece by Barry Truax where sound grains are likened to water drops that accumulate to create the image of large river flow.

nodes.label: DMX-1000
nodes.description: Real-time processor controlled by a host microcomputer used in early implementation of granular synthesis algorithm.

nodes.label: Musiques Formelles
nodes.description: A 1971 work by Iannis Xenakis that defined the first compositional theory based on sound grains.

nodes.label: De Poli
nodes.description: Researcher cited for defining granular synthesis in 1981 as a technique exploiting discrete-time functions to create chains of elementary sounds.

nodes.label: Mass/Spring Paradigm
nodes.description: A physical modeling approach developed by Hiller and Ruiz in 1971 that requires precise description of physical characteristics (length, width, thickness, mass, elasticity) and boundary conditions, using difference equations to obtain a wave equation describing the resulting sound signal.

nodes.label: MSW Synthesis
nodes.description: A physical modeling approach developed by McIntyre, Schumacher, and Woodhouse in 1983 based on precise study of wave birth and propagation, partitioning the physical model into a non-linear excitation mechanism and a linear resonator.

nodes.label: MOSAIC
nodes.description: A synthesis program that incorporated modal synthesis methodology for physical modeling.

nodes.label: MODALYSE
nodes.description: A synthesis program that incorporated modal synthesis methodology for physical modeling.

nodes.label: Hiller
nodes.description: Co-developer of the mass/spring paradigm for physical modeling in 1971.

nodes.label: Ruiz
nodes.description: Co-developer of the mass/spring paradigm for physical modeling in 1971.

nodes.label: Calvet
nodes.description: Co-developer of modal synthesis for physical modeling in 1990.

nodes.label: Laurens
nodes.description: Co-developer of modal synthesis for physical modeling in 1990.

nodes.label: Adrien
nodes.description: Co-developer of modal synthesis for physical modeling in 1990.

nodes.label: McIntyre
nodes.description: Co-developer of MSW synthesis for physical modeling in 1983.

nodes.label: Schumacher
nodes.description: Co-developer of MSW synthesis for physical modeling in 1983.

nodes.label: Woodhouse
nodes.description: Co-developer of MSW synthesis for physical modeling in 1983.

nodes.label: Smith
nodes.description: Co-developer of the waveguide model for physical modeling between 1982-1993.

nodes.label: Cook
nodes.description: Co-developer of the waveguide model for physical modeling between 1982-1993.

nodes.label: Yamaha
nodes.description: Synthesizer manufacturer that uses waveguide model technology in commercial applications.

nodes.label: Korg
nodes.description: Synthesizer manufacturer that uses waveguide model technology in commercial applications.

nodes.label: CShell
nodes.description: A previous generation MS-DOS application for Csound that preceded WCShell's development.

nodes.label: Microsoft Visual Basic 5.00
nodes.description: The programming language used to write WCShell.

nodes.label: Scorex
nodes.description: An application designed to convert Csound scores into spreadsheet format, allowing manipulation of p-fields through operations like addition, multiplication, interpolation, and random value generation.

nodes.label: Iterated Nonlinear Functions
nodes.description: A synthesis technique based on chaos theory that applies recursive transformations to generate audio samples with turbulent, noisy, or harmonic properties.

nodes.label: Iterated Function Synthesis
nodes.description: A class of synthesis techniques where a stream of samples is calculated as the sequence of nth iterations of some function, with the iteration itself determining coherent or chaotic patterns rather than the nonlinear function being iterated.

nodes.label: Chebychev Polynomial
nodes.description: A mathematical function commonly used in waveshaping synthesis to transform input signals.

nodes.label: GSC4
nodes.description: A Csound program for granular synthesis that generates four independent stereo streams of sonic grains with automated grain generation at the micro-level while preserving control over synthesis parameters.

nodes.label: Musica/Complessità
nodes.description: An Italian seminar held in summer 1988 where Barry Truax presented research and musical compositions based on real-time granular synthesis.

nodes.label: GEN Methods
nodes.description: Csound functions (GEN7, GEN10, etc.) used to create control functions and waveforms for synthesis parameters in the score file.

nodes.label: John Strawn
nodes.description: Co-editor of Foundations of Computer Music (1985) and Digital Audio Signal Processing (1985).

nodes.label: Charles Rosen
nodes.description: Music theorist whose works The Classical Style and Sonata Forms were translated to Italian by Riccardo Bianchini.

nodes.label: Politecnico University
nodes.description: Italian university where Riccardo Bianchini studied Piano, Composition, Electroacoustic Music, and Engineering.

nodes.label: Conservatorio S. Cecilia
nodes.description: Music conservatory in Rome where Alessandro Cipriani completed his studies in music composition and electroacoustic music.

nodes.label: RAI (Italian State Radio)
nodes.description: Italian broadcasting organization with which Riccardo Bianchini collaborated from 1983 to 1991.

nodes.label: Alba D'Urbano
nodes.description: Visual artist who collaborated with Alessandro Cipriani on intermedia pieces and sound-video installations since 1989.

nodes.label: Ist. Mus. V. Bellini
nodes.description: Music institution in Catania where Alessandro Cipriani has taught electroacoustic music since 1995.

nodes.label: Edison Studio
nodes.description: Studio in Rome co-founded by Alessandro Cipriani.

nodes.label: Stefano Taglietti
nodes.description: Collaborator with Alessandro Cipriani on the electroacoustic work 'Il Pensiero Magmatico'.

nodes.label: Kontakte
nodes.description: Electronic music composition by Karlheinz Stockhausen that was the subject of multiple analytical papers by Alessandro Cipriani.

nodes.label: Il Pensiero Magmatico
nodes.description: Electroacoustic composition by Alessandro Cipriani and Stefano Taglietti for tape, piano, percussions and mixed choir, released on the Edipan label.

nodes.label: Bourges International Electroacoustic Music Competition
nodes.description: International competition where Alessandro Cipriani's works 'Visibili' and 'Recordare' received mentions and finalist selections.

nodes.label: Musica Nova
nodes.description: Electroacoustic music competition in Czech Republic where Alessandro Cipriani's 'Terra Fluida' won the main prize.

nodes.label: Rome
nodes.description: Italian capital city where Alessandro Cipriani studied and co-founded Edison Studio.

nodes.label: Electroacoustic Tradition
nodes.description: Theoretical concept developed by Alessandro Cipriani exploring the relationship between oral, written, and electronic music traditions.

nodes.label: Nyquist Theorem
nodes.description: Fundamental principle stating that sampling rate must be at least twice the highest frequency to avoid aliasing.

nodes.label: Heterodyne Analysis
nodes.description: Fourier analysis technique in Csound using HETRO.EXE for the adsyn additive synthesis generator.

nodes.label: HRTF Processing
nodes.description: Head-related transfer function processing for 3D spatial audio in Csound using the hrtfer opcode.
